## §0. The arc, in one paragraph

V3.0 and V3.1 built the system. V3.2 makes it earn its keep. The bot
runs three engines on paper across 11 disciplines, captures every
signal/gate/regime/near-miss faithfully, and has a solid order safety
perimeter. What it does not have: an analytics layer to read the
captured data, a runtime for the validated recommendation pipeline, a
surfaced regime×discipline edge matrix, or a cutover path. V3.2 closes
those four gaps in five phases. Crucially: cutover is gated by **edge
proven in data**, not by calendar. There is no rush.

---

## §1. Operating principles for V3.2

These supplement (do not replace) the constitutional layer in
`DECISIONS_HISTORY.md` §B.

**1.1 — Cutover is gated by data, not date.** No live-money flip until
at least 2 cells of the regime×discipline matrix are PROVEN_EDGE for
30+ days, AND at least one quarter of paper trading shows positive
walk-forward EV across active engines.

**1.2 — Slow is the right pace.** V3.0 and V3.1 ran at ~10 drops/week.
V3.2 targets ~1 significant drop/week. The work is research, not
debugging. Each drop should be designed and reviewed before code
starts.

**1.3 — Every analytic earns its place by answering a real question.**
No dashboard tile without a question it answers. No metric without a
threshold for action. No chart without a hypothesis it tests.

**1.4 — Statistical honesty is non-negotiable.** Every reported metric
ships with a 95% bootstrap CI. Point estimates are forbidden in V3.2
deliverables. "60% win rate at n=5" is not a finding.

**1.5 — When in doubt, persist.** Capture-First (Principle 7) carries
forward. New tables, new columns, new sidecar rows are cheap.

**1.6 — Conservative-failure direction (added 2026-05-11).** When code
can't compute a value with confidence (FX rate unavailable, instrument
can't be hydrated, partial data on a position), bias toward NOT causing
harm. Example: Y23 `_y23_compute_usd_values` returns `None` on FX
failure so dashboard shows "—" rather than a wrong number. Y25
`gross_deployed_usd` contributes 0 on hydrate failure (under-counts
rather than inflating). Other gates catch over-deployment via
independent paths. Block-on-failure makes the bot fragile to provider
hiccups; conservative-failure does not. This is a §22.x-class invariant
— see also §22.18-§22.20.

## §2. The five phases

| Phase | Goal | Drops | Operator-time estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2.1** Make it boring | No babysitting required | 7 | 1-2 weeks |
| **2.2** Make data legible | Edge becomes visible | 10 | 4-6 weeks |
| **2.3** Make tuning safe | Hypothesis loop runs itself | 7 | 2-3 weeks |
| **2.4** Cutover prep | Real money, gated by proof | 6 | 2-3 weeks (deferred) |
| **2.5** Edge-hunting | Continuous improvement | 5+ | Ongoing |

**Phase 0 prelude (added 2026-05-07):** Before Phase 2.1 began, an
audit of captured signal data found that 5-7 of the 8 stock-discipline
DayTrade gates were either always-pass stubs (sector-strength,
earnings-blackout, session-phase) or always-fail data bugs
(premarket-gap, premarket-volume on non-US markets). Per-market gate
redesign was inserted as a precursor track. See §2.0 below.

## §2.0. Phase 0 — DayTrade gate redesign track (precursor)

**Goal:** every DayTrade discipline runs on a research-grounded
per-market gate set instead of the legacy 8-gate stock template that
was US-tuned and ineffective elsewhere.

**Status:** ✅ Complete as of 2026-05-08. Architecture proven.
Broker-side fix follow-up (0.1e) blocks soak-data accrual.

| Drop | Engine | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1a | Scanner unblock + sector routing fix | ✅ shipped 2026-05-07 |
| 0.1b | Crypto 6→4 + ATR R-tier stops | ✅ shipped 2026-05-07 |
| 0.1c | US 8→5 + per-discipline routing + dashboard fixes | ✅ shipped 2026-05-07 |
| 0.1d | FTSE + ASX 8→4 (combined) | ✅ shipped 2026-05-08 |
| **0.1e** | **Broker reconcile fix + /health liveness probe** | **⬜ next** |
| 0.2 | FX-aware EUR sizing (port 2.1.0 Swing pattern) | ⬜ |
| 0.3 | Tune & soak | ⬜ |

**Architectural outcome:** per-market gate dispatch in
`_evaluate_symbol_stock` routes by `market_name` to dedicated
evaluators. Each market has its own threshold dataclass for
independent tuning. Three new gate modules under
`alphabot/strategy/signals/`:
- `daytrade_us_gates.py` (5-gate set)
- `daytrade_eu_apac_helpers.py` (3 shared gates: vwap-hold,
  relative-volume-intraday, ema-fast-slow)
- `daytrade_ftse_gates.py` (4-gate, EU/APAC base + break-of-prior-day-high)
- `daytrade_asx_gates.py` (4-gate, EU/APAC base + auction-follow-through)

Plus the existing `daytrade_crypto_gates.py` (4-gate from 0.1b).
Legacy 8-gate path preserved in `_evaluate_symbol_stock_legacy` as
fallback; no canonical market reaches it post-0.1d.

**Why this isn't part of Phase 2.1:** Phase 2.1 is operational
hardening (zombie sweeps, audit views, parity enforcement). Phase 0
was a quality fix that had to land before any Phase 2.x soak data
would be meaningful — measuring "how often does the bot win" is
useless if the gates are always-pass stubs.

**Why 0.2 and 0.3 are still in Phase 0 not Phase 2.1:** they're
direct dependencies of the gate redesign — FX sizing (0.2) fixes a
P&L visualisation bug for EUR conversion that the new gates
expose; tuning + soak (0.3) is the validation that the new gates
actually improve signal quality. Once 0.3 closes, Phase 2.1 begins.

## §3. Phase 2.1 — Make it boring

**Goal:** the bot runs for 7+ days without operator intervention.
Clean logs, no manual stop-cancellations, no naked positions, no
deploys to fix recurring edge cases.

### Drop 2.1.0 — Reconcile loop fix

> **Status (2026-05-10): superseded.** The crash class this drop
> was scoped to fix has been resolved across multiple May 9–10 drops
> — see HISTORY §F.4. Specifically: Hotfix 2026-04-28 added per-symbol
> tolerance, Drop A fixed the discipline-from-contract derivation,
> Drop V (2026-05-10) rewrote the entire reconcile mechanism around
> a Binance WebSocket User Data Stream + 60s REST sweep, and Drop
> 1.4.9 fixed venue resolution from IBKR contract. The original
> 2.1.0 scope no longer matches code reality. Drop deferred / closed.
>
> **Residual gap from the May 8 0.1e plan:** `/health` endpoint
> still reports HEALTHY based on connection state alone, not actual
> endpoint liveness (e.g. canary `/historical/bars` self-test). Not
> shipped under any later drop. Tracked as an open item in HANDOVER.

**What it does in plain terms:** stops the broker shouting a `ValueError`
every cycle when reconciling ASX positions. The bug is silent (non-fatal)
but it pollutes journalctl and hides real warnings.

**Technical:** `_discipline_for_symbol` in the reconcile path defaults to
STOCK_SWING when symbols carry ASX disciplines. Resolve from the
position's stored discipline, not the lookup default.

**Files:** `alphabot/broker/reconcile.py`. ~10 lines changed.

### Drop 2.1.1 — Crypto loss-stop tracker parity

**What it does in plain terms:** if crypto has a brutal day, the engine
halts itself like Swing and DayTrade do. Right now crypto's daily P&L
isn't feeding the per-engine loss-stop breach detector built in 1.2.3a.

**Technical:** `LossStopTracker` constructed in `broker/main.py` for
IBKR side. Mirror the construction in `broker_binance/main.py`. Wire
it to the close-fill path.

**Files:** `alphabot/broker_binance/main.py` + tests.

### Drop 2.1.2 — Cross-pollination structural enforcement

**What it does in plain terms:** even if a future bug forgets to filter,
SQLite refuses to write a crypto row to the IBKR position table or
vice versa. The DB itself becomes the firewall.

**Technical:** CHECK constraints on shared tables (`positions`, `stops`,
`fills`, `orders`, `trades`) enforcing discipline-to-broker mapping.
Plus a triggered audit on insert that logs any rejected write.

**Files:** new migration. Updated tests. ~50 lines.

### Drop 2.1.3 — Stop-table cleanup + zombie sweep

**What it does in plain terms:** automatically cancels orphan stops —
either a `stops` row marked ACTIVE with no matching position, or an
IBKR open STP order with no DB row. Today these have to be cleaned by
hand.

**Technical:** one-shot script `scripts/zombie_sweep.py` + nightly
systemd timer `alphabot-zombie-sweep.timer`. Runs at 02:00 UTC, logs
every cancellation to audit.

**Files:** new script, new systemd unit, tests. ~150 lines.

> **Note (2026-05-12):** much of this scope was effectively absorbed by
> the Y30b janitor sweep J1 (zombie position cleanup, 1h grace). Stops
> dimension still queued — see §22.11 retention boundary.

**What it does in plain terms:** you can see at a glance whether

**Technical:** new endpoint `GET /api/master/reconcile-state`. Frontend

**Goal:** every position has a working exit. Crypto + IBKR + Swing
all use exchange-side TP/SL where the venue supports it; runner-side
exits cover what the venue doesn't.

**Status as of 2026-05-13 end of session:**

The Y-series was triggered by the cascade described in HISTORY §F.1:
five drops over two days each shipping clean but system-level

that crypto exits had been built piecewise across multiple drops,

### Drop Y2 — Binance OCO broker primitive ✅ shipped 2026-05-10 evening

Atomic OCO support added to `broker_binance`. Per Binance docs verified
during the May 10 review (and updated to current API state):

- OCO = LIMIT_MAKER (TP leg) + STOP_LOSS / STOP_LOSS_LIMIT (stop leg)
- Both legs same quantity
- TP leg fires → stop leg auto-cancels (and vice versa)
- `trailingDelta` only applies to the stop leg
- 1 OCO consumes 2 order slots in `EXCHANGE_MAX_ORDERS` filter
- Endpoint moved from legacy `POST /api/v3/order/oco` (deprecated) to
  current `POST /api/v3/orderList/oco` with `aboveType`/`belowType`
  shape. Implemented via `python-binance` 1.0.30's
  `v3_post_order_list_oco`.

New endpoint: `POST /stops/attach-oco` (parallel to existing
`/stops/attach`; HANDOVER pre-Y2 said `/orders/submit-oco`, operator
approved the renamed shape on Y2 ship). Schema extended via migration
031: `tp_price`, `tp_order_id`, `tp_client_order_id`, `oco_list_id`,
`oco_client_list_id` columns on `crypto_stops` (all nullable;
existing rows continue to validate). Partial UNIQUE index on
`oco_list_id` for O(1) listStatus reverse lookup. **Pure additive;
nothing calls it post-Y2 — Y3 wires it up.**

Tests: 34/34 pass. Locks the OCO primitive contract for §22.8.

### Drop Y3 — Daytrade crypto switches to OCO ✅ shipped 2026-05-10 evening

`daytrade/crypto.py::_attach_initial_stop` switched from
`attach_crypto_stop` (Drop X path) to OCO submission via Y2's
`attach_crypto_oco`. TP leg = entry × (1 + `DAYTRADE_TAKE_PROFIT_R_MULTIPLE`
× stop_loss_pct/100) = entry × 1.03 at default 2:1 R-multiple over 1.5%
stop. Stop leg = entry × (1 - stop_loss_pct/100) with native
`trailingDelta`. `reconcile.py` extended with `_handle_list_status` for
listStatus events; resolves exit reason from per-leg clientOrderId
prefix matching (`tp-` vs `stp-`).

**Architecture impact:** TP for crypto daytrade is exchange-side. Bot
crash → TP still fires. Runner's TP evaluation becomes a no-op for
crypto daytrade in the steady state (kept in place as defense-in-depth
fallback; race window <100ms vs runner 5s tick). Time-stop and
emergency-attach stay with the runner. **Caveat:** Y3 only affects new
BUYs. The 8 legacy crypto daytrade positions held at Y3 deploy time
remain on single-leg stops (with audit-default 5% width); they exit
normally and Y3 takes effect on the next entry. Also fixes a Drop X
bug where `atr_value` was silently dropped from the strategy override
signature.

Tests: 29/29 pass. Mypy net -1 (Y3 fixes Drop X). Locks §22.5 to OCO.

### Drop Y4 — Swing active management overhaul ✅ shipped 2026-05-10 night

**Re-scoped during build session per operator clarification.** Initial
Y4 spec was "swing crypto OCO + first TP for swing." Operator clarified
the actual ask was *"very good stale equity logic that gets rid of buys
that are doing nothing — when there are other highly rated stocks
waiting they get sold."* Y4 became swing active management (eviction
logic), not OCO-for-swing. OCO for swing equity stays queued (Y6/Y7).

**What shipped:**

1. **Hard time stop.** Operator-locked at 5 days. Any swing position
   held ≥ 5 days exits unconditionally, ignores P&L, ignores rotation,
   ignores all other rules. Reads `positions.opened_at` directly
   (verified reliable; `position_meta` is unreliable per forensics).
   Original swing-strategy plan called for this; was never wired.

2. **Stale-progress eviction.** New tier on top of existing flat-tier
   stale audit. Existing flat-tier requires |pnl| ≤ 0.5% — misses
   "+1.2% sitting forever" cases. New criteria: held ≥ 1 day AND
   pnl < 5% AND no new highs in last 6 bars (~24h on H4, 6 days on
   D1). The "no new highs" gate is what prevents evicting positions
   that are still climbing.

3. **Observability on legacy stale-capital audit.** Forensics found
   93 stale-capital log lines but only 2 actual evictions in 14 days.
   Most cycles silently skip on `pnl_pct is None` or `current_price
   missing`. Y4 surfaces skip counts at DEBUG level so future
   debugging is fast.

**Operator-locked params, wired in `main_swing.py`:**
- `time_stop_days = 5`
- `stale_progress_minutes = 1440` (1 day)
- `stale_progress_pnl_threshold_pct = 5.0`

### Drop Y4.2 — position_meta backfill / naked-audit fix ✅ shipped 2026-05-12

Verified 2026-05-10: the naked-position audit calls `attach_stop` (or
`attach_crypto_stop`) directly to recover positions, bypassing
`record_entry()` which is what writes `position_meta`. Result: 13/13
currently-held swing positions and several daytrade-crypto positions
(ADAUSDT class) had no `position_meta` row. Anything that reads
`position_meta.entry_price` or `position_meta.take_profit_target` for
currently-held positions silently missed, falling back to `avg_cost`
which is wider than the original entry → wider implied stops → wider
implied TP targets → "bot held +3.4% instead of taking profit at
configured 3%" failure mode.

**What shipped:** the naked-position audit now writes synthetic
`position_meta` rows when re-attaching, using `avg_cost` as
`entry_price` with `position_meta.synthetic_entry=1` flag so analytics
can tell the difference. Idempotent under race conditions during
emergency-exit. Unblocks Y8 (dashboard TP/SL columns) reading
position_meta for legacy positions.

### Drop Y25 — Cross-engine gross-cap rationalisation ✅ shipped 2026-05-12

11 files, 178 KB. Closes audit bug **#4** — the highest-priority
not-previously-queued item.

**The bug.** Pre-Y25 the bot-wide `MAX_GROSS_DEPLOYED_PCT=0.60` cap
(operator-locked per CAPS §1) was only enforced by the **daytrade**
engine. Swing and Scalp had no bot-wide cap at all. Daytrade's
enforcement itself was pence-blind: `_gross_deployed_eur(positions)`
summed `|qty * avg_cost|` treating all currencies as account-base.
LSE positions contributed pence as if USD (100× inflation).

**New shared helper** `alphabot/shared/gross_cap.py`:

- `gross_deployed_usd(positions, fx)` — sums `|qty * avg_cost|` in
  USD across positions. Pence-aware via
  `units_per_major_for(instrument)` (Y23 module). FX-aware via
  duck-typed input: accepts either a dict `{currency: usd_per_unit}`
  (strategy side, from `fetch_fx_rates(broker)`) OR an object with
  `usd_value(amount, currency) -> float` (broker side, `fx_service`).
  USD-pegged currencies (USD, USDT, USDC, BUSD) passthrough without FX
  call.
- `gross_deployed_passes_cap(...)` — predicate returning
  `(passes: bool, details: dict)`. Details dict carries
  `gross_deployed_usd_current`, `_projected`, `gross_cap_usd` for
  SkipReason logging. Supports `rotated_position` arg that subtracts
  the rotated notional from the projected sum.
- `_hydrate_instrument(p)` — tries `position.instrument` first
  (broker-side has full Instrument), falls back to
  `Instrument.from_canonical_id(position.instrument_canonical_id)`
  (strategy-side post-Y25). Returns `None` if neither path works.
- **Conservative-failure design throughout**: hydrate failure or FX
  outage contributes 0 to the deployed sum (under-count rather than
  wrong-units inflate). Aligns with the project's broader
  conservative-failure direction (§1.6).

**Broker→strategy plumbing.** `instrument_canonical_id` field added to:
- `broker/api/_models.py:PositionResponse`
- `broker/api.py` (the duplicate local PositionResponse class — legacy
  split — and the construction site)
- `broker/api/routes_positions.py` (construction site)
- `strategy/broker_client.py:Position` dataclass (empty-string default
  for back-compat with mocks/tests)
- `strategy/broker_client.py:list_positions` reads the field from the
  response payload

**Daytrade fix.** `_sizing.py`: both call sites (engine cap step 9 +
bot-wide cap step 10) switched to the shared helper.
`_gross_deployed_eur` kept (deprecated comment) for any external test
imports. `PortfolioState` gains
`fx_rates: dict[str, float] | None = None`. `_base.py` state builder
imports `fetch_fx_rates` and threads it into both happy and
degraded-path PortfolioState returns. **Note:** `portfolio_value_eur`
field is misnamed — actually populated from
`account.portfolio_value_usd`, so the cap math is FX-neutral.

**Swing addition.** `_shared.py`: new gross-cap gate inserted in
`_evaluate_one` just before `_submit_buy_and_attach`. Reads
`MAX_GROSS_DEPLOYED_PCT` from settings; passes `positions`, `equity`
(= USD), `fx_rates`, and `target_usd=sizing.shares*last_price_usd` to
the predicate. On block: logs `GROSS_DEPLOYED_USD_CAP` near-miss reason;
sends rejected entries to READY-zone for re-qualification next cycle.

**Scalp addition.** `_sizing.py`: new `GROSS_DEPLOYED_USD_CAP` value
added to `ScalpSkipReason` enum. `ScalpPortfolioState` gains
`fx_rates`. `ScalpSizingConfig` gains `max_gross_deployed_pct`. Step 6
(existing scalp engine cap) upgraded to use the shared pence-aware
helper filtered to scalp disciplines. New step 6b (bot-wide gate)
inserted after engine cap. `target_qty` bounded by bot-wide headroom
in addition to engine headroom. `_base.py` state builder fetches
fx_rates; `_build_sizing_config` populates `max_gross_deployed_pct`
from settings.

**Tests:** 40/40 Y25 (34 source-pin + 6 behaviour layer sandboxing
real `Instrument.from_canonical_id` hydration, FX dict-vs-service
equivalence, rotation arithmetic, conservative-failure paths). 89/89
stacked Y22+Y23+Y15+Y25.

**Lesson: §32.1 (re-baseline per drop) needs special care for any file
other drops have touched. See §22.19.**

## §3.6 — Cross-cutting decisions logged during the Y-series

### Decision: Forensic cap audit drove drop re-sequencing (2026-05-11 PM)

**Trigger.** Post-Y22 deploy at 17:42, dashboard showed +9707% P&L on
the LSE positions — visible only because IBKR market data
subscriptions had been purchased earlier in the day. Operator asked:
*"have you audited everythig? if not dont stop."*

**Forensic audit ran.** Findings filed at `cap_audit_final.md`: 11
real bugs found across cap/sizing/exposure surface. Six were
pence-blindness variants (LSE pence treated as pounds/USD); three were
scope bugs (filters misapplied to position sets); three were config
drift (stale numeric values).

**Decision.** The pence-blindness cluster was **atomic** — shipping
one without the others would just rotate bug manifestations. So Y23
was rescoped from "fix the broker risk gate alone" to "fix all six
pence-blind sites in one drop". Plus bug #4 (bot-wide gross cap) had
no queued slot at all — it was extracted into a new drop Y25 between
Y15 and Y8.

**Revised queue at the time:** Y22 (deployed) → Y23 (atomic pence) →
Y24 (gateway compose) → Y15 (config rationalisation) → **Y25
(gross-cap, NEW SLOT)** → Y8 (dashboard TP/SL) → Y12 (.env cleanup) →
Y11 (FTSE/ASX scalp; folds in latent bugs #8 and #10).

All of the above shipped by 2026-05-12.

### Decision: Conservative-failure direction as a project-wide invariant

See §1.6 above. This is a §22.x-class invariant: when adding new gate
logic, default to conservative-direction failure unless there's a
specific reason otherwise.

### Decision: `alphabot/shared/gross_cap.py` is the canonical cross-engine cap helper

**Principle.** Pre-Y25 each engine had its own deployed-sum function
(`_gross_deployed_eur` in daytrade, `_gross_deployed_eur_engine` in
scalp, nothing in swing) with subtly different semantics —
pence-blind, scope-blind, currency-name misleading. Y25 unifies on ONE
helper in `shared/` that all three engines call.

**Going forward.** Any new code that needs to sum deployed capital
across positions (a new engine, a new cap, a new dashboard analytics
panel) **must** import from `alphabot.shared.gross_cap` rather than
rolling its own sum. The legacy `_gross_deployed_eur` and
`_gross_deployed_eur_engine` functions are retained as
deprecated-comment stubs for any external test imports but **must not
be used in production sizing chains**.

**Why `shared/` not `strategy/sizing/`.** The helper is structurally
cross-engine: it's called from both broker-side (eventually, when
broker-side gross-cap gates ship) and strategy-side; it must not
import from either engine; it depends only on `shared/instrument.py`
and `shared/price_units.py`. Placement under `shared/` is the natural
fit.

### Decision: Deploy convention locked — PowerShell + VPS in every drop (2026-05-13)

Every drop response must include PowerShell + VPS deploy commands.
Operator hard rule mid-session: *"powershell and vps please. make sure
you give them to me at every drop"*. This holds for all future drops.

### Decision: JS file shipping policy (2026-05-13, post-Y36 revert)

JS files SHOULD NOT be shipped as full files in drop zips unless the
assistant has verified its local baseline matches the deployed file
byte-for-byte. Default: ship the change as a sed patch / deploy script
that edits the deployed file in place. Reasoning: §22.19 + operator's
small attention budget for re-verifying every JS file. Python files
don't typically hit this class — they're shipped as full file
replacements per drop.

## §4. Phase 2.2 — Make the data legible

**Goal:** any reasonable question about edge gets a confident answer in
under 30 seconds. The dashboard stops showing only "what's happening
now" and starts showing "what's working over time."

### Drop 2.2.0 — EV-per-discipline with bootstrap CIs

**What it does in plain terms:** for every discipline (US Swing, FTSE
Swing, ASX Swing, smallcaps, intraday, crypto disciplines) the
dashboard shows expected value per trade with a 95% confidence
interval. You can see which disciplines are honestly making money and
which are noise. No more point estimates.

**Technical:** DuckDB query on `trades` table, walk-forward 30-day
window. Bootstrap 1000 resamples for CI. Render as horizontal bars with
whiskers, sorted by lower-CI bound.

**Files:** new analytics module `dashboard/analytics/ev.py`,
DuckDB integration via `sqlite_scanner`, frontend chart.

### Drop 2.2.1 — Score calibration curves

**What it does in plain terms:** does a score of 7 actually win 70% of
the time? Plot expected vs realised win rate per score bucket
(5.0-5.5, 5.5-6.0, ...). If the curve is well-calibrated, score-based
gating works. If it isn't, score is broken and we fix it.

**Technical:** signal score on entry vs trade outcome on exit. Buckets
of 0.5. Per discipline, with sample-size labels.

**Files:** `dashboard/analytics/calibration.py`, frontend. **High
leverage — likely surfaces a structural issue immediately.**

### Drop 2.2.2 — Gate funnel

**What it does in plain terms:** answers your original question — "are
the gates the right ones?" For every 1000 candidates evaluated, shows
how many fail at gate 1, gate 2, etc. Per discipline, per regime. If a
gate filters 80% of candidates but the survivors don't outperform the
rejects, the gate is just noise.

**Technical:** query on `signal_gates` sidecar table (V3 Phase 0
foundation). Sankey-style or stacked bar. Hover shows pass-rate and
post-gate win rate.

**Files:** `dashboard/analytics/gate_funnel.py`, frontend.

### Drop 2.2.3 — Per-discipline P&L heatmap by hour-of-day

**What it does in plain terms:** shows when each discipline makes money.
US session as a heatmap (hours 13:30-22:00 UTC). FTSE session
(08:00-16:30 UTC). ASX session (00:00-06:00 UTC). Crypto 24/7. Tells
you whether Scalp performs better in the first 90 minutes, whether
crypto crushes during Asian hours, etc.

**Technical:** trade entry hour × P&L, segmented by discipline.

**Files:** `dashboard/analytics/temporal.py`, frontend.

### Drop 2.2.4 — Exit-reason breakdown

**What it does in plain terms:** tells you whether you're making money
via target-hits or via trailing stops, and whether stop-losses are
eating your gains. Per discipline, the distribution of exit reasons
(TAKE_PROFIT / TRAIL_STOP / STOP_LOSS / ROTATION / EOD_FLATTEN /
SIGNAL_EXIT / EMERGENCY_EXIT / STALE_CAPITAL).

**Technical:** `trades.exit_reason` is captured already (Drop 8.5.35).
Aggregate, render as stacked bars per discipline.

**Files:** `dashboard/analytics/exit_reasons.py`, frontend.

### Drop 2.2.5 — Near-miss counterfactual replay

**What it does in plain terms:** the hard one. Takes every
SCORE_NEAR_MISS row (signal that scored just below threshold), runs
forward bars from the captured features to compute simulated P&L.
Aggregates by tier — PREMIUM, STANDARD, WATCH-BAND. Tells you "the 47
PREMIUM near-misses you skipped this week would have made +$430 if
taken." Direct evidence for threshold tuning.

**Technical:** `near_miss_outcomes` table is partially populated
already. Build the replay simulator that consumes
`near_misses.persisted_features` and stepwise computes hypothetical
position lifecycle including stops. Persist results in
`near_miss_outcomes`.

**Files:** new module `alphabot/analytics/near_miss_replay.py`,
backend job (nightly), dashboard view, tests. **Most complex drop in
Phase 2.2.**

### Drop 2.2.6 — Per-engine performance leaderboard

**What it does in plain terms:** operator's morning coffee view. Win
rate, avg win, avg loss, profit factor, max drawdown — segmented by
score bucket, time of day, day of week, regime. Three tabs: Swing,
DayTrade, Scalp. Sortable, filterable. The thing you check every
morning.

**Technical:** DuckDB views over `trades` joined with `signals` (for
score) + `regime_snapshots` (for regime). Frontend with column
sorters.

**Files:** `dashboard/analytics/leaderboard.py`, frontend.

### Drop 2.2.7 — Regime × discipline EV matrix

**What it does in plain terms:** §18 made manifest. 11 disciplines × 4
regimes (BULL/BEAR/FLAT/TRANSITION). Each cell shows EV, n, CI, and
state (UNKNOWN / INCONCLUSIVE / PROVEN_EDGE / NO_EDGE). Cells turn from
grey to green/red as evidence accrues. **This is where you find edge —
by discovering which (discipline, regime) combinations earn and which
don't.**

**Technical:** matrix view as a heatmap-table hybrid. State transitions
(`UNKNOWN → INCONCLUSIVE` at n=15, `INCONCLUSIVE → PROVEN_EDGE` when CI
above zero, etc.) are computed nightly into a `participation_matrix`
table.

**Files:** new migration for the matrix table, nightly compute job,
dashboard view.

### Drop 2.2.8 — NO_EDGE state declaration

**What it does in plain terms:** when all active cells are NO_EDGE or
UNKNOWN and nothing scores above threshold, the strategy engine
declares state NO_EDGE on the dashboard with a reason —
"stock_swing NO_EDGE in CHOPPY (EV -$1.40, n=31)." The bot can
honestly say "not broken, not trading, here's why." Prevents
threshold-lowering panic during slow periods.

**Technical:** strategy daemon checks the matrix at cycle start. If
state is NO_EDGE, emits a structured event with full audit detail.
Dashboard surfaces a banner.

**Files:** `alphabot/strategy/main.py`, dashboard banner component.

### Drop 2.2.9 — Feature-distribution snapshots

**What it does in plain terms:** nightly snapshot of the distribution
of every feature value (RSI, volume_ratio, regime mix, etc.) per
discipline. Foundation for drift detection — if RSI distributions look
very different in November vs September, the world has changed and
your scoring assumptions might too.

**Technical:** new table `feature_drift_snapshots`. Nightly job
computes percentiles (5/25/50/75/95) per feature per discipline. Stored
forever.

**Files:** new migration, nightly job, no UI yet (Phase 2.3 reads it).

**Phase 2.2 outcome:** real analytics surface. Edge or its absence is
visible. Every "should I tune X?" question has a way to answer it with
statistics. The bot stops being an opaque box.

---

## §5. Phase 2.3 — Make tuning safe

**Goal:** every config change goes through hypothesis → shadow window →
statistical verdict → learn from failures. Compound learning over time.
No more vibe-based threshold tweaks.

### Drop 2.3.0 — Hypothesis intake form

**What it does in plain terms:** dashboard form for proposing changes.
Required fields: config delta (what's changing), discipline scope,
predicted outcome with numeric threshold, required sample size,
evidence cited. Vague proposals rejected at submission. Even before
the runtime exists, the act of filling this in kills 50% of bad ideas.

**Technical:** new endpoint `POST /api/experiments/propose`. Form
validation. Stores to `experiments` table (already exists from V2
Phase 5).

**Files:** `dashboard/api/routes_experiments.py`, frontend form, tests.

### Drop 2.3.1 — Shadow lifecycle runtime

**What it does in plain terms:** when you submit a hypothesis, the
engine spawns a shadow strategy with the proposed config. Shadow sees
identical candidates, places synthesized orders, never reaches IBKR.
Runs for 14 days. Writes to `experiment_events` continuously.

**Technical:** strategy daemon picks up shadow strategies from
`experiments` table at startup and on `/experiments/start` event.
Routes its orders via `executor_shadow.py` (already exists). Daily
heartbeat into `experiment_events`.

**Files:** `alphabot/strategy/shadow_lifecycle.py`,
`alphabot/strategy/main.py` integration, tests. **Most complex drop in
Phase 2.3.**

### Drop 2.3.2 — Verdict engine

**What it does in plain terms:** at window close, computes Mann-Whitney
U on trade P&L distributions and bootstrap CI on EV delta. Outputs one
of CONFIRMED / REGRESSED / MIXED / INCONCLUSIVE / INVALID. The
experiment gets an honest verdict.

**Technical:** nightly job checks for windows reaching their end date.
Runs the stats. Writes to `experiment_verdicts` (already exists).

**Files:** `alphabot/analytics/verdict.py`, nightly job, tests.

### Drop 2.3.3 — Adoption queue with PIN

**What it does in plain terms:** CONFIRMED verdicts enter a promotion
queue on the dashboard. Operator approves with PIN. Config delta
applies on next strategy restart. No auto-promotion.

**Technical:** new table `adoption_queue`. Endpoint
`POST /api/experiments/adopt`. PIN check. Config-write goes through
the existing `config_history` audit trail.

**Files:** new migration, dashboard view, PIN handler, tests.

### Drop 2.3.4 — Post-adoption verification

**What it does in plain terms:** adopted changes stay watched for 30
days. If actual EV falls >50% below shadow-measured EV with n≥15,
dashboard offers one-click rollback. Catches the case where the
experiment looked good but reality is different.

**Technical:** nightly job compares post-adoption trades against
shadow-window EV. Surfaces a "rollback recommended" badge with
explanation if delta breaches threshold.

**Files:** `alphabot/analytics/post_adoption.py`, dashboard, rollback
handler.

### Drop 2.3.5 — `lessons_learned` writer

**What it does in plain terms:** REGRESSED and MIXED experiments
populate `lessons_learned` (table already exists, currently empty)
with hypothesis text, regime distribution during the window, why it
likely failed. Indexed for full-text search. Failed experiments become
permanent institutional memory.

**Technical:** verdict engine extension. FTS5 index on
`lessons_learned.hypothesis_text + reason_text`. Surfaced in
hypothesis intake form (Drop 2.3.0) so similar past hypotheses appear
during composition.

**Files:** migration for FTS5 index, writer extension, intake-form
integration.

### Drop 2.3.6 — Weekly Claude intelligence run

**What it does in plain terms:** Sunday evening cron job. Claude reads
the previous week's analytics, near-miss replay results, regime-cell
transitions, lessons_learned matches. Produces a structured report:
state of each engine, three highest-leverage hypotheses ranked by
information gain, drift warnings. **This is the actual loop — Claude
reads what the bot captured, proposes tests, operator runs them
through the pipeline.**

**Technical:** new module `alphabot/intelligence/weekly_run.py`.
Generates a structured prompt from DuckDB analytics. Calls Anthropic
API. Writes report to `intelligence_runs` table. Surfaces on
dashboard with prominent badge. (Operator decides whether to wire as
auto-cron or manual trigger.)

**Files:** new module, optional systemd timer, dashboard surface.

**Phase 2.3 outcome:** the system tunes itself within bounds the
operator sets. Every change is statistically validated. Failed
hypotheses make future Claude runs smarter. Compound learning at human
cadence.

---

## §6. Phase 2.4 — Cutover preparation

**DEFERRED until at least 2 cells of the regime×discipline matrix are
PROVEN_EDGE for 30+ days, AND at least one quarter of paper trading
shows positive walk-forward EV across active engines.**

This is the live-money phase. Don't touch it until evidence supports
it.

### Drop 2.4.0 — Two-person live rule (§20.7)

**What it does in plain terms:** prevents a single misread `.env` file
or a single accidental `systemctl edit` from flipping to live money.
Two independent signals required.

**Technical:** env var `IS_LIVE=true` AND signed flag file at
`/home/alphabot/alphabot2/LIVE_ENABLED` modified within last 60
minutes, owned by `alphabot` user. Either alone — broker refuses to
start in live mode.

### Drop 2.4.1 — Pre-cutover safety closure

**What it does in plain terms:** closes the §20 RED items that only
matter when real money is on the table.

**Items shipped together:**
- VIX-extreme halt (VIX > 35 → halt equity disciplines, keep crypto)
- News blackout windows (earnings, FOMC, CPI, NFP)
- Fat-finger gate (reject if implied qty is 100× the symbol's average)
- Monthly B2 restore test as a systemd timer (alphabot-restore-test.timer)
- Cross-discipline aggregate exposure cap (40% gross)

### Drop 2.4.2 — Slippage-haircut infrastructure

**What it does in plain terms:** when live trading starts, the
`live_paper_slippage` table records the difference between expected
fill price and actual fill price for every order. After 4 weeks of
live data, fit a regression model and apply the slippage haircut to
shadow EV. Keeps shadow EV honest after the live flip.

**Technical:** writer hooks on broker fill event. Regression module.
Shadow EV computation extended to apply haircut.

### Drop 2.4.3 — Cutover checklist + pre-flight

**What it does in plain terms:** dashboard view that shows every red
Safety Register item, every PROVEN_EDGE cell, restore-test status,
last reconcile drift, IBKR paper-vs-live account configuration. All
green or the broker refuses to start in live mode.

**Technical:** pre-flight check at broker startup. Refuses to enter
live mode if any item is red or stale.

### Drop 2.4.4 — Live-shadow window

**What it does in plain terms:** first 14 days of live trading. Real
money runs at quarter-Kelly while shadow keeps running at full size in
parallel. Compares slippage and fill quality between live IBKR and
shadow simulator. Real-money exposure capped at 25% of edge-implied
size. Gives you slippage data without betting the farm.

**Technical:** extra `quarter_kelly_live` mode in sizing. Shadow runs
unchanged. Reconciliation between live and shadow daily.

### Drop 2.4.5 — IS_LIVE flip

**What it does in plain terms:** the moment everything has been
working toward. Anticlimactic by design. Config change after every gate
has passed.

**Technical:** `IS_LIVE=true` in env + flag file written + pre-flight
green. Restart broker. Trades real money at full size.

**Phase 2.4 outcome:** real money, with statistical proof that edge
exists. No vibes, no rush, no premature celebration.

---

## §7. Phase 2.5 — Continuous edge-hunting

**Ongoing, post-live (or post-Phase 2.3 if operator decides edge can
be hunted in paper too).**

### Drop 2.5.0 — Overnight backtest grid

**What it does in plain terms:** weekly cron job that proposes new
threshold combinations across all disciplines × gates. Top 3 by
predicted edge feed into the hypothesis intake form for human review.
Generates research candidates faster than humans can.

### Drop 2.5.1 — Intraday decay analysis

**What it does in plain terms:** for each discipline, shows how edge
decays vs hold time. Are we holding winners too long? Cutting losers
too fast? Feeds back into exit logic.

### Drop 2.5.2 — News-event attribution

**What it does in plain terms:** cross-references trade entries
against news events (earnings windows, macro releases, social sentiment
spikes). Tells you whether the bot earns through news periods or
around them.

### Drop 2.5.3 — Monte Carlo drawdown stress test

**What it does in plain terms:** simulates 10,000 random reorderings
of historical trades to project worst-case drawdown distributions. You
know your real risk profile, not just the historical realisation.

### Drop 2.5.4 — Autonomous proposal generation

**What it does in plain terms:** Claude reads `lessons_learned` +
recent feature drift + regime transitions and generates experiment
proposals automatically. Still requires PIN approval to enter shadow.
The recommendation loop closes — system proposes, human approves,
system tests, system learns.

**Phase 2.5 outcome:** the bot is no longer being built. It's being
operated.

| 2026-05-20 | **Y93 — `fill_listener` handles BUY against existing short** | ✅ shipped (pending broker restart deploy) | Closes the catastrophic class surfaced by the 2026-05-20 OPTU runaway. Pre-Y93 ``PositionBook.apply_fill`` (`alphabot/broker/positions.py`) raised `ValueError("Phase 3 does not support shorts")` whenever a fill arrived for a position whose direction didn't match Phase 3's long-only design. The "everything else" branch caught a case that DOES occur in practice — shorts created accidentally (operator TWS SELL races bot SELL, both fire, position runs through zero, six such shorts on 2026-05-20 alone). Once short, every controlled BUY-to-close triggered the raise; the in-memory PositionBook never updated; strategy kept reading the stale short qty; a fresh BUY-to-close fired every cycle; IBKR kept filling them. The OPTU loop was 4 × 27,408 = ~110k shares of intended close-orders all FILLED inside 15 minutes before the operator halted the swing daemon (per HANDOVER_15 §12). Y93 adds `_reduce_short` — a sign-symmetric mirror of `_reduce_long` — and wires it from `apply_fill`. Math: short qty < 0; BUY reduces abs(qty) toward 0; realized P&L on the closed portion = `(avg_cost - fill.price) * closed_qty` (shorts profit on price drops). Defensive: overshoot raises with a pointer to `gate_buy_close_quantity` (Y87) which is meant to clamp at submit time. SELL against existing short still raises (would deepen — `gate_sell_quantity` Y76/Y87/Y92 prevent at submit; the fill-side raise is belt-and-suspenders for a future gate regression). 1e-9 epsilon mirrors Z5's tolerance for IEEE-754 drift. **Tests:** new `tests/test_drop_y93_fill_listener_shorts.py` (13 tests across 6 classes — full close, partial close, P&L profit + loss + accumulation, overshoot raise + no-mutation-on-raise, epsilon tolerance, SELL-against-short still raises, the OPTU runaway scenario end-to-end). **Deploy:** broker restart only — strategy daemons are halted overnight per the Y92 cron-at job; if that job restarts them at 03:00 Paris, Y93 must be live first OR the runaway can recur. Recommended sequence: ship Y93 broker restart now, then the 03:00 Paris auto-restart of swing/daytrade is safe regardless of what the book looks like. See `HANDOVER_15.md §12`. |

## §10. Operational incident log

### 2026-05-13 ~20:45 UTC — Disk filled to 100% during Y36.3 deploy

**Root cause:** 22GB syslog from strategy-daytrade retry-traceback
firehose during the broker crash-loop window, plus 27GB of accumulated
DB backups (Y30a creates but never deletes them).

**Resolution:** truncating syslog + removing old `.bak.*` files. Disk
back to 49%.

**Three Y37 candidates identified:**
1. Rate-limit strategy connection-failure logging.
2. Broker disk preflight (`shutil.disk_usage` before migrations).
3. DB backup retention ("keep last N", deletes older).

Not in scope for the FTSE/ASX bug fix session. Carried forward to §8
backlog.

**§22 amendment — Y94a (2026-05-22), swing + scalp engines retired.**
The daytrade-desk transformation (`docs/Y94_SPEC.md`) removed the swing
and scalp engines. The locks that governed those engines are now
**historical** — the engines they constrained no longer exist:

- **§22.8** (Swing exit philosophy — trail + 5d time-stop +
  stale-progress + flat-stale + signal-exit, no TP) — **superseded**.
  The swing engine is gone. DayTrade exit semantics are now governed
  by the Y94d hybrid stop (breakeven floor + ATR trail + time stop).
- **The scalp constitutional lock** (the scalp 6-gate / 0.6%→0.3%
  squeezing trail / 1% per-trade-risk / 30s-cycle params held in
  `DECISIONS_HISTORY.md §22`) is **lifted** — the scalp engine is gone.

Locks §22.1–§22.7 and §22.9–§22.21 are unaffected — they govern the
broker, crypto, daytrade, janitor, and dashboard subsystems that
remain. Historical `*_swing` / `*_scalp` / `*_smallcap` DB rows and
their `Discipline` enum values are retained for parsing. See the §8
Y94a changelog row.

## §14. V3 Drop Y57 — WAL durability hardening (2026-05-16)

Coordinated drop closing the root causes behind the 2026-05-15→16 WAL
runaway (a leaked never-closed read transaction pinned the WAL; it grew
to 4.72 GB and blocked checkpoints). Scoped from the Y57 discovery
report. Deployed under "Option B" — Binance broker + the three strategy
daemons + janitor restarted; the IBKR broker stayed halted (the Y56
Monday snapshot test depends on its parked state).

**Decisions:**

1. **Connection lifecycle is the caller's job — now enforced.**
   `open_connection()` already documented "callers own the lifetime."
   The three strategy-daemon connections wired in `_daemon_common.py`
   (per-strategy `_db_conn`, two sites; the loss-stop tracker conn) are
   now closed in the daemon shutdown path. The five raw
   `with sqlite3.connect(...)` sites (4 in broker_binance, 1 in
   strategy/cooldown.py) are replaced with `open_connection()` + an
   explicit `close_connection()` — `with` on a sqlite3 connection only
   commits, it does NOT close.

2. **Long-lived daemon connections open `autocommit=True`.** A
   connection idle inside Python's implicit deferred transaction holds
   a WAL read-mark, which is what pins the WAL. `open_connection()`
   gained an `autocommit` flag (`isolation_level=None`); the three
   strategy connections use it. Multi-statement atomicity, where
   needed, uses an explicit `with conn:` block.

3. **WAL growth has explicit backstops.** `connection.py` now sets
   `journal_size_limit` and an explicit `wal_autocheckpoint`.
   `journal_size_limit = 64 MiB` (67108864) — operator-decision class,
   chosen as ~8× a healthy WAL (~8 MB): generous headroom for burst
   writes between checkpoints, but a hard cap so a post-incident WAL is
   truncated back to ≤64 MB rather than left multi-GB. It does NOT cap
   growth while a reader pins the WAL — that is what J7 addresses.

4. **The janitor owns the active WAL drain (sweep J7).** Passive
   auto-checkpoint cannot drain a reader-pinned WAL. A new janitor
   sweep, `J7_WAL_CHECKPOINT`, runs `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` every
   janitor cycle and logs the three checkpoint counters (busy /
   log_frames / checkpointed_frames). The janitor is the right home:
   it already owns infra-wide DB maintenance, and as shared infra it
   restarts under Option B (an in-broker checkpoint loop would have
   stayed dead while the IBKR broker is halted).

5. **`backup_db.sh` survives writer contention.** Adds `.timeout`
   (busy-timeout) so `.backup` waits out a busy writer instead of
   aborting on the first `SQLITE_BUSY`, and an EXIT trap + size check
   so a failed backup leaves NO file, never a 0-byte one (the
   2026-05-16 03:30 run left a 0-byte `alphabot.db.2026-05-16-0330`).

6. **Persistence failures are visible, not silent.**
   `PersistentEventSink.emit()` still swallows DB-write failures (a DB
   hiccup must not crash the broker) but now counts them
   (`persist_failures` / `persist_failures_by_type`) and logs the
   cumulative count. Deliberately NOT a retry queue — just visibility.
   The misleading "kept in memory / a later reconcile re-fetches from
   IBKR" docstring was corrected.

**Out of scope (Y57):** the `_derive_canonical_for_fill`
US-equity-hardcoded fallback in `persistent_sink.py`; centralising the
PRAGMA settings that `retention/`, `agent/`, `market_data_daemon/` each
re-declare independently. (Y58 below took the cold-start-tolerance work,
not these — they remain open backlog.)

## §15. V3 Drop Y58 — strategy cold-start tolerance for an unreachable IBKR broker (2026-05-16)

Single-outcome drop. Y57's Option-B restart exposed a latent bug: the
three strategy daemons cannot cold-start while the IBKR broker is
halted. `StrategyEngine.run()` waits on `wait_until_healthy()` and
re-raises `BrokerUnreachableError` unconditionally, so the daemon exits
non-zero and systemd crash-loops it. AlphaBot trades crypto 24/7 against
the Binance broker; the daemons must be able to cold-start and run
crypto cycles on weekends / overnight when the IBKR broker is
intentionally down. Scoped from the Y58 discovery report, with one
correction made before code was written (see decision 2).

**Decisions:**

1. **The cold-start health gate is conditional on equity-session
   state.** `StrategyEngine.run()` (`engine.py`) still calls
   `wait_until_healthy(timeout_sec=120.0)`. On `BrokerUnreachableError`
   it now consults `any_equity_market_in_session()`: in session, the
   original fatal re-raise is preserved (an unreachable IBKR broker
   during equity hours is a real failure and must surface as a
   crash/alarm); out of session it logs a `COLDSTART_IBKR_TOLERATED`
   warning and proceeds. The fix lives at exactly one site — the gate
   in `run()`. Everything downstream is already tolerant of a down
   IBKR broker (`_strategy_loop` catches every `step()` exception;
   `MultiBrokerProxy` tolerates one broker down).

2. **`any_equity_market_in_session()` reuses `shared/time.py`, not the
   pool-builder's session table.** The Y58 spec proposed hoisting
   `pool_config.py`'s `SESSION_WINDOWS` / `is_market_in_session()` into
   a new `shared/sessions.py`. Discovery had missed that
   `alphabot/shared/time.py` already owns DST-aware, weekday-aware
   equity-session helpers (`is_us_open` / `is_ftse_open` /
   `is_asx_open`). The pool-builder helper is weekday-blind and
   DST-blind — it compares `now.time()` to fixed UTC windows and would
   report US "in session" at Saturday 15:00 UTC, defeating the whole
   weekend use-case. `any_equity_market_in_session()` is therefore a
   one-line OR of the existing `time.py` helpers, added to `time.py` —
   no `sessions.py`, `pool_config.py` untouched. (`pool_config`'s
   weekday-blind `is_market_in_session` is left as-is; it drives the
   pool-refresh schedule, out of Y58 scope — flagged for a later
   audit, see Y58 notes backlog.)

3. **In-session behaviour is unchanged — Monday's snapshot test still
   bites.** Because the gate stays fatal whenever any equity market is
   in session, an IBKR broker that is genuinely broken during US /
   FTSE / ASX hours still crash-loops the daemon exactly as before.
   Y58 only relaxes the weekend / overnight out-of-session case.

**Holiday caveat:** `any_equity_market_in_session()` is holiday-blind
(inherited from `is_session_open`). On an equity holiday the gate still
treats the market as in-session and stays fatal — the safe direction
(an alarm, not silence). Holiday awareness is deferred to the
holiday-calendar improvement already noted on `is_session_open`.

## §16. V3 Drop Y59 — crypto universe single source of truth (2026-05-16)

The crypto trading universe had three sources that could disagree: the
market-data daemon's crypto pool, the Binance broker's `active_universe()`
/ `GET /universe`, and the operator-curated `DAYTRADE_CRYPTO_UNIVERSE` /
`SCALP_CRYPTO_UNIVERSE` tuples. Three lists, three cadences, three
opinions of "what is tradeable". Y59 collapses them to one. Scoped from
the Y59 discovery report; built carefully against the prior session's
approved spec + three operator adjustments + verification additions
V8–V10 (all carried in `HANDOVER_6.md §Y59`).

**Decisions:**

1. **The market-data daemon's crypto pool is the single source of
   truth.** All three crypto engines (swing / daytrade / scalp) consume
   it via `GET /pool?market=crypto` through a new `CryptoPoolScanner`.
   This is locked — see §22.21.

2. **`/pool` gets a discipline-less crypto branch — crypto is NOT added
   to `DISCIPLINE_PROJECTIONS`.** Pre-Y59 `/pool` 404'd for crypto:
   `discipline` was required and `(market, discipline)` validated
   against `DISCIPLINE_PROJECTIONS`, which has no crypto key. Y59 makes
   `discipline` optional and serves the **whole** crypto `pool_snapshot`
   for `market=crypto` — no projection, no cap (`discipline`/`cap` come
   back `null`). Crypto is deliberately kept out of
   `DISCIPLINE_PROJECTIONS` because that dict also drives the
   `universe_snapshots` projection writer — a crypto entry would create
   dead rows nobody reads. Equity `/pool` behaviour is unchanged.

3. **The broker retires its universe — delete, not repoint.**
   `crypto_universe.py` (`active_universe`/`is_tradable`/
   `refresh_universe`), the `GET /universe` endpoint, and the
   `active_universe` membership check in `/contracts/qualify` are all
   deleted. `/contracts/qualify` keeps **only** its exchange-filters
   check — it is now order-feasibility validation only. Repointing
   `/contracts/qualify` at pool membership was rejected: it would gate
   order feasibility on pool membership and **break exits on a held
   coin that ages out of the pool**. The broker must qualify any symbol
   whose order respects the exchange filters. (Verified — V8.)

4. **One unified quality floor, all three slices.**
   `CRYPTO_MIN_QUOTE_VOLUME_USDT = $5M/day` (operator decision
   2026-05-16) plus stablecoin / wrapped / leveraged-token exclusions,
   applied in `binance_scanner.py` before ranking so the liquid,
   volatility, and unusual slices all inherit them. Pre-Y59 only a $1M
   dust gate touched the volatility/unusual slices. The floor was set
   on tradeable merit, not to clear the curated tail — the discovery's
   live-volume finding showed the curated tuples contain genuinely dead
   coins ($0.1M–$0.6M/day), so "clear the curated tail" was a
   meaningless anchor. ~68 USDT pairs clear $5M on a live mainnet pull;
   the realised pool lands well under the 150 budget by design (quality
   over a cosmetic 150 — operator adjustment 2).

**Curated tuples + env vars retired:** `scanners/daytrade_crypto.py`,
`scanners/scalp_crypto.py`, `scanners/_refresh.py`
(`RefreshableUniverseMixin`) deleted; `BINANCE_UNIVERSE_LIMIT` /
`BINANCE_UNIVERSE_MIN_VOLUME_USDT` removed from both `shared/config.py`
and `strategy/config.py` (the audit found the pair declared twice).

**Verified:** 21/21 Y59 tests; full regression 0 new failures vs the
234/9 pre-Y59 baseline; ruff clean. No schema migration.

**Deployed 2026-05-17** (merge `6417d7a`; restart order market-data →
broker-crypto → the three strategy daemons; IBKR broker untouched).
Post-deploy verification green: V1 — `/pool?market=crypto` serves the
whole pool, `discipline`/`cap` null; V9 — realised crypto pool **63
coins** (held 6, liquid 54, volatility 3, unusual 0); V6 — all three
engines scan the 63-pool (swing `universe=63`, daytrade `scanned=63`,
scalp `scanned=63`); V8 — a held coin absent from the pool (`ARBUSDT`)
still qualifies via `/contracts/qualify`. The crypto-pool single source
of truth is **live**.

**Aftermath — two architectural issues surfaced (see §17).** The
broker-crypto restart that the deploy required exposed two pre-existing
DB-vs-exchange quantity-mismatch bugs (not Y59 regressions — Y59 didn't
touch order submission or stop attachment). Both characterised, both
deferred to follow-up drops. Full forensic:
`docs/Y59_AFTERMATH_OCO_NAKED_POSITIONS_2026-05-17.md`.

## §17. Architectural issues surfaced by the Y59 deploy (2026-05-17)

Two pre-existing bugs, neither introduced by Y59, both exposed when the
Y59 deploy restarted `alphabot-broker-crypto`. Recorded here as the
architectural record; each awaits a scoped follow-up drop. **No fix is
proposed yet** — the audit programme (Tier 1) reviews the evidence
first.

**Issue A — reconcile-tolerance vs exit-exactness mismatch.** The
broker's reconcile loop treats a DB-vs-exchange position drift within
`1% / $5` as `NO_ACTION` (§22.4 tolerance). But the exit path submits
the *exact* DB quantity. When a position drifts sub-tolerance in the
`DB > exchange` direction (e.g. XRPUSDT DB 71.1 vs exchange 70.9;
ATOMUSDT 49.12 vs 48.89), the reconciler leaves it — correctly, by its
rule — yet every full-position exit order then fails Binance `-2010`
(insufficient balance), because you cannot sell 71.1 when you hold 70.9.
The broker degrades on the consecutive `-2010` burst. Characterised
2026-05-17; the two affected positions were DB-reconciled to the
exchange balance as an immediate unblock (one-off `positions` UPDATEs,
operator-approved), but the structural mismatch remains.

**Issue B — OCO-attach `-2010` is silent (no DEGRADED, no alarm).** The
daytrade-crypto OCO stop-attach uses the strategy's pre-trade sizing
estimate (`decision.qty`) as the attach quantity, not the broker's
actual fill. When the fill differs from the estimate the OCO attach
requests a stop for a quantity not held → Binance `-2010` → the BUY is
left **naked**. Worse: the OCO-attach failure is raised inside
`broker_binance/stops.py::attach_oco_stop`, which — unlike the order
`executor` path — never calls `state.record_error()`. So the failure
never increments `consecutive_errors`, never trips `DEGRADED`, never
alarms. The broker reports `HEALTHY` while failing to protect every
position it opens. Six naked `crypto_daytrade` positions were created
this way on the 2026-05-17 07:36 restart before the daytrade engine was
halted to stop the bleed. Characterised 2026-05-17.

Both issues are the same shape — **a quantity the bot believes vs the
quantity the exchange holds** — and both await follow-up drop scope
after Audit B2 / C / D.

---

## §18. V3 Drop Y60 — Binance order-quantity correctness (2026-05-17)

The follow-up drop for §17 Issue B (OCO-attach `-2010` → silent naked
position). Scope boundary, operator-set: **Binance broker layer only.
IBKR untouched. Reconciler tolerance policy (§17 Issue A / §22.4)
untouched.** Principle: after any order fills on Binance, the exchange's
view of the balance is authoritative; the bot must use exchange truth
before any downstream SELL.

**Change A — OCO sized from the entry BUY's actual fill.**
`CryptoStopManager.attach_oco_stop` no longer trusts the caller's
`position_qty` (a pre-trade sizing estimate). New `_buy_fill_qty()`
sums `fills.quantity` keyed by the BUY's `client_order_id`
(= `attached_to_order_id`) — a local DB read, no Binance call. Falls
back to the caller estimate with a warning if no fill rows exist.
Root-cause fix for the ATOM incident: an OCO sized 161 against a real
fill of 48 → `-2010` → naked.

**Change B — SELL-quantity clamp at the broker order layer.**
New `BinanceClient.clamp_sell_quantity()`: `final = min(intended,
exchange free balance)`, round DOWN to stepSize, validate LOT_SIZE
minQty + NOTIONAL. Raises `SellClampError` — a clean abort, no order
sent, **not** a broker error (no `record_error()`, no `DEGRADED`).
Called at the **three SELL caller sites** (`CryptoExecutor.submit`,
`attach_stop`, `attach_oco_stop`) before the row is persisted or the
order submitted — deliberately NOT a chokepoint inside
`new_order`/`create_oco_order`, so the persisted `crypto_stops` row
matches exactly what is sent to Binance (a chokepoint clamp would split
DB state from broker truth — the bug class Y60 exists to fix).
`cancel_replace_order` is excluded by design (carries an
already-accepted qty; a resting STOP_LOSS_LIMIT SELL holds its base
asset in `locked`, not `free`). The discipline replacing the
unbypassable guarantee, documented in the `clamp_sell_quantity`
docstring: any new SELL entry path MUST call the clamp before
submission, and a 4th caller MUST add a janitor audit feeder. *(A
§22.x lock for this invariant is a candidate — flagged for operator
decision, not taken unilaterally.)*

**Files:** `broker_binance/client.py`, `broker_binance/stops.py`,
`broker_binance/executor.py`; new test
`test_drop_y60_sell_quantity_correctness.py` (16 tests); 3 mock-client
helper edits in existing broker tests; recovery utility
`scripts/reattach_naked_crypto_y60.py`.

**Deployed 2026-05-17** — commit `3891e9e`, hotfix `5765786`. The
hotfix: `_buy_fill_qty` read the aggregate by `row[0]`, but the broker
connection's `row_factory` is `_dict_row` (dict keyed by column name)
→ `KeyError: 0`, a 500 on the first recovery attach. Fixed to alias the
aggregate `AS fill_qty` and read it by name; the Y60 test harness was
using `sqlite3.Row` (which supports `row[0]` and so masked the bug) and
was switched to the production `_dict_row` factory.

**Recovery — the three naked `crypto_daytrade` positions from §17
Issue B** (ATOMUSDT, CHZUSDT, LUNCUSDT) were re-attached via
`reattach_naked_crypto_y60.py`, operator-confirmed one symbol at a
time, through the Y60-fixed path. All three now ACTIVE in
`crypto_stops` (ids 37054 / 37055 / 37056). `alphabot-strategy-daytrade`
was restarted; the first cycle's 13 OCO attaches all sized to the BUY
fill — Change A corrected a consistent ~3.3× caller oversize on every
one — with 0 `-2010` and 0 clamp aborts.

**Verified:** 16/16 Y60 tests; regression sweep 0 new failures vs
baseline (19 = 19 on the `broker_binance` + OCO surface). No migration,
no schema change → clean `git revert`.

**Deferred / still open:** §17 Issue A (reconcile-tolerance vs
exit-exactness) is untouched — separate drop. The upstream question of
*why* the daytrade caller `position_qty` is a deterministic ~3.3× the
executed fill is NOT fixed by Y60 — Change A makes the OCO correct
regardless, but the sizing-chain overstatement remains a live backlog
item (HANDOVER_6 open item #2; carried to HANDOVER_7).

**Addendum — Drop Y60.1 (2026-05-17, commit `df48d51`).** Y60 Change A
fixed only `attach_oco_stop`. The parallel single-stop path
`attach_stop` (`/stops/attach`, the `STOP_LOSS_LIMIT`-only attach used
when an OCO is not appropriate) still trusted the caller's
`position_qty`. Y60.1 applies the same Change-A shape there: before the
Change-B clamp, `attach_stop` now calls `self._buy_fill_qty(
attached_to_order_id)` and prefers the BUY's executed fill over the
caller estimate (same fallback-with-warning when no fill rows exist;
log tag `[y60.1-changeA]`). ~15 lines, no new helper — reuses the
`_buy_fill_qty` from Y60. Tests extended in
`test_drop_y60_sell_quantity_correctness.py`; deployed via
`alphabot-broker-crypto` restart; regression 0 new failures. The two
attach paths (`attach_stop` / `attach_oco_stop`) now both fill-source
and both clamp — a future drop to **unify** them into one protective-
order attach path is logged in MASTER_TODO §6 (architectural research
backlog), not taken in Y60.1.

## §19. V3 Drops Y62 + Y62.1 — bracket parent MKT → LMT (2026-05-17)

**The bug.** IBKR rejects a TRAIL/STP bracket *child* whose *parent* is
a MKT order — Error 328 ("the order's parent order type does not
support attaching a child order"). A bracket child can only attach to a
LMT or STP_LMT parent. The daytrade engine submitted its bracket entry
with `entry_order_type="MKT"`; IBKR accepted the parent, then
auto-cancelled the TRAIL child via the OCA group. Production evidence
from the `orders` table: `us_daytrade` showed 25/25 TRAIL children
cancelled, 0 fills — every equity daytrade position opened **naked of
its protective stop**. This is the equity-side analogue of the Binance
naked-position class (§17/§18), but with a different root cause: not a
quantity mismatch, an order-type incompatibility.

**Y62 — daytrade fix (commit `c422882`).**
`daytrade/_base.py:_submit_bracket_entry` now submits the parent as a
**marketable LMT**: `entry_limit_price = round_to_tick(entry_price ×
(1 + 10bps), …, direction=UP)` — a 10-basis-point buffer above the
reference price, rounded up to the venue tick so the limit clears
immediately like a market order would but presents IBKR a LMT parent
the TRAIL child can legally attach to. `entry_order_type` MKT → LMT;
the `BRACKET-FILLED` log line became `BRACKET-SUBMITTED` (the order is
no longer assumed instantly filled). Marker `# V3 Drop Y62`.

**Y62.1 — scalp fix (commit `60a456d`).** Scalp shares the bracket
submission shape and had the same MKT parent. The fix in
`scalp/_base.py:_submit_entry` is **conditional on venue**, because
scalp runs both IBKR equity and Binance crypto: when `self.exchange` is
truthy (IBKR equity) it builds the same 10bps marketable-LMT parent
(tick-rounded UP); when `self.exchange` is `""` (crypto) it keeps MKT —
Binance brackets do not have the Error-328 constraint and crypto
protective orders go through the separate `crypto_stops` / OCO path.
Marker `# V3 Drop Y62.1`.

**Tests.** `test_y54_daytrade_bracket_lmt.py` re-pointed Y54 → Y62
(4/4). New `test_y62_1_scalp_bracket_lmt.py` — 6 static-source tests:
marker, the `self.exchange` gate, the LMT branch, the MKT branch, the
10bps buffer, the UP rounding. Regression 0 new failures on both drops.

**Deployed 2026-05-17** via `alphabot-strategy-daytrade` /
`alphabot-strategy-scalp` restarts — strategy-side code only, the
brokers needed no restart. No migration, no schema change → clean
`git revert`.

**Verification deferred to Monday 2026-05-19** — the equity market is
closed over the weekend, so the fix cannot be observed live until the
next session. Monday: confirm equity daytrade/scalp open *protected*
positions (bracket parents filling, TRAIL children no longer
cancelled) and that `alphabot-broker`'s journal shows no Error 328.

## §20. V3 Drop Y63 — scalp ATR multiplier mirror reconciliation (2026-05-17)

**The bug (F-Y61-3, surfaced by the Y61 test triage).** Drop Y54
tightened the broker scalp ATR multiplier `3.0/3.5 → 2.0` in
`shared/stop_sizing.py::ATR_MULTIPLIER` but left two strategy-side
mirrors — `_SCALP_ATR_MULTIPLIER` in `strategy/strategies/scalp/_sizing.py`
and in `strategy/scalp_stop_runner.py` — at the old `us_scalp 3.0 /
crypto_scalp 3.5`. The scalp strategy therefore sized and cached its
stop against the old multiplier (a wider stop) while the broker
attached the protective order at 2.0× — a Layer-1 strategy/broker
contract violation. The two lockstep guard tests
(`test_atr_multiplier_matches_broker`, `test_lockstep_with_broker_constants`)
were left red by Y61 as deliberate guards on this captured bug.

**The fix (commit `9a2ac6a`).** Both mirrors reconciled to
`{us_scalp: 2.0, crypto_scalp: 2.0}`, matching the broker's Y54 value.
The mirrors only carry `us_scalp` / `crypto_scalp` keys; the
`.get(discipline, 2.0)` default already covered `ftse_scalp` /
`asx_scalp`, which the broker also holds at 2.0.

**Tests — same drop, per CLAUDE.md §3.** Updating the multiplier moved
every stop-distance / stop-price / qty / TP value derived from it. Nine
scalp tests were re-baselined to 2.0× in the same commit:
`test_scalp_sizing.py` (7) and `test_scalp_stop_runner_124c.py` (2). Two
test names that referenced crypto's old "higher multiplier" were renamed
(`test_crypto_scalp_uses_higher_multiplier_and_floor` →
`test_crypto_scalp_floor_wins_when_atr_tight`;
`test_crypto_uses_higher_multiplier_and_floor` →
`test_crypto_atr_path_used_when_wide`) — crypto no longer uses a wider
multiplier than us_scalp. The two lockstep guards now pass.

**Deployed 2026-05-17 17:00 UTC** via an operator-approved
`alphabot-strategy-scalp` restart (pre-deploy snapshot taken first). The
new PID came up clean — the running scalp daemon now sizes against the
2.0× mirror. Strategy-side code only; the brokers needed no restart. No
migration, no schema change → clean `git revert`.

**Regression.** Full suite after Y63: 6202 passed, 1 failed, 71 skipped.
The single remaining failure is the F-Y61-5 guard
(`test_drop_1_3_4e_resolver_market_data_and_bars.py`), still captured

## §21. V3 Drop Y64 — universe_symbols canonical persistence fix (2026-05-17)

**The bug (F-Y61-5, surfaced by the Y61 test triage).**
`broker/universe.py::UniverseRefresher.refresh_exchange` walks the seed
symbol list, qualifies each against IBKR, and writes the qualified set
into the `universe_symbols` table. Each row was built with
`"symbol": symbol` — the raw *seed* loop variable — while every other
field (`primary_exchange`, `long_name`, `sec_type`) read from the
IBKR-resolved `contract` dict. So `universe_symbols` stored the
un-resolved Yahoo-style ticker (`BP`, `AV`) instead of IBKR's canonical
(`BP.`, `AV.`), contradicting both the module's own docstring and
`symbol_resolver.py`'s contract ("the resolved symbol is what callers
persist into `universe_symbols`"). Effect: the resolver re-ran
`reqMatchingSymbolsAsync` every cycle instead of hitting cache, and any
direct reader of `universe_symbols` got a symbol IBKR rejects. Moderate
severity — perf + data quality on a live table, not capital-at-risk.

**The fix (commit `46d6dd2`).** One line:
`"symbol": symbol` → `"symbol": contract.get("symbol", symbol)`. The
deliberate red guard
`test_drop_1_3_4e_resolver_market_data_and_bars.py::test_resolved_canonical_persisted_when_qualify_returns_canonical`
goes green with no test change.

**No deploy by Claudio.** Y64 touches a broker-side file
(`alphabot-broker`, the IBKR broker); deploy is an `alphabot-broker`
restart, approval-gated separately from the commit. Y64 is committed and
pushed to `origin/main`; the running broker still carries the old code
until restarted. No migration, no schema change → clean `git revert`.

**Regression.** Full suite after Y64: 6203 passed, **0 failed**, 71
skipped. The Y61 test baseline — 234 failed / 9 collection errors at
Y61 start — is now fully clean. Both captured bugs (F-Y61-3 → Y63,
F-Y61-5 → Y64) are resolved.

## §22. V3 Drop Y65 — Audit D activity fixes (2026-05-17)

Audit D (`docs/AUDIT_REPORTS/AUDIT_D_daytrade_scalp_activity_2026-05-17.md`)
found why the Scalp and crypto-DayTrade activity streams were dead /
stalled. Y65 is the operator-approved fix drop.

**Finding D-1 — Scalp was in dry-run.** `scalp/_base.py::_maybe_submit_entry`
gates order submission on `SCALP_DRY_RUN` (config default `True`). The
flag had never been overridden, so the scalp engine generated signals,
sized them, logged `WOULD-SUBMIT-SCALP … (DRY_RUN)` and returned without
ever submitting an order. Not a code bug — a config gate left closed
since the Drop 1.2.4c scalp rebuild.

**Fix D-1:** `.env` gains `SCALP_DRY_RUN=false` (VPS-only, not committed;
the `config.py` default stays `True` as the safe fallback for a blank
deploy). Scalp now places live paper orders.

**Finding D-2 — DayTrade crypto hit a 25/day count cap.** The daytrade
sizing chain's per-strategy daily cap (`MAX_TRADES_PER_STRATEGY_PER_DAY=25`)
is tuned for a ~6.5h equity session; a 24/7 crypto engine on a 30s cycle
exhausts it within hours and then idles until UTC midnight. Plus D-2b:
the counter was in-memory and reset to zero on every daemon restart, so
the "25/day" cap was really "25 per daemon-lifetime."

**Fix D-2 (operator chose Option B + C):**
- The per-strategy daily cap is now discipline-aware in
  `daytrade/_base.py`. `crypto_daytrade` uses the new
  `MAX_TRADES_CRYPTO_DAYTRADE_PER_DAY=200`; equity daytrade keeps 25.
  The bot-wide `MAX_TRADES_DAYTRADE_PER_DAY` is raised 100 → 200.
- The daily entry counters are re-seeded from the `orders` table on
  rollover (`_maybe_rollover_counters`), which also fires on the first
  cycle after a restart — so the caps are now genuine UTC-day caps, not
  per-daemon-lifetime caps. Fail-open: a DB read error falls back to
  empty counters (pre-Y65 behaviour).

**Scalp — no daily count cap (operator decision).** The scalp sizing
chain's step-4 daily count caps (`PER_SYMBOL_DAILY_CAP` /
`PER_STRATEGY_DAILY_CAP`) are removed entirely. Scalp exposure stays
bounded by the per-discipline position-count cap, the 5% scalp-engine €
cap, the 60% bot-wide gross cap and the 1% per-trade risk cap. The
skip-reason enum values and the config/state count fields are retained
(back-compat / analytics) but the chain no longer reads them.

**Note — daytrade daily counters are per-discipline, not a shared pool.**
`_daytrade_trades_today` is per strategy instance; `crypto_daytrade`
running its 200 does NOT consume equity daytrade's budget — each equity
discipline keeps its own 25/day. A genuine shared cross-discipline
daytrade trade-count pool (where crypto overnight could starve US) would
be a separate change; flagged to the operator, not built in Y65.

**Files:** `shared/config.py`, `strategy/strategies/daytrade/_base.py`,
`strategy/strategies/scalp/_sizing.py`,
`tests/test_strategy/test_strategies/test_scalp_sizing.py`. Commit
`6b44f49`, pushed to origin/main. `.env` edited on the VPS (not committed).

**Verified:** regression 6202 passed / 0 failed / 71 skipped (Y64
baseline 6203; −1 net = 3 scalp step-4 tests removed, 2 guards added).
ruff clean — no new errors. No migration. Deployed 2026-05-17 ~17:58 UTC
via `alphabot-strategy-scalp` + `alphabot-strategy-daytrade` restarts
(brokers untouched). Post-deploy: daytrade seeded 84 entries from the DB
on first cycle and resumed evaluating with no `per_strategy_daily_cap`
block (84/200 used); scalp restarted clean.

**Deferred:** the upstream ~3.3× daytrade `decision.qty` sizing
overstatement (HANDOVER_7 open #1) is untouched. A genuine shared
cross-discipline daytrade trade-count pool — see the note above.

## §23. V3 Drop Y66 — retire orphan broker universe refresher + daemon weekday-aware market hours (2026-05-17)

Operator-directed drop. After an `alphabot-broker` restart the broker
was observed flooding IBKR with contract-qualification calls. Two
related fixes: retire the orphaned broker-side universe refresher (the
flood source), and give the market-data daemon's market-hours checks
genuine calendar awareness so it stops scanning IBKR on weekends.

**Part 1 — retire the broker universe refresher (Drop 8.6.6).**
`broker/universe.py` held `UniverseRefresher` + `UniverseScheduler`.
The scheduler wakes every minute and, on a broker restart past the
day's scheduled refresh time (LSE 07:30 / SMART 13:30 / ASX 22:00
UTC), immediately fires `refresh_exchange` — walking the entire equity
seed list (swing + smallcap tuples) through `qualifyContractsAsync`,
one IBKR round-trip per symbol. That is the restart flood. The
scheduler is also clock-only (no weekday gate), so it fired on
weekends too.

The refresher predates the Y47/Y59 pool model. The market-data daemon
now owns universe discovery; the refresher's output was orphaned:

- `strategy/broker_client.py::get_universe_for_exchange` (the only
  consumer of the `/universe/{exchange}` endpoint) had **zero callers**.
- `SymbolResolver` does **not** read `universe_symbols`; it caches
  in-process. The per-cycle qualify path is independent and unaffected.
- No dashboard surface reads `universe_symbols` or `/universe`.

**Fix Part 1:** delete `broker/universe.py` and
`broker/api/routes_universe.py` (unwired from `api/_app.py`); remove
`_init_universe_refresher` + scheduler wiring from `broker/main.py`;
drop the dead `get_universe_for_exchange` from `broker_client.py`. The
`universe_symbols` / `universe_refresh_runs` tables and migration 010
are **left in place** (additive-migrations-only constitutional rule) —
they simply stop receiving new rows. Retention rules for them are
harmless and untouched.

**Part 2 — daemon weekday-aware market hours.** The market-data
daemon's market-hours logic was time-of-day only: both
`market_data_daemon/universe.py::MarketHours.is_open` (drives
`UniverseCoordinator.desired_universe` → the streaming universe → IBKR
subscriptions) and `market_data_daemon/pool_config.py::is_market_in_session`
(drives the pool builder's IBKR scans) treated every Saturday/Sunday
in the time window as a live session.

**Fix Part 2:** new `pool_config.is_trading_weekday(market, now)` —
converts `now` to the market's **local** timezone before reading the
ISO weekday (Mon–Fri). Local conversion is required for ASX: its UTC
session window (22:45 → 06:00) opens on the UTC day *before* the
Sydney trading day, so a naive UTC-weekday check would be off by one
(dropping the first 75 min of every Monday session, keeping
Friday-night UTC — Saturday in Sydney — open). Gated into
`is_market_in_session`, `UniverseCoordinator.desired_universe`'s equity
loop, and the standalone `universe.is_market_open`. Holiday gating is
deliberately out of scope — no holiday calendar exists, and
`strategy/market_hours.py` makes the same documented choice.

**Files:** deleted `broker/universe.py`,
`broker/api/routes_universe.py`, `tests/test_8_6_6_universe_refresher.py`,
`tests/test_8_6_6_broker_endpoint.py`; modified `broker/api/_app.py`,
`broker/main.py`, `strategy/broker_client.py`,
`market_data_daemon/pool_config.py`, `market_data_daemon/universe.py`,
`tests/test_broker/test_drop_1_3_4e_resolver_market_data_and_bars.py`
(dropped `TestUniversePersistResolved`), `tests/market_data_daemon/test_pool_config.py`
+ `test_universe.py` (13 new weekday/weekend tests). Commit `6c623c8`,
pushed to origin/main.

**Verified:** regression 6198 passed / 0 failed / 71 skipped (Y65
baseline 6202; net −4 = 17 universe-refresher tests removed, 13
weekday tests added). ruff: no new errors. No migration.

**Deploy:** broker-side + daemon-side change → an `alphabot-broker`
restart and an `alphabot-market-data` restart. The broker restart also
lands the pending Y64.

**Known pre-existing (NOT introduced by Y66, NOT fixed here — Rule 6):**
`broker/api.py` (the pre-1.1.1 monolith, shadowed dead by the
`api/` package) still carries a now-stale `from alphabot.broker.universe`
import — harmless (the file is unimportable), recommend deletion in a
hygiene drop. `broker/main.py`, `market_data_daemon/universe.py` and
`tests/market_data_daemon/test_universe.py` carry pre-existing
`ruff format` drift (present at HEAD `915ec62`); Y66's edited regions
are format-clean but a whole-file reformat was declined as scope creep.
