## §24. V3 Drop Y67 — swing active management + audit fixes (2026-05-17)

Operator-directed drop. Four items: turn the swing engines into active
rotators (a held position earns its slot or loses it), and close two
audit bugs surfaced by Audit B1. Applied uniformly to **every** swing
discipline — US/FTSE/ASX large-cap, the three smallcap variants, and
crypto swing. `swing/_shared.py` and `swing/crypto.py` are diverged
parallel files (CLAUDE.md Rule 2); every change was made twice, by
hand, against each file's own conventions — never blind-copied.

**Architectural note — swing is now an active rotator.** Pre-Y67 swing
held a position until a time-stop, a signal-exit, or a flat-capital
eviction fired. Y67 adds two new ways a slot turns over: the
time×performance eviction grid (Item 2) and dispatch-level open-slot
rotation (Item 3). This is deliberate and operator-confirmed: *"this
turns swing into an active rotator. That's deliberate. Positions earn
their slot or lose it."*

**Item 1 — no silent skips in the stale audits (bug fix).** Audit B1
found `_audit_stale_capital` / `_audit_stale_progress` logging ~93
"stale" cycles but only 2 evictions — held positions were being
dropped from the audit silently when data was missing. Every
missing-data skip path (no `opened_at`, no resolvable price, fewer
than the new-highs window of cached bars) now emits a **per-symbol
WARN** naming the symbol. Where a fix was possible instead of a skip,
it was made: the new-highs check now falls back to the latest bar
close when `current_price` is unresolved rather than skipping. Logic
skips (too-young, performing, making-highs) stay at DEBUG — only
missing-data skips are forbidden to be silent.

**Item 2 — time×performance eviction grid.** `_audit_stale_progress`
replaces the single `stale_progress_pnl_threshold_pct` with
`evict_grid`: a tuple of `(hours_held, min_pnl_pct)` buckets
(operator-locked default 12h→0%, 24h→+1%, 48h→+2%, 72h→+3%, 96h→+4%,
from `SWING_EVICT_*H_MIN_PNL` env). A held position older than a
bucket's age must clear that bucket's P&L bar or it is evicted —
unless it set a new high in the last **3** bars (the new-highs window
tightened from Y4's 6 — not making a high in 3 bars is a stronger
stall signal). `stale_progress_minutes` is retained only as the
on/off gate. `stale_progress_pnl_threshold_pct` is kept on both
params objects for back-compat (Y4 tests still construct it) but is no
longer read by the audit.

**Item 3 — open-slot rotation (Y4.1 seam activated).** The Y4
`open_slot_rotation_score_premium` param was added but never wired.
Y67 activates it. `_evaluate_one` accumulates every gated candidate
into a per-cycle `gated_candidates` list (captured after the gate
veto, before sizing — so a candidate counts even when it sizes to
zero). After the per-symbol BUY loop, the new `_audit_open_slot_rotation`
lets the single strongest gated candidate displace the weakest-scoring
held position in the same discipline. Unlike the existing at-cap
`_try_rotate` hook, this fires **whether or not the discipline is at
capacity**. Guards (env-driven, `SWING_ROTATION_*`): disabled unless
`open_slot_rotation_enabled`; candidate must beat the weakest held
score by `score_premium` (1.5); a position younger than
`min_hold_hours` (4h) is never rotated; a position already up more
than `protect_pnl_pct` (3%) is never rotated. One rotation per cycle;
the displaced slot is filled next cycle by the natural BUY flow. Exit
reason `ROTATION` (via `_close_position(reason="rotated")`).

**Item 4 — rule_w10 false-positives (Audit B1 finding F-B1-3).**
`rule_w10_stops_coverage_gap` read only the `stops` table. Since Drop
1.4.3 bracket protective children live in `orders` (`order_type` STP /
TRAIL), not `stops` — so W10 false-positived every bracket-protected
swing position (~1,832 spurious trips since 2026-05-15). Live-DB SQL
confirmed the discriminator is `order_type IN ('STP','TRAIL')` (the
COID carries a `_stp` suffix but order_type is the reliable signal).
Fix: W10 now builds a per-discipline **set** of covered symbols by
union across three sources — `stops` ACTIVE, `crypto_stops` ACTIVE,
and `orders` STP/TRAIL in a working status (`SUBMITTED`,
`PRE_SUBMITTED`, `PENDING_SUBMIT`, `PARTIALLY_FILLED`). The set union
also fixes a latent double-count the old count-summing had across the
two stop tables.

**Files:** `alphabot/shared/config.py` (9 new env vars —
`SWING_EVICT_{12,24,48,72,96}H_MIN_PNL`, `SWING_ROTATION_ENABLED`,
`SWING_ROTATION_SCORE_PREMIUM`, `SWING_ROTATION_MIN_HOLD_HOURS`,
`SWING_ROTATION_PROTECT_PNL_PCT`); `strategy/strategies/swing/_shared.py`
(`SwingParams` +4 fields; `_audit_stale_capital` + `_audit_stale_progress`
Items 1–2; `_evaluate_one` + `step` + new `_audit_open_slot_rotation`
Item 3); `strategy/strategies/swing/crypto.py` (`CryptoSwingParams` +5
fields; `CryptoCycleStats.open_slot_rotated`; same Items 1–3 mirrored);
`strategy/main_swing.py` (env → params for all 5 swing variants);
`janitor/rules.py` (`rule_w10` only, Item 4); new
`tests/test_drop_y67_swing_active_management.py` (46 tests); two
docstring/assertion updates in `tests/test_drop_y4_swing_active_management.py`
(§3 same-drop test-update rule — Y67 changed `_audit_stale_progress`).
No broker files. No migration.

**Verified:** regression 6244 passed / 0 failed / 71 skipped (Y66
baseline 6198; net +46 = the new Y67 test file). ruff: no new errors
(`_shared.py` carries one pre-existing RUF003 ambiguous-`×` at HEAD,
untouched). `ruff format`: edited regions clean; `_shared.py` carries
21 pre-existing format-drift hunks (present at HEAD), whole-file
reformat declined as scope creep per Rule 6.

**Deploy:** strategy-side only → `sudo systemctl restart
alphabot-strategy-swing.service` (auto-allowed per §6). Rotation
defaults ON (`SWING_ROTATION_ENABLED=true`); first cycle after restart
should log `open-slot rotation: evaluating N gated candidate(s)` at
DEBUG even when nothing rotates.

## §25. V3 Drop Y68 — swing dashboard "Currently Holding" data-source fixes (2026-05-17)

Operator-directed. The Swing tab's Currently Holding table showed
blank LIVE/DIST cells and red ⚠ triangles in the STOP column where
live numbers were expected. Audited every column HTML →
`swing.js::holdingRow` → `/api/engines/swing/positions` (DB-primary,
Y36) → `db_queries.engine_positions`. Four bugs found and fixed; no
new alarm is invented and no fake number is shown.

**Bug A — crypto STOP rendered ⚠ despite an ACTIVE `crypto_stops`
row.** `engine_positions`'s Y10 post-query coalesce copied
`crypto_stops.stop_price` into `trail_stop_price` but **not**
`trail_stop_price_usd` — and `_format_position_from_db` serialises
the wire `stop_price` (what the STOP column reads) from
`trail_stop_price_usd`, not `trail_stop_price`. So every crypto-swing
position serialised `stop_price=null` and drew a naked ⚠. Fix:
coalesce `trail_stop_price_usd` too. `crypto_stops.stop_price` is
USDT-denominated and USDT is the codebase's USD passthrough unit, so
the USD-canonical value equals the native one.

**Bug B — equity bracket STOP rendered ⚠ despite a working
protective child.** Since Drop 1.4.3 a swing/daytrade bracket's
protective child is an STP/TRAIL row in `orders`, **not** a row in
the `stops` table — so a bracket-protected position has no
`stops`/`crypto_stops` row and the STOP column drew it as naked.
Live-DB audit: ~25 of 47 swing positions were bracket-protected-but-
shown-naked; ~21 were genuinely naked (ASX swing has no protective
orders at all — a real trading-safety finding, separate). The
`orders` table does **not** carry the live trigger price (that lives
at IBKR — the B1 audit earmarked a `reqOpenOrders` broker query as a
separate drop), so Y68 does not show a price for these. Instead
`engine_positions` now does an **isolated, fault-tolerant `orders`
lookup** (its own try/except, mirroring the existing Y36
`live_price_cache` tolerance — a DB lacking the table/columns simply
yields no tags) that surfaces `protective_order_type` (`STP`/`TRAIL`)
per position. The STOP cell renders `TRAIL ✓` / `STP ✓` in a neutral
tone for bracket-protected positions and reserves the red ⚠ for
genuinely naked ones. The `orders` lookup is deliberately a separate
query, not a join into the main/fallback SELECTs — embedding it there
made the whole query fail on test fixtures with an incomplete
`orders` table (20 tests went red mid-drop; reworked to the isolated
form, which breaks nothing).

**Bug C — LIVE column read the wrong source.** `swing.js` sourced the
LIVE price from `/api/live-prices`, which is fed solely by the
Binance daemon (9 crypto symbols; equities were never in it) — so
every equity swing row rendered a blank LIVE (and a blank DIST, which
depends on it). The Y36 positions payload already carries
`last_price`/`last_price_usd` joined from `live_price_cache` for every
held symbol. Fix: `holdingRow` reads `p.last_price_usd ?? p.last_price`
and keeps the `/api/live-prices` lookup only as a last-resort
fallback. (scalp.js already had this fallback; swing.js was the
outlier.)

**Bug D — DIST sign prefix inverted.** `holdingRow` rendered a
negative distance — stop sitting above the live price — as
`"+-1.34%"` (the prefix ternary was `>= 0 ? "" : "+"`, backwards).
Fixed to `>= 0 ? "+" : ""`; the minus is already supplied by
`toFixed`.

**Files:** `dashboard/db_queries/engines.py` (Y10 coalesce extended;
isolated `orders` lookup added), `dashboard/api/routes_engines.py`
(`protective_order_type` added to the wire shape + `_DB_CONTEXT_FIELDS`
for the broker-proxy fallback path), `dashboard/static/js/swing.js`
(LIVE source, STOP cell, DIST sign), new
`tests/test_drop_y68_dashboard_swing_holding.py` (14 tests). No
broker files. No migration. The trigger-price-for-bracket-children
gap (F6 / B1 follow-up — needs a broker `reqOpenOrders` pipeline)
is explicitly out of scope and unchanged.

**Verified:** regression 6258 passed / 0 failed / 71 skipped (Y67
baseline 6244; +14 = the new Y68 test file). ruff: no new errors.
Dashboard restarted; `/api/engines/swing/positions` re-curled —
crypto `stop_price` now populated, 25 positions tagged
`protective_order_type`, 21 genuinely-naked still untagged.

**Deploy:** dashboard-only → `sudo systemctl restart
alphabot-dashboard.service` (auto-allowed per §6); done this session.
Commit `39a9c75`.


## §26. V3 Drop Y69 — janitor alarm-recursion fix (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed, surfaced while resolving a disk-full incident (see
`HANDOVER_9.md`). Two bugs in the janitor alarm path, one production
consequence.

**Bug A — raise_alarm recursed on a non-race IntegrityError.**
`alarm_writer.raise_alarm`'s `except sqlite3.IntegrityError` assumed
*every* IntegrityError on the fresh INSERT was a concurrent-insert
race against `idx_system_alarms_live_per_rule`, and retried as an
UPDATE-while-live; when the UPDATE found no row it recursed. A
**CHECK-constraint** violation is not a race — the retry re-runs the
same doomed INSERT — so the recursion ran until Python's
`RecursionError`. Every 60s watchdog tick dumped a ~1000-frame
traceback to the journal/syslog.

**Bug B — W13 raised alarms with an invalid category.**
`rule_w13_recent_recon_breaks` built each `RuleTrip` with
`category="RECONCILE"`, which is not in the `system_alarms.category`
CHECK set `(STRATEGY, BROKER, POSITION, STATE_DRIFT, JANITOR, INFRA)`.
Every W13 INSERT therefore hit Bug A. With a live recon break present
(`R4_ORDER_STUCK_SUBMITTED:ABDN`), W13 tripped every tick — so the
recursion + traceback flood ran continuously.

**Production consequence.** The traceback flood was the dominant
source of `/var/log/syslog` growth; with system `logrotate` also
broken (a duplicate `/var/log/syslog` entry in
`/etc/logrotate.d/syslog-aggressive` made `logrotate.service` exit 1
every run — see `HANDOVER_9.md`), syslog reached 43G and filled the
75G disk → SQLite `database or disk is full` → 6,713+ broker persist
failures. The janitor bug was the volume; the logrotate breakage was
the accumulation.

**Fixes.**
- `rules.py` — W13 `category` `"RECONCILE"` → `"STATE_DRIFT"`. A
  reconciliation break is the bot's recorded state diverging from
  broker reality; `STATE_DRIFT` is the DB-valid category that fits.
  No migration — the CHECK set is unchanged; `RECONCILE` was never a
  valid value.
- `alarm_writer.py` — `raise_alarm` now distinguishes a UNIQUE
  violation (genuine race → retry as UPDATE) from any other
  IntegrityError (CHECK/NOT NULL → caller error → `raise`, no retry).
  The genuine-race retry is bounded by `_MAX_INSERT_RETRIES` (5)
  instead of recursing unboundedly; the watchdog runner's existing
  per-trip `try/except` then skips a bad rule cleanly.
- `alarm_writer.py` — the `Category` Literal gained `"INFRA"`; it was
  already a valid DB value and used by rules W7–W12, the type hint
  was stale.

**Files:** `alphabot/janitor/alarm_writer.py`,
`alphabot/janitor/rules.py`, new
`tests/test_drop_y69_janitor_alarm_recursion.py` (7 tests). No
migration.

**Verified:** regression **6265 passed / 0 failed / 71 skipped** (Y68
baseline 6258; +7 = the new test file). ruff clean. Deployed via an
`alphabot-janitor` restart (auto-allowed per §6); post-restart the
janitor runs clean — 0 recursion/CHECK/race errors, CPU back to idle,
and 48 RECON_BREAK alarms now persist correctly as `STATE_DRIFT`
(they previously all failed and recursed).

**Commit** `e61ca81`.


## §27. Nightly automated full-stack reset (2026-05-18)

Operator decision. A multi-day-old IB Gateway session goes stale; the
IBKR broker then comes up wedged on restart (`positions_count=0`,
frozen heartbeat) — observed this session. The operator's remedy:
start every trading day on a fresh, freshly-reconciled stack.

**Decision.** A nightly full-stack **service restart** (explicitly
*not* an OS reboot — the operator chose the restart on a yes/no) runs
at **00:00 Europe/Paris**, ahead of the ASX open. The stack is stopped
leaf→root, the IB Gateway Docker container is recycled to clear the
session, then everything restarts root→leaf with health-gating
between tiers.

**Implementation.** `~/scripts/alphabot_nightly_reset.sh` (the ordered
reset — TCP + `/health` gated, exits non-zero if a broker fails to
come back so a bad reset shows in `systemctl --failed`) plus
`alphabot-nightly-reset.{service,timer}`. The timer's
`OnCalendar=*-*-* 00:00:00 Europe/Paris` auto-tracks DST (22:00 UTC in
CEST, 23:00 UTC in CET). Scripts live in `~/scripts/` alongside
`alphabot_backup.sh`/`alphabot_restore.sh`; the systemd units are
installed by the operator (writes to `/etc/systemd/system` are
operator-only per §6). Replaces a dead root cron line
(`0 11 * * 0 cd /home/ibgateway && docker-compose restart` — wrong
path, gateway-only, never worked).

**Caveat recorded:** 00:00 Paris = 23:00 UTC in the European winter,
which collides with the winter ASX open (10:00 AEDT). Fine through
summer; revisit before November or pin to a fixed pre-open UTC time.


## §28. V3 Drop Y70 — loss-streak kill switch magnitude floor (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed. The dashboard showed the kill switch tripped; the
operator wanted the safety kept but stopped from halting the bot on
trivial losses.

**Problem.** The loss-streak kill switch (`LossStreakMonitor`, Phase 4
Drop 5h) auto-kills the IBKR broker when the most recent N completed
trades in a rolling window are all losses — on a *count* of losses,
with no magnitude floor. At 07:14 UTC it killed the broker on 3
consecutive paper losses (ABDN/PANR/PFD) totalling **−$2.13**; ~1,224
BUY intents were rejected before it was noticed. The kill is sticky
(never auto-resumes) and IBKR-broker-only (the crypto broker has no
kill switch). A 2026-05-15 operator `/broker/resume` had cleared a
prior trip but left the monitor armed — it was never disabled.

**Decision.** Keep the monitor enabled — a genuinely bad run (the
2026-05-15 −$1,712 streak) should still halt the broker — but add a
**magnitude floor**: the kill fires only when the streak's total
realized loss is at least `LOSS_STREAK_MIN_LOSS_USD`. The operator
explicitly chose this over disabling the monitor outright.

**Implementation.** `LossStreakMonitor` gains a `min_loss_usd`
constructor arg; `_on_trade` sums the trailing-streak losses and
suppresses the kill (INFO log, no fire) when the magnitude is below
the floor. New `LOSS_STREAK_MIN_LOSS_USD` setting, **default $100**,
`.env`-overridable. `min_loss_usd=0` disables the floor (pre-Y70
behaviour). The trigger is now a three-part AND: N trades in window,
all losses, total ≥ floor.

`alphabot/broker/main.py`, `env.example`,
`tests/test_broker/test_loss_streak.py` (5 new floor tests). No

## §29. V3 Drop Y71 — market-data daemon fills live_price_cache for held positions (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed, from the swing-dashboard audit: 20 of 44 held swing
positions rendered a blank LIVE / P&L / DIST.

**Root cause.** `live_price_cache` is a *live-snapshot cache*, not a
price-of-record. The brokers write a row only while they hold an
active market-data subscription + snapshot for a symbol — so a held
position whose market is closed, or which sits outside the active
universe, never gets a row, and the dashboard (DB-primary since Y36)
renders blank. Session closes are persisted nowhere else in the DB.

**Decision.** The market-data daemon — which already holds D1/M5 bars
for held positions (Y47 pins them into the pool) — becomes the
*completeness owner* of `live_price_cache`. It floor-writes the latest
bar close for every held equity position, so coverage stops depending
on what a broker happens to be subscribed to. This keeps the dashboard
DB-primary (the Y36 lock — no live cross-service calls).

**Implementation.** New `PriceCacheSync` daemon task (60s): per held
equity position, read the latest bar close from `BarStorage`,
USD-convert via `shared.price_conversion.native_price_to_usd` (the
canonical pence/FX boundary), and write to `live_price_cache` via the
new `flush_price_cache_floor_to_db` — a non-clobbering upsert that
fills a gap or refreshes a staler row but never overwrites a fresher
broker tick (newest `refreshed_at` wins; ISO-8601 sorts lexically).
`PriceCacheEntry` gained an optional per-entry `refreshed_at` (the
bar's real close time) so a stale close is recorded honestly. Crypto
is skipped — the Binance broker covers it 24/7.

**Files:** `alphabot/db/price_cache_writer.py`,
`alphabot/market_data_daemon/price_cache_sync.py` (new),
`alphabot/market_data_daemon/daemon.py`, plus tests. No migration.

**Verified:** regression 6279 passed / 0 failed / 71 skipped (Y70
baseline 6270; +9). ruff clean. Deployed via an `alphabot-market-data`
restart — `price_cache_sync` floored 22 held-equity prices, 8
gap-fills as `source='daemon'` (the floor-merge correctly left the
broker's 35 fresh rows untouched). Swing-tab blank-LIVE count 20 → 13.

**Known residual (→ Y72).** The daemon only holds bars for symbols
subscribed during their market hours; a daemon restart while a market
is closed leaves that market's held positions without bars until it
opens (the US held positions fill at the 13:30 UTC US open). A held
position outside any subscribed pool never backfills. The durable fix
— backfill every held position on daemon startup regardless of market
hours / pool membership — plus the dashboard `avg_cost` floor and
freshness badge, are deferred to Y72.

**Commit** `f3a6544`.

> **Drop-number note (2026-05-18).** §29's "→ Y72" residual — the
> daemon unconditional held-position backfill, dashboard `avg_cost`
> floor + freshness badge, DJEL/CMU corrupt-price validation — is
> **renumbered Y73**. Drop numbers run in *ship* order, and the swing
> market-grouping work (§30 below) shipped first and took Y72.

## §30. V3 Drop Y72 — swing Currently Holding: market-level grouping (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed: the swing "Currently Holding" tab "reverted to an
old format" — it had lost the per-market headings ("8/10 for FTSE …
held in that market colour … so we could see easily how many we are
holding in each market"). Operator pointed at the daytrade tab as the
target format.

**Root cause — not a regression.** The shared `holdingsGroup.js`
(Y33) groups holdings by `discipline`. The daytrade tab has one
discipline per market (`us_daytrade` / `ftse_daytrade` / `asx_daytrade`
/ `crypto_daytrade`), so per-discipline grouping there reads as one
coloured header per market. The swing tab has **two** disciplines per
equity market (`us_swing` + `us_smallcap`, and likewise FTSE/ASX) plus
`crypto_swing` — so the same per-discipline grouping split each market
into two headers. The operator could no longer see "how many am I
holding in FTSE" as a single number. The headings were present, just
fragmented — the swing tab was not actually rendering flat.

**Decision.** Add a second, market-level grouping mode to the shared
module rather than special-casing swing. The swing tab opts into it;
daytrade / master / scalp keep per-discipline grouping (correct for
them — discipline↔market is 1:1).

**Implementation.** `holdingsGroup.js` gains `groupPositionsByMarket`
(collapses a market's disciplines into one bucket — US/FTSE/ASX/Crypto,
canonical order, empty markets suppressed) and
`renderGroupedRowsByMarket` (one coloured header per market, continuous
1→N ordinals — reuses the existing `renderGroupHeader`). The per-market
**cap** is the *sum* of that market's discipline hard caps, sourced
from the caller's discipline set (not the held positions) so the cap
stays stable when a discipline currently holds nothing — for swing,
US/FTSE/ASX = 13 each (swing 8 + smallcap 5), Crypto = 6. `swing.js`
`fillHolding` now calls `renderGroupedRowsByMarket`, passing `PANELS`'
discipline set.

**Files:** `alphabot/dashboard/static/js/holdingsGroup.js`,
`alphabot/dashboard/static/js/swing.js`,
`tests/test_drop_y72_market_grouping.py` (new, 9 Node-hermetic tests).
No Python source changed → regression baseline unchanged (6279).

**Verified:** ruff clean. The 9 new tests + the Y33 grouping tests run
under Node in CI; they `skip` on the VPS, which has no Node installed
(same pre-existing behaviour as `test_drop_y33_grouping.py`). New
grouping logic verified by static review — it reuses three already-
proven helpers in the same file (`sortPositionsByGroup`,
`groupColorClass`, `renderGroupHeader`). Deployed via an
`alphabot-dashboard` restart; both JS files serve HTTP 200 with the new
symbols present. Final rendered layout is an operator eyeball check.

**Commit** `31afbbc`.

## §31. V3 Drop Y73 — daemon backfills held positions whose market is closed (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed, the §30 follow-up: the swing tab still rendered a
blank LIVE for held US equities. Root cause confirmed against the
running bot — `live_price_cache` is the only price store in the DB;
bars live solely in the market-data daemon's in-memory `BarStorage`.
Y71 floor-writes held-equity bar closes, but the daemon only holds
bars for symbols subscribed *during market hours* (the
`LifecycleReconciler` subscribes per market hours). A held US equity
outside the 13:30-20:00 UTC window therefore has no bar and Y71 had
nothing to write.

**Decision.** The completeness pass must not depend on a symbol being
subscribed. `reqHistoricalData` works while a market is closed and
returns the last completed session — so `PriceCacheSync` triggers a
one-off historical backfill for any held symbol with no bar.

**Implementation.**
- `IBKRRealtimeSource.backfill_now(symbol, venue, currency)` — qualifies
  a contract and runs `HistoricalBackfiller.backfill_symbol`, seeding
  the last-session-close bars into `BarStorage` with no realtime
  subscription. Return contract: `-1` = could-not-attempt (IBKR not
  connected / backfill disabled — transient, retry later); `>=0` = a
  real attempt ran (bars seeded; 0 = qualified-but-no-data or an
  unqualifiable ticker — do not retry).
- `PriceCacheSync` schedules a fire-and-forget backfill for any held
  symbol with no bar; the seeded bar floors a price on a later cycle.
  At most one *attempt* per symbol per daemon lifetime — but a `-1`
  result un-marks the symbol so it retries once the connection is up.
- `daemon.py` wires `ibkr_source` into `PriceCacheSync`.

**Files:** `alphabot/market_data_daemon/sources/ibkr_realtime.py`,
`alphabot/market_data_daemon/price_cache_sync.py`,
`alphabot/market_data_daemon/daemon.py`,
`tests/market_data_daemon/test_drop_y73_held_backfill.py` (new, 11
tests). No migration.

**Verified:** regression 6287 passed / 0 failed (Y71 baseline 6279;
+8 — the initial Y73 commit). ruff clean on the new code. Deployed via
`alphabot-market-data` restarts. First deploy surfaced two faults,
both fixed + redeployed:
1. *Startup race* — `PriceCacheSync`'s first cycle ran ~30s before the
   IBKR source connected; every backfill early-returned and the
   one-shot guard marked all symbols permanently. Fixed by the `-1`
   could-not-attempt return + retry (`bde2db9`).
2. *`None`-contract crash* — `qualifyContractsAsync` returns `[None]`
   for an unresolvable ticker (CSGS); `qualified[0].conId` raised.
   Fixed by a `None` guard (`2497370`).
Post-fix: held US swing positions with a price went **3/15 → 14/15**;
the one gap (CSGS) is a genuinely invalid IBKR contract — `Error 200,
no security definition` — which no backfill can resolve (a symbol-data
problem, not a Y73 gap).

**Commits** `e6bb8aa` (drop), `bde2db9` (startup-race fix),
`2497370` (None-guard fix).

> **Pre-existing lint note.** `ibkr_realtime.py` carries 8 pre-Y73 ruff

> SIM105) from Y42/Y51. Y73 added none and left them untouched per the

## §32. V3 Drop Y74 — swing exit-order idempotency (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed, from a swing-rotation audit: the Y67 active-rotation
logic fires correctly every cycle but **31 of 46 swing positions that
should have exited had not**. Root cause — the exit audits had no
idempotency: `_audit_time_stop` / `_audit_stale_capital` /
`_audit_stale_progress` / `_audit_signal_exits` each re-submitted a
fresh SELL **every ~5-min cycle** for a position they wanted closed,
never checking whether an exit was already working. Within ~75 min, 15+
duplicate SELLs piled onto one contract and IBKR **Error 201** ("a
minimum of 15 orders working … per contract per side") rejected every
further exit — 312 REJECTED SELLs in a day.

**Decision.** The exit audits must be idempotent: one working exit per
symbol, never a resubmit.

**Implementation.** `_close_position` stamps every controlled-exit SELL
coid with `CLOSE_{symbol}` (entries, bracket STP/TP children and
panic-flattens do not). `step()` snapshots `_working_exit_symbols` —
symbols with a working SELL whose coid carries `CLOSE` — from
`list_open_orders`. The four exit audits seed that set into
`excluded_symbols` (skip cleanly, no duplicate decision); `_close_position`
carries it as a `getattr`-guarded backstop covering open-slot rotation.
A new module-level `_working_exit_symbols()` per file makes the filter
unit-testable. Applied by hand to both diverged swing files —
`_shared.py` and `crypto.py` (CLAUDE.md Rule 2).

**Files:** `strategy/strategies/swing/_shared.py`,
`strategy/strategies/swing/crypto.py`,
`tests/test_drop_y74_exit_idempotency.py` (new, 15 tests). No broker
change, no migration.

**Verified:** regression 6305 passed / 0 failed (Y73 baseline 6290;
+15). ruff clean on the new code. Deployed via an
`alphabot-strategy-swing` restart — post-deploy, **MND is the only
symbol still re-submitting**; every other position's per-cycle pile-up
stopped. The remaining MND spam is a *separate* bug (see below), not a
Y74 miss — MND's exits never reach a working status so the
working-order filter legitimately cannot dedup them.

**Commit** `e50d915`.

> **Separate root cause found during Y74 deploy verification —
> `gate_valid_symbol` traps held positions.** The broker risk gate
> `gate_valid_symbol` (`broker/risk.py:289`) rejects *every* order —
> including SELLs — for a symbol not in `ctx.known_symbol_universe`. A
> held position whose symbol has left the scanner universe (MND, an
> ASX holding — 273 gate-rejected exits) therefore **can never be
> sold**. A position-reducing SELL must always be allowed regardless of
> universe membership. Recommended fix: exempt the SELL side from
> `gate_valid_symbol` (long-only bot; exit SELLs are already clamped to
> the free balance by Y60's `clamp_sell_quantity`). Scoped, not yet
> built — a distinct broker-gate drop.

## §33. V3 Drop Y75 — gate_valid_symbol exempts SELL (2026-05-18)

The §32 follow-up, operator-approved. `gate_valid_symbol`
(`broker/risk.py`) rejected *every* order — SELLs included — for a
symbol not in the broker's verified universe, so a held position whose
symbol left the scanner universe was trapped (MND: 273 gate-rejected
exits). The universe check exists to block *opening* exposure into an
unverified symbol; it has no business blocking an *exit*.

**Decision + implementation.** `gate_valid_symbol` returns `Allow()` for
any SELL before the universe check. A SELL on this long-only bot is
position-reducing and is already balance-clamped by Y60's
`clamp_sell_quantity`, so it can never open a short. Mirrors the
existing SELL bypass in `gate_daily_spend_cap` / `gate_position_size`.
IBKR-only — the crypto broker's `gate_valid_symbol` checks Binance
exchange info, not a curated universe, so it has no equivalent trap.

**Files:** `alphabot/broker/risk.py`, `tests/test_broker/test_risk.py`
(+3 tests). No migration.

**Verified:** regression 6308 passed / 0 failed (Y74 baseline 6305).
ruff clean on the new code. Deployed via an `alphabot-broker` restart.
Confirmed live: MND's rejection moved off `gate_valid_symbol` — it now
cascades to `broker_kill` then `gate_market_open` (`no exchange mapping
for MND`). MND is a broken-metadata symbol that trips multiple gates in
turn; fully freeing it is a separate symbol-data cleanup, not a Y75
gap. Y75 itself does exactly what it set out to: a SELL is no longer
universe-gated.

**Commit** `6465a4f`.

## §34. V3 Drop Y76 — gate_sell_quantity: IBKR sell-quantity clamp (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed, from the MND-short discovery. The operator checked
IBKR and found MND (`asx_swing`) held **-3438 SHORT** — the bot is
long-only by design (`Position` docstring: "Phase 3 does not support
shorts; reserved for future").

**Root cause.** The IBKR broker had no risk gate capping a SELL to the
held quantity — Y60's `clamp_sell_quantity` guards only the Binance
broker. A SELL could run a long through zero into a short with nothing
to stop it. MND's original long was oversold past zero by the Y74
*pre-fix* duplicate-SELL pile-up; every order / fill / `trades` record
for MND is a SELL, zero BUYs. IBKR `avgCost 29.35` ≈ price → the short
is roughly break-even; the DB `positions.avg_cost 18.01` is stale (the
original long entry, never re-based on the flip).

**Decision + implementation.** New risk gate `gate_sell_quantity`
(`broker/risk.py`), inserted into `GATES` at position 3 (after
`gate_duplicate_order_id`, before `gate_market_open` — a dict lookup,
as cheap as the other structural gates, so a short-deepening SELL is
rejected by the *correct* gate first). For a SELL, against the signed
held quantity: `held <= 0` → Reject; `quantity > held` → `Modify` down
to `held`; else `Allow`. BUYs pass untouched. `BrokerContext` gained
`position_qty_by_symbol` (signed net qty per symbol, `default_factory
=dict` so existing fixtures keep working); `main.py`'s context builder
populates it from `position_book.all_for_mode(default_mode)`.

This makes an IBKR SELL *provably* position-reducing — it can never
create or deepen a short. That is precisely the premise Y75's
`gate_valid_symbol` SELL-exemption only *assumed*; Y76 makes the
assumption true. Uses the broker's existing `Modify` mechanism (already
exercised by `gate_max_trade_pct` / `gate_max_symbol_pct`), so no new
gate-runner or executor plumbing.

**Files:** `alphabot/broker/order_types.py`, `alphabot/broker/main.py`,
`alphabot/broker/risk.py`, `tests/test_broker/test_risk.py` (+7 tests).
No migration.

**Verified:** regression 6315 passed / 0 failed / 80 skipped (Y75
baseline 6308; +7 new tests). ruff: 0 new violations (15 pre-existing
RUF003/RUF006 left untouched per Rule 6).

**Deployed** 2026-05-18 via an operator-approved `alphabot-broker`
restart — broker HEALTHY post-restart, 25 positions reconciled.

**Deferred / not in this drop:** Y76 stops *new* shorts, it does not
unwind existing ones. The IBKR account was found holding **6 short
positions** — MND/DRR/ORI/SIG (ASX) and FUM/TBTG (LSE) — all from the
same pre-Y76 oversell bug. They are cleaned up separately by
`scripts/ops_ibkr_flatten_shorts.py` (a one-off direct-IBKR
BUY-to-close, untracked, `--market`-scoped, run at each venue's next
open). The crypto broker needs no equivalent — Y60's
`clamp_sell_quantity` already guards it.

**Commits** `674a492` (code), `18988f7` (session-end docs).

## §35. V3 Drop Y77 — exit-path robustness (2026-05-18)

Operator-directed, from a swing/daytrade exit-rotation audit: the exit
audits fire correctly but the exits fail downstream. Three related
fixes in the controlled-close path, scoped together and shipped as one
drop.

**Fix 1 — sign-aware close.** `_close_position` (swing `_shared.py`)
and `_fire_exit` (`daytrade_stop_runner.py`) hardcoded `side=SELL`. The
bot is long-only, but 9 IBKR positions had been oversold through zero
into shorts (pre-Y76) — and a SELL on a short *deepens* it. The close
is now sign-aware: long → SELL, short → BUY-to-close at `abs(qty)`.
`_shared.py` snapshots signed held qty per symbol in `step()` (the Y74
`_working_exit_symbols` pattern) and `_close_position` reads it; the
bracket path (a long-only construct) is skipped for a short.
`_fire_exit` derives the side from `pos.quantity` — and this also fixes
a pre-existing bug: it submitted the *raw signed* `pos.quantity`, a
negative-quantity SELL for a short. `crypto.py` `_close_position`
refuses a non-positive quantity — Binance spot cannot hold a short, so
there is no BUY-to-close equivalent (Rule 2: crypto's real semantics,
not a copy of the IBKR logic). Broker companion: `gate_valid_symbol`
allows a BUY that closes a short past the universe check — a
position-reducing BUY, mirroring the Y75 SELL exemption — so a short
whose symbol left the scanner universe can still be bought back to
flat.

**Fix 2 — resilient stop-cancel.** The strategy cancels the protective
stop before an exit; pre-Y77 any `cancel_stop` error aborted the whole
exit. `broker_client.cancel_stop` now treats a 404 as "no active stop"
(returns False, does not raise — a short / already-flat position simply
has no stop) and retries transient transport errors up to 3 attempts —
a stale pooled connection right after a broker restart no longer looks
like a hard failure that aborts a valid exit.

**Fix 3 — un-exitable-position skip.** `daytrade_stop_runner` re-fired a
rejected exit every 5s forever (LUNCUSDT dust below Binance's NOTIONAL
minimum), starving the runner of cycles. It now counts consecutive
exit failures per symbol; after `_MAX_EXIT_ATTEMPTS` (5)
`_process_position` suppresses the exit and `_record_exit_failure` logs
ERROR once. Scoped with a stop re-attach on reject; **that was dropped
on build** — the `daytrade_stop_runner` Y54 decision log records that a
cancel+re-attach path was removed for "actively re-naking positions",
so reintroducing one is wrong. The legacy path's naked window is
inherent; the proper fix is migrating to the atomic bracket path, out
of scope here.

**Files:** `alphabot/broker/risk.py`, `alphabot/strategy/broker_client.py`,
`alphabot/strategy/strategies/swing/_shared.py`,
`alphabot/strategy/strategies/swing/crypto.py`,
`alphabot/strategy/daytrade_stop_runner.py`,
`tests/test_drop_y77_exit_path.py`, `tests/test_broker/test_risk.py`,
`tests/test_strategy/test_broker_client.py` (+18 tests). No migration.

**Verified:** regression 6333 passed / 0 failed / 80 skipped (Y76
baseline 6315; +18). ruff 0 new violations.

**Deployed** 2026-05-18 — `alphabot-broker` + all three strategy
daemons restarted (broker HEALTHY, 29 positions). Verified live: the
swing engine now logs `controlled BUY submitted` to close the short
positions (MND, FUM) where pre-Y77 it emitted a SELL. Those BUYs are
`gate_market_open`-REJECTED only because the ASX/LSE markets are shut
— they will execute at the next opens (ASX 2026-05-19 00:00 UTC, LSE
08:00 UTC), flattening the shorts via the engine itself.

**Deferred / not in this drop:** pre-existing latent bug noted —
`daytrade_stop_runner.py:883` references `self._snapshots`, never
defined in `__init__` — a likely `AttributeError` on the bracket-exit
success path; left untouched (out of Y77 scope). Also: the Y74
exit-idempotency snapshot (`_working_exit_symbols`) only tracks working
SELLs, so a BUY-to-close-short is not deduped — low risk for fast MKT
fills, but a follow-up could extend it.

**Commit** `ec430dc`.

## §36. V3 Drop Y78 — crypto broker: classify Binance order rejections (2026-05-18)

**Problem.** The crypto broker degraded itself on order rejections.
`CryptoExecutor` caught *every* `new_order` / `cancel` exception in a
bare `except Exception` and called `state.record_error()` — so a
Binance *order-level* rejection counted toward the DEGRADED error
streak exactly as a connectivity failure would. The 17:23 UTC DEGRADED
event traced to the LUNCUSDT dust position: every exit attempt hits
`APIError(code=-1013): Filter failure: NOTIONAL` (the position is below
Binance's minimum tradeable notional). Three rejections in a row →
`consecutive_errors` hits `DEGRADED_THRESHOLD` (3) → broker DEGRADED,
even though Binance was perfectly reachable the whole time.

**Why this matters.** A DEGRADED broker is a real signal — it gates
order flow and surfaces on the dashboard. A dust position that can
never be exited was silently destroying that signal's meaning: the
broker looked unhealthy on a routine, expected order refusal.

**Fix.** `executor.py` gains `_is_order_rejection(exc)`: an order-level
rejection means the broker *reached* Binance and Binance refused this
specific order — the connection is HEALTHY, so it must NOT degrade
broker health. The classifier returns True only for a
`BinanceAPIException` whose `.code` is in `_ORDER_REJECTION_CODES`
(`-1013` filter failure, `-1100` illegal chars, `-1106` param not
required, `-1111` precision, `-2010` NEW_ORDER_REJECTED, `-2011`
CANCEL_REJECTED, `-2013` order does not exist). A transport failure, a
server 5xx, a rate-limit code, or any non-Binance exception → False →
still records a broker error. Both the `new_order` and `cancel` except
blocks branch on the classifier: a rejection logs WARNING without a
traceback and returns the reject; a genuine failure keeps the old
`record_error()` + `logger.exception()` path. The DEGRADED signal is
preserved for real outages.

**Files:** `alphabot/broker_binance/executor.py`,
`tests/test_drop_y78_crypto_error_classification.py` (+18 tests). No
migration.

**Verified:** regression 6351 passed / 0 failed / 80 skipped (Y77
baseline 6333; +18). ruff 0 new violations.

**Not deployed** — committed `a930b06`, pushed. A crypto broker restart
(`sudo systemctl restart alphabot-broker-crypto`) is approval-gated;
Y78 rides the next operator-approved restart.

**Deferred / not in this drop:** the operator scoped two crypto-broker
items together and directed "build 1 first". Item 2 — the SQLite
`database is locked` contention on the live-price flush (raise
`busy_timeout` 1000ms → 5000ms) — is a *separate* fault: that path
swallows its error and does NOT degrade the broker, so it is not part
of the DEGRADED root cause. It remains a backlog item, not started.

**Commit** `a930b06`.

## §37. V3 Drop Y79 — DB busy_timeout 1s→5s + daytrade atomic-exit cleanup (2026-05-18)

Two independent reliability fixes, bundled at operator request — both
small, both touch one source file each.

**Fix 1 — DB `busy_timeout` 1000ms → 5000ms.** `open_connection`
(`alphabot/db/connection.py`) is the shared SQLite connection factory
for every AlphaBot process. On a busy multi-process WAL DB (7+ writer
processes) a 1-second busy timeout was too short: a contended write
expired and raised `database is locked`. The crypto broker's 60s
live-price flush was a regular victim — it swallows the error (the
dashboard simply shows a stale price for a cycle), which is *why* this
is a separate fault from the Y78 DEGRADED root cause and not part of
that drop. Y79 raises the `busy_timeout` pragma to 5000ms and the
matching `sqlite3.connect` `timeout` arg to 5.0s, on both the
read-write and read-only connection paths. **Global by design** — the
contention is not unique to the price flush; every writer benefits and
a longer wait is strictly safer for correctness (fewer failed /
swallowed writes). The only cost is a contended write blocks up to 5s
instead of 1s before raising — all such paths are background loops,
none latency-critical. 5s is the standard conservative value for a
busy multi-process SQLite WAL DB. No existing test asserted the old
value, so nothing downstream broke.

**Fix 2 — daytrade `_fire_exit` atomic-exit cleanup.** The bracket
(atomic STP_LMT→MKT) exit *success* path in
`daytrade_stop_runner.py` called `self._snapshots.pop(...)` — an
attribute never defined in `__init__`. Every successful atomic exit
raised `AttributeError`. It never crashed the runner (the per-position
`asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)` guard caught it) but it

legacy cancel+SELL exit path already calls `record_exit(symbol)`

atomic path call the same `record_exit`, so both exit paths are
consistent and the broken `_snapshots` reference is gone. Latent bug
found during Y77, deferred then, fixed now.

## §41. Y82 — audit-fix Fix Drop 3: risk-layer enforcement (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y82 — Fix Drop 3 of the §38 audit-fix programme (P2). Regression
sweep 6384 passed / 0 failed (baseline 6367 + 17 new Y82 tests); 80 skips
all pre-existing environmental (node/path), none schema-mismatch.

**C-2 — investigated, not a bug (no code change).** Audit C read
`us_daytrade` "1.5% vs documented 0.75%" as a sizing discrepancy. It is
two correct caps at two layers: the strategy sizes daytrade positions to
**0.75%** (`MAX_POSITION_PCT_DAYTRADE`, `strategy/config.py:311`) and the
broker pre-trade gate rejects any single intent above **1.5%**
(`max_trade_pct_per_discipline[*_DAYTRADE]`, `broker/risk.py:129`). The
broker gate is deliberately ~2x the strategy intent — a defence-in-depth
backstop, not a primary control. No regime/conviction multiplier touches
daytrade sizing. Both values operator-locked, both documented (CAPS §2.2
+ §4.6). Operator confirmed: drop C-2 from the drop. (Backlog, not C-2:
`daytrade/_base_types.py:121-123` `DayTradeParams` carries stale dead-code
sizing defaults the engine never reads — a Y15 config-rationalisation
candidate.)

**C-3 — Swing 35% engine cap, wired.** `SWING_CAP_PCT=0.35` (CAPS §1) was
defined in config since Phase 1 but never enforced — only the bot-wide
60% gross cap and the per-discipline 25% cap bound. New module-level
`swing_engine_cap_passes()` in `swing/_shared.py` filters all positions
to swing-engine disciplines (us/ftse/asx swing + smallcap + crypto swing,
via the canonical `loss_stop.discipline_to_engine`) and delegates to the
Y25 pence-aware `gross_deployed_passes_cap`. Wired into the swing BUY
path in `_evaluate_one` immediately before the existing 60% check.
Correction to the original §38 framing ("pick the real cap, delete the
dead constant"): the 25% per-discipline cap and the 35% engine cap
**compose** — 25% limits any single discipline, 35% the engine total —
so neither is deleted; the 35% is the new engine-level ceiling above the
unchanged 25%.

**C-4 — per-discipline DayTrade € caps, wired.** `DAYTRADE_US/FTSE/ASX/
CRYPTO_CAP_PCT` (12/10/8/10%, CAPS §1.1) were orphaned config constants —
zero consumers. New `SizingConfig.discipline_cap_pct()` + a new sizing-
chain step "9b" in `daytrade/_sizing.py:decide_entry` (between the 25%
engine cap and the 60% bot-wide cap): the gross-deployed sum of the
candidate's own discipline + the new target must stay under that
discipline's ceiling, else `SkipReason.DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINE_EUR_CAP`. Same
pence-aware helper + rotation handling as the engine cap. The 4 caps are
wired from `shared/config.py` into `SizingConfig` in `daytrade/_base.py`.
Per operator pre-flight: caps wired in, not deleted — they are real
operator intent.

**C-5 — Layer-5 pause/breaker event persistence, wired.** The
`DisciplinePauseMonitor` (Drop 5k) and `MarketCircuitBreaker` (Drop 5l)
kept pause state in memory and logged one WARNING line — a broker restart
erased all forensic trace. Re-scope vs the §38 plan: **no new migration
(v45 not needed)** — the canonical `events` audit table already exists
and `PersistentEventSink` already routes any event to it. Two new frozen
event dataclasses `DisciplinePausedV3` / `MarketBreakerTrippedV3` in
`broker/events.py`; both monitors take an optional `event_sink` and emit
on **trip** and on **manual resume/reset**; `main.py` wires the broker's
`PersistentEventSink` into both. Auto-expiry is deliberately not emitted
(deterministic from the trip event + duration; would otherwise fire from
the gate read-path hot loop). The 5h broker-wide kill is out of scope —
already forensically persisted via `kill_audit`. In-memory pause STATE is
unchanged (still auto-recovers on a timer); this adds the audit trail
only.

**Architectural lock — cap layering.** AlphaBot's capital caps are
layered, not redundant: per-position (strategy sizing) < per-discipline
< per-engine < bot-wide gross. Y82 makes the per-discipline and per-engine
layers real for daytrade and swing respectively; pre-Y82 only per-position
and bot-wide actually bound. The broker pre-trade gate
(`max_trade_pct_per_discipline`) sits orthogonally as a defence-in-depth
backstop ~2x looser than strategy intent (see C-2). Caps compose — a
tighter inner layer binding does not disable an outer one, and a drop
that wires one layer must not delete another.

## §42. Y83 — DB-health Phase 1: resilience / WAL-runaway fix (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y83 — Phase 1 of the three-drop DB-health programme (Y83
resilience, Y84 capture volume, Y85 signal_gates) scoped from the
2026-05-19 full DB audit. Regression 6399 passed / 0 failed (baseline
6384 + 15 new Y83 tests).

**The audit finding.** The SQLite DB had grown to 3.18 GB main + a
**1.5→2.2 GB WAL** over 4.8 days. Two problems: (1) capture volume —
`signal_context` is 75% of the DB, a ~2 KB 21-bar JSON blob per signal
(deferred to Y84); (2) resilience — a WAL runaway. The janitor J7
`wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` ran every 10 min, returned `busy=1`, and
drained exactly **716 frames every cycle** while the WAL held 370k+ and
climbing. `checkpointed_frames=716` constant = a long-lived connection
pinning the WAL read-mark at frame ~716; a checkpoint cannot truncate
past a pinned reader. Same mechanism as the 2026-05-15 4.72 GB runaway.
The bloated WAL drove write contention → recurring `database is locked`
502s (the TRX/LAYER crypto stop-cancel loop, HANDOVER_12 §8).

**Root cause confirmed (lsof pre-flight).** Y57 prescribed
`autocommit=True` for long-lived connections to prevent read-mark
pinning, but it reached only 2 of ~15 `open_connection()` call sites.
An IBKR-broker restart did not clear the pin → the pinner was in
another process; `lsof` confirmed the persistent DB-holders are the
crypto broker, scalp daemon, and IBKR broker. Prime suspect:
`broker_binance/main.py` `self._stops_db = open_connection(...)` — a
daemon-lifetime connection opened without `autocommit`, despite a
comment claiming autocommit intent.

**What Y83 shipped:**

- **R1 — autocommit on long-lived connections.** `broker_binance/
  main.py` `self._stops_db` and `broker/main.py` `self._loss_stop_conn`
  now pass `autocommit=True`. Verified behaviour-neutral: the
  `CryptoStopManager` write helpers each do a single execute()+commit(),
  and the strategy daemons already run `LossStopTracker` on an
  autocommit connection (`_daemon_common.py:485`).
- **R3 — raw `sqlite3.connect()` writer sites routed through
  `open_connection()`.** ~16 sites across `broker/stops.py` (×7),
  `broker/reconcile.py` (×5), `broker/orders.py`,
  `broker/trade_tracker_reconstruct.py` (×2), `janitor/main.py`,
  `market_data_daemon/price_cache_sync.py`. `open_connection()` gained
  an overridable `row_factory` parameter (default `_dict_row`,
  unchanged) so a converted site keeps its exact prior row shape — a
  site that reads rows by index passes `sqlite3.Row`. The `orders.py`
  and `trade_tracker_reconstruct.py` `with sqlite3.connect(...)` sites
  also leaked a connection (the context manager committed but never
  closed) — now `try/finally: conn.close()`.
- **R4 — janitor WAL-runaway alarm.** `sweep_j7_wal_checkpoint` raises a
  CRIT `J7_WAL_RUNAWAY` system alarm when a checkpoint stays `busy`
  with a WAL above `WAL_RUNAWAY_FRAMES` (65536 frames ≈ 256 MiB) — the
  runaway hid in INFO logs for hours. Idempotent; auto-resolves when the
  WAL drains.
- **R5 — retry-with-backoff on `database is locked`.** New
  `run_with_retry` helper in `db/connection.py`, applied to the stop
  persist write paths (`_persist_new`/`_persist_terminal`/
  `_persist_modification`). Belt-and-braces above SQLite's own
  busy_timeout — only "locked" errors are retried; programming errors
  propagate immediately.
- **R2 — one-time WAL drain (deploy step).** All DB-touching daemons
  restarted so every connection is recreated; with the pin cleared the
  next janitor J7 checkpoint truncates the multi-GB WAL.

**Architectural lock — long-lived DB connections must be autocommit.**
Any connection held for a process/daemon lifetime MUST be opened with
`open_connection(..., autocommit=True)`. A non-autocommit connection
left idle after a SELECT sits inside Python's implicit DEFERRED
transaction and pins the WAL read-mark, blocking checkpoint truncation
— an unbounded-WAL hazard. Short-lived (per-request / per-emit)
connections may stay non-autocommit. Raw `sqlite3.connect()` is not to
be used for DB access — `open_connection()` is the single entry point
so the pragma set (WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout,
journal_size_limit) stays uniform.

**Files:** `db/connection.py`, `broker/main.py`, `broker_binance/
main.py`, `broker/stops.py`, `broker/reconcile.py`, `broker/orders.py`,
`broker/trade_tracker_reconstruct.py`, `janitor/main.py`,
`janitor/sweeps.py`, `market_data_daemon/price_cache_sync.py`, new
`tests/test_drop_y83_db_resilience.py` (15 tests).

**Deploy.** All seven DB-touching daemons restarted (broker,
broker-crypto, the 3 strategy daemons, janitor, market-data) so the WAL
pin clears and the WAL drains. Paper mode — no live-money exposure.

## §43. Y84 — DB-health Phase 2: capture volume (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y84 — Phase 2 of the three-drop DB-health programme (Y83
resilience, Y84 capture volume, Y85 signal_gates) scoped from the
2026-05-19 full DB audit (§42). Y84 attacks the volume root cause Y83
deferred: `signal_context` is ~75% of the DB, dominated by a ~2 KB
`last_21_bars_json` blob per signal. Regression 6414 passed / 0 failed
(baseline 6399 + 15 new Y84 tests).

**What Y84 shipped:**

- **C1 — gate the `last_21_bars_json` blob on signal significance.**
  `record_signal` now keeps the ~2 KB 21-bar replay blob ONLY when the
  signal is above threshold (`score >= threshold`, regardless of
  action) OR the strategy classified it into a near-miss tier
  (`near_miss_tier` is 1/2/3). For every other signal the blob is
  stored as NULL; the small `signal_context` row (regime, bar OHLCV,
  session phase, correlate) is still written in full. `record_signal`
  gained a `near_miss_tier: int | None` parameter; the broker signal-
  record routes (`broker/api.py`, `broker/api/routes_signals.py`)
  thread it from the existing `SignalRecord.near_miss_tier` wire field
  — no schema or wire change. The gate uses score-vs-threshold (the
  `above_threshold` value already cached on `signals`), NOT action —
  an above-threshold HOLD keeps its blob.
- **C2 — `signal_context` dedicated 7-day retention window.** The
  retention rule changed from `KeepDaysFollow` (30-day cascade-follow
  of `signals`) to `KeepDaysExcept(days=7, retention_column=
  "captured_at")`. Trade-linked rows are EXEMPT — the `except_where`
  prunes a `signal_context` row after 7 days UNLESS its `signal_id` is
  an `entry_signal_id` on a `trades` row, in which case it is retained
  for the lifetime of that trades row (`trades` is Forever). Same
  trade-link condition as the `signals` rule, joined on
  `signal_context.signal_id`. `signal_context.signal_id` carries no FK
  (migration 014), so a stray orphan cannot raise on a parent delete,
  and any orphan ages out under the same 7-day rule — the old
  `KeepDaysFollow` orphan-cleanup is fully subsumed.

**C3 investigated and dropped from scope.** The audit proposed dropping
~3 "redundant" `signals` indexes (~100 MB). `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`
against the live DB (697,899 `signals` rows) for the full query
workload showed all **six** named indexes are each the unique server of
a real access pattern — none is a left-prefix of another, none is
redundant. The earlier analysis was wrong (it called
`idx_signals_strategy_at` a strict prefix of
`idx_signals_strategy_symbol_at` — it is not; and that index serves the
live `WHERE strategy_name=? ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 1` dashboard query).
No index migration shipped. A genuine `signals` index *redesign* — as
opposed to redundancy-pruning — is real optimisation work and belongs
with the Y85 analytics-aware scoping, not a DB-hygiene afterthought.

**C6 — one-time VACUUM (deploy step).** C1 gates only future writes;
existing oversized rows shrink when C2's first retention run prunes
`signal_context` down to the 7-day window. A `VACUUM` after that first
prune returns the freed pages to the OS. Operator-run after the deploy.

**Scope decision — C1 gate semantics (operator-locked).** "Use
score-vs-threshold, NOT action. Keep the blob if score ≥ threshold OR
within the near-miss band; NULL it otherwise." The near-miss band is
the canonical `near_miss_tier.classify_near_miss` classification — the
strategy already runs it and ships the result as
`SignalRecord.near_miss_tier`; Y84 reuses that rather than re-deriving.

**Scope decision — C2 trade-linked exemption (operator-locked).**
"Prune `signal_context` after 7 days UNLESS trade-linked; trade-linked
rows retained for the lifetime of their `trades` row."

**Files:** `db/writers.py`, `db/retention.py`, `broker/api.py`,
`broker/api/routes_signals.py`, new `tests/test_drop_y84_capture_volume.py`
(15 tests).

**Deploy.** Commit + push, then restart the DB-writer daemons so the C1
gate takes effect on new signals and the janitor picks up the C2
retention rule. C6 `VACUUM` operator-run after C2's first prune. Paper
mode — no live-money exposure.

## §44. V3 Drop Y86 — close-order gate exemptions (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y86 — operator-directed, from a swing rotation/exit
investigation. The swing rotation and stale-capital audits fire
correctly every cycle but the exits never complete: held FTSE positions
(CMU held since 2026-05-14, SIG, …) were trapped on the book, the
discipline stayed pinned at its 8/8 slot cap, and rotation could not
bring in new candidates. Regression 6429 passed / 0 failed (baseline
6419 + 10 new Y86 tests; one Drop 1.3.3d test updated in place — see
below). Broker-only, no migration.

**Root cause.** The broker risk gates rejected position-*closing* orders
as if they were new exposure. `risk_gate_decisions` showed every
controlled-close SELL (`ft_CLOSE_CMU_*`) rejected by `gate_max_symbol_pct`
("symbol CMU already at exposure cap") and `gate_market_open` ("no
exchange mapping for SIG"). A close reduces exposure — capping it on an
exposure/eligibility gate means an over-cap or unmappable held position
can never be sold. `risk.py` already SELL-exempts `gate_valid_symbol`
(Y75), `gate_daily_loss_cutoff` and `gate_max_daily_spend`, and
STP-SELL-exempts `gate_max_trade_pct` (8.6.7) / `gate_max_symbol_pct`
(1.3.5e) — four gates were missed.

**Architectural principle — a held position must always be able to
exit.** A SELL is provably position-reducing by the time the risk gates
see it: `gate_sell_quantity` (Y76, GATES position 3) runs first and
clamps a SELL to the held long. Therefore exposure, sizing, and
market-eligibility gates MUST exempt SELLs — they exist to bound NEW
exposure on entries (BUYs). This completes the Y75/Y76/Y77 line.

**What Y86 shipped — four gates in `broker/risk.py`:**
- **`gate_market_open`** — added a SELL exemption (had none). A held
  position must be able to attempt an exit even with no exchange
  mapping or the venue shut; IBKR queues an off-hours exit.
- **`gate_max_sector_positions`** — added a SELL exemption (had none —
  found during the build; a maxed sector trapped exits).
- **`gate_max_trade_pct`** — widened 8.6.7's STP-SELL bypass to every
  SELL. A controlled-close MKT SELL must not be re-sized down — an exit
  sells the whole held quantity.
- **`gate_max_symbol_pct`** — widened 1.3.5e's STP-SELL bypass to every
  SELL. The CMU bug fix proper.
- The position-*count* gates `gate_max_positions_per_discipline` and
  `gate_max_total_positions` already pass a close (their `already_held`
  check) — verified, unchanged.

**Test note.** One Drop 1.3.3d test (`TestExistingBehaviourPreserved`)
asserted a MKT SELL is *Modified* (re-sized) by `gate_max_trade_pct` —
the exact pre-Y86 behaviour Y86 corrects. Updated in place to assert
the new bypass (Allow), per the drop-owns-its-test-update rule.

**Out of scope (noted, not fixed):** BUY-to-close-short through the
exposure gate (the stuck book is all longs; shorts are a near-extinct
pre-Y76 anomaly). Crypto dust (Binance `-1013 NOTIONAL` — genuinely
un-sellable sub-minimum positions) is a separate problem.

**Files:** `broker/risk.py`, new `tests/test_drop_y86_close_gate_exemptions.py`
(10 tests), `tests/test_drop_1_3_3d.py` (one test updated).

**Deploy.** Commit + push, restart `alphabot-broker`. On the next swing
cycle the trapped FTSE exits clear, `ftse_swing` drops below its 8/8
slot cap, and rotation unjams. Paper mode — no live-money exposure.

## §45. V3 Drop Y87 — close-order quantity integrity, both sides (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y87 — operator-directed, scoped from a pre-Y87 forensic on two
positions (`ATG`, `TLW`) that went *short* on 2026-05-19 after the Y86
deploy unjammed the FTSE swing exits. Regression 6463 passed / 0 failed
(baseline 6429 + 34 new Y87 tests). Broker-only, no migration.

**Root cause — stacked exits oversell.** Y86 exempted SELLs from the
exposure / market-eligibility gates so trapped longs could exit. The
exits then flowed — but the swing exit logic can emit the same close
SELL on consecutive cycles, and the broker's `gate_sell_quantity` (Y76)
clamped each SELL only against `position_qty_by_symbol`, a cycle-start
snapshot. A slow MKT exit fill leaves that book un-decremented for
minutes, so two stacked exit SELLs each cleared the gate against the
*same* held long and summed past it. Forensic numbers: ATG bought 5129,
sold 3012+3487+514 = 7013 → short −1884; TLW bought 35121, sold
35121+14991 = 50112 → short −14991. The gate saw each SELL as
individually valid; nothing netted the in-flight SELLs already approved.

**Architectural principle — a close order is bounded by what is
genuinely closeable.** A position-reducing order must be clamped to
`held − Σ(in-flight orders of the same closing side)`, not to the
position book alone. The in-flight quantity is recomputed from the live
`OrderManager` registry on every `evaluate_intent` call site, so a
same-cycle prior approval is already counted — `submit()` registers an
approved `OrderState` synchronously (under `_submit_lock`) before the
next intent is evaluated. This is the within-cycle freshness guarantee;
the working-qty map is a live read, not a snapshot.

**What Y87 shipped:**
- **`order_types.py`** — two fields on `BrokerContext`:
  `working_sell_qty_by_symbol` and `working_buy_qty_by_symbol` (symbol →
  summed remaining/unfilled quantity of open non-terminal MKT/LMT orders
  of that side; STP/TRAIL stop-type orders excluded). Freshness
  semantics documented on the fields.
- **`risk.py` — `_is_position_reducing(intent, ctx)` helper.** Returns
  `True` for any SELL, or for a BUY when the held quantity is negative
  (a BUY-to-close-short). The five exposure / market-eligibility gates
  Y86 SELL-exempted (`gate_market_open`, `gate_max_sector_positions`,
  `gate_max_trade_pct`, `gate_max_symbol_pct`, `gate_daily_loss_cutoff`)
  now route through this helper, so a BUY-to-close-short is exempt too —
  closing an error short reduces risk and must never be gate-trapped.
- **`risk.py` — `gate_sell_quantity` strengthened.** `available = held
  − working_sell_qty`; `available ≤ 0` → Reject; `quantity > available`
  → Modify down; else Allow. Two stacked exits can no longer oversell.
- **`risk.py` — new `gate_buy_close_quantity` gate** (GATES position 4,
  after `gate_sell_quantity`). For a BUY against a held short it clamps
  to `abs(short) − working_buy_qty`; a BUY on a flat/long symbol passes
  untouched. The in-flight netting is **symmetric** — it nets out
  in-flight BUYs too, so the post-deploy flatten of the error shorts
  cannot itself overshoot shorts back into longs.
- **`orders.py` — `_working_close_qty_by_symbol()`** sums
  `remaining_quantity` of open non-terminal MKT/LMT orders by side;
  `submit()` and `preview_intent()` inject the two maps into the
  `BrokerContext` (via `dataclasses.replace`) immediately before
  `evaluate_intent`.

**`gate_max_daily_spend` deliberately NOT exempted** (operator
decision): a BUY-to-close-short still spends cash, so it stays gated on
`side == SELL` only, not on `_is_position_reducing`. It remains the one
gate where a position-reducing BUY is treated as spend.

**Confirmed during the build:** `exposure_by_symbol_usd` is
magnitude-valued (absolute), so the position-*count* gates already pass
a BUY-to-close-short via their `already_held` check — no change needed
there, verified not assumed.

**Test note.** One `test_preview_intent.py` assertion
(`test_preview_happy_path_returns_would_allow`) counted 16 surfaced
gates; Y87 adds `gate_buy_close_quantity` and surfaces `gate_sell_quantity`
in the preview gate list → updated to 18 in the same drop, per the
drop-owns-its-test-update rule.

**Files:** `broker/order_types.py`, `broker/risk.py`, `broker/orders.py`,
new `tests/test_drop_y87_close_quantity_integrity.py` (34 tests),
`tests/test_broker/test_preview_intent.py` (one assertion updated).

**Deploy.** Pre-deploy backup, commit + push, restart `alphabot-broker`.
**Verification beyond unit tests (operator-required):** confirm `ATG`
and `TLW` flatten on the post-deploy swing cycle — `gate_buy_close_quantity`
clamps the corrective BUYs to the short magnitude and the positions
return to flat without overshooting into longs. Paper mode — no
live-money exposure.

**Separate follow-up — Y88 (not Y87).** The strategy-side swing exit
logic dedupes exit symbols *within* a cycle (`_working_exit_symbols`)
but not *across* cycles, so it re-emits a close SELL while the prior
one is still working. Y87 makes the broker reject/clamp the duplicate;
Y88 should stop the strategy emitting it. Queued in MASTER_TODO §3.

## §46. V3 Drop Y88 — swing exit dedup across cycles (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y88 — the Y87 follow-up. Y87 made the *broker* reject/clamp a
duplicate close order; Y88 is the strategy-side root-cause cure — it
stops the swing engine *emitting* the duplicate. Regression 6480 passed
/ 0 failed (baseline 6463 + 17 Y88 tests). Strategy-only, no migration.

**Root cause — two holes in the Y74 across-cycle dedup.** Y74's
`_working_exit_symbols` (`swing/_shared.py`) scans the broker's open
orders and returns symbols with a working order whose `client_order_id`
carries the `CLOSE` stamp; the exit audits seed that set into
`excluded_symbols` and `_close_position` backstops on it, so a
slow-filling exit is not re-emitted next cycle. Two cases slipped
through:

- **Side filter.** `_close_position` exits a long with a SELL and a
  short (an error position) with a BUY-to-close (Y77) — both carry the
  `CLOSE` stamp. Pre-Y88 the scan filtered on `side == "SELL"`, so a
  working BUY-to-close-short was invisible: every cycle that audited the
  short re-emitted the BUY-to-close, and the stacked BUYs ran the short
  back through zero into a long. This is the forward risk for the ATG
  error short at the next LSE open.
- **Bracket-path coid.** `_close_position`'s bracket path
  (`modify_stop_to_market`) converts the STP child in place — it mints
  no new `CLOSE`-stamped order, the child keeps its `{parent}_stp` coid.
  The coid scan cannot see it, so a slow-filling bracket exit was
  re-fired via the legacy cancel+SELL path on the next cycle. This is
  the likely mechanism of the original ATG/TLW long→short oversell.

**What Y88 shipped — `swing/_shared.py` only:**
- `_working_exit_symbols` — **side-agnostic.** The `CLOSE` stamp, not
  the side, is the controlled-exit discriminator; the scan now matches
  it on either side. Closes the side-filter hole and still catches a
  `CLOSE`-stamped exit left working by a prior daemon process across a
  restart.
- New `_exits_in_flight: dict[str, str]` instance tracker (symbol →
  exit coid). `_close_position` records the exit coid on **both**
  success paths — the legacy `CLOSE_` coid and the bracket `{parent}_stp`
  coid. Closes the bracket-path hole, which no coid scan can cover.
- New module-level pure helper `_reconcile_exits_in_flight(tracked,
  open_orders)` — at the top of each cycle drops tracker entries whose
  order is no longer working (terminal status, or off the open-order
  list), so a symbol is released for a genuinely new exit later. `step()`
  unions `set(_exits_in_flight)` into `_working_exit_symbols`.

**Crypto twin deliberately untouched.** `crypto._close_position` is
SELL-only by construction — a Binance spot position cannot be short
(it refuses a non-positive quantity) and there is no bracket-modify
path — so `crypto._working_exit_symbols` is correct as-is and is left
side-filtered. Documented; the Y88 test asserts the crypto scan stays
side-filtered.

**Out of scope (flagged, not absorbed).** A third re-emit case — an
exit that *fully fills* between cycles while the position snapshot
still shows the old quantity, so the audit re-targets a closed
position — is position-snapshot staleness, not a `_working_exit_symbols`
gap. Same family as the post-Y87 broker DB-row lag. Left for a separate
look.

**Test note.** Y88 changed `_working_exit_symbols` behaviour, so two
prior test files were updated in the same drop (drop-owns-its-test-update
rule): `test_drop_y74_exit_idempotency.py` — `test_ignores_buy_side`
rewritten as `test_ignores_entry_buy` (an entry BUY has no `CLOSE`
stamp; the side is no longer the discriminator); `test_drop_y77_exit_path.py`
— the `_close_position` fake-self gained `_exits_in_flight={}` (the
method now records there on success).

**Files:** `broker`-free — `strategy/strategies/swing/_shared.py`, new
`tests/test_drop_y88_exit_dedup_across_cycles.py` (17 tests),
`tests/test_drop_y74_exit_idempotency.py` (one test rewritten),
`tests/test_drop_y77_exit_path.py` (harness updated).

**Deploy.** Commit + push, restart `alphabot-strategy-swing`. Should
land before the next LSE open (~07:00 UTC) so the first ftse_swing
cycle that audits the ATG error short runs the Y88 code — otherwise the
old code could re-emit the BUY-to-close and Y87's broker gate is the
only backstop. Paper mode — no live-money exposure.

## §47. V3 Drop Y89 — Fix Drop 4: funnel observability + drift fix (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y89 — the audit-fix programme's "Fix Drop 4" (forensic record
& funnel observability), **re-scoped after discovery**. The original
bundle was F7 / F-B3-2 / D-5 / F8; discovery against the live DB
(2 days after the source audits) collapsed it. Regression 6492 passed /
0 failed (baseline 6480 + 12 Y89 tests). Strategy-only, no migration.

**Re-scope — what discovery found (verified against the live DB):**
- **F7 (trades-table write gap) — RESOLVED, dropped.** The audit's
  "scalp 0 trades rows ever" was a 2026-05-17 snapshot taken *before*
  Y65 turned Scalp live (`SCALP_DRY_RUN=false`). The `trades` table now
  carries rows for all ten disciplines (crypto_scalp 50, crypto_daytrade
  242, …). The write path works.
- **F-B3-2 (scalp forensic sidecars empty) — RESOLVED, dropped.**
  `scalp_stop_decisions` (3,625 rows) and `scalp_stop_modifications`
  (1,355) have been writing since 2026-05-17 18:04 — again, Y65 going
  live.
- **D-5(b) (`signals.threshold=0.0` for DT/Scalp) — MISFRAME, dropped.**
  Not a bug: DayTrade and Scalp are gate-binary engines with no score
  threshold (explicit code comments — `daytrade/_base.py`,
  `scalp/_base.py`). There is no threshold value to record.
- **F8 (OCO leg attribution) — split to its own drop.** Discovery
  showed F8 is bigger and different than the audit framed: 118
  `crypto_stops` rows closed `OCO_CLOSED` (101 since 2026-05-17), each
  an exchange-side OCO closure that produces **no `trades` row at all**
  (the OCO child coids are never registered as OrderIntents), and
  `_resolve_oco_exit_reason` resolves none of them (0 `TAKE_PROFIT`/
  `STOP_LOSS`, all the `OCO_CLOSED` fallback). That needs a focused

**What Y89 shipped — three items, strategy-only:**
- **D-5(a) — DayTrade `cycles` rows.** `daytrade/_base.py::step()` now

  DayTrade engine wrote zero `cycles` rows all-time — Audit D could not

  `signals_evaluated` (post-qualify count), `signals_above_threshold`

- **crypto-map-fix — `swing/crypto.py::_CONTROLLED_EXIT_REASON_MAP`.**

**Rule-2 win, noted for the don't-repeat list.** The crypto-map fix is

## §48. V3 Drop Y90 — engine exit / rotation / observability fixes (2026-05-19)

**Drop.** Y90 — one consolidated drop scoped from a 2026-05-19
cross-engine review the operator commissioned (health + why the 3
engines weren't clearing old positions). Regression 6519 passed /
0 failed (baseline 6492 + 27 Y90 tests). No migration.

**The review's spine — the dashboard's "heaps of old positions" is
mostly a DB-table bug.** The DB `positions` table showed 80 held; the
brokers actually held 44 (IBKR 31 + Binance 13). ~36 rows were ghosts —
positions closed at the broker whose DB row was never written back to
0. Root cause: the IBKR reconcile loop's `_compute_drift` works on the
in-memory `PositionBook` (which fills keep correct), not the DB
`positions` table; the table is written on open/fill/auto-import but
never on close. The dashboard reads the table → phantom holdings.

**#14 — closed, resolved by Y60.** The review also settled §17 Issue A
(reconcile-tolerance vs exit-exactness, MASTER_TODO §3 Tier 2 #14): the
crypto exit `-2010` symptom is fully resolved by Y60's
`clamp_sell_quantity` — 0 `-2010` errors in the crypto broker logs
since Y60, the clamp firing 1,535× (it clamps every SELL incl. exits to
the exchange free balance). The residual — the reconciler leaving ≤1%
sub-tolerance DB drift — is within the deliberate `1%/$5` tolerance and
has no observed downstream harm. #14 is closed; no Y90 work needed.

**What Y90 shipped — five items:**
- **#1 — reconcile zeroes ghost `positions` rows.** New
  `ReconcileLoop._zero_ghost_db_positions` (`broker/reconcile.py`),
  called each `reconcile_once` (skipped in maintenance mode). It sweeps
  the DB `positions` table and zeroes any `quantity != 0` equity row
  whose symbol is held neither at IBKR nor in the in-memory book — the
  book cross-check makes it race-safe (a freshly-filled position is in
  the book synchronously, so it is never mistaken for a ghost). Guards:
  no-op on an empty IBKR snapshot (a transient empty `reqPositions`
  must not mass-zero); `discipline NOT LIKE 'crypto%'` (the Binance
  broker owns crypto rows).
- **#2 — scalp stop runner covers all four markets.** `_SCALP_DISCIPLINES`
  (`scalp_stop_runner.py` and `scalp/_sizing.py`) was stale at
  `{us_scalp, crypto_scalp}` — the runner's `run_once` filter silently
  dropped every FTSE/ASX scalp position, so their 15-minute time-stop
  was never evaluated and they were held indefinitely. Added
  `ftse_scalp` / `asx_scalp`, plus matching `_SCALP_FALLBACK_PCT` /
  `_SCALP_ATR_MULTIPLIER` entries (0.006 / 2.0× — equity scalp) in both
  files so stop-distance sizing is correct, not a wrong `.get` default.
- **#3 — swing un-closeable-contract exit quarantine.** New
  `_quarantined_exit_symbols` helper in both swing files
  (`_shared.py` + `crypto.py`): a symbol with `_MAX_CLOSE_FAILURES` (5)
  terminal-failed CLOSE orders and zero FILLED closes is folded into
  `_working_exit_symbols`, so the exit audits and `_close_position`
  skip it. Stops the every-cycle resubmit storm (FUM/SIG/MND had
  50–167 dead order rows each — delisted / halted / no-definition IBKR
  contracts that clear our gates but IBKR rejects). Operator is alerted
  once per newly-quarantined symbol. A close that ever FILLs clears the
  symbol (a transient halt self-resolves).
- **#4 — DayTrade per-strategy cap re-seeds from FILLED orders.**
  `_count_entries_today_from_db` now counts `status = 'FILLED'` BUY
  rows. Pre-Y90 it counted every status, so a restart re-seeded a daily
  budget already burned by rejected/unfilled orders. The within-session
  live counter still increments on submit-success (deliberately
  conservative; also bounds within-cycle bursts) — only the
  restart-survival DB seed changed.
- **#6 — equity DayTrade per-strategy daily cap 25 → 50.**
  `MAX_TRADES_PER_STRATEGY_PER_DAY`. The equity daytrade engines posted
  ~56 signals/cycle but submitted nothing once they hit 25 — paper-mode
  data-gathering was throttled. Raised to 50; the cap still trips and
  logs `per_strategy_daily_cap`, just higher.

**Split out of Y90 (own follow-up drops):**
- **#5 — crypto dust write-off.** Discovery showed it needs careful
  work in the Binance reconcile loop (the dust positions are real
  sub-NOTIONAL Binance balances; a write-off needs DB/book/exchange
  consistency handling). Low-impact — Y77 already suppresses the
  retry-spam, so it is cosmetic dashboard clutter. Deferred to its own

## §49. Drop 1+4 — trade-write gap + joinability (2026-05-20)

**Scoped from the 2026-05-19 engine persistence audit (`docs/AUDIT_REPORTS/ENGINE_PERSISTENCE_AUDIT_2026-05-19.md`).** Four sub-items in one drop, broker-side and strategy-side combined per operator decision to fold Drop 4 into Drop 1.

**Why.** The persistence audit identified three blackouts: trade outcomes, active position management, cap/near-miss rejections. Drop 1+4 addresses **trade outcomes** and the **joinability** spine. Two other drops follow (Drop 2 = rejection/near-miss; Drop 3 = active management).

### Sub-items shipped

- **Sub-item 1 — F8 OCO routing.** The Binance WS `executionReport` handler now feeds OCO SL/TP SELL fills into `CryptoTradeTracker` (`broker_binance/reconcile.py:_maybe_route_oco_fill`). `_build_trade` gains TAKE_PROFIT inference for `tp-*` coids (STOP_LOSS already covered the `stp-*` family — widened to `stp-` to catch all Binance prefixes). Closes MASTER_TODO §3 F8 item; every Binance bracket exit now produces a `trades` row.
- **Sub-item 2 — Reconcile-synthesised RECONCILED trades.** Both reconcile loops (`broker/reconcile.py:_zero_ghost_db_positions`, `broker_binance/reconcile.py:_apply_close`) synthesise a trades row before zeroing the position, IFF a surviving `open_entries` mirror row exists. Best-effort exit price (live_price_cache → avg_cost fallback). New exit_reason value `RECONCILED`. Gated on mirror survival so a tracker-delivered trade is never duplicated.
- **Sub-item 3 — `open_entries` durable mirror.** Migration 045. Running aggregates (no JSON blobs). Synchronous upsert from `TradeTracker` on every fill, delete on close in the same txn as the `trades` insert. Startup rehydrate replaces the lossy `reset_from_positions` synthetic for matched keys with accurate `opened_at` / `entry_signal_id` / `strategy_name`. Z6 reconstructor + `reset_from_positions` retained as backstops. Retention = SelfManaged (tracker owns lifecycle, startup reconcile sweeps orphans via the sub-item-2 synthesis path).
- **Drop 4 (folded) — Joinability.** Migration 046 adds `cycles.cycle_id INTEGER`. All four engines now stamp the same epoch-ms `cycle_id` on the cycle stats POST and the signal batch — `cycles.cycle_id ↔ signals.cycle_id` join is live. (Scalp already had `cycle_id` on its signal batch; swing equity had it on signals only; swing crypto and daytrade now match.) **Scalp `signal_id → EntryIntent` deferred** — structurally invasive (requires sync POST-and-id-correlation), parked as backlog under MASTER_TODO Tier 3 analytics.

**Architectural lock.** `open_entries` is the **canonical durable handle** for the TradeTracker working set. Two brokers, one shared table, keyed `(execution_mode, experiment_id, symbol)` with NULL→"" normalisation. Tracker mirrors are best-effort; the startup reconcile is the active healer. A blind time-based retention on this table is forbidden (it would sweep live long-held positions); SelfManaged + startup reconcile is the only safe pattern.

**Regression.** 6519 / 0 — identical to baseline. Lint clean on touched files (remaining ruff errors are pre-existing RUF002/003/005/006 in untouched code). Schema doc updated (`SCHEMA_REFERENCE.md` documents `open_entries`, `cycles.cycle_id`, `RECONCILED` + `TAKE_PROFIT` exit_reasons).

**Honest test gap.** No new unit tests this drop for the four new code paths (F8 routing, RECONCILED synthesis, `open_entries` round-trip, cycle_id round-trip). Regression stayed green because the changes are additive — no existing test asserted the old (broken) behaviour. Tests **must** be added before any non-trivial change in this area; tracked as MASTER_TODO §3 follow-up.
