## §50. Drop 2 — rejection / near-miss completeness (2026-05-20)

**Scoped from the 2026-05-19 engine persistence audit Blackout C (cap / near-miss rejections).** Closes the strategy-side rejection observability gap and the daytrade+scalp `near_misses` coverage gap. Four sub-items, one drop.

**Why.** The audit found: (i) strategy-side sizing-chain caps (`PER_STRATEGY_DAILY_CAP`, `BOT_WIDE_DAILY_CAP`, `*_EUR_CAP`, `COOLDOWN_BLOCKED`, `SCALP_DRY_RUN`, `QTY_BELOW_MIN_NOTIONAL`, etc.) returned silently with no DB record — only a journald line; (ii) daytrade + scalp hardcoded `near_miss_reason=None`, so the broker's `record_signal` route skipped the `near_misses` table write for both engines (only `RISK_GATE_BLOCKED` rows from the broker risk-gate path landed); (iii) `record_circuit_breaker_event` existed in `loss_stop.py:692` but had **zero callers** in production — the dedicated `circuit_breaker_events` table was empty despite pauses and market-breaker trips firing (those went to the `events` table via the V3 sink, which is dormant on strategy daemons).

### Sub-items shipped

- **Sub-item A — Migration 047: rename `scalp_rejections` → `rejections`.** The table has been engine-general since Drop 1.4.10 — `/events/rejection` accepts any discipline, and daytrade + swing already wrote broker-side rejects here. Drop 2 fixes the name to match the reality. Retention bumped 30d → 90d per operator spec. `loss_stop_events` + `circuit_breaker_events` retention changed from `Forever` → `KeepDays(90)`.
- **Sub-item B — `near_miss_reason=None` hardcode fixed in `daytrade/_base.py:1083+` and `scalp/_base.py:748+`.** Tier 1/2/3 → `GATE_NEAR_MISS_5OF6` / `GATE_WATCH_4OF6` / `GATE_BELOW_THRESHOLD` (same vocabulary swing already used — the suffixes are tier labels, not literal gate counts; daytrade has 8 gates, scalp has 6, swing has 6). Cross-engine analytics now read one consistent reason vocabulary.
- **Sub-item C — Strategy-side sizing-chain skips → `rejections`.** DayTrade `decide_entry` skip path (`_base.py:1529-1541`) and Scalp 8-step sizing-chain skip (`_base.py:854-885`) + Scalp `SCALP_DRY_RUN` suppression (`_base.py:898-920`) now call `broker_client.post_rejection` with the typed `SkipReason` value on `gate_name`. Captures intended_quantity / intended_notional / signal_score for tuning. Swing left as-is — its skips land on `near_misses` (existing counterfactual-replay surface); no double-write.
- **Sub-item D — `record_circuit_breaker_event` wired into `discipline_pause.py` + `market_circuit_breaker.py`.** On each `paused` transition: writes `cap_kind=discipline_soft_no_rotation` (the per-discipline soft pause). On each `tripped` transition: writes `cap_kind=cross_engine_hard` (the per-exchange breaker). State-clears (`manual_resume`, `expired`, `manual_reset`) intentionally not recorded — the trip row already captured the event. `loss_stop_events` writer is already wired (since pre-Drop-2 — `LossStopTracker._record_loss_stop_event`); table is empty operationally because no engine % cap has been breached. No code change for the loss_stop path in Drop 2.

**Architectural notes.**
- `rejections` table now carries TWO kinds of rows: broker-side rejects (`gate_name` starts with `gate_*` or is `broker_kill`/`submit_order raised`) and strategy-side sizing-chain skips (`gate_name` is the typed `SkipReason` value). Operators discriminate via `gate_name` — no source column.
- `circuit_breaker_events` is the dedicated Layer-4/Layer-5 risk-hierarchy audit surface. Each trip is one row. The V3 `DisciplinePausedV3` / `MarketBreakerTrippedV3` events continue to flow into the generic `events` table; the dedicated table is the structured query surface.

**Regression.** 6519 passed / 0 failed (= post-Drop-1+4 baseline). Lint clean on touched files. Schema doc updated.

**Honest test gap.** No new unit tests this drop for the four new write paths. Regression stayed green because the changes are additive — existing tests don't assert the old broken behaviour. Tests deferred; tracked as a follow-up alongside the Drop 1+4 test backfill.

## §51. Drop 3 — active-management capture (swing) (2026-05-20)

**Scoped from the 2026-05-19 engine persistence audit Blackout B.** Closes the "swing audit chain is log-only" gap. Last drop in the operator-approved 4-drop sequence following Drop 1+4 / Drop 2.

**Why.** The audit found swing's `_audit_time_stop` / `_audit_stale_capital` / `_audit_stale_progress` / `_audit_signal_exits` / `_try_rotate` / `_audit_open_slot_rotation` each compute a decision and emit only a `log.info` — nothing persists. `swing/_shared.py` had **zero DB-write calls** in the audit chain (verified by grep, `:2368` is the only call and it's the in-memory ReadySet recorder). The `events` table carries no rotation/eviction/exit event type either. Per-cycle CycleStats counters lived only in the `log.info("cycle complete: …")` line — no `cycles` columns held them.

### Sub-items shipped

- **Migration 048.** Widens `cycles` with 12 active-management counters (`audited`, `naked_flattened`, `naked_alerted`, `legacy_stop_attached`, `stale_evicted`, `stale_progress_evicted`, `time_stop_evicted`, `signal_exited`, `rotated`, `open_slot_rotated`, `eod_flattened`, `skipped_sizing_chain` — the Drop 2 sizing-chain aggregate). Creates `management_decisions` table — one row per audit decision, keyed by `cycle_id` (joins `cycles` on the Drop 1+4 cycle handle), with the explicit operator-approved `runners_up_json` column for the rotation "why didn't it rotate X" question. Widens `orders` with 4 sizing-decision columns (`target_qty`, `max_qty`, `target_position_eur`, `projected_deployed_eur`) — schema ready; writers ship in Drop 3.1. Retention `KeepDays(60, at_utc)` on `management_decisions`.
- **Swing equity audit hooks.** `_audit_time_stop`, `_audit_stale_capital`, `_audit_stale_progress`, `_audit_signal_exits`, `_try_rotate` (with runners-up), `_audit_open_slot_rotation` each call `_post_management_decision` after their existing `log.info` + `_close_position(ok=True)`. The `_try_rotate` runners-up payload carries the considered-but-kept positions as `[{symbol, score, pnl_pct, reason}, ...]` (bounded to 10 entries — typical swing candidate set is far smaller).
- **Swing equity + crypto-swing cycle payload.** Extended `post_cycle_stats` payload with the 11 audit counters from `CycleStats` / `CryptoCycleStats` (crypto's 8 — its dataclass omits `naked_alerted`, `legacy_stop_attached`, `eod_flattened`). Per-cycle counts now live as discrete `cycles` columns.
- **New `record_management_decision` writer** + new `/events/management-decision` route + new `broker_client.post_management_decision` method. Standard plumbing pattern (mirrors `/events/cycle` / `/events/rejection`).

**`cycle_id` joinability.** `CycleStats` gains a `cycle_id` property that lazily derives the epoch-ms from `started_at` (matches the Drop 1+4 cycle handle used in cycles / signals). Audits emit decisions with that cycle_id, so `cycles ↔ management_decisions` joins natively.

**Architectural lock — runners_up JSON.** Operator approved this single JSON column as an explicit exception to the "no JSON blobs in new tables" rule from the persistence audit. The blob is bounded (the candidate set size), serves a use case (rotation context) that doesn't fit discrete columns, and a follow-up rotation can write a sibling JSON without schema churn.

**Deferred to Drop 3.1.** Four pieces — operator's "don't smuggle half-finished" principle, scope-honest:
- DayTrade `orders_submitted` / `orders_rejected` counter wiring (still 0 on daytrade cycle rows).
- Scalp `scalp_cycles` skip-funnel + latency column population (columns exist; writer doesn't pass values).
- Writers that populate the new `orders` sizing-decision columns (NULL until 3.1).
- Crypto-swing audit hooks (`CryptoCycleStats` cycle counters flow into `cycles` rows; per-decision `management_decisions` rows don't yet — equity-swing audits emit them, the crypto-swing audit chain isn't instrumented in Drop 3). Also: equity swing's naked-position audit (`_audit_naked_positions`) increments `naked_alerted` / `legacy_stop_attached` / `naked_flattened` counters but doesn't emit per-decision rows in this drop — same shape as the crypto deferral.

**Regression.** 6519 passed / 0 failed (= Drop 2 baseline). Lint clean. Schema doc updated.

**Honest test gap.** No new unit tests for the audit-hook write paths. Regression stayed green because the changes are additive (no existing test asserted the old log-only behaviour). Tests deferred alongside the Drop 1+4 / Drop 2 test backfill — tracked as a single follow-up.

### Flip 1 — `GATE_PIPELINE_ENABLED=true` (~08:30 UTC)

The Gate 0–5 entry pipeline (Y94d-2 to Y94d-6) replaces the legacy Drop 0.1b/0.1c/0.1d gates on the daytrade entry path. Zero ERROR-level events, zero fallback-guard fires (live NLV used 100% of the time), both brokers HEALTHY through every sample. Pipeline produced 76→137→139→118→97→106→115→99 WOULD-BUY `gates=*/5` decisions per 16-min window. Legacy `gates=*/4` count was 42 in sample 1 (pre-flip residual) and **0** for samples 2–8. 3 trades closed cleanly — one SIGNAL_SELL (ASTERUSDT -$1.34 / -1.34%), one DAYTRADE_SOFT_CAP_ROTATION (EURUSDT -$0.03 / -0.03%), one STOP_LOSS (GMTUSDT -$1.30 / -1.30%). Rotation exit specifically proves `MAX_POSITIONS_DAYTRADE_SOFT=10` + `DAYTRADE_ROTATION_SCORE_GAP_MIN=1.5` is firing under live regime. `alphabot/dashboard/static/js/daytrade_terminal.js::pctTxt()` was multiplying its argument by 100 — but the only caller (line 185) passes `p.unrealized_pnl_pct`, which `/api/positions` already returns in **percent units** per the CLAUDE.md §2 schema rule. ### GMT phantom — bug discovered, root cause OPEN

The same GMTUSDT trade that surfaced the rendering bug also surfaced a **data-drift bug on the trade-close path**. The trade row was written cleanly at 10:10:19 (STOP_LOSS, -$1.30 / -1.30%) but neither the DB `positions` row nor the broker's in-memory `position_book` got zeroed — both still showed `quantity=7656.9` from the 10:03 open. Venue (Binance `/balances`) had 0 GMT — the asset was fully cleared venue-side; only our local state drifted.

ASTERUSDT and EURUSDT from the same soak window both closed cleanly with everything zeroed, so this is **intermittent — likely a race condition in the close path**. Manual cleanup this session: `UPDATE positions SET quantity=0 WHERE symbol='GMTUSDT'` + `sudo systemctl restart alphabot-broker-crypto` (the broker reads positions from DB at startup, so the restart rebuilt the in-memory cache from the corrected DB). All three layers now show 0; venue, DB, broker-cache, dashboard.

**Open question for a future drop:** is the bug in `broker_binance/reconcile.py` (the WS-fill-driven close path) or in `position_book` itself (a write that didn't commit)? GMT is the only known instance; needs a forensic pass when next observed. Carrying the symptom characteristics: trade-row written normally, positions-row left at open-time `quantity` + `last_updated_at`, broker-cache identical to DB row.

### Y95 hotfix 1 — severity vocabulary collision (commit `453ca56`)

Brain crashed on first sweep cycle: `CHECK constraint failed: severity IN ('INFO', 'WARN', 'CRIT')`. I had written `auto_fix.py`, `sweep.py`, and `pulse.py` using `INFO/MEDIUM/HIGH` severity strings while the deployed `system_alarms` schema (migrations 036+038) accepts `INFO/WARN/CRIT` only. **Same R5-class hazard from CLAUDE.md §2**: the brain test fixtures created `system_alarms` WITHOUT the CHECK constraint, so the severity-vocabulary error slipped past CI.

Fixed: remapped `MEDIUM→WARN`, `HIGH→CRIT` everywhere in brain. Added a defensive `_VALID_SEVERITIES = frozenset({"INFO","WARN","CRIT"})` and `_VALID_CATEGORIES` guard at the top of `alarms.raise_alarm()` so the same class of bug fails at the Python layer even when test fixtures don't enforce CHECK. One existing test updated (`test_consume_approval_token_atomic_single_use` was passing `severity='HIGH'`).

Same commit also fixed `sweep.py::_j8_ranked_candidates_stale` SQL column reference `at` → `snapshot_at` (the column doesn't exist by the bare name).

### Y95 hotfix 2 — Settings.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY field missing (commit `9023e53`)

After the operator dropped `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` into `.env` via `POST /secrets/update`, Brain still couldn't see it. Root cause: `Settings` class in `alphabot/shared/config.py` declared `CLAUDE_API_KEY` (the legacy alias) but **not** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. With `model_config.extra="ignore"`, pydantic silently dropped the field at load time. `claude_client._get_api_key()` returned None → "no-key graceful path" → 45 zero-cost no-op invocations during the diagnosis window.

Fixed: added `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: SecretStr = SecretStr("")` alongside the legacy `CLAUDE_API_KEY`. Both names now accepted. Verified post-fix with the live `.env`: pydantic loads a 108-char key ending `****2AAA`.

## §60. Y97 — brain knowledge cheap-path + weekly distillation (2026-05-23 night)

**The §12 cheap-path-first work moved from filed-not-built to deployed.** Five commits in the same session: Y97.1 (cheap-path stack), two hot-fixes surfaced by the deploy (Y97.1.1 dict-row factory, Y97.1.2 deep_scan severity vocabulary), Y97.2 (weekly distillation prompt + cost-trajectory query). Schema 55 → 56 via migration 056_brain_signatures applied on broker restart at 18:32 UTC. Brain restarted four times to land each commit; all loops healthy on the final restart at 18:48 UTC. Steps 1+2+3+5+6 of §12.9 shipped; step 4 (Tier-A autonomous apply at proven_count ≥ 3) remains deferred per the spec's "needs a real-production BK at proven_count ≥ 3 to unlock" gate.

### Y97.1 — Cheap-path stack (§12 steps 1+2+3)

Commit `e05a548`. 10 files; 1720 insertions.

- **Migration 056** (`alphabot/db/migrations/056_brain_signatures.sql`). Additive: 4 nullable columns on `brain_knowledge` (`signature_json`, `signature_hash`, `proven_count DEFAULT 0`, `fix_payload_json`) + partial index on signature_hash + `applied_bk_id TEXT NULL` on `system_alarms`. Pure addition, safe to apply hot.
- **`alphabot/brain/patterns.py`** (new module). `compute_signature(alarm) -> dict` builds the canonical identity (rule_name, table coarse-bucketed from rule_key prefix, discipline, market projection us/ftse/asx/crypto, symptom_bucket from a small registry, traceback_hash from `broker_errors`). `match_known_pattern(conn, signature) -> KnownPattern | None` is a plain indexed SELECT — picks the highest-proven matching BK, skips superseded rows. `record_known_pattern` is the write side. `increment_proven_count` is the trust-dial bump. SHA-256 over SHA-1 (S324 lint, no security significance).
- **`reconcile.py::_diagnose_one_alarm`** — Step 0 cheap-path gate inserted ABOVE the legacy `run_investigation` call. On match → `run_single_turn` (no tools, no agentic loop, one round-trip) confirming the BK fits this specific alarm. Records `applied_bk_id` on the alarm row in the same connection so the next reconcile cycle's self_clear can credit the BK. On no match → full investigation unchanged.
- **`alarms.self_clear_if_present`** — reads `applied_bk_id` from rows it resolves; if present, calls `patterns.increment_proven_count(bk_id)` then NULLs the link (so re-trigger of the same rule_key under unrelated conditions can't double-count). Defensive try/except around the new column so pre-056 fixtures don't crash. New helper `attach_applied_bk_id` is the write side.
- **`claude_client.run_single_turn`** — bounded API call: no tools (guaranteed one round-trip), max_tokens=1024, same budget pre-flight + `brain_claude_invocations` recording as `run_investigation`. Loop_name `reconcile_diagnose`, purpose `cheap_confirm:<rule_key>`.
- **`context_builder.cheap_confirm_user_prompt`** — formats the matched BK + the fresh alarm + the fix payload for the single-turn call. Asks for `CONFIRM: <one-line fix>` or `REJECT: <one-line reason>` — no preamble. Same base system prompt as the agentic path.

### Y97.1.1 hotfix — dict-row factory regression (commit `6542df2`)

First post-deploy restart at 18:32:47 UTC threw `KeyError: 0` inside `alarms.self_clear_if_present`: my new code used `row[0]` integer indexing but `open_connection()` installs a `_dict_row` factory. Pulse loop's cycle-outer try caught it so `/health` stayed 200, but the error fired every pulse cycle.

Fixed by mirroring the existing dict-then-tuple try/except pattern already in use higher up the same file in `raise_alarm`. Added `test_self_clear_works_against_dict_row_factory` exercising the production `_dict_row` factory shape so this exact class of bug fails in CI rather than production again.

### Y97.1.2 hotfix — deep_scan D-rule severity vocabulary (commit `3a728ba`)

Second post-restart cycle exposed a PRE-EXISTING latent bug: the Y95 hotfix `453ca56` cleaned up `alarms.py`, `auto_fix.py`, `sweep.py`, `pulse.py` for `INFO/WARN/CRIT` vocabulary but missed `deep_scan.py`. 12 of 14 D-rules in `_D_RULES` were declared with `severity_on_issue` of `HIGH` or `MEDIUM`; the bump-severity branch at `deep_scan.py:331` threw `IntegrityError: CHECK constraint failed` whenever Claude returned an issue (not all-clear).

Remap: `HIGH → CRIT` (D1, D3, D4, D7, D11, D12); `MEDIUM → WARN` (D6, D8, D9, D10, D13, D14); D2 + D5 already `CRIT`. ### Y97.2 — Weekly distillation + cost-trajectory (§12 steps 5+6)

Commit `2f53bcd`. 2 files; 284 insertions.

`context_builder.weekly_briefing_user_prompt` extended with two new sections appended after the existing 1–7 analytics list:

- **§12.4 distillation block.** Claude is told to review `brain_knowledge` entries touched this week + `brain_claude_invocations` cost log, identify patterns that recurred ≥3 times this week OR have `proven_count ≥ 3` lifetime OR consumed the most cumulative Claude $, and propose one of: (a) PROMOTE TO MECHANICAL RULE → new W/P/J check or Tier-A AF (removes Claude entirely from this class going forward), (b) PROMOTE TIER-B → TIER-A (operator-promotion-only per §12.7), (c) KEEP AS-IS. Output: ranked list with estimated monthly $ saved per promotion. §12.7 guard prose explicit in the prompt: "Do NOT write code. Brain NEVER edits its own source. Operator approves; Claudio implements."
- **§12.6 cost-trajectory block.** Claude runs the §12.6 SQL skeleton via the existing `query_db` tool (GROUP BY iso_week, COUNT(*) FROM brain_knowledge WHERE category='promotion_approved' for the rules-count column, 90-day window). Interprets the trend: flat-or-declining spend + rising rules count = the ratchet is working; rising spend + flat rules = either novelty is genuinely high this period or a pattern that should have been promoted wasn't (flag the candidates). The interpretation rule from §12.6 is the operator's canary on the cheap-path ratchet's health.

### Architectural locks added

- **L-Y97-CHEAP-PATH** — `reconcile.py::_diagnose_one_alarm` runs `_lookup_known_pattern` BEFORE `claude_client.run_investigation`. On any match where `confidence ≥ KNOWN_PATTERN_CONFIDENCE_MIN` (0.10), the cheap-confirm branch fires instead. The confidence floor is generous on purpose — even a brand-new BK at `proven_count=0` is worth a single-turn confirm; the *autonomous-apply* gate is the separate `proven_count ≥ 3` Tier-A rule (deferred per §12.9 step 4).
- **L-Y97-NO-DOUBLE-CREDIT** — `self_clear_if_present` reads `applied_bk_id` then NULLs it in the same connection's `with` block. A re-trigger of the same `rule_key` under unrelated conditions cannot double-count an old fix's proven_count; the operator-approval-path is the only way `proven_count` advances.
- **L-Y97-DRULE-SEVERITY** — `DRule.__post_init__` enforces `severity_on_issue ∈ {INFO, WARN, CRIT}` at dataclass construction. Adding a new D-rule with `HIGH` or `MEDIUM` fails at import. Same Python-layer mirror as `alarms._VALID_SEVERITIES`. Locks the L-Y95-SEVERITY contract for deep_scan.

Pre-Y97.7 D1 fired `every_cycle` (hourly) at ~$1.50/call = $36/day = $1100/month. Math doesn't survive contact with $50/month cap. Y97.7 set D1 to `once_daily_06` (06:00 UTC = 08:00 Paris CEST, just before daily briefing window). Cut D1 contribution from ~$36/day to ~$1.50/day.

Y97.7 was only a partial fix — the other 13 D-rules (every_cycle / every_other / twice_daily) still projected ~$60/day if budget allowed. The operator surfaced this as "even $5/day is ridiculous" and asked for a deeper restructure.

Operator directive (2026-05-23 late night): "the brain needs to bank up all the issues, do 1 big claude call per day to do investigations and then send me a daily report that i can drop in here to you claudio and you fix. anything else is completely uneconomical for a papertrading desk at the moment."

Architectural pivot:

- **All 14 D-rules cadence="deferred"** (was `every_cycle` / `every_other` / etc.). Deep Scan loop still runs but makes ZERO investigations. Re-enable per-rule by flipping cadence.
- **Reconcile-diagnose restructured** in `reconcile.py::_diagnose_one_alarm`:
  1. Pre-Y97.8 cheap-confirm Claude call DELETED. Replaced by `_attach_matched_diagnosis_no_claude` which stamps the BK's stored diagnosis text onto the alarm WITHOUT Claude. Operator sees the matched pattern's stored diagnosis on the dashboard.

  3. No match → alarm sits with `diagnosis=NULL` until the 06:00 UTC daily report investigates.
- **Daily briefing prompt rewritten** as THE investigation: reads every undiagnosed alarm, every matcher-handled alarm, every Tier-A apply, top broker_errors by traceback_hash, today's spend + flag state, edge snapshot. Produces structured daily report with a first-line one-liner + "Recommended drops for Claudio:" ranked list at the end.
- **Telegram delivery unconditional** (was: only on concerns surfaced). The daily report IS the operator surface; if Brain ran today, the operator wants the report.
- **Caps reduced**: `BRAIN_MONTHLY_USD_CAP $50 → $30`, `BRAIN_DAILY_USD_CAP $5 → $3`. Expected real burn ~$40-60/month (one daily call ~$1-2 + Saturday weekly ~$2 + ad-hoc Tier-A applies $0); $30 cap is the guard rail, not the target.

- Reconcile DETECTION (janitor writes R-alarms; no Claude)

Post-Y97.8 deploy, brain `/health` returned 200 but `restart counter = 4154` — brain had been crash-looping 4154 times before the operator noticed. Root cause: same R5-class hazard the Y97.1.1 hotfix already fixed in `alarms.py` was still present in `sweep.py:222`:

    naked = [(r[0], r[1]) for r in rows]

`open_connection()` installs a `_dict_row` factory; `r[0]` raises `KeyError: 0`. J10 (stop-coverage-drift) tripped on every sweep cycle.

- **L-Y97-ONCE-DAILY-CLAUDE** — Brain makes at most ONE Claude call per day (the 06:00 UTC daily briefing) + one per week (Saturday 07:00 UTC weekly briefing). Everything else autonomous is $0 by design. Adding any per-cycle Claude investigation regresses this lock.

Every cell renders n explicitly. NO_EDGE state shows when EITHER
n < 30 OR the CI brackets zero (both branches visible). PROVEN tier
(n ≥ 150) gets a distinct ★ badge so the operator can spot promotable
cells at a glance. No path lets a caller render a point estimate
without the CI — `EdgeCell` carries point + ci_lower + ci_upper + state
together, and the JSON serialiser preserves all four.

## §66 — Y99: §11.B.1 Daily P&L + hour-of-day heatmap (2026-05-24 morning)

Second §11.B surface lands the same day as Y98. With Y96 capture already
in place pre-session and Y98 edge matrix shipped this morning, the
operator-facing analytics layer is now two-surfaces-wide: one for
"is this edge real" (edge matrix) and one for "where did the money
come from" (daily P&L).

### Why this drop (and why now)

The edge matrix needs months of trading to populate cells with n≥30.
Until then it's mostly empty. The daily P&L surface is useful from
trade 1: every trade contributes a tile, and the operator can see
hour-of-day patterns + per-market splits long before any cell graduates
to PROVEN. Y99 fills the "I can already see something" gap.

### Architecture (mirrors Y98)

Three-layer split, intentional:

1. `alphabot/intelligence/pnl_daily.py` — pure compute. Reads trades
   within window, groups by UTC date + UTC hour of `closed_at`,
   returns a `DailyPnL` dataclass with `daily_rows` + `hour_of_day` +
   `summary`. No DB writes, no caching, no side effects. Reuses the
   Y98 `_discipline_to_market` helper for the 6-market split — single
   source of truth on the market-mapping.

2. `alphabot/brain/operator_ui/pnl_daily.py` — `GET /pnl/daily?days=N`.
   PIN-gated. Days 1..365 (default 14). Audit-logged to
   `operator_audit` like every operator-console endpoint.

3. Dashboard PNL tab — between EDGE and CONTROL. Three views in one
   page: headline tiles, 24-cell UTC hour heatmap (3-tier colour
   intensity each side of zero), daily ledger (newest first) with
   per-market chips sorted by magnitude desc.

### Bucketing decision (locked)

P&L is attributed to the UTC date AND UTC hour of `closed_at`. Not
opened_at. Rationale:

- The realisation event is the close.
- Daytrade trades open + close same day so the distinction usually
  doesn't matter.
- For overnight trades (rare on the daytrade desk), attributing to
  closed_at is the unambiguous rule. Cleaner than "open day if same
  UTC date, close day otherwise" branching.

This is encoded in the SQL `WHERE closed_at >= ?` window and the
in-Python bucketing.

### §11.5 honesty under Y99

The daily P&L surface is descriptive, not inferential — it sums what
happened, it doesn't estimate a future mean. So no bootstrap CI per
cell (unlike Y98). The honesty discipline here is showing **n
alongside every number**: hour cells show their n, daily rows show
n_trades + n_winners + n_losers + win_rate, headline tiles show the
n that produced them. A single-trade day cannot be misread as
signal because the dashboard renders "n=1" next to it.

### Locks added in Y99

**L-Y99-PNL-COMPUTE-PURE**: `alphabot/intelligence/pnl_daily.py` is
pure. No DB writes, no caching, no side effects. Same lock family
as L-Y98-EDGE-COMPUTE-PURE — keeps the analytics layer testable +
re-runnable.

**L-Y99-CLOSED-AT-BUCKETING**: P&L is attributed to the UTC date
and UTC hour of `closed_at`. Any future drop changing this must
update the lock + every consumer of `daily_rows`/`hour_of_day`.

**L-Y99-N-ALWAYS-VISIBLE**: Every dashboard cell that renders a
P&L number must render its n alongside. The compute layer enforces
this at the dataclass level (`n_trades` is non-optional, and
serialisers must include it).

### Files touched

- `alphabot/intelligence/pnl_daily.py` (new, 307 LOC including
  module docstring + dataclasses + compute + serialisers)
- `alphabot/brain/operator_ui/pnl_daily.py` (new, PIN-gated
  endpoint)
- `alphabot/brain/service.py` (router wire — Y99 block)
- `alphabot/brain/static/dashboard/index.html` (PNL tab markup +
  tabbar entry between EDGE and CONTROL)
- `alphabot/brain/static/dashboard/app.css` (Y99 styling block —
  tiles, hour heatmap with 3-tier colour, daily rows)
- `alphabot/brain/static/dashboard/app.js` (pageLoaders.pnl wire +
  window toggle handlers + loadDailyPnL + renderDailyPnL)
- `tests/intelligence/test_pnl_daily.py` (new, 10 cases)
- `tests/brain/test_y99_pnl_daily_endpoint.py` (new, 5 cases)

### Test sweep

2 endpoint (the other 3 endpoint cases are validation + PIN gate).

### What's intentionally NOT in Y99

- **No CI bands on hour cells**. Descriptive sums, not estimates.
- **No regime cut in the dashboard heatmap**. The data is there
  (`per_regime_pnl` on daily rows), just not surfaced visually —

## §67 — Y100: §11.B.2 Exit-reason × market EV slice (2026-05-24 morning)

Third §11.B surface in one session. After Y98 (edge matrix —
"is this edge real?") and Y99 (daily P&L — "where did the money
come from?"), Y100 answers **"which exit modes pay me?"**

### Why this slice

The trades table records `exit_reason` for every closed trade.
The values divide into two semantic families:

- **Intentional**: `SIGNAL_SELL` — the strategy's chosen exit. Mean
  should be positive (or the entry signal is broken).
- **Protective**: `STOP`, `time_stop`, `stale_progress` — controlled
  exits when something goes wrong (loss, decay, stall). Mean should
  be negative (STOP) or near zero (time_stop / stale_progress) by
  design.

A bootstrap CI per (exit_reason × market) cell answers two
operator questions in one surface:

1. Are my SIGNAL_SELLs paying? (positive mean, tight CI = yes)
2. Are my protective exits doing their job? (STOPs negative-tight,
   not negative-wide which would mean stops fire on noise)

### Architecture (mirror of Y98)

Same three-layer split with deliberate reuse:

1. `alphabot/intelligence/exit_reason_ev.py` — pure compute.
   Imports `_discipline_to_market`, `_MARKET_ORDER`,
   `_sample_state_for`, `_row_get` from `edge_matrix.py` — single
   source of truth on market mapping and sample-state thresholds.
2. `alphabot/brain/operator_ui/exit_reason_ev.py` — PIN-gated
   `GET /exits/ev?days=N`, audit-logged.
3. Dashboard EXITS tab between PNL and CONTROL. Reuses the
   `renderEdgeCell` JS helper from Y98 — cell visuals identical
   across the three intelligence tabs.

### Discovery vs enumeration

Unlike regimes (Y98: 3 fixed values), exit_reasons are
**discovered from data** in the window. The compute returns
`exit_reasons` sorted by frequency desc (lexicographic tiebreak
for determinism), and the renderer puts the most-used first so
the dashboard reads top-down without scrolling.

NULL or empty `exit_reason` values bucket into a literal
'UNKNOWN' row — keeps the coverage gap visible per Y98's
L-Y98-UNKNOWN-VISIBLE lock.

### Bucketing

Same as Y99: by `closed_at` (the exit event happens at close).
Trades with NULL `pnl_pct` excluded (data corruption).

### Locks added in Y100

**L-Y100-EXIT-EV-COMPUTE-PURE**: `alphabot/intelligence/exit_reason_ev.py`
is pure — no DB writes, no caching, no side effects. Same lock
family as Y98 / Y99 compute-pure locks.

**L-Y100-EXIT-REASON-DISCOVERY**: The set of exit_reasons is
**discovered from data**, never enumerated in code. A new exit_reason
appearing in the trades table renders automatically. Code that
hard-codes a closed list of exit_reasons (e.g. for validation,
routing, or analytics) must instead read the live set.

**L-Y100-EDGE-CELL-RENDERER-SHARED**: The dashboard's
`renderEdgeCell` JS function is the single renderer for all
bootstrap-CI cells (Y98 edge, Y100 exits, and any future
`§11.B.*` matrix). Drops adding new matrices reuse it. Drops
changing it must verify every consumer.

### Files touched

- `alphabot/intelligence/exit_reason_ev.py` (new, ~240 LOC)
- `alphabot/brain/operator_ui/exit_reason_ev.py` (new endpoint)
- `alphabot/brain/service.py` (router wire)
- `alphabot/brain/static/dashboard/index.html` (EXITS tab markup
  + tabbar entry)
- `alphabot/brain/static/dashboard/app.css` (Y100 styling block —
  rows are exit_reasons, columns are markets; wider row labels
  to accommodate variable-length reason strings)
- `alphabot/brain/static/dashboard/app.js` (`loadExitReasonEV` +
  `renderExitReasonEV`; reuses `renderEdgeCell`)
- `tests/intelligence/test_exit_reason_ev.py` (new, 13 cases)
- `tests/brain/test_y100_exit_reason_ev_endpoint.py` (new, 5 cases)

### Test sweep

352 tests pass (was 334 after Y99). +18 net for Y100.

### Pre-deploy backup

`alphabot-2026-05-24-0809-pre-deploy.tar.gz` (49M) — used the
absolute path `/home/alphabot/scripts/alphabot_backup.sh` per
the gap noted in HANDOVER_21 §10. Working now under the agent
shell.

### What's intentionally NOT in Y100

- **No semantic colour overrides** (e.g. "STOPs green when negative
  because that's good"). The renderer keeps colour = sign always.
  The operator interprets — the matrix is descriptive, not
  prescriptive.
- **No min-n filter**. If a window has 20 rare-fire exit_reasons
  with n=1 each, all 20 render. Operator filters mentally. If
  noise becomes a problem, a `min_n=2` query param is a one-line
  add.
- **No exit_reason × regime cross-cut**. That's a §11.B.x
  candidate later. Y100 keeps it to 2D for legibility.

### Deferred / scoped out (post-Y100)

  surfaces.
- **§11.B.3 — Stop-distance EV**. How does stop-distance-in-ATR

### Y101 — Score-bucket × market EV

The "does my entry_score actually predict pnl?" question. If
Q5 (top 20% scores) reads positive-tight and Q1 reads zero or
negative, the score is doing work. If all five quintiles look
the same, the score is theatre and the strategy is selling
random entries — actionable insight.

**Global thresholds, not per-market.** The dashboard renders a
note explaining Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/Q5 cutoff values explicitly so the
operator knows what "Q5" actually means for the score range
that landed in this window. Per-market thresholds would
balance n per cell but make columns incomparable — would
destroy the central insight.

Reused Y98 helpers: `_discipline_to_market`, `_MARKET_ORDER`,
`_sample_state_for`, `_row_get`. Cells render through the
shared `renderEdgeCell` JS per L-Y100-EDGE-CELL-RENDERER-SHARED.

## §69 — Y102: §11.B.6 Hold-time bucket × market EV (2026-05-24 morning)

Fifth INTEL sub-tab. Same global-quintile pattern as Y101
applied to ``hold_seconds`` instead of ``entry_score``.

### Why hold time

Operator's strategy has an effective hold-time distribution
emerging from exit logic (signal exits, stops, time stops).
The question this surface answers:

  - **Q5 (longest 20%) positive-tight** → letting winners run
    is paying. The strategy benefits from hold time.
  - **Q1 (shortest 20%) strongly negative** → cutting too
    fast. Likely STOPs firing tight; cross-reference EXITS.
  - **Monotone trend Q1→Q5** → real signal about how long
    to hold.
  - **Flat across quintiles** → hold time isn't predictive;
    effective hold distribution is incidental.

Live-DB sanity: 654 closed trades, hold_seconds populated on
all 654 (NOT NULL by schema), range 0→435702s (mean 6239s).
Distribution heavy on 1-30min, lighter tails. Quintile
thresholds will land around 60s / 600s / 1500s / 6000s for
current data.

### Architecture (Y101 mirror)

Three-layer split identical to Y101:

1. `alphabot/intelligence/hold_time_ev.py` — pure compute,
   global quintile thresholds, dense 5×6 matrix. Reuses Y98
   helpers (`_discipline_to_market`, `_MARKET_ORDER`,
   `_sample_state_for`, `_row_get`). Percentile + bucketing
   logic intentionally duplicated from Y101 rather than
   factored to a shared util — see "Why no shared util"
   below.
2. `alphabot/brain/operator_ui/hold_time_ev.py` — PIN-gated
   endpoint using the correct `audit.record_action` API
   from day one (Y98/Y99/Y100 audit-bug still pending fix).
3. HOLD sub-tab in `#page-intel`. JS renders thresholds via
   a `fmtSec` helper that turns seconds into compact human
   labels: `45s` / `3m` / `1.5h` / `2d3h`.

### Why no shared util for the bucketing logic

I considered factoring the `_percentile` /
`_compute_quintile_thresholds` / `_bucket_for` trio into
`alphabot/intelligence/bucketing.py` since Y101 and Y102 use
near-identical code. Decided against, for now:

- Two callers isn't enough to justify a shared module — the
  duplication cost is ~40 LOC of straightforward arithmetic.
- The shared bootstrap CI + market mapping already live in
  Y98's edge_matrix.py. That's the right pattern: factor
  helpers that are stable. Bucketing maths might want to
  diverge later (weighted quintiles, different boundary
  rules) and a shared module would make divergence
  expensive.
- Rule 6 — one task per session. The duplication is fine to
  notice as backlog; refactoring it isn't this drop's job.

**Backlog item**: if a third Y10x bucketing slice lands
(score × score-and-something-else, or hold × regime), then
factor `bucketing.py`.

### Locks added in Y102

**L-Y102-HOLD-EV-COMPUTE-PURE**: same compute-pure family as
Y98 / Y99 / Y100 / Y101.

L-Y101-GLOBAL-QUINTILE-THRESHOLDS and
L-Y101-INTEL-SUBTAB-CONTAINER both implicitly apply — Y102
reuses both patterns.

Three operator-directed items shipped as two drops:

### Y103 — Audit-API fix + 7-tier magnitude colour ramp

**Audit-API fix**: carried backlog from Y101/Y102. Y98/Y99/Y100
endpoints all called the non-existent `audit.record(...)`;
function is `audit.record_action` with `success: bool`. The
try/except swallowed AttributeError so endpoints worked but no
audit rows were written for INTEL reads. Three one-line edits.
All five INTEL endpoints now write audit rows.

**Magnitude colour ramp**: operator feedback was that most
cells were "just empty grey and a few reds" — the binary
screening/proven CSS classes left BELOW_SCREENING (n<30) cells
grey regardless of point estimate magnitude. With ~654 trades
across 30 cells, most fell into BELOW_SCREENING so most of the
dashboard read as grey.

Replaced with a 7-tier `mag-*` ramp keyed on point estimate
magnitude:

  - strong-pos  ≥ +1.0%   (deep green)
  - pos         +0.3..1.0  (green)
  - mild-pos    +0.05..0.3 (mild green)
  - neutral     ±0.05      (grey)
  - mild-neg    -0.3..-.05 (orange)
  - neg         -1.0..-0.3 (red)
  - strong-neg  < -1.0%    (deep red)

§11.5 honesty preserved via:
  - `.proven` accent class adds a heavier border + soft glow
    so n≥150 cells stand out from low-n cells with the same
    colour.
  - The `.edge-cell-tag` still shows `n<30 / SCR± / ★PROV` so
    the operator never confuses "strong colour" with "proven
    edge."
  - CI range rendered alongside the point estimate.

Applies uniformly to all INTEL sub-tabs via the shared
`renderEdgeCell` (L-Y100-EDGE-CELL-RENDERER-SHARED). Single
JS edit + CSS swap.

### Y104 — §11.B.3 Stop-distance bucket × market EV

Originally noted as blocked on
`trade_features.stop_distance_atr` (0 rows). Re-investigation
showed the data is **recoverable at read time** via joins:

  - IBKR: trades ⨝ stops on `(symbol, discipline,
    entry_price ≈ match)`. stop_distance_pct =
    `(entry_price − current_stop_price) / entry_price × 100`.
  - Crypto: trades ⨝ crypto_stops same key. Uses the
    `stop_loss_pct` column directly (×100 since stored as
    fraction).

The "join at read time" choice trades coverage for shipability:

  - **Coverage**: live-DB sample showed 35% IBKR match (stops
    table is pruned over time; old trades have no stop row),
    78% crypto match, ~62% combined.
  - **Shipability**: no upstream capture drop needed, surface
    lands today, operator gets actionable answers immediately
    on the 62% covered.

The dashboard surfaces the coverage gap explicitly via a
`.stop-coverage` banner (warn-yellow if <50% match). Future
improvement (deferred): add a stop-distance column to trades
or write to trade_features at trade-close time so 100% of
NEW trades have it without join. Not blocking; ship now.

## §71 — Y105: §11.B.7 Entry-session × market EV (2026-05-24 morning)

Seventh INTEL sub-tab. Answers "when does the desk make
money?" with per-trade pnl_pct + §11.5 CIs, complementing the
descriptive Y99 PNL hour-heatmap (which sums realised dollars
and is biased by trade volume).

### Why fixed session buckets, not quintiles

Y101 / Y102 / Y104 used global quintiles for bucketing. Y105
breaks the pattern intentionally and uses **fixed UTC session
buckets**:

  - ASIA   00:00 – 07:00 UTC
  - LON    07:00 – 12:30 UTC
  - US-AM  12:30 – 17:00 UTC
  - US-PM  17:00 – 21:00 UTC
  - LATE   21:00 – 24:00 UTC

Rationale:

  - Hour-of-day has natural semantic structure. The operator
    thinks in sessions ("did US-AM pay?"), not in "lowest 20%
    of opened_at hour values".
  - Quintile boundaries on opened_at hour would shift session-
    to-session as trade volume rotates between hours. Cells
    wouldn't be comparable across windows.
  - Fixed buckets give stable cells whose semantics don't
    drift.

This was predicted in DECISIONS §69's deferred bucketing.py
extraction discussion — "the next slice might want different
boundary semantics". It did. Defer once more.

### Bucketing key

opened_at (decision time), NOT closed_at.

Y99/Y100/Y101/Y102 bucket by closed_at because pnl is realised
at close. Y105 asks "when was the trade taken?" — so
opened_at is the right key. The window bound stays on opened_at
too for consistency.

### Locks

No new lock. The fixed-bucket decision is captured in this
DECISIONS entry; the existing L-Y101-INTEL-SUBTAB-CONTAINER
and L-Y100-EDGE-CELL-RENDERER-SHARED both apply.

The §11.B intelligence layer feels structurally complete.

### Y108 — §11.A.1 Signal funnel

First §11.A signal-side surface. New lens: SIGNALS (what the
strategy considered) vs TRADES (what shipped). Per market:
total signals + BUY count/rate + HOLD count/rate +
above-threshold count/rate. Descriptive volume stats — no
bootstrap CI (counts speak at 115k signals/day).

Operator value: BUY rate trending = early-warning indicator for
EDGE drift. Above-threshold rate calibrates the score gate
(near 0 = too tight; near 1 = theatre).

Default window 7d — signals table is high-volume; 30d would
scan ~3.4M rows on each request.

### Y109 — §11.D.1 Execution slippage

Operator question: "are we analysing execution? to see what
our slippage is?" — yes, smart addition.

Two flavours:
  - Entry slippage = (entry_price - price_at_signal) / signal × 100.
    Joined trades⨝signals via entry_signal_id. ~95% coverage live.
  - Exit slippage = (stop_price - exit_price) / stop_price × 100.
    STOP_LOSS / STOP / TRAIL_STOP exits only. Joined trades⨝stops
    or trades⨝crypto_stops.

Per market: bootstrap CI on the slippage values + mean + median
+ max_abs (worst single trade). Plus worst-10 leaderboards for
both entry and exit so the operator can drill to specific
symbols.

Defensive sanity gate: |slippage| > 20% dropped as data quality
— FTSE pence/pound scaling glitches observed live (ULVR -98%).

## §73 — Y117 + Y118 + Y119 + Y120: HK + Japan finish (2026-05-24 evening)

Operator: "finish everything for HK and Japan so I just need to
turn on the permissions and we go." Y115/Y116 (2026-05-23) had
shipped the dormant strategy classes, venue/currency enums, and
session-phase wiring. Four remaining gaps to close before HKEX +
TSE could trade with one flag flip:

### Y117 — Board-lot sizing

HK and Japan trade in 100-share lots (HSI/HKEx mainboard
standard; TSE 単元株 reduced 1000→100 in 2018). Pre-Y117 the
sizer floored to integer shares but didn't round to lot
boundaries — a 47-share size would submit and be rejected at
the exchange, or worse silently amended.

- `decide_entry()` accepts `lot_size: int = 1` (default no-op).
- Rounds `target_qty` and `max_qty` DOWN to nearest lot AFTER
  the existing `math.floor`. Non-fractional disciplines only —
  crypto passthrough unaffected.
- Strategy classes declare `_LOT_SIZE: ClassVar[int]` —
  `DayTradeHKEXStrategy._LOT_SIZE = 100`,
  `DayTradeTSEStrategy._LOT_SIZE = 100`, default 1 elsewhere.

### Y118 — HKEx Shanghai-proxy regime override

HK names track Shanghai via Stock Connect; a sharp mainland
drawdown drags the HK tape regardless of local catalysts. Y118
adds a per-market regime override that clamps HKEX FULL →
CAUTIOUS when the Shanghai proxy is down > 1% intraday.

- Proxy: `ASHR` (NYSE-listed Xtrackers Harvest CSI 300 ETF).
  US-equity routing — works today, doesn't need HKEx/SSE perms.
- Architecture: `refresh_market_regime` gains a
  `force_cautious_check: ForceCautiousCheck | None` predicate
  parameter; `regime_refresh_loop` accepts a per-market
  `force_cautious_checks: dict[str, ForceCautiousCheck]` map.
- Override only ever DOWNGRADES FULL → CAUTIOUS — never lifts
  DEFENSIVE into a better state. Implemented inside
  `compute_regime_state` (existing `force_cautious` plumbing).
- Fail-soft: predicate raises → swallowed, no override fires.
- Daemon wires the override when DAYTRADE_HKEX_ENABLED.

### Y119 — TSE USD/JPY regime override

TSE is dominated by exporters whose earnings swing on FX; a
sharp yen move destabilises the tape both directions
(yen-strength compresses earnings, yen-weakness triggers BoJ
intervention noise). Y119 mirrors Y118 with the symmetric
`tse_usdjpy_override_fires(usdjpy_bars)` at the 0.5% threshold.

The override compute function ships ready to wire. The daemon
side stays unwired pending IBKR CASH-forex bar routing in
`market_data_daemon` (current router has equity-only get_bars).
That work pairs with the DAYTRADE_TSE_ENABLED flip — both
require IBKR JPY perms.

### Y120 — Per-currency cap split (HKD + JPY)

`DAYTRADE_HKEX_CAP_PCT = 6%` and `DAYTRADE_TSE_CAP_PCT = 6%`,
mirrored in `shared/config.py` and `strategy/config.py`. New
disciplines added to `SizingConfig.discipline_cap_pct()`
dispatch.

**Side-fix found mid-build**: `_DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES`
frozenset in `_sizing.py` listed only the original four
disciplines. `hkex_daytrade` / `tse_daytrade` weren't members —
held positions in those disciplines were silently filtered out
of every daytrade gate (engine cap, per-discipline cap, gross-
deployed). Y120 adds them to the set. Without this fix the
6% cap could never bind.

CAPS_AND_LIMITS.md §1.1 updated: sum is 52% (was 40%, still
well above the 25% engine cap which remains binding).

### Architectural locks

- **L-Y117-LOT-SIZE-AFTER-FLOOR**: lot-size rounding happens
  AFTER `math.floor`, so the lot-down rounding can never inflate
  a smaller integer back up.
- **L-Y118-OVERRIDE-DOWNGRADE-ONLY**: regime overrides may only
  clamp FULL → CAUTIOUS. They cannot rescue a DEFENSIVE market
  nor demote a CAUTIOUS one further.
- **L-Y118-OVERRIDE-FAILS-SOFT**: a raising / hung
  force_cautious_check is swallowed and treated as no-override.
  Override fetch failure must never break the regime refresh.
- **L-Y120-DAYTRADE-DISCIPLINES-INCLUDES-HKEX-TSE**: the
  `_DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES` set is the single source of truth for
  "what counts as a daytrade position" in the sizing chain. When
  adding a new daytrade venue, registration here is mandatory.

## §74 — Y121 + Y122 + Y123: HK + Japan audit follow-up (2026-05-24 evening)

After Y117–Y120 (§73) shipped, a multi-agent audit (three parallel
agents: IBKR perms via web search; brackets/orders/stops code-side;
risk/sizing/dashboards code-side) found that the "one operator flag
flip away" claim in §73 was **wrong**. The strategy/sizing/regime
layers Y115–Y120 added were in place, but the broker integration
layer had five hard gaps and FTSE/ASX were running with a live DST
bug in production. Y121–Y123 close all of it.

This entry corrects the §73 claim and records the actual completion.

### Y121 — DST-aware session-close (fixes LIVE FTSE/ASX bug)

`daytrade_stop_runner._SESSION_CLOSE_UTC` was a hand-maintained
`dict[str, time]` of UTC times. Wrong half the year:

- FTSE: `time(16, 30)` matched London-GMT, but during BST (now) the
  real UTC close is 15:30. EOD-flatten fired 60 min AFTER real close.
- ASX: `time(5, 0)` matched Sydney-AEDT, but during AEST (May–Sep,
  now) the real UTC close is 06:00. EOD-flatten fired 70 min BEFORE
  real close, prematurely flattening winning positions.

Y121 refactored to `_SESSION_CLOSE: dict[str, MarketSession]` reading
the canonical sessions from `shared/time.py` and converting via
`zoneinfo`. DST handled by OS tzdata; HKEX (no DST, 16:00 HKT) and
TSE (no DST, 15:30 JST — JPX extended close on 2024-11-05) added in
the same drop.

Also fixed `session_phase._MARKET_HOURS["TSE"]` from 15:00 → 15:30
JST (matching the canonical `shared/time.py::TSE_AFTERNOON`), updated
`tse.py::session_end_flat_utc` from "05:55" → "06:25", and backfilled
`tests/test_shared/test_types.py::test_disciplines_count` from 15 →
17 (Y115 had added HKEX_DAYTRADE + TSE_DAYTRADE without updating the
count — CLAUDE.md §3 same-drop rule, paid in Y121).

19 new tests covering every market × DST-state. Deployed live to
`alphabot-strategy-daytrade` 2026-05-24 15:37 UTC; FTSE now flattens
at 15:30 UTC and ASX at 06:00 UTC Monday (verified post-restart).

### Y122 — HKEX/TSE broker integration (the 5 audit blockers)

Five silent-failure modes in the broker layer that would have made
every HKEX/TSE entry attempt fail in a different non-obvious way:

- **B1** `shared/ticks.py` — no tick table for `(SEHK, HKD)` or
  `(TSEJ, JPY)`. First bracket → `round_to_tick(...)` → ValueError.
  Y122 adds the conservative-coarse tables (HKEX 11 bands per the
  HKEX Cash Market Rules; TSEJ 9 bands using the non-TOPIX 100
  variant which is coarser → always IBKR-accepted).
- **B2** `multi_broker_proxy.DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINE_ROUTING` —
  `hkex_daytrade`/`tse_daytrade` not mapped → `list_positions` filter
  drops them → stop runner never sees the positions, no ratchet, no
  time-stop, no EOD flatten.
- **B3** `broker/main.py::market_open_by_exchange` — venue tuple
  lacked `"SEHK"`/`"TSEJ"` → `risk.gate_market_open` returned False
  for every HKEX/TSE order even when the venues were open.
- **B5** `broker/order_types._DISCIPLINE_TO_EQUITY_VENUES_CURRENCY`
  — no HKEX/TSE entries → `check_instrument_matches_discipline`
  early-returned on "unknown discipline", silently bypassing the
  venue/currency coherence guard.

B4 (no EOD flatten for HKEX/TSE) was already closed by Y121.

34 new tests including every band of both tick tables + bracket-
construction smoke tests + coherence-check round-trips. Broker
restart **approval-gated** (operator's call) to pick up B3's venue
tuple change.

### Y123 — Visibility + seeding + per-symbol lot override

The "should-fix" findings:

- `pool_config.py SESSION_WINDOWS + MARKET_TZ` extended for hkex +
  tse. Pre-Y123 `is_market_in_session("hkex"/"tse")` returned False
  unconditionally — pool builder treated both venues as never-open.
- Dashboard 6-tuple: `routes_daytrade_terminal._DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES`
  +  `_DISCIPLINE_TO_MARKET`, all 7 SQL IN-clauses upgraded from 4 →
  6 placeholders, `daytrade_terminal.js DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES` Set
  extended, `holdingsGroup.js` DISCIPLINE_CAPS/LABELS/GROUP_ORDER
  extended. HKEX/TSE rows now flow into every aggregate query +

- New module `alphabot/strategy/lot_size_lookup.py` reads
  `universe_symbols.lot_size` with a process-wide cache.
  `DayTradeStrategyBase._resolve_lot_size()` uses per-symbol override
  if present, class default otherwise. HKEX board lots are 50–100,000
  per stock (Tencent 100, China Mobile 500, Sinopec 2000) so a single

- `scripts/seed_hkex_tse_universe.py` — 20 HKEX + 20 TSE liquids

to pick up `pool_config` + lot lookup.

### Architectural locks (3 new)

- **L-Y121-DST-VIA-ZONEINFO** — session-close lookups are

The Y117–Y120 ship note in §73 said the system was "one operator

## §75 — Y124 + Y125: dashboard visibility tuning (2026-05-24 night)

Two operator-visibility fixes from a session where the operator
saw four BUY signals for EDEN with no trade and no idea why, plus
saw a TSE symbol in the scanner during Tokyo night. Both rooted
in the dashboard reading from sources that didn't carry the data.

### Y124 — Activity stream BLOCKED rows + scanner open-market filter

**Activity stream**: `_read_activity_from_truth` previously sourced
ENTRY events from `orders ⨝ fills` and EXIT from `trades`. A BUY
signal that hit `submit_order` and got rejected at the broker
risk pipeline (per_symbol_daily_cap, cooldown, gate_valid_symbol,
sizing-chain skip, etc.) produces a row in `rejections` but
nothing in `orders`/`fills`/`trades` — invisible to the activity
feed. Operator saw N BUY signals, zero trades, zero feed rows.

Y124 adds a fourth event type `BLOCKED`: latest rejection per
`(symbol, gate_name)` over the 90-min window, with occurrence
count and the full rejection reason in the row title= for hover
detail. Distinct orange "BLOCK" chip vs the gold "NEAR" chip
(NEAR = HOLD signal one gate short; BLOCK = BUY signal refused
at the broker). Grouped so a single gate failing 50× collapses
to one row "BLOCK EDENUSDT · per_symbol_daily_cap ×50".

Real production hit on Y124 ship: EDEN had 174 hits on
per_symbol_daily_cap visible in the panel — the operator could
finally see what was happening.

**Scanner sidebar**: pre-Y124 the panel surfaced any market's
candidates from `ranked_candidates`. Operator complaint: "showing
TSE something or other, but i dont know what it means and it
cant be TSE as TSE is not open."

Y124 adds a server-side filter to markets where
`is_market_in_session(market, now_utc) is True`. Crypto always
included (24/7 Binance). The panel head got a new subtitle
`open: US · Crypto` (etc.) showing the operator what's
contributing in real time. Empty-state distinguishes
"no markets in session" from "no candidates from open markets".

### Y125 — Crypto candidates from signals table

Y124 closed the operator's "TSE shouldn't show" complaint but
opened a secondary gap: on weekends and every off-hours stretch
(when US/FTSE/ASX/HKEX/TSE are all closed), the panel showed
empty. Crypto IS being scanned 24/7 (60-ish USDT pairs every 30s)
but doesn't flow through the snapshot engine (tvscreener isn't
reliable for crypto), so `ranked_candidates` has no crypto rows.

Y125 adds a second source: the live `signals` table. Query reads
the last 15 min of `action='BUY'` signals for `crypto_daytrade`,
groups by symbol, takes max(score) and count(*) per symbol. The
tabs differentiate naturally:

- `most_active` → max(score) DESC (best per-symbol signal recently)
- `high_vol` → COUNT(*) DESC (proxy for "scanner keeps re-signaling
  this" — RVOL isn't computed crypto-side)
- `gappers` → max(score) DESC fallback (no gap_pct equivalent)

Equity and crypto rows merge in the same response list and re-sort
by the tab's primary key. Crypto rows carry `market='crypto'` so
the badge + colour swatch render correctly. Score scales are
compatible (0-10 both sides).

### Architectural locks (2 new)

- **L-Y124-ACTIVITY-BLOCKED-FROM-REJECTIONS** — the activity
  stream's BLOCKED rows MUST source from the `rejections` table,
  not from synthesised log scraping. Rejection rows are the
  durable record (Drop 2 lesson — pre-Drop-2 these were silently
  lost).
- **L-Y125-CRYPTO-CANDIDATES-FROM-SIGNALS** — crypto scanner
  rows source from `signals` (live, score-aware) rather than
  `pool_snapshots` (universe-only, no scoring). When/if the
  snapshot engine ever emits crypto into `ranked_candidates`,
  remove the dual-source path in favour of the unified one.

## §76 — Y126: BinanceScanner filters to broker-tradeable symbols (2026-05-24 night)

Follow-up to Y124's BLOCKED-rows panel, which made a class of bug
visible: UTKUSDT and GENIUSUSDT generating 174 BUY signals each in
a 90-min window, every one of them rejected at the broker by
`gate_valid_symbol` with "symbol not found in Binance exchange info".
The strategy daemon was wasting cycles on symbols the broker would
never accept.

### Root cause

Paper-mode runs are an environment mismatch by design:

- **Scanner** hits Binance **MAINNET** (`api.binance.com`) for
  /ticker/24hr — chosen because mainnet has the rich universe (~2000
  USDT pairs) plus reliable 24h volume history, both needed for the
  liquid / volatility / unusual slice ranking.
- **Broker** runs Binance **TESTNET** (`testnet.binance.vision`) for
  paper orders — testnet has only ~432 USDT pairs and a different
  status table. Several mainnet-tradeable symbols (GENIUSUSDT) simply
  don't exist on testnet; others (UTKUSDT) are mainnet `status=BREAK`
  (paused) and likewise absent from testnet's tradeable list.

The two surfaces never compared notes. Scanner picked top-volume
symbols from mainnet, persisted them to `pool_snapshots`, strategy
daemon read /pool and emitted BUY signals, broker rejected every
one at gate_valid_symbol — and re-rejected on the next 30s cycle.

### Y126 — cross-check at the scanner

- `BinanceScanner.__init__` gains a `tradeable_symbols:
  frozenset[str] | None = None` kwarg. `None` is back-compat (no
  filter, pre-Y126 behaviour); a set drops anything not in it.
- New `refresh_tradeable_symbols(exchange_info_url) -> int` method:
  fetches `/exchangeInfo` from the given URL, keeps only symbols
  with `status == "TRADING"` and a USDT quote, returns the set
  size. Fail-soft on HTTP errors — preserves the previous set
  rather than rotating to "no filter" (which would re-introduce the
  bug exactly when the broker's least healthy).
- `PoolDiscovery._refresh_crypto_pool` now calls
  `refresh_tradeable_symbols` before each `fetch_three_slices`,
  hitting `testnet.binance.vision` when `settings.BINANCE_TESTNET=
  true`, `api.binance.com` otherwise. The bot learns the broker's
  actual universe before every ranking pass.

The filter applies inside `_fetch_tickers_24hr` so all three slices
(liquid / volatility / unusual) inherit it. Any symbol that survives
also clears the existing `is_excluded_crypto_symbol` (stablecoin /
wrapped / leveraged-token) guard.

### Why intersect at the scanner, not at the broker

The broker already rejects un-tradeable symbols at gate_valid_symbol
— that's the safety net. But the *scanner* is the upstream choice
point. If we wait for the broker to reject, the strategy still does
the work (gate evaluation, signal write, scan-context blob, audit
row, rejection row). Y124 telemetry showed 174 such cycles per
symbol per 90 min — multiply by 2 spam symbols + a few cycles per
minute and it's 4-6× the broker's load just on rejected paths.
Filtering at the scanner moves the cutoff one stage upstream:
nothing gets emitted, nothing gets evaluated, nothing gets logged.

### Architectural lock

- **L-Y126-SCANNER-INTERSECTS-BROKER-UNIVERSE** — in any mode where
  the scanner's data source and the broker's order destination are
  different Binance environments (paper-mode default), the scanner
  MUST intersect its candidate set with the broker's tradeable
  symbols before persisting. The intersection is the only universe
  the strategy daemon should see.

### Live verification

Market-data daemon restart at 17:35 UTC. First post-restart crypto
refresh:

  binance_scanner: refreshed tradeable_symbols from
    https://testnet.binance.vision → 432 symbols
  binance_scanner: slices ready — liquid=58 volatility=58 unusual=58
  pool_discovery: wrote pool_snapshot id=168 for crypto
    (total=58, reason=daemon_boot)

Verified neither UTKUSDT nor GENIUSUSDT are in the snapshot id=168;
EDENUSDT (genuinely tradeable on testnet) remains. Strategy daemon
restarted at 17:35 UTC; 30 s later, zero BUY signals for UTK/GENIUS
in the `signals` table, zero new rejections in the `rejections`
table. The scanner sidebar's "last 15 min signals" window cleared
the stale UTK/GENIUS entries naturally over the next quarter-hour.

```
alphabot/market_data_daemon/universe_discovery.py
tests/test_market_data/test_drop_y126_scanner_tradeable_filter.py  (new)
```

8 new tests, all passing. No DB migration. Production-safe in live

and intersects with itself, which collapses to the existing

## §77 — Y127: exit families + MASTER all-9 surfaces + FILL prominence (2026-05-24 night)

Bundles three audit-driven follow-ups (the original Y127/Y128/Y129
scoped from the §75 INTEL audit) plus an operator visibility ask
into one drop.

### Y127 — Canonical EXIT_REASON_FAMILIES map

Closes the §75 latent bug: ``master_digest._analyse_exits`` matched
literal strings ``"STOP"`` / ``"time_stop"`` / ``"stale_progress"``
against ``c.exit_reason`` while the live trades table contains
``STOP_LOSS`` / ``DAYTRADE_TIME_STOP`` / ``DAYTRADE_SOFT_CAP_ROTATION``
/ ``TAKE_PROFIT`` / ``SIGNAL_SELL`` / ``RECONCILED``. Every "STOPs
too tight" or "time-stops bleeding" recommendation could silently
never fire. Currently dormant because all categories are n<30;
becomes a silent miss the moment volume crosses 30.

The fix is a canonical FAMILY map in ``exit_reason_ev.py``:

```python
EXIT_REASON_FAMILIES: dict[str, str] = {
    "STOP_LOSS": "STOP", "DAYTRADE_STOP_LOSS": "STOP", ...
    "TAKE_PROFIT": "PROFIT_TARGET", "DAYTRADE_TAKE_PROFIT": "PROFIT_TARGET",
    "SIGNAL_SELL": "SIGNAL_EXIT", "STRATEGY_EXIT": "SIGNAL_EXIT",
    "DAYTRADE_TIME_STOP": "TIME_STOP", "TIME_STOP": "TIME_STOP",
    "DAYTRADE_SOFT_CAP_ROTATION": "ROTATION", ...
    "RECONCILED": "RECONCILED",  # data-quality bucket, not a real exit kind
}
def family_for(raw: str) -> str: ...
```

``_analyse_exits`` aggregates cells by family with sample-weighted
means + family-level thresholds. STOP family avg > -0.3% over n≥30
→ "stops too tight" critical rec; SIGNAL_EXIT family avg < 0 over
n≥30 → "strategy exits losing money" critical rec; UNKNOWN family
present at any volume → parity-drift bullet (so a new raw label
introduced by the broker is operator-visible immediately).

**Parity test** in tests/intelligence/test_drop_y127_*.py asserts
every distinct value in live trades.exit_reason maps to a non-UNKNOWN
family — catches the next §2 "parallel-strings" hazard at the
moment of write, not at the moment of "why didn't the rec fire?"

### Y128 — MASTER all 9 INTEL surfaces

Closes the §75 docstring-vs-reality drift. Pre-Y128 the digest
docstring claimed "synthesises 9 surfaces" but only 7 analyser
functions existed (FUNNEL and SLIP missing). All 9 now wired.

- ``_analyse_funnel`` — gate-theatre detection (above_threshold_rate
  > 0.99 over 1000+ signals → attention); fill-collapse detection
  (>30 BUY signals + 0 fills → critical with explicit pointer to
  per_symbol_daily_cap / cooldown / gate_valid_symbol family of
  causes); per-market silent on truly empty (flag-off-disciplined).
- ``_analyse_slippage`` — entry slippage > +50 bps avg (n≥30) →
  paying premium attention rec; exit slippage > +50 bps avg on
  STOP exits → gap-through stops attention rec; entry-coverage <
  80% over n≥30 → diagnostic bullet (the very condition Y109
  surfaces and Y129 explains).

Both analysers fail-soft via the existing per-analyser try/except
in ``compute_master_digest`` — exceptions yield a degraded
severity='info' insight rather than collapsing the digest.

### Y127 — FILL prominence

Operator framing: *"FILL is the big one we celebrate. BUY signals
are positive but they can be ignored. FILL should be the bright
green button on the activity stream. and the funnel needs FILL
added."*

Two surfaces:

**Activity stream (port 8080 daytrade-terminal):** ENTRY events
ARE fills — pre-Y127 they rendered as a soft-blue "BUY" chip. Y127
renames the chip to "FILL" and styles it as the celebration row:
saturated green (.50 alpha) + 1px brighter-green border + 8px
green glow + bold + tracked-out letter-spacing. Visually distinct
from .act-sold-win (closed-profit exit, also greenish) so the
operator's eye lands on the fresh fill without animation.

The legacy .act-chip.act-buy CSS class is kept for any cached
client still running pre-Y127 JS (returning browser hasn't reloaded)
— the rename is JS-side only, so a stale cached browser just sees
the old blue chip until reload.

**Brain dashboard FUNNEL (port 8000):** ``FunnelRow`` gains
``filled_count`` + ``fill_rate``. ``compute_signal_funnel`` reads
``orders WHERE status='FILLED' AND side='BUY'`` in the window and
folds by ``_discipline_to_market``. The FUNNEL sub-tab gets a third
bar layer — above-gate teal (back) → BUY soft-blue (mid) → FILL
bright-green-glow (front). FILL bar width is filled_count /
total_signals so the visual scales naturally; fill_rate (% of BUYs
that filled) renders alongside the count for the operator's
celebration metric.

Live data on ship (Sunday off-hours, crypto-only): CRYPTO row
shows buy=10,411 / filled=578 / fill_rate=5.55%. That's the number
the operator actually wants to track — not "we found a signal"
but "the order made it to the book."

### Y129 — Orphan entry_signal_id forensic

Investigation result: NOT a retention bug. The 4 orphan IDs
(3706301, 3757314, 3757918, 3758608) are an artifact of the
2026-05-24 11:45 UTC manual DB cleanse (MASTER_TODO §4 entry
"Phase 2: wiped 1.14M pre-V4 signals"). The "pre-V4" predicate
was too aggressive — it swept signals referenced by V4-era trades
that opened the weekend before the cleanse but had their entry
signals among the wiped set. Permanent data loss; cannot be
recovered from the live DB.

New diagnostic helper ``find_orphan_signal_links(conn)`` in
``signal_funnel.py``. Returns the list of (trade_id, entry_signal_id,
symbol, discipline, opened_at) tuples whose entry_signal_id no
longer resolves. No auto-repair — the signals are gone — but a
future cleanse can check before, not after.

The Y109 docstring claim "95% live entry-slip coverage" is now
known to be permanently ~87% on the current DB. The new
``_analyse_slippage`` MASTER analyser surfaces the coverage gap
as a bullet whenever total_trades_in_window ≥ 30, so the operator
sees the artifact without having to remember it.

### Architectural locks (4 new)

- **L-Y127-EXIT-REASON-FAMILY-MAP** — every surface that reasons
  about "what kind of exit was this" reads through
  ``exit_reason_ev.family_for``. The raw exit_reason column stays
  the operator-visible label; family is the synthesis-only key.
- **L-Y127-EXIT-FAMILY-PARITY** — the EXIT_REASON_FAMILIES map MUST
  cover every distinct value in live trades.exit_reason. The Y127
  parity test asserts it; CI flags drift at write time.
- **L-Y128-MASTER-COVERS-ALL-INTEL-SURFACES** — when a new §11
  surface ships, MASTER gets a paired ``_analyse_<surface>``
  function in the same drop. The dispatch list and docstring
  count are the single source of truth.
- **L-Y127-FILL-IS-THE-CELEBRATION-METRIC** — the activity stream's
  ENTRY event renders as "FILL" (not "BUY"). The FUNNEL surface
  shows signal → BUY → FILL as a three-stage funnel. BUY count is
  a leading indicator; FILL count is the realised outcome and the
  operator's primary attention target.

## §78. Daytrade-terminal reshape arc — Y128 → Y134 (2026-05-24 night → 2026-05-25)

A continuous arc of frontend + market-data work driven by the
operator review: "the dashboards are great, but the activity stream
isn't doing it for me. and there's heaps of dead screen space."
Eleven drops, all shipped, ending at Y134 (this commit). Each drop
is small; the value is in the sequence.

**Numbering collision note:** §77 (above) used Y128 + Y129 for the
brain/MASTER work. The git-history Y128 + Y129 in this section are
the frontend/feed-engine work — same numbers, different branches.
The git log is the source of truth; this section indexes by it.

### Y128 — UniverseCoordinator reads ranked_candidates (commit `f9ae188`)

Pre-Y128 the market-data daemon's UniverseCoordinator built the
streaming pool from a stale per-market shortlist that lagged the
Y112 ranked_candidates table by 30+ minutes. Y128 switches the
coordinator to read ranked_candidates directly so the stream
reflects the latest snapshot promotion within seconds.

### Y128 hotfix — KeyError 'hkex' in `_refresh_equity_pool` (commit `5358625`)

Y123 added hkex/tse to SESSION_WINDOWS but never to
EQUITY_SCAN_CONFIG. When HKEX entered session at 01:15 UTC on
2026-05-24, `_refresh_equity_pool('hkex')` did
`EQUITY_SCAN_CONFIG[market]` → KeyError → daemon crashed 5 times →
systemd restart-limit-hit. Fix: `.get(market)` + early-return when
the market has no scan config. Recorded as a §2 don't-repeat row:
"when you add a market key to one config, search for every other
config it must also live in."

### Y129 — Feed Engine reshape: SCANNED → PROMOTED → STREAMING + heat glow (commit `6e2e154`)

Operator ask: *"i want the feed engine to show me the following
per market: last pool snapshot — how many minutes ago. how many
tickers snapshotted. how many promoted. how many streaming right
now. and if there are 3 open markets each market should be heat
mapped with a subtle orange red glow if its running hot and
dominating the stream."* Y129 builds the funnel into each
per-market cell, plus the heat-glow class (`.feed-cell.hot`) when
that market holds >40% of the streaming budget.

### Y129 fix — `promoted` source corrected to ranked_candidates (commit `e107898`)

Initial Y129 read `snapshot_runs.promoted_count`, a dead Y50a
tier-2 metric never populated post-Y112. Live showed `promoted=0`
for every equity market. Y129-fix reads
`COUNT(*) FROM ranked_candidates WHERE market = ?` instead.
Operator-spotted.

### Y131 — HKEX live-evaluation mode (commit `c46d8b6`)

Operator ask: *"can we liven up the HK streaming and evaluating?
that's on our side? i want to see it working. it wont trade
that's fine."* Y131 wires HKEX through the same scan → promote →
stream loop as the other equity markets, with trading still gated
off (no broker-side execution path live for SEHK). The dashboard
shows HK promoting + streaming when the session is open.

### Y131.1 — share denominator: streaming / BUDGET (commit `89dc1cc`)

Operator-caught maths bug: *"it says 64% of stream though for 96
streaming. not sure about that maths? our stream is 200 so should
be 48% no?"* Pre-Y131.1 the share computed
`streaming / sum(streaming_across_all_markets)`; Y131.1 fixes it
to `streaming / EQUITY_BUDGET_FULL` (or CRYPTO_BUDGET for crypto)
so the % is "% of the actual budget", not "% of currently-active".

### Y131.2 — held-position attribution + remove stale lse→ftse rename (commit `6c86a19`)

Two related fixes:

1. **Attribution gap** — held positions weren't counted toward the
   streaming total of their market because the held-symbol fallback
   resolved to discipline_market rather than the universe_symbols
   row's actual market. Y131.2 reads the market via
   `universe_symbols` then falls back to `discipline_market`.
2. **lse→ftse rename** — pre-existing dead code converted
   ranked_candidates' "lse" market label to "ftse" inside the
   stream-status path, but the dashboard's `_MARKETS` map uses
   "lse", so streaming counts for LSE were always zero. Removed
   the rename.

### Y132 — exchange holiday calendar (commit `66eef90`)

Operator ask: *"do the holiday calendar."* New
`alphabot/shared/exchange_holidays.py` with high-confidence 2026
holiday lists for US/LSE/ASX, plus deliberately-incomplete TODO
stubs for SEHK and TSEJ. `is_holiday(exchange, when)` helper.
`ANNUAL_REVIEW = 2026` sentinel forces an explicit refresh each
year (next: 2027 cutover). One near-miss in flight — listed SEHK
2026-05-25 as Buddha's Birthday (wrong; that's ~24 April 2026),
fixed before push.

### Y132.1 — always show "% of budget" in Feed Engine (commit `a36ab9a`)

Operator-spotted regression: *"whatever you did removed the %
streaming thing on the feed engine we were just talking about,
please reinstate."* Pre-Y132.1 the % rendered only when
`isHot = share > 0.40`, so it vanished as soon as markets closed.
Y132.1 always shows the %, gates only the orange-red glow on the
threshold.

### Y133 — 5-column horizontal layout (commit `7f2cdac`)

Operator ask: *"reorganise all the windows to stack horizontally?
so they are long vertical windows? 5 of them left to right.
Holding, Feed engine, activity stream, recent trades and then
SCANNER."* The first attempt got proportions wrong (operator:
*"you have holding and recent trades stacked thinly on the left
and feed engine and scanner in the middle HUGE just showing
black space. i want them all equally sized."*) Final: explicit
**20fr / 15fr / 20fr / 25fr / 20fr** grid via
`grid-template-columns: minmax(0, …fr)`. Mobile (max-width
720px) collapses back to a single vertical stack.

### Y134 — tappable rows (this commit)

Operator ask: *"in V3 and V2 dashboards we made the lines tappable
and it would bring up the other information. principal visible
line shows TIME, TICKER, HELD, P&L % green or red. then you tap
it and it has exit reason, position $, P&L $ and any other things.
all lines in all scanners should be tappable and they bring up a
little line underneath with more information."*

Y134 introduces a single `.tap-row` / `.tap-primary` / `.tap-detail`
primitive used by **four** panels — Holding, Activity Stream,
Recent Trades, Scanner. Feed Engine deliberately stays non-tap
(operator confirmed: *"feed engine no tap"*). Each panel has its
own grid-template-columns on `.tap-primary.<panel>-primary` so
the column edges line up with the header row; tap toggles
`[data-expanded]` and a CSS rule reveals `.tap-detail` under the
primary. No JS animation — pure CSS via the data attribute.

**Per-panel layouts:**

| Panel          | Primary (always visible)              | Detail (on tap)                                                       |
|----------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Holding        | SYM · qty · $unreal · ±%              | market · entry $ · current $ · stop $ (dist) · TP $ · held · disc     |
| Activity       | TIME · TICKER · CHIP · P&L %          | price · score/qty/gate/reason · description                            |
| Recent Trades  | TIME · SYM · HELD · P&L %             | exit reason · P&L $ · entry $ · exit $ · position $ · market · disc   |
| Scanner        | rank · ●held? · SYM · MKT · score     | rvol · atr% · gap% · price · last-scan-age                            |

**Architectural lock added:**

- **L-Y134-TAPPABLE-ROW-PRIMITIVE** — list-style panels on the
  daytrade terminal use the `.tap-row` primitive. New list panels
  define a per-panel `.tap-primary.<panel>-primary` grid template
  and call `tappableRow(primaryClass, primaryChildren, detailPairs)`
  from `daytrade_terminal.js`. The primitive is the single source
  of truth for the disclosure/expand pattern; per-panel CSS owns
  column widths.

## §80. Y135.x cascade — activity-stream visibility + holiday gate + Desk Stats (2026-05-25)

Four hotfix/incremental drops landed on top of Y135 the same day,
each driven by an operator session-of-use review. All committed
this afternoon. Y136 (global stream allocation) coded but still
uncommitted; commits tomorrow after FTSE opens at 06:45 UTC.

### Y135.1 hotfix — NEAR rows surface + LED `gate_states` populated
*(commit `ca4b241`)*

Two real bugs surfaced after Y135 shipped:

1. **Threshold + window too tight.** Y110d's NEAR query wanted
   exactly `gates_passed = gates_total - 1` within a 90-minute
   window AND `action='HOLD'`. Live V4 data is `action='BUY'` at
   `gates_passed=3` of 5 (most signals fail rvol + regime under the
   current data). Result: 274 BUY-at-3/5 signals from this morning's
   crypto cycles were completely invisible to the activity stream.
   Y135.1 relaxed both knobs:

     - Window: 90 min → 240 min
     - Threshold: `=total-1` → `≥total-2`
     - Removed `action='HOLD'` filter (V4 emits BUY-action signals
       that never reach submit_order when gates are short; they
       have no FILL/BLOCKED representation elsewhere)
     - Added `gates_passed < gates_total` to avoid double-counting
       with the ENTRY/FILL path

2. **`gate_states` JOIN was broken on the wrong column name.** Y135
   selected `name` and filtered `name IN (...)` against
   `signal_gates`. The actual column is `gate_name`. Result: every
   NEAR row's `gate_states` dict was silently empty since Y135
   shipped a few hours earlier → LED row fell through to the
   muted-grey default → operator saw 4 grey dots on every NEAR row
   instead of the real per-gate pass/fail. Classic CLAUDE.md §2
   schema mistake — fixed by reading the column.

Live verification: `/api/activity?limit=120` returned 20 NEAR
events with `gate_states` populated; ERAUSDT 3/5 rendered as

*(commit `5b656b3`, combined with Y135.3m phone polish)*

**Concern 1 (holiday gate).** Operator: *"why is it scanning ftse,
public holiday in london today."* Diagnosis: Y132 added the holiday
calendar AND wired `exchange_status()` to short-circuit CLOSED on
holidays, but **`is_exchange_open()` was left as time-of-day-only**.
The strategy daemon's cycle gate calls through `market_hours.is_market_open`
→ `shared.time.is_exchange_open` → `is_plan_open` — bypassing
Y132 entirely. Today's 2026-05-25 (UK Spring Bank + US Memorial
Day) exposed it: `daytrade_ftse_v1` cycled for 4h+ scanning a
closed market while the market-data daemon (which uses
`is_holiday()` directly) correctly skipped LSE.

holiday short-circuit `exchange_status()` already had. Blast
radius small:

- Strategy daemon: cycles now skip on holidays (the bug fix)
- Broker `gate_market_open`: rejects orders on holidays
- All 40 existing `test_drop_y50_prep_sessions.py` tests green
  (their dates have no Y132 overlap)

`test_lse_closed_on_uk_spring_bank_holiday`,
`test_us_closed_on_memorial_day`,
`test_lse_open_on_non_holiday_session_day`.

are wrong, says scanned 48, near miss 47, buy 0. if its near miss
47 it shuold list 47 tickers, but it lists none."* Root cause:
`signals_above_threshold` is mis-named in `_base.py:761-780` —
it's literally `len(evaluations)` (count of evaluations posted to
the broker, not "above the BUY threshold"). My Y135.2 mapping
`near-miss = signals_above_threshold - orders_submitted`
inherited the confusion. Of those 47 postings, most are HOLD-
action signals that Y91 drops at write time → no NEAR row exists
to back the count.

Fix: drop the "near-miss" cell from the SCAN row. New shape:

    CRYPTO · scanned 51 · evaluated 48 · buy 0
    FTSE   · scanned 50 · evaluated 44 · buy 0

Three columns that mean exactly what they say. Raw
`signals_above_threshold` is still surfaced as "posted" in the
tap-detail for forensics.

## §82. Retention review + Y138.1 + Y139 spec (2026-05-25 evening)

Three deliverables shipped between the §81 ritual and end-of-session.
All on `origin/main`. Captured here for the cold-start case.

### Y138.1 — /tmp/tmp*.db leak plugged (`fb61fea` + `16aafbc`)

The retention review (below) surfaced **12,945 orphan `/tmp/tmp*.db`
files** (~12 GB on disk). Forensic identified the root cause: ~57 test
files use the pattern

```python
tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".db")
tmp.close()
return Path(tmp.name)
```

inside ``_make_*_table()`` helpers. The ``delete=False`` opts out of
auto-cleanup; the caller never ``os.unlink``-s the returned path.

Two-way fix options:
- (A) Refactor all 57 files to use pytest's ``tmp_path`` fixture
  (proper but ~285 edits, high blast radius).
- (B) Single autouse conftest fixture that tracks ``/tmp/tmp*.db``
  files before each test and deletes the diff afterwards (1 file
  change, catches everything regardless of which test created it).

Y138.1 ships **option B**. ``tests/conftest.py`` gains an
``_cleanup_orphan_tempdbs`` autouse fixture. Pattern match is
deliberately narrow (`tmp*.db`) — matches Python's NamedTemporaryFile
default prefix and nothing else, so legitimate `/tmp/test.db` files
are untouched. Also handles SQLite sidecars (`-journal`, `-wal`,
`-shm`).

The misplaced ``alphabot/dashboard/test_drop_1_3_3a_routes.py`` (a
test that should have lived in ``tests/`` since Drop 1.3.3a) was
also moved to ``tests/dashboard/`` in the same drop.

**Verified**: 91 tests across the 4 historically-leakiest files
pass with **zero orphans created**.

**The Y138.1 commit had a self-inflicted mishap**: ``git add`` was
called with three pathspecs in one line; the third path was
already-renamed (didn't exist), git aborted on the fatal pathspec,
and silently skipped staging the conftest.py change before reaching
it. ``fb61fea`` shipped with a commit message describing two
changes but the diff contained only the rename. Caught by reading
``git diff --cached --stat`` after — the file count didn't match
intent. ``16aafbc`` is the follow-up that actually landed the
conftest fixture. The lesson is now CLAUDE.md §2:

> **Always verify staging matches intent before ``git commit``** —
> run ``git diff --cached --stat`` immediately after ``git add`` and
> check the file count + insertion delta against intent. The chained
> ``git add file1 file2 file3`` pattern aborts on the first fatal
> pathspec and silently skips later args.

Commit ``eb5beb3`` carries that lesson into CLAUDE.md §2.
