### Y139 spec filed (`4a7e794`)

Operator question that opened the conversation:

> *"on the master page of the brain and then downstream all the tabs
> that populate with data? are they populating automatically? if so,
> at what frequency? with no reliance on claude API?"*

Answered: yes, all the dashboard tabs auto-populate from local DB
data; the MASTER tab is on-demand sub-second pure-SQL (zero Claude);
the only Claude calls are the 1 daily + 1 weekly briefing. The Brain
runs continuously on **$0 mechanical loops** and bills only the
synthesis surface.

Then operator asked: were the four standard cost levers (prompt
caching, model routing, batch API, stacked architecture) factored
into the Y97.8 cost decision? Honest answer from the code:

  - Prompt caching: **NOT implemented** anywhere (`grep -rE "cache_control" alphabot/brain/` → empty)
  - Haiku routing: **NOT used** anywhere (all calls Sonnet or Opus)
  - Batch API: **NOT used** anywhere
  - Stacked architecture: **partial only** (Y97.8 was binary "Claude vs no-Claude" rather than layered)

The Y97.8 pivot was made on naive Sonnet-standard pricing
assumptions. The math reprises dramatically under the optimised
path. Operator then lifted budget from $30 cap → **$40 target /
$50 ceiling** and asked for proper scope.

**Y139 spec** lives at `docs/Y139_SPEC.md` (495 lines, full
specification following the Y50_SPEC.md / Y94_SPEC.md pattern).
Headline architecture:

```
L0 Mechanical (Pulse / Sweep / Reconcile-detect / Tier-A /
              matched-no-claude)                              $0
L1 Local embedding triage (nomic-embed-text-v1.5 on CPU)      $0
L2 Daily mega-batch (Sonnet+cached+batched, 06:00 UTC)        ~$9/mo
L3 Weekly distillation (Opus+batched, Sat 07:00 UTC)          ~$9/mo
L4 CRIT escalation (Sonnet-Standard+cached, manual)           ≤$3/mo
L5 ✨ Trade post-mortems (Haiku+batched on losing trades)    ~$4.5/mo
L6 ✨ Signal-quality audit (Sonnet+batched, daily)            ~$7.5/mo
L7 ✨ Operator Q&A surface (Sonnet+cached, rate-limited)      ~$6/mo
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  ~$39/mo
```

Eight phases (`Y139.1` → `Y139.8`), each independently shippable,
total ~26 hours effort. **Y139.1 is the right starting phase** —
pure prompt-caching addition with no behavioural change, zero cost
impact, sets the baseline cache-hit rate measurement for the rest
of the architecture.

Five new architectural locks proposed:
- L-Y139-LAYERED-COST-MODEL
- L-Y139-CACHE-MANDATORY
- L-Y139-LOCAL-FIRST-TRIAGE
- L-Y139-SPEND-CAP-IS-FLOOR-NOT-CEILING
- L-Y139-NO-PROXIES

Locks attach when Y139.1 ships, not before — the spec authored them
but they're not in force yet.

## §83. Y139.1 — prompt caching + cache telemetry (2026-05-25 afternoon)

Phase 1 of 8 in the Y139 Brain cost re-optimisation arc. Commit
`aa6fd6b`, deployed live same session (alphabot-broker restart for
migration 058 + alphabot-brain restart to load the new system-block
shape).

**What landed in code**:

- ``alphabot/brain/claude_client.py`` — every outbound Anthropic call
  now sends the system field as a list-of-blocks with
  ``cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}`` (via new helper
  ``_system_block``). Both code paths fixed: ``run_investigation``
  (multi-turn tool-use loop, used by deep_scan + briefing_daily +
  briefing_weekly + reconcile_diagnose) and ``run_single_turn`` (the
  Y97.1 cheap-confirm path). Cache tokens summed across turns via the
  new ``_extract_cache_tokens`` helper. The Anthropic 5-min ephemeral
  TTL means the first call in any 5-min window writes the cache
  (~1.25x input rate); subsequent calls read it (~0.10x).
- ``alphabot/brain/claude_budget.py`` — ``cost_for`` accepts the two
  new lanes (``cache_hit_tokens`` and ``cache_write_tokens``) with the
  per-model pricing matrix updated to include both. Haiku 4.5 pricing
  corrected from the placeholder ``$0.80/$4.00`` to the operator-
  verified ``$1.00/$5.00`` per Y139_SPEC §3.1. ``record_invocation``
  accepts four new optional kwargs (``cache_hit_tokens``,
  ``cache_write_tokens``, ``api_endpoint``, ``layer``) and writes them
  on every row.
- Migration 058 (additive, schema 57 → 58) on
  ``brain_claude_invocations``: ``cache_hit_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL
  DEFAULT 0``, ``cache_write_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0``,
  ``api_endpoint TEXT``, ``layer INTEGER``. The two telemetry-int
  columns default to 0 so historical rows still compute correctly.
- 21 new tests in ``tests/brain/test_drop_y139_1_prompt_caching.py``
  cover: migration schema shape, the cache-controlled system block
  payload shape, ``_extract_cache_tokens`` reader robustness,
  ``cost_for`` cache pricing on Sonnet/Opus/Haiku, ``record_invocation``
  persistence, ``run_investigation`` summing cache tokens across
  multi-turn loops, ``run_single_turn`` carrying the same payload, and
  the no-key fallback writing zero-cache rows.
- 5 existing brain test fixtures updated to apply migration 058 (per
  CLAUDE.md §3 "drop owns its test updates"): Y95.1.4, Y95.1.6,
  Y97.1, Y97.2, Y97.3. Plus the two schema-pin tripwire tests
  (test_drop_y92, test_db/test_migrations).

**Library choice — fastembed, not sentence-transformers**.

VPS is 3.7 GB total RAM with ~1 GB free during the operator's

## §85. Y140 + manual cleanup A — OCO close-path race finally fixed (2026-05-25 evening)

Closes ``HANDOVER_26 §4 #2`` and ``MASTER_TODO §3 Tier 0 item 2``,
both flagged 'GMT close-path race — root cause OPEN'. Commit
``79f7c76``, deployed live same session (alphabot-broker-crypto
restart).

**Third hit forced a real fix**. Same signature each time:

- ``crypto_stops`` row: TRIGGERED → OCO_CLOSED, clean.
- ``trades`` row: closed with STOP_LOSS or TAKE_PROFIT, clean.
- ``positions`` row + ``position_book``: BOTH stuck at entry qty.
- Binance balance: reflects the close (asset balance accumulated
  across many paper-testnet cycles).

The three confirmed incidents:

| Symbol | When | Stuck qty | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GMTUSDT | 2026-05-23 soak window | 7656.9 | First sighting; original report in §58/§78 |
| ERAUSDT | 2026-05-25 08:45:21 UTC | 612.7 | Same signature; manually cleaned this session |
| PHAUSDT (2nd round) | 2026-05-25 17:06:19 UTC | 2083.0 | Same signature; manually cleaned this session |

**Manual cleanup A** (operator-approved 2026-05-25 ~17:42 UTC) zeroed
both stuck rows via direct ``UPDATE positions SET quantity = 0`` +
``alphabot-broker-crypto`` restart. Same pattern Garrath used on
2026-05-23 for GMT.

**Root cause located** in ``alphabot/broker_binance/reconcile.py``:

- ``_maybe_route_oco_fill`` (the F8 routing handler from Drop 1
  2026-05-20) deliberately did NOT decrement ``position_book``. Its
  docstring punted to the reconcile sweep: "the book stays consistent
  at the next reconcile sweep (``_apply_close`` zeroes the now-orphan
  position row)".
- The sweep's ``_decide`` returns CLOSED only when
  ``exchange_qty == 0 and db_qty > 0``. With residual balance from
  prior cycles (3581 ERA, 12336 PHA), ``exchange_qty > db_qty`` falls
  into the **EXCESS_WARNED branch** — "manual deposit; not auto-
  importing". The position row never zeros.
- The original sweep logic was correct for the IBKR-style world
  where balances reset on close. It was wrong for any account with
  residual exchange-side balance, which is the testnet steady state.

**Y140 fix — two layers**:

PRIMARY in ``_maybe_route_oco_fill``: the moment the tracker emits
``CompletedTrade`` (``completed is not None``), zero
``position_book`` + ``positions`` row directly. New helper
``_zero_position_after_oco_close`` encapsulates the mutation so tests
can drive it. Mirrors the canonical pattern from ``_apply_close``:
``dataclasses.replace(pos, quantity=0.0)`` →
``position_book.upsert_from_snapshot(zero_pos)`` →
``_db_close_position(symbol, reason='oco_closed')``. Single INFO log
line at completion records the fix firing live so we can spot it in
the journal. Idempotent — if the sweep ever does fire first, the
second writer sees qty=0 and no-ops via ``_db_close_position``'s
existing "position not in book" guard.

DEFENCE in ``_decide``: new ``recent_oco_close`` kwarg. New helper
``_has_recent_oco_close(symbol, db_qty, window_minutes=5)`` queries
``crypto_stops`` for a TRIGGERED row whose quantity matches db_qty
(within ``DRIFT_QUANTITY_TOLERANCE_PCT``) and whose ``closed_at`` is
within 5 min. ``_compute_drift`` runs this lookup per position and
passes the flag through. When True AND ``exchange_qty > db_qty``,
decide CLOSED instead of EXCESS_WARNED. Catches the case where the
WS message never arrived (network blip, restart mid-fill).

**Verification**:

- Y140 tests: 14/14 pass (3 chunks: primary, defence, lookup,
  idempotency)
- broker_binance + Y3 OCO suite: 238/238 pass (no regression in
  adjacent surfaces)
- Full sweep: 6800 pass / 34 fail = baseline exactly, **zero net
  new failures**
- Lint: clean on touched files

**Live behaviour starting now**: next OCO close on any crypto
daytrade will land qty=0 immediately on the WS handler call.
Observable proof: ``Y140: zeroed position after OCO close —
symbol=X coid=Y qty=Z -> 0`` lines in the journal, and no new
stuck rows in ``positions``.

**3 architectural locks attached**:

- **L-Y140-WS-CLOSE-IS-AUTHORITATIVE** — the WS close-fill handler IS
  the source of position-close truth (not the sweep). Punting
  position mutation to the sweep is now explicitly out of policy.
- **L-Y140-SWEEP-DOES-NOT-ASSUME-ZERO-BALANCE** — ``_decide`` handles
  the non-zero residual balance close case via the OCO_CLOSED
  lookup. Future changes to drift detection MUST preserve this
  branch.
- **L-Y140-OCO-CLOSE-WITHIN-5MIN-IS-CLOSED** — the defence-path time
  window matches the sweep cadence. Tightening to less than 1 min
  risks missing legitimate races; widening risks mis-attributing
  re-opens of the same symbol.

**Out of scope**:

- Backfill of historical GMT/ERA/PHA state — already manually cleaned.
- Any change to ``_handle_list_status`` (OCO state machine).
- IBKR-side reconcile changes (different code path, different bug
  surface).
- Forensic logging that would have caught this — no longer needed
  now that root cause is known and fixed.

## §86. Gateway recovery (2026-05-25 ~17:34 UTC)

Operator-flagged: dashboard showing IB Gateway + IBKR broker as
failed. Diagnosis: Java IB Gateway process was alive 17h+ but stuck
listener — port 4002 listening per ``ss -tlnp`` but
``accept()`` not completing (``strace`` showed zero syscalls in 2 s;
bash TCP probe to 4002 timed out). Broker reported FATAL with 10
reconnect attempts since the Y139.1 broker restart at 16:58 UTC —
the existing broker→gateway socket dropped on broker restart and the
stuck-listener gateway refused the fresh connection.

Operator-approved gateway restart at 17:34 UTC. New Java pid
1212587. After ~45 s for IBKR-server login, broker /health flipped
to HEALTHY with 5 positions reconciled (the parked V3 FTSE longs;
the 2 ASX shorts correctly refused on auto-import per long-only
policy). Some benign 162/200 errors for UKX/XJO index data — same
correlate-cache fallbacks we've seen since Y50.

The bash TCP probe still times out post-restart because the gateway
only accepts API-protocol handshakes, not raw TCP connects — correct
behaviour, not a problem. ``/health`` is the authoritative test.

**Lesson noted**: a stuck-listener gateway can survive 17+ hours
silently because (a) the systemd unit is the oneshot pattern that
exits 0 immediately after starting the Docker compose, and (b)
``ss -tlnp`` happily reports the port as listening even when the
process is wedged. The broker FATAL-state alarm IS the canary —
when broker reports FATAL with timeout errors, the gateway needs
a restart even if its systemd unit looks healthy.

## §88. Y139.4b — Layer-2 daily mega-batch replaces Y97.8 (2026-05-25 night)

Phase 4b of 8 in the Y139 arc. The Y97.8 daily briefing — one
Claude call per day producing the daily report — is now replaced
by a batched submission of N+1 requests via the Anthropic Messages
Batch API (the wrapper substrate landed in Y139.4a). The Batch API
is 50% off standard rates with a 24h SLA (typical resolve <5 min);
for a daily briefing's tolerance the latency is irrelevant and the
price drop compounds with the prompt-caching and answer-cache
savings already in place.

The reshape sweeps in the previously-undiagnosed alarm tail too:
Layer-1 (Y139.2b) auto-attaches diagnoses to ~30% of new alarms
via local-embedding triage; the remainder (novel + suggested-without-
auto-attach) used to sit forever with ``diagnosis IS NULL``. Y139.4b
batches the un-diagnosed tail into the same daily submission so
each alarm gets a Claude diagnosis at half-price-after-cache,
attached to its alarm row.

### What shipped

- **Migration 061 — ``brain_batch_jobs``** (schema 60 → 61, purely
  additive). One row per submitted batch: ``batch_id`` (UNIQUE),
  ``loop_name``, ``purpose`` (e.g. ``2026-05-26``), ``submitted_at``,
  ``processing_status``, ``request_count``, ``completed_at``,
  ``succeeded_count``, ``errored_count``, ``total_cost_usd``,
  ``results_url``. Two indexes: ``batch_id`` for poll/complete writes,
  ``(processing_status, submitted_at DESC)`` for in-flight lookup at
  brain restart. The table is the single source of truth for batch
  state — a restart mid-batch reads the row and resumes polling
  without duplicate submission.

- **``alphabot/brain/loops/daily_batch.py``** — the lifecycle. Three
  phases on one ``run_once()`` entry, idempotent across ticks:

  1. **Phase A — submit.** At 06:00 UTC (window 00:00-14:59 minute),
     ``_should_submit`` checks for a pre-existing
     ``DAILY_BRIEFING:YYYY-MM-DD`` alarm row (idempotency gate);
     ``_gather_undiagnosed_alarms`` pulls today's alarms with
     ``diagnosis IS NULL`` AND ``local_triage_decision IN
     ('novel', 'suggested') OR NULL``, ordered CRIT > WARN > INFO,
     capped at 50. The briefing alarm row gets pre-opened so the
     report has somewhere to land. ``batch_client.submit_batch``
     posts N+1 requests (N per-alarm prompts + 1 daily-report
     prompt). ``_record_batch_job`` writes the brain_batch_jobs row.

  2. **Phase B — poll.** Inline poll (``_poll_phase``) bounded by
     ``DAILY_BATCH_POLL_MAX_S=600s``. Typical batch resolves <5 min
     so this is one tick, but the cap protects against the 24h SLA
     worst case — if still in-progress at the cap, return
     phase='polling' and the next loop tick (PULSE_INTERVAL_S) will
     resume polling via the in_progress row.

  3. **Phase C — process.** Stream results via
     ``batch_client.stream_batch_results``. For each per-alarm
     ``succeeded`` row: cost via ``claude_budget.cost_for`` with the
     Y139.1 cache-hit/write counts, ``claude_budget.record_invocation``

     Layer-2 batch]`` prefix), and best-effort

     ``(rule_key, signature_hash, broker_state_hash)`` tuple hits
     the Y139.3 cache at $0. The daily-report row attaches to the
     briefing alarm + resolves it + sends a Telegram alert via the
     existing ``telegram.brain_alert`` path. Errored results still
     write an invocation row (for visibility) and the briefing row
     still gets a fallback message so the operator always wakes up
     with *something*.

- **L-Y139.4b-BATCH-JOBS-DURABLE** (new) — the
  ``brain_batch_jobs`` row is the single source of truth for

  and brain restarts because it reads the in-progress row FIRST,

## §89. tvscreener restore + Y136 ship + Y141 ASX pipeline (2026-05-26 early hours)

Continuation arc post-Y139.4b. Operator surfaced "asx did nothing
again and is only streaming 2" at 05:04 UTC. Investigation cascaded
through four distinct breakages and produced three deploys + two
permission-settings cleanups.

### tvscreener restore (commit `50f0b25`)

Y50a/Y111 snapshot_engine imports ``tvscreener`` at scan time to
populate ``ranked_candidates`` for all 5 equity markets. The library
had been installed manually into the venv but was never added to
``pyproject.toml``. When ``uv sync`` ran at 17:04 UTC on 2026-05-25
(during the Y139.2a fastembed deploy), it evicted ``tvscreener``.
The market-data daemon kept running with the module cached in memory
until the 22:02:31 UTC restart; post-restart every snapshot_engine
cycle crashed with ``ModuleNotFoundError: No module named
'tvscreener'``, leaving ``ranked_candidates`` empty since 21:56 UTC.

Effect on the operator surface: ``/pool`` falls back to
``pool_snapshots`` when ``ranked_candidates`` is stale (Y112 logic).
``pool_snapshots`` had ``[DRR, ORI]`` for ASX (held-only — the
IBKR ``STK.AU`` scanner returns 0 chronically, see §89.D below).
So strategies saw 2 ASX symbols, scanned 2, traded 0.

Fix: ``tvscreener==0.3.0`` hard-pinned in ``pyproject.toml`` (the
column-schema is captured against that exact version — drift breaks
the scan silently per the module docstring). ``uv sync`` installed
it. ``alphabot-market-data`` restarted; first post-restart scan at
05:17 UTC returned 1223 ASX rows, 67 promotable. The
``SNAPSHOT_SCAN_FAILED:asx`` and ``SNAPSHOT_SCAN_DEGRADED:asx``
alarms (15 + 13 trips accumulated) both cleared on the same cycle.
ASX strategy logged ``[daytrade_asx_v1] cycle 1: scanned=40
signals_posted=13`` at 05:46 — first ASX evaluation in 7+ hours.

### Y136 ship (commit `5b6bcfd`)

In-flight on disk from a prior session ("operator brief: i want it
fully dynamic. there is no point giving 100 slots to a market that
is doing nothing while another market is going crazy"). Algorithm
Option C — 10-slot per-market floor + global merit pool by
``promotion_score`` across every open equity market.

New module ``alphabot/market_data_daemon/stream_allocator.py`` —
pure-maths allocator, no I/O. ``universe.py`` rewired at
``desired_universe`` to read all open markets' ranked candidates in
one SQL query and call ``allocate_global_stream``. Legacy
``pool_snapshots`` fallback preserved for markets whose
``ranked_candidates`` are stale or absent.

29 Y128 + Y136 tests green; 303 market_data_daemon suite green.

Architectural lock: **L-Y136-STREAM-IS-GLOBAL-COMPETITION** —
equity streaming slots are allocated by global top-by-score across
open markets with a per-market floor (default 10). No hard-coded
per-market splits.

### Y141 — ASX-evaluation pipeline end-to-end (commit `5c66d40`)

Diagnostic finding A: the Y136 stream allocator includes HKEX and
TSE the moment their session windows open, regardless of the
``DAYTRADE_HKEX_ENABLED`` / ``DAYTRADE_TSE_ENABLED`` flags. The
Y117-Y120 dormancy-by-default contract was honoured by the
*strategy* daemon but not the *market-data* daemon. So HKEX was
chronically consuming the IBKR 50-subs-per-600s rate-limit budget
that should have gone to ASX. Operator's exact word: "HK and JAPAN
we havent turned on yet!! why is this happening!"

Diagnostic finding B: within a single batch dispatch, the
``SubscriptionManager`` sort key was ``(priority, symbol)``. HKEX
numeric codes (``"1038"``, ``"1055"``...) collated alphabetically
**before** ASX uppercase letters. HKEX won the rate-limit race
every cycle even when ASX closed 2h45m sooner.

Diagnostic finding C (live IBKR probe at 05:39 UTC): the paper
account's market-data scanner permissions cover **US only**.
LSE/ASX/HKEX/TSE all return Error 162 ("Market Scanner is not
configured for one of the chosen locations"). 4 of 5 equity scans
have been silently broken since the markets were enabled. The bot
already falls back to ``ranked_candidates`` (Y112) so trading
works — but the diagnostic was silent.

Y141 closes A and B in code, surfaces C as an operator-visible
alarm.

**Y141.A — Streaming dormancy gate.**
``pool_config._DORMANCY_FLAG_BY_MARKET = {"hkex": "DAYTRADE_HKEX_ENABLED",
"tse": "DAYTRADE_TSE_ENABLED"}``. New helper
``is_market_streaming_enabled(market)`` reads ``Settings`` at call
time. ``desired_universe`` filters ``eligible_markets`` through it.
US/FTSE/ASX have no flag → always on (preserves pre-Y141 behaviour).

Architectural lock: **L-Y141-STREAMING-HONOURS-DORMANCY** — adding
a new "live" market is a deliberate two-flag flip (enable +
ensure scanner config exists), not a side-effect of the
session-window calendar.

**Y141.C — Close-proximity dispatch.** New helper
``pool_config.seconds_until_close(market, now)`` correctly handling
wrap-midnight sessions (ASX 22:45→06:00, TSE 23:45→06:45).
``SubscriptionRequest`` gains a ``market`` field; sort key bumps to
``(priority, seconds_until_close, symbol)``. ``priority=0`` held
positions still dispatch first regardless of market. Within
``priority=1+``, soonest-closing market wins the rate-limit race.

**Y141.D — IBKR scanner empty-result alarm.** New
``IBKR_SCANNER_EMPTY:{market}`` WARN alarm raised when an
in-session refresh returns 0 across all three slices.
Auto-resolves on recovery. Summary names the IBKR Account
Management fix and confirms the ``ranked_candidates`` fallback is
active so trading still works.

**Y141.B — pool ranked_candidates fallback.** Originally scoped
into Y141 but DROPPED on discovery — ``/pool`` endpoint already
implements this via Y112. The earlier confusion came from reading
``universe_discovery._refresh_equity_pool`` (writes
``pool_snapshots``) without tracing what ``/pool`` actually reads.

30 Y141 tests across A/C/D (13 + 12 + 5). Full
market_data_daemon suite 333/333 green. Cross-suite with brain:
779/779 green.

### Operator-side IBKR work (NOT a code task)

Per the §89.D live probe, the paper account is missing scanner
subscriptions for LSE, ASX, HKEX, TSE. Fix is in IBKR Account
Management → Settings → Market Data Subscriptions → enable scanner
for each venue (SMART/AUD for ASX, SMART/GBP for LSE, SEHK for
HKEX, TSEJ for TSE). Until that's done, the bot routes entirely
through tvscreener → ``ranked_candidates`` — which is the
preferred path anyway (more comprehensive than IBKR scanner top-N).

## §90. Y141.1 + Y139 finish arc — Layers 2/3/5/6/7 complete (2026-05-26 morning)

Continuation of §89 immediately. After Y139.4b's first production
submission produced a tool-call-hallucination disaster ($0.08 of
fabricated `<tool_call>` XML and invented alarm IDs in the daily
report), this session's morning arc:

1. Fixed the hallucination at the root with Y141.1 batch-mode
   prompts.
2. Shipped the remaining four Y139 phases (.5/.6/.7/.8) all on the
   same batch-mode foundation, plus added the operator Q&A
   endpoint as the final piece.

Net result: the Y139 cost-reshape arc (Y139_SPEC §1, ~$39/mo
target at full build-out) is complete. Current daily Brain cost
≈ $0.70/day = ~$21/mo. Schema climbed 60 → 65 across five
purely-additive migrations.

### Y141.1 — Batch-mode prompts (commit `afa6d2d`)

The Y139.4b first-production submission at 06:00:14 UTC produced
fabricated `<tool_call>` XML and simulated DB-query results
containing alarm IDs (134/135/152…) that don't exist in our DB
(real IDs were 14644/14522). Root cause: `daily_batch._submit_phase`
used `context_builder.build_base_system_prompt()` which advertises
read_brain_knowledge / query_db / bootstrap_ci / read_journal as
tools — appropriate for `claude_client.run_agentic_loop` but not
for the Anthropic Messages Batch API (single-turn, no tools).
The model improvised by writing tool-call syntax in the response.

Two changes:

1. **`build_batch_system_prompt`** — new function in
   `context_builder.py` carrying the same FACTS as the agentic
   prompt (role, architecture, gotchas, locked constraints) but
   explicitly: *"ONE turn with NO tools available. Do NOT emit
   `<tool_call>` XML or simulated tool responses — there is no
   executor on the other side, and inventing tool output is
   hallucination."* Strips the Investigation Protocol + tool-
   budget framing entirely.

2. **`daily_briefing_batch_user_prompt`** + new `BriefingData`
   dataclass + `_gather_briefing_data` helper — replaces the
   agentic daily-briefing prompt (which walked Claude through 7
   steps of DB queries) with one that embeds all six sections
   INLINE as text (banked alarms, matched_no_claude, Tier-A
   outcomes, top broker_errors, spend+flags, yesterday's trades
   by discipline). Model summarises from that data alone.

**L-Y141.1-BATCH-PROMPT-IS-TOOL-FREE** (new) — every caller of
`batch_client.submit_batch` MUST use `build_batch_system_prompt`,
not `build_base_system_prompt`. Mixing the agentic prompt into a
batch request always hallucinates tool calls.

18 new tests across 4 sections. 464/464 brain regression.
Wasted $0.08 in the hallucinated submission already paid for the
diagnosis — no rollback needed.

### Y139.5 — Weekly Opus distillation + mining (commit `d469454`)

The Saturday 07:00 UTC weekly briefing migrated from agentic
`claude_client.run_investigation` to Batch API + Opus 4.7 (same
class of fix as Y141.1 for the daily, applied to weekly). Added
the new mining lever:

- **`weekly_briefing_batch_user_prompt`** + `WeeklyBriefingData`
  — embeds the Y106 master_digest plus six new "mining input"
  sections: novel-alarm clusters, repeated Layer-2 diagnoses,
  proven_count climbs, top-cost BKs, bot_params changes, feature
  drift. Asks the model for a `<proposals>JSON</proposals>`
  envelope with three proposal types:
    - `new_bk` — clustered novel-pattern alarms become BK
      candidates (cluster by `rule_name`, not `rule_key` — live-
      per-rule_key unique index means rule_keys never repeat
      across live rows; rule_name groups across symbols)
    - `new_af_rule` — repeated Y139.4b-stamped diagnoses become

    - `tier_b_to_a` — fixes with `proven_count ≥ 3` become

- **`brain_proposals`** table (migration 062) — pending /

32 new tests. Two existing Y95.1.6 weekly tests rewired from
mocking httpx → mocking batch_client (same-drop rule).

### Y139.6 — Trade post-mortems (commit `7d1c70c`)

Layer 5 added INSIDE the existing daily mega-batch (rather than a
separate submit/poll path) — Y139.4b infrastructure already
handles N requests, just route by custom_id prefix in
`_process_phase`. One Haiku post-mortem per losing trade:

- Picker: `pick_losing_trades(conn, since, threshold_usd,
  threshold_pct, max_picks)` — either threshold OR semantics
  (`pnl_usd < -$5` OR `pnl_pct < -0.5%`, both env-tunable),
  worst-first sort, NOT EXISTS join against `trade_postmortems`
  for idempotency, capped at `BRAIN_POSTMORTEM_MAX_PER_DAY=50`.
- Context builder: joins trades → signals → signal_gates →
  signal_context to assemble (trade row + entry signal score +
  every gate's pass/fail/raw_value + regime + 21-bar OHLCV
  summary).
- Output: 4 labeled sections (SUMMARY / GATE / PATTERN / RULE),
  regex-extracted. Simpler than the Y139.5 JSON envelope because
  each post-mortem is ~80-120 words flat.
- Writer parses `bk_match_id` from the PATTERN line (e.g.
  "matches BK-NOISE-FADE") so future weekly distillation can
  count "BK-NOISE-FADE seen 5 times this week" as input.

`trade_postmortems` table (migration 063): id, trade_id (FK),
written_at, model, pnl_usd, pnl_pct, summary, gate_analysis,
suggested_rule, bk_match_id, cost_usd. Index on trade_id.

`brain_claude_invocations` writes `layer=5` for post-mortems so
`/spend/by-layer` separates them from Layer-2 alarm/report.

23 new tests. Cost target $4.5/mo at 10 losers/day × $0.0025
Haiku batched. Today's data: 6 losers/24h.

### Y139.7 — Signal-quality audit (commit `8b34f56`)

Layer 6 — one Sonnet call per day inside the same daily mega-
batch. Samples N=20 signals from yesterday, asks for per-gate
calibration scores 0-10, top threshold tweak, confidence.

- Sampler: `sample_signals_for_audit` stratifies across
  `(action, above_threshold)` to mix BUY-fired / BUY-blocked /
  HOLD / SELL when populated; falls back to oversampling when
  strata are empty (today's data: all BUY-fired).
- Output envelope: `<audit>JSON</audit>` with
  `{calibration, top_suggestion, suggested_param, suggested_value,
  confidence}`. Confidence CHECK-constrained to low/med/high
  in `gate_calibration_audit` (migration 064).
- 6-stage parser validation (missing_tags / json_decode /
  shape_invalid / calibration_missing / confidence_invalid /
  top_suggestion_missing). Garbage responses still write a row
  with `parse_error` set so the operator sees structured-output
  drift.
- Model scores **whatever gates appear in the data** — not a
  hardcoded spec list. Works across V3 (ema/macd/rsi/volume/
  momentum/vwap) and V4 daytrade (rvol/catalyst/vwap/atr_pct/
  regime) gate vocabularies.

Y91/§80 touchpoint: this layer's `top_suggestion` automatically
surfaces "the near-miss tier classifier should be relaxed/
tightened by X" when the data warrants — closing the long-
standing forensic that's been on the backlog.

29 new tests. Cost target $7.5/mo at one $0.025 Sonnet call/day.

### Y139.8 — Operator Q&A (commit `7b5107e`)

Layer 7 — the only Y139 phase NOT in the daily mega-batch.
Operator types a question into the dashboard (or curls);
**STANDARD Messages API** (not batched) for sub-10s response;
Sonnet+cached single-turn call.

- **`POST /brain/qa`** — PIN-gated, body `{"question": "..."}`,
  returns `{outcome, answer, cost_usd, calls_today, cap}`. Audited
  via `agent_audit`. Same outcome-shape contract as
  `/brain/escalate` (Y139.4a): UI distinguishes by body, not HTTP
  code.
- **Rate limit**: `BRAIN_QA_CALLS_PER_DAY_MAX=5` per UTC day
  (env-tunable). Counter reads `qa_history` rows since
  `today_00:00`. Cap stops further calls — the standard API costs
  ~10x batched, so a runaway operator (or misconfigured automation
  re-asking) would chew spend fast.
- **Context builder**: 6 sections (held positions + today's
  trades + last hour's signals + open alarms + spend + flag
  state), capped at 10k chars. Best-effort tolerant: missing
  tables / empty queries render `"(none)"` rather than crashing.
- **`build_batch_system_prompt`** for the system block (Y141.1
  lock). Single-turn, no tools. Q&A user prompt restates the
  no-tools instruction for belt-and-braces.

`qa_history` (migration 065): asked_at, question, answer, model,

## §91 — Y143 desk-health widget shipped (2026-05-26 morning)

### Scope

Operator request: "one extremely useful thing the brain could do
for me is the following. i often ask you to tell me the status of
the whole bot. gateway and binance healthy, strategies scanning
currently open markets, 1276 scanned, 127 qualified, 87 streamed.
strategies scanning 82. can i have a widget next to the spend
canary that shows all of that, like an overall trading desk health
but its live..."

Y143 extends GET `/status` (the existing dashboard endpoint) with
five new live signals and renders them in a new `desk-health`
strip under the existing market chips. No new endpoints, no new
storage — purely a read-aggregation widget.

### Commit

`d3925df` — Y143 desk-health widget (live trading-desk status
strip). +967 / -5 across 5 files.

### Endpoint shape extended

`GET /status` response now includes (in addition to the existing
`markets`, `daemons`, `schema_version`, `open_alarms_*` fields):

- **`markets[].scanned`** — latest `snapshot_runs.symbols_scanned`
  per market (null when no run yet).
- **`markets[].qualified`** — latest `pool_snapshots.total_count`
  per market (the `/pool` figure strategies receive).
- **`markets[].gated`** — true when the market's dormancy flag is
  off (HKEX → `DAYTRADE_HKEX_ENABLED`, TSE →
  `DAYTRADE_TSE_ENABLED`); dashboard renders as "dormant" italic.
- **`strategies[]`** — array of `{name, cycle_at, minutes_since,
  scanned, signals_above}` per daytrade strategy, derived from
  the latest `cycles` row. Stale = `minutes_since > 5`.
- **`services[]`** — array of `{name, state}` for the 6 tracked
  alphabot-* units (gateway, broker, broker-crypto, market-data,
  brain, strategy-daytrade). State ∈ {healthy, degraded, down,
  unknown}. Probe is `systemctl is-active` via subprocess with a
  2s per-unit timeout, run on `asyncio.to_thread`.
- **`streams`** — `{ibkr, binance}` integers from the HTTP fan-out
  to market-data and crypto-broker `/count`-style endpoints, 1.5s
  per-endpoint timeout. Either field can be null on timeout/error
  — the dashboard renders "--" as the fallback.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y143-STATUS-IS-READ-AGGREGATION** — `/status` is a pure
  read-aggregator over existing tables (`snapshot_runs`,
  `pool_snapshots`, `cycles`) and live OS state (`systemctl
  is-active`). It never writes. New signals join here without
  schema migrations.
- **L-Y143-FANOUT-IS-BOUNDED** — service-health subprocess timeout
  capped at 2s per unit, HTTP fan-out capped at 1.5s per
  endpoint, all wrapped in `contextlib.suppress(Exception)`. A
  degraded peer must not delay the dashboard.

### Backend extensions (alphabot/brain/operator_ui/status.py)

Per-service `_ServiceHealth` gained:

- `active_since` (ISO timestamp) + `uptime_seconds` from

- `sub_state` (running / exited / failed) for the few seconds
  between systemctl saying "active" and the daemon actually

  from a journalctl probe of the last 15 minutes. Content-scans

  `Error <N>` fragments. Caught XJO/IND 162 + UKX 200 noise on

  because Python loggers route ERROR to journald priority 6.
- `kpi{}` — per-service compact KPI dict from DB queries:

Per-market `_MarketState` gained:

Top-level `_StatusResponse` gained:

  summed. Drives the bottom-of-card "errors last 15min" chip.
- `open_scanner_empty_markets` — UI labels of currently-open
  IBKR scanner-empty alarms. Drives the amber banner inside
  the card.

Caching: heavy probes (`systemctl show`, `journalctl`) go through
a 15s module-level cache (`_detail_cache`). Cold call ~170ms,
cached ~50ms — verified on the live deploy.

LSE label split: discovered during Y143.1 that `snapshot_runs`
writes `market='lse'` while `pool_snapshots` writes
`market='ftse'`. Y143 used a single mapping and silently lost
the LSE scanned count. Y143.1 maintains `_UI_TO_DB_MARKET` (for
pool) and `_UI_TO_SNAPSHOT_MARKET` (for snapshot) — both label
conventions now resolve correctly.

- `.desk-health` row removed from inside `.desk-strip`.
- New `.desk-health-card` rendered as a `.dgrid` sibling of

  Error chip's `title` carries up to 3 sample journal lines for

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y143.1-STATUS-IS-READ-AGGREGATION** (extending the Y143
  lock) — every new helper added in Y143.1 is read-only over
  existing tables / live OS state / journalctl. No writes, no
  new schema.
- **L-Y143.1-HEAVY-PROBES-ARE-CACHED** — `systemctl show` and
  `journalctl` calls go through `_detail_cache` with a 15s TTL.

- **L-Y143.1-ERROR-SCAN-CONTENT-NOT-PRIORITY** — journalctl

## §93 — Y144 + Y145 + Y146: noise quieting + capital-safety fix (2026-05-26 afternoon)

Three drops that all close out items the Y143.1 desk-health card
surfaced this morning. Operator: "we will do 144-146" while
recovering from food poisoning — sequenced + deployed under
standing approval; only the Y146 `cp` + `daemon-reload` await
an explicit yes.

### Y144 — XJO/UKX regime-probe noise quieted (commit `534898f`)

The CorrelateCache refresh was calling the doomed primary every
60s for both UKX@ICEEU and XJO@ASX, IBKR refused (paper account
market-data subs missing for those Index contracts), ib_async
logged Error 200/162 at ERROR level BEFORE the fetcher's
`except` block could see the empty result. The fallback ETF
(ISF.L / IOZ.AX) served the regime data correctly, but the noise
filled the broker journal: ~60 Error 162 + ~80 Error 200 lines
per hour.

Fix in `alphabot/broker/correlate_fetchers.py`: the
`make_ibkr_correlate_with_fallback` factory now tracks per-instance
`primary_empty_streak`. After `_PRIMARY_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=5`
consecutive empty primary responses (~5 min at 60s refresh) a
sticky `primary_disabled` flag is set and the primary is skipped
for the rest of the broker lifetime. Any successful primary fetch
resets the streak — protects against transient empties (market
closed for a cycle, IBKR hiccup). Broker restart re-enables.

Net effect: cycles 1-5 after a broker restart still emit error
noise (5x); from cycle 6 onwards the journal is quiet for that
contract. Tests: 6 new in `test_drop_y144_correlate_primary_disable.py`
covering disable trigger, sticky stay-disabled, streak reset, Drop
1.2.5a happy-path preservation, single-empty no-disable, and
independent state across multiple fetcher instances.

Deployed via `alphabot-broker` restart at ~18:21 UTC. Live
behaviour verified post-deploy.

Architectural lock attached:

- **L-Y144-CORRELATE-PRIMARY-STICKY-DISABLE** — once a correlate's
  primary contract has gone empty for N consecutive cycles within
  a broker lifetime, the fetcher skips primary entirely. Broker
  restart re-enables. Any future code that adds new correlate
  primaries gets the same behaviour for free.

### Y145 — daytrade brackets unblocked under HYBRID_STOP_ENABLED (commit `db8bfbf`)

**Capital-safety fix, not noise.** The Y143.1 card showed ~190
[ERROR] lines/15min on `alphabot-strategy-daytrade` for FTSE
EntryIntent construction failure. Same error fired on every
daytrade engine (US/FTSE/ASX). Investigation showed every signal
was being SILENTLY REJECTED — the strategy logged ERROR +
"skipping submit" and the bracket never reached the broker.
~3 days of silent equity-daytrade dormancy since both Y94d flags
went live 2026-05-23 (per the alphabot-v4-nomenclature memory).

Root cause in `daytrade/_base.py::_submit_bracket_entry`. Y94d-8
(2026-05-23) added a gate
    `_use_trailing_stop = not _settings.HYBRID_STOP_ENABLED`
so the bracket child becomes a static STP_LMT (ratcheted by the
hybrid stop runner). The boolean was correctly passed to
`use_trailing_stop=` on EntryIntent. But the adjacent line was
left as `trailing_percent=stop_loss_pct` unconditional —
violating the Drop Y6 invariant:

    "trailing_percent set but use_trailing_stop=False — either
     set both or neither"

So with HYBRID_STOP_ENABLED=True every signal raised ValueError
inside EntryIntent.__post_init__, the strategy's try/except
caught it, and the bracket was dropped on the floor.

Fix: gate `trailing_percent` on `_use_trailing_stop`. One line.
`stop_price` / `stop_limit_price` (computed earlier) already
drive the static-stop child — `trailing_percent` is meaningless
in that path. Pass None when not trailing.

Deployed via `alphabot-strategy-daytrade` restart at ~18:27 UTC.
Immediately verified live: `daytrade_us_v1 cycle 1: scanned=88
signals_posted=88` — that's 88 signals POSTED to the broker
that were previously dropped. Zero EntryIntent ERROR lines in
the 30s since restart.

Tests (3 new in `test_drop_y145_daytrade_hybrid_trailing_gate.py`):

- Source-level guard — asserts the gated form is in _base.py and
  the unconditional anti-pattern is not. Catches a future revert.
- EntryIntent invariant behavioural guard — Y94d-8/Y145 correct
  combo constructs cleanly; broken combo raises with the exact
  error message production was logging.
- Drop Y6 edge — use_trailing_stop=True without trailing offset
  still raises. Contract preserved end-to-end.

Strategy regression: 17 failed (baseline HEAD) → 11 failed. The
6 fixed are `test_drop_1_4_4_daytrade_brackets.py` cases that
were already failing on HEAD for the same Y145 reason — the
broken invariant was silently breaking them too. Y145 unblocks
the whole class.

Architectural lock attached:

- **L-Y145-ENTRYINTENT-TRAILING-PAIRED** — any code that
  constructs an EntryIntent MUST keep `use_trailing_stop` and
  `trailing_percent` (or `trailing_amount`) in lockstep. Source
  test in `test_drop_y145_daytrade_hybrid_trailing_gate.py`
  catches a regression at the call site; behavioural test catches
  any future weakening of the EntryIntent invariant itself.

### Y146 — brain EnvironmentFile + agent reboot-race (commit `8c30121`)

Two systemd hygiene items.

**Brain EnvironmentFile** (built, committed, awaits operator
`sudo cp` + `daemon-reload`):

Before Y146 the brain process only saw env vars declared on the
systemd `Environment=` lines + pydantic Settings model fields.
pydantic Settings has `extra="ignore"` so undeclared fields drop
silently — meaning a new secret added via the operator console's
POST /secrets/update never reached pydantic's environment scope.
Y95 hit this with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (commit 9023e53 added it as
a Settings field). Y146's systemd-level fix is more durable: load
.env via `EnvironmentFile=-/home/alphabot/alphabot2/.env`, so
every var present in .env is exported to the brain process
regardless of whether pydantic declares it.

Deploy is approval-gated (cp to /etc/systemd/system + daemon-reload).
Surfaced to operator with verbatim command at ship time. Brain
restart itself is auto-allowed once the unit file is in place.

**Agent reboot-race** (hard-denied — operator runs):

`sudo systemctl disable alphabot-agent` — operator chose
"stop without disable" when freeing :8000 for brain (Y95 era).
On a fresh reboot both agent + brain race for :8000; whoever
loses the port-bind fails. The hard-denied `disable` resolves it.
Filed verbatim for operator to run when ready.

## §94 — Y147 + Y148 + Y149 + Y150 — HKEX live trading unblocked (2026-05-27 morning)

Long arc, started with the 2026-05-26 ASX session-end flatten that
appeared to fail (Y147), continued into operator enabling HKEX +
TSE (Y148), then a per-symbol-issue debug of every HKEX rejection
class (Y149 lot-size, Y150 KID).

### Y147 — orders.ibkr_order_id back-fill (commit `0862fba`)

Yesterday's ASX flatten "failure" was a display bug. The SELLs DID
execute at IBKR; the orders.ibkr_order_id column just never got
populated. Root: `persistent_sink._dispatch` branch for
OrderSubmittedV3 was a documented NO-OP. The broker's in-memory
`OrderState.ibkr_order_id` worked (gates + reconcile saw the value),
but every analytical query saw NULL.

Fix: `writers.update_order_ibkr_ids(client_order_id,
ibkr_order_id, ibkr_perm_id)` with COALESCE on each column. Sink
now writes from OrderSubmittedV3 dispatch. 5 new tests.

### Y148 + Y148b — HKEX/TSE risk-config entries (commits `4125fa3`, `62e297c`)

After operator flipped DAYTRADE_HKEX_ENABLED + DAYTRADE_TSE_ENABLED,
three discipline-keyed dicts on RiskLimits had no entries for
HKEX_DAYTRADE / TSE_DAYTRADE. Sequential gate fails surfaced one at
a time as each prior gate got fixed:

1. `max_positions_per_discipline` (Y148, +12 slots each)
2. `max_trade_pct_per_discipline` (Y148b, 1.5% each)
3. `trade_count_exempt_disciplines` (Y148b, daytrade exempt)

Same-drop test guard `test_y148_hkex_tse_daytrade_in_every_discipline_dict`
iterates all 3 dicts so a future regression is caught at unit-test
time. Also bumped `test_default_limits_total_slot_count` 131 → 155.

### Y149 + Y149a + Y149b — HKEX board-lot sizing (commits `f391f1b`, `f006740`, `981bca6`)

After Y148 unblocked the gates, HKEX BUYs reached IBKR but were
rejected with Error 388 ("Order size 100 is smaller than the
minimum required size of 1,000"). Strategy hardcoded qty=100 for
every HKEX symbol; HKEX board lots vary 50/100/500/1000/2000+.

Three-part fix:

- **Y149**: broker now captures `contract.minSize` from IBKR at
  qualify time and UPSERTs into `universe_symbols.lot_size`.
  Strategy sizer learns per-symbol lots via the existing Y123
  lookup machinery. New `LOT_TOO_LUMPY` skip reason with operator-
  chosen 2.0× tolerance: when target-qty rounds to 0, allow 1 lot
  if its notional is ≤ 2× target_position_eur (still under 4%
  max_symbol_pct hard cap). Configurable.
- **Y149a (hotfix)**: schema gap — `universe_symbols.currency` is
  NOT NULL; my INSERT only supplied (exchange, symbol, lot_size).
  Fix derives currency per-venue (SEHK→HKD, TSEJ→JPY) and builds
  `instrument_canonical = equity:VENUE:SYMBOL:CURRENCY`. Also
  added per-symbol fallback to `lot_size_lookup` — the bulk cache
  loads once per exchange per process; new symbols written by the
  broker need to be visible without daemon restart.
- **Y149b**: FX correction. `target_position_eur × lumpy_lot_tolerance`
  compared against `lot_size × current_price` — but current_price is
  in LOCAL currency. For HKD (10× weaker than EUR magnitude) the
  comparison silently false-rejected. Fixed via new
  `_eur_to_local_rate(fx_rates, discipline)` helper that uses
  PortfolioState.fx_rates (USD-per-unit). Math now runs in local
  currency throughout the lumpy-lot path.

Live verification: 1783 went qty=100 (rejected) → qty=1000 (filled
ibkr_id=3130 at 07:25 UTC), with diverse captured lots from IBKR
(1300=2000, 2565=50, 1783=1000, 3268=100). 8+8 tests across two
files cover the sizing tolerance + the Y117 contract preservation +
6 daytrade bracket tests that were already failing on HEAD for
the underlying invariant issue.

### Y150 + Y150b + Y150c — IBKR Error 201 → not_tradable blacklist (commits `4abd47f`, `ab789be`, `26fa206`)

After Y149 cleared lot-size rejections, 3046 and 3431 kept failing
with IBKR Error 201:

    Order rejected - reason: No Trading Permission, Customer
    Ineligible; This product does not have a KID in English or in
    a language approved for your country.

PRIIPs/KID regulation — packaged retail products without a Key
Information Document on file at IBKR are blocked for UK/EU retail
clients. Code-side workaround: blacklist the symbol so the
strategy stops trying.

Three-part discovery:

- **Y150**: hooked `LiveExecutor._handle_status` to scan
  trade.log for errorCode=201 and call `not_tradable_cache.record_not_tradable`
  on hit. Also added `/contracts/qualify` pre-check: blacklisted
  symbols return qualified=false without an IBKR roundtrip.
- **Y150b (debug discovery)**: live deploy traced statusEvent
  firing BEFORE errorEvent for IBKR server-side rejections. The
  trade.log codes are [0, 0] at statusEvent time; the 201 hadn't
  been appended yet. Initial bridge approach (reqId pending-set
  populated by errorEvent, consumed by statusEvent) didn't help
  because errorEvent always arrived too late.
- **Y150c**: web research (ib_async docs) confirmed errorEvent
  carries the contract object directly. Refactored to write
  not_tradable from the connection's errorEvent handler with full
  contract context (symbol/exchange/currency). The statusEvent
  trade.log check stays as backup for edge cases.

6 unit tests cover the trade.log detection + qualify pre-check.
The errorEvent direct-write path is untested live — HKEX session
ended at 08:00 UTC before the Y150c deploy could catch any fresh
201s. Will be verified next HKEX session.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y147-VENUE-IDS-BACKFILL-FROM-ACK** — the sink's
  OrderSubmittedV3 dispatch MUST UPDATE the orders row's
  ibkr_order_id / ibkr_perm_id. The pre-Y147 documented NO-OP was
  load-bearing.
- **L-Y148-DISCIPLINE-CONFIG-COMPLETENESS** — when adding a new
  Discipline enum value AND wiring its strategy, the three
  RiskLimits dicts must all receive an entry. Test guard exists.
- **L-Y149-LOT-SIZE-FX-AWARE** — lumpy-lot tolerance arithmetic
  must use local-currency for both the target and the lot
  notional. EUR-blind comparison falsely rejects HKD/JPY symbols
  by ~10×.
- **L-Y149-LOT-CACHE-FALLS-BACK** — the strategy's lot_size_lookup
  bulk cache loads once per exchange; per-symbol fallback to DB on
  cache miss is required so qualify-time UPSERTs are visible
  without daemon restart.
- **L-Y150-ERROR-201-IS-PERMANENT** — IBKR Error 201 with
  "Customer Ineligible" text is a permanent regulatory block for
  retail clients (PRIIPs/KID). Symbol gets 7-day not_tradable
  blacklist; operator action (KID acquisition or institutional-
  client upgrade) clears it.
- **L-Y150-ERROR-EVENT-IS-AUTHORITATIVE** — for IBKR server-side
  order rejections, errorEvent fires AFTER statusEvent. Detection
  must happen on errorEvent, not statusEvent. trade.log codes are
  unreliable at the statusEvent moment.

## §95 — Y151 + FTSE avg_cost FX-quality bug surfaced (2026-05-27 ~08:43 UTC)

Operator while checking /api/positions: "doesnt show everything and
the FTSE ones have the wrong pricing showing a huge loss. it doesnt
have any of the HK buys in there, please check the dashboard logic
for HK and japan to flow everywhere"

Two distinct issues found from one diagnostic.

### Y151 — dashboard HKEX/TSE discipline completeness (FIXED + DEPLOYED)

The dashboard's `/api/positions?engine=daytrade` was returning rows
for us/ftse/asx/crypto only — HKEX positions (1783, 2565, 2658) and
TSE positions were silently absent. Same "silent zero rows" failure
mode the dashboard's `engines.py` docstring (line 56-61) warns about.

**Root cause** — two parallel lists both missing the new disciplines:

1. `alphabot/dashboard/db_queries/engines.py::_disciplines_for_engine`
   — the candidates list for `engine='daytrade'` enumerated only
   us/ftse/asx/crypto_daytrade.
2. `alphabot/strategy/loss_stop.py::_DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES` — the
   frozenset used by `discipline_to_engine()` to classify a
   discipline string into an engine bucket. Without hkex_daytrade /
   tse_daytrade entries, `discipline_to_engine("hkex_daytrade")`
   returned the default (not "daytrade"), so the dashboard filter
   would also fail at classification time.

Same hazard family as the stops/crypto_stops parallel-table bug
(R5 reconciler) and the Y89 swing/_shared.py ↔ swing/crypto.py map
drift. Whenever a new discipline is added, the project has at least
THREE places that must be updated in lock-step — Y148 caught the
broker risk-config dicts; Y151 closes the dashboard + loss_stop gap.

**Fix** — added `hkex_daytrade` and `tse_daytrade` to both lists.
Test guard (`test_drop_y151_dashboard_discipline_completeness.py`,
2 tests) asserts both sides simultaneously to prevent future drift.

**Deployed** — commit da255c3 (2026-05-27 08:42 UTC), pushed,
dashboard restarted. Verified live: `/api/positions?engine=daytrade`
now returns 12 rows including HKEX 2658 / 1783 / 2565. TSE zero
rows is correct — no TSE positions opened yet (next session is
2026-05-28 00:00 UTC).

### FTSE pricing wildly wrong — diagnosed, NOT fixed (deferred to Y152)

Operator's second complaint: "FTSE ones have the wrong pricing
showing a huge loss." Diagnostic from `data/alphabot.db`:

| Symbol | qty | fills (native GBp) | stored avg_cost USD | expected USD @ FX=1.345 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PETS  |  3 | 193.1                | 2.23 | 2.60 | 0.86  (rate ~1.155) |
| PAGE  | 15 | 120.3 × 5            | 1.39 | 1.62 | 0.86  (rate ~1.155) |
| GNC   |  1 | 229.4 + 226.6        | 7.26 | 3.07 | **2.36** (rate ~3.18) |
| BOWL  |  5 | 281.5 × 5            | 7.88 | 3.79 | **2.08** (rate ~2.80) |

GNC + BOWL filled 07:35-07:50 UTC and stored at FX-rate-implied
~2.8-3.2 USD/GBP. PETS + PAGE filled 08:18-08:37 UTC and stored
at ~1.155. Live `fx_service.get_rate('GBP')` reads 1.345 now.

The conversion code path (`shared/price_conversion.py::native_price_to_usd`)
is correct: divide by units_per_major (100 for LSE/GBP), multiply
by `fx_service.get_rate(currency).rate`. So the bug is the
fx_service returning **bad rate values during the broker's early-
morning lifetime** — specifically during 07:30-08:00 UTC. By 08:18
the rate had improved (still slightly low) and by ~08:42 it was
correct. This implies stale-cache hydration or initial public-API
fallback returning a wrong rate, then self-correcting.

Position `avg_cost_per_share` is set-once at fill (or updated via
weighted-average on subsequent fills using whatever rate is current
at that moment). It is NOT corrected by the reconcile loop. So the
wrong-rate-at-fill-time poison is permanent until either the
position closes or a one-time UPDATE statement re-derives avg_cost
from the fills table using a corrected rate.

**Y152 (scoped, not yet built)** — two-part:
1. **Fix the source.** Audit `alphabot/shared/fx.py` to find why
   the FX rate was 2.0-2.4× too high at 07:30 UTC. Likely
   suspects: IBKR `reqHistoricalData` startup race, public_api
   fallback returning a bad pair (e.g. inverted), or cache
   pre-population with a stale value. Web-search recommended for
   ib_async FX-rate gotchas (per operator's standing instruction
   on IBKR integration matters).
2. **Heal the current data.** Recompute avg_cost for GNC + BOWL
   (and HKEX 1783 at ratio 0.85, which is also off though smaller)
   from the fills table using a vetted FX rate at fill time. One-
   off SQL UPDATE wrapped in a migration. Either that, or just
   accept the wrong-rate cost-basis through to position close —
   the realised P&L will reconcile against IBKR's own statements
   eventually, but the dashboard will keep showing a fake huge
   loss until then.

Operator decision on which path (heal-now vs accept-and-move-on)
required before Y152 ships.

## §96 — Y152 FX root cause + heal + Y152.1 follow-up (2026-05-27 ~09:10 UTC)

Followed up on §95 in the same session. Operator: "source-fix the
fx rate, then heal the data and also these. why is LSE only
streaming 5 tickers".

### Root cause (confirmed via direct IBKR probe)

Account `DUQ191770` is **EUR-base** (CashBalance EUR=250 000,
USD=−1666, BASE=287465). IBKR's `accountValues()` `ExchangeRate`
tag is quoted in **account base currency per foreign**, including
for the USD entry:

```
ExchangeRate USD = 0.8589   (EUR per USD)
ExchangeRate GBP = 1.1545   (EUR per GBP)
ExchangeRate AUD = 0.6145   (EUR per AUD)
ExchangeRate HKD = 0.1096   (EUR per HKD)
ExchangeRate EUR = 1.00     (trivially)
```

`shared/fx.py::_try_ibkr` read these as USD-per-foreign with no
account-base detection. Every non-USD position stored ~14% too
low (1.155/1.345 ≈ 0.86). Bug A.

### Fix (commit b6d304d)

Two-pass over `accountValues()` collecting the requested
currency's rate AND the USD anchor; renormalise:

```python
usd_per_foreign = ibkr_rate[foreign] / ibkr_rate[USD]
```

For USD-base accounts IBKR doesn't emit `ExchangeRate=USD`,
anchor defaults to 1.0, division is a no-op — backward
compatible. 2 new tests; 136-test FX-related regression sweep
green.

Verified live after broker restart 08:58 UTC:
- GBP 1.1545 → 1.3441 ✓
- AUD 0.6145 → 0.7155 ✓
- HKD 0.1096 → 0.1276 ✓
- EUR 1.0 → 1.1642 ✓ (had been wrong too — silent because EUR
  is the operator's account base, no positions in EUR)

### Reconcile interaction — second bug surfaced

After broker restart, `reconcile.py::_y35_avg_cost_to_usd`
pulled IBKR's `position.avgCost` and applied the now-correct
FX. But IBKR's `avgCost` includes **paper-account commissions
+ FX cross-currency sleeve fees** baked in:

```
PETS: raw fills £5.79 → IBKR avgCost £9.82 (×1.70)
GNC:  raw fills £4.56 → IBKR avgCost £12.55 (×2.75)
PAGE: raw fills £18.05 → IBKR avgCost £38.14 (×2.11)
```

Dashboard continued to show huge FTSE losses even with correct
FX, because the reconciled values had IBKR's all-in cost-basis
× correct FX = inflated USD.

### Heal (operator-approved 09:05 UTC, applied 09:06 UTC)

Single-shot UPDATE on `positions` table. For each non-USD
position with quantity > 0 and recent fills, computed
``avg_cost = sum(buy_qty × buy_native/units_per_major × current_fx) / sum(buy_qty)``.
7 of 10 healed; FCIT and KOS skipped (no buy fills in DB,
basis unavailable):

| Symbol | Pre | Post | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| GNC  | 8.4348 | 3.0652 | −63.7% |
| PAGE | 3.4173 | 1.6173 | −52.7% |
| PETS | 4.4007 | 2.5960 | −41.0% |
| 2565 | 1.2188 | 1.1945 | −2.0% |
| GNG  | 4.1327 | 4.0855 | −1.1% |
| APE  | 15.6241 | 15.4978 | −0.8% |
| 2658 | 7.7773 | 7.7210 | −0.7% |

Dashboard `/api/positions` confirmed showing healed values.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y152-IBKR-EXCHANGE-RATE-IS-BASE-PER-FOREIGN** — IBKR's
  `accountValues()` `ExchangeRate` tag is quoted in the account
  base currency per foreign, not always USD per foreign. Must
  read the USD anchor and renormalise. Test
  `test_y152_eur_base_account_renormalises_to_usd` asserts.
- **L-Y152-IBKR-AVGCOST-INCLUDES-COMMISSIONS** — IBKR's
  `position.avgCost` is the all-in cost basis (raw price +
  commission + FX cross-currency fees). For internal P&L
  purposes the bot's fills-derived basis is more accurate.
  Reconcile's auto-import path needs to know.

### Heal persistence problem (Y152.1, NOT BUILT)

Broker's in-memory PositionBook still has IBKR's inflated
values. IBKR also still reports the inflated avgCost. Reconcile
sees no drift → no DB overwrite. The heal will persist for the
current broker lifetime.

**But on next broker restart**, the broker's auto-import on
startup will reload positions from IBKR and overwrite the heal
back to inflated values. Y152.1 needs to either:

1. **Prefer DB's fills-derived basis** when available, falling
   back to IBKR's avgCost only for older positions with no
   fills (recommended).
2. **Subtract IBKR's commission overhead** from `avgCost` before
   applying FX. Needs the commission rate IBKR is charging
   (paper-account default).

Operator decision pending. Until Y152.1 ships: **do not restart
the broker** unless ready to redo the heal.

Not a bug. Lever for more LSE candidates: drop

### Y153 — dashboard native currency display (approved, NOT BUILT)

Operator-approved: show native + USD side-by-side on Holdings

### Y152.1 — reconcile prefers DB fills-derived basis

New helper `_y152_1_fills_derived_avg_cost` on `ReconcileLoop`:
- Walks fills chronologically for the symbol.
- On BUY: weighted-average (same formula as
  `PositionBook._add_to_long`), converting each fill's native
  price to USD via the canonical `native_price_to_usd` helper
  with the **current** FX rate (not historical).
- On SELL: reduces running qty, leaves running avg unchanged.
- Returns running avg when terminal qty matches IBKR-reported qty
  within 1e-6. Else returns None.

Wired into `_fetch_ibkr_positions`'s auto-import:
```python
fills_basis = self._y152_1_fills_derived_avg_cost(...)
if fills_basis is not None:
    usd_avg_cost = fills_basis
else:
    usd_avg_cost = self._y35_avg_cost_to_usd(...)  # IBKR fallback
```

### Y153 — dashboard native-currency display

`/api/positions` now includes per-row:

### Y153b — adaptive promotion floor for quiet venues

Operator brief verbatim: *"the promote score should only
dynamically drop if the ftse pool is under say 20 and only for
that session"*.

Implementation in `snapshot_engine.scan_once`:
```python
if market in ADAPTIVE_FLOOR_MARKETS and len(promotable) < 20:
    relaxed = [c for c in scored
               if not c.excluded and c.score >= 1.5]
    if len(relaxed) > len(promotable):
        promotable = relaxed
```

Constants: `ADAPTIVE_FLOOR_TARGET=20`, `ADAPTIVE_FLOOR_FALLBACK=1.5`
(matches `AWAKENING_BAND_LOW`), `ADAPTIVE_FLOOR_MARKETS=
{lse, asx, hkex, tse}`. US deliberately excluded — large universe
always populates; prevents pre/post-market quirks from accidentally
flooding US pool with low-quality candidates.

Hard-excluded candidates (penny floor, ADV floor, gap-bomb) never
bypass at any threshold. Per-scan only; next scan re-evaluates at
the default 2.5 floor.

**Live verification.** Adaptive floor wired but **didn't engage
today** — LSE scan at 09:22 had 6 promotable; the other 1186 LSE
names are hard-excluded by the penny floor (£1) and other Gate 0
filters. No candidates exist in the 1.5-2.5 awakening band today.
Mechanism is in place for days when scoring clusters in that band.

(Operator may want to revisit the LSE penny floor — £1 may be too
high if it excludes most of the awakening-band names. Filed as
implicit Y153c if it comes up again.)

## §99 — Y174 Cloudflare no-cache (2026-05-27 ~09:53 UTC)

Y153e Feed Engine "open markets to top" shipped to disk in §98
but the operator reported on both desktop + iPhone that the
reorder wasn't visible. Investigation:
- Local JS verified to contain the Y153e sort logic
- `node` execution of the sort against live API data produced
  the correct `[lse, crypto, asx, tse, hkex, us]` ordering
- Bumping `?v=y143.6 → ?v=y153f` cache buster didn't help

Root cause: Cloudflare on this operator's domain ignores query
strings for cache keying. Y143.6 → Y153f required a manual
Cloudflare purge every drop, which Y143.6 era flagged as Y174
(scoped, declined at the time).

**Fix.** Subclass `StaticFiles` in `routes_root.py` as
`_Y174NoCacheStaticFiles`. `get_response` override injects
`Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate` on every /static/*
response. Cloudflare respects origin Cache-Control and refuses
to cache. Browser may keep a local copy but must revalidate
with the origin, which sends fresh bytes whenever the file
ETag changes (which happens on every meaningful diff).

Trade-off: every page-load issues a request to origin for each
/static/* asset. Bandwidth ~50KB total (JS+CSS) and the dashboard
is single-operator-trafficked — a handful of requests per hour.
Worth it to eliminate the cache-bust dance permanently.

**Live verification.**
```
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8080/static/js/daytrade_terminal.js
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: no-cache, must-revalidate
etag: "800d61d012b2bb413ffa4d03258ea0ee"
```

**Operator one-time action.** Hard-refresh already-open tabs
(Cmd-Shift-R / Safari close+reopen on iPhone) to flush the
existing Cloudflare cache copy. After that, every future
dashboard drop ships immediately — no Cloudflare purge needed.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y174-STATIC-NO-CACHE-AT-ORIGIN** — `/static/*` MUST emit
  `Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate`. The
  `_Y174NoCacheStaticFiles` subclass at `routes_root.py:22` is
  the only path that mounts the static dir; any future static
  mount must follow the same pattern. Test
  `test_drop_y174_static_no_cache.py` asserts.

## §100 — Y153h + Y153i + Y153j (2026-05-27 ~10:08 UTC)

Three operator-flagged dashboard issues, one drop.

### Y153h — FTSE sizing was 100× undersized

Operator: "GNCs 2 trades today on FTSE were £5 and £2 positions.
what is making the positions so small? seems silly?"

Root cause in `daytrade/_sizing.py` (non-lot-aware path,
lot_size=1 which is every LSE single-share symbol):
```python
target_position_eur = portfolio_value_eur * target_position_pct
                      # USD-denominated despite the _eur suffix
                      # (per the existing line 685 comment)
target_qty = math.floor(target_position_eur / current_price)
                                              # NATIVE units (GBp for LSE)
```

For GNC at 224.7 GBp:
- `target_position_eur` = $248k × 0.005 = $1240
- `current_price` = 224.7 (in pence — 1/100 GBP)
- `target_qty` = floor(1240 / 224.7) = 5 shares
- After Y94d-3 gate multipliers (climax 0.6 × atr-high 0.6) → 1 share
- 1 share × 224.7 GBp = £2.247 — operator's "£2" complaint

The math should have been:
- `current_price_usd` = 224.7 / 100 × 1.345 = $3.022 per share
- `target_qty` = floor(1240 / 3.022) = 410 shares
- 410 × 224.7 GBp = £921 = 0.5% × $248k ✓

The lot-aware path (HKEX/TSE) had partial FX correction via Y149a's
`_eur_to_local_rate` but treated USD-as-EUR (also off by ~16% for
HKEX, smaller impact because HKD ≈ EUR magnitude). Same root cause.

Fix: new `_native_price_to_usd_for_sizing(native_price, discipline,
fx_rates)` helper. Maps discipline → (currency, units_per_major)
and computes:
```python
usd_per_share = native_price / units_per_major × fx_rate(currency)
```

Wired into the non-lot-aware sizing branch immediately after
`current_price` is read. Both `_supports_fractional_qty(discipline)`
and integer-share paths use it.

`_DISCIPLINE_LOCAL_CURRENCY` extended from {hkex, tse} to all 6
disciplines. `_DISCIPLINE_UNITS_PER_MAJOR` new table — only LSE
has a non-1 value (100). Fallback chain: if `fx_rates` is None,
divides by `units_per_major` so LSE doesn't stay 100× off even
on transient FX outage.

10 new tests cover all 5 equity venues + crypto + the
fallback-no-FX path. End-to-end test asserts GNC scenario produces
qty ≈ 410 instead of 5.

### Y153i — last_price prefers close over midpoint

Operator: "US holding MBC. price is wrong, closing price was 8.29."

Root cause: `broker/market_data.py::snapshot` priority chain was
`last → ib_async marketPrice (midpoint) → close`. For MBC at US
pre-market (10:00 UTC; US session 13:30-21:00) with stale wide
spread:
- `last`: None (no live trade)
- `bid`: $3.31, `ask`: $8.50 (stale, wide)
- `ib_async marketPrice`: (3.31+8.50)/2 = $5.905
- `close`: $8.29

The midpoint of a stale wide spread is meaningless; close is
authoritative when the venue is shut.

Fix: swap chain to `last → close → marketPrice → bid+ask midpoint`.
Close beats midpoint; midpoint is kept as last-resort for the
rare case where ib_async hasn't populated close yet (newly-listed
names mid-session).

Live-verified after broker restart: MBC `last_price: 5.905 → 8.26`.
The slight 8.26 vs operator-reported $8.29 is just the close-price
snapshot moment vs end-of-session — within tolerance.

2 new tests (the MBC scenario reproduced + the existing
falls-back-to-market-price test updated to require no-close
condition).

### Y153j — Snapshot cadence 30 → 15 min

Operator: "30 minutes for the snapshots is too long, please change
to 15."

`SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` default 1800 → 900. Updated three sites:
- `market_data_daemon/config.py` `_envint` default
- `market_data_daemon/snapshot_engine.py` `interval_s` default
- `tests/market_data_daemon/test_drop_y50a_config.py` baseline

Env var `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` override still works for ops
who want a different cadence.

Live-verified: `snapshot_engine: starting — markets=us,lse,asx,hkex,tse
interval=900s`.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y153h-SIZING-USES-USD-PER-SHARE** — the sizing function MUST
  divide USD-denominated target by USD-converted per-share price.
  Mixing target units (USD) with native price units (GBp / HKD /
  AUD) produces 100× errors on LSE specifically. The
  `_native_price_to_usd_for_sizing` helper is the canonical
  converter; tests cover all 5 equity venues.
- **L-Y153i-CLOSE-AUTHORITATIVE-WHEN-VENUE-SHUT** — `last_price`
  priority chain prefers close over midpoint. Midpoint of a stale
  wide bid/ask spread is meaningless before/after market hours.

## §101 — Y154a + Y154b (2026-05-27 ~10:42 UTC)

Operator: "BOWL on ftse is being blocked by max symbol daily cap.
but its only traded once". And separately: "desk stats only show
12 trades but we are up to 13 now".

### Desk-stats 12 vs 13

Triple-checked: trades table 12 (by opened_at AND closed_at);
/api/desk-stats `today.trades = 12`; /api/trades/recent returns
12. System internally consistent. The operator's "13" appears
to be off-by-one perception or a different widget; quoted source
needed for further investigation. No code change.

### BOWL was blocked by cap after one trade

**Root cause.** Pre-Y154 the per-symbol cap counter incremented
on every BUY submission. BOWL morning trace: 5 qty=1 BUY orders
submitted 30 sec apart because LSE limit-order matching sat
unfilled. PositionBook had no FILLED position yet so ALREADY_HELD
couldn't fire. Each successful submission bumped the counter.
After 5, the cap (`max_trades_per_symbol_per_day = 5`) fired.

From operator's view: 1 round-trip lifecycle (the BOWL morning
trade). From the system's view: 5 cap-bearing submissions. The
cap was meant to bound round-trips, not raw submissions.

### Y154a — IN_FLIGHT_BUY gate

- New ``SkipReason.IN_FLIGHT_BUY`` (string value
  ``"in_flight_buy"`` for analytics stability).
- ``PortfolioState`` gains ``in_flight_buys: frozenset[str]``.
- ``_build_portfolio_state`` queries the orders table per cycle:
  ```sql
  SELECT DISTINCT symbol FROM orders
  WHERE side='BUY' AND discipline=?
  AND execution_mode='paper'
  AND status NOT IN ('FILLED','CANCELLED','REJECTED','EXPIRED')
  ```
- ``decide_entry`` fires ``IN_FLIGHT_BUY`` between ALREADY_HELD
  and the per-symbol cap. Operator sees "still working" rather
  than "cap reached".

**Deploy hotfixes.** Two follow-ups needed during the live
verification:

1. **Bracket-submit counter increment missed** (`d551742`). The
   original `cf7873e` removed the in-memory increment on the
   OLD `_submit_order` path (line 2005) but missed a SECOND
   increment at the bracket-submit path (line 2485). The
   daytrade strategy uses brackets, so the counter was still
   bumping on submit. Fixed.

2. **`_settings` NameError** (`70c26f7`). The helper used
   `_settings.DB_PATH` but `_settings` was never imported into
   `_fetch_in_flight_buys`'s local scope. Every call raised
   `NameError` and the `except Exception` fail-open returned
   an empty set — the gate never fired in production. Caught
   by adding a temporary `log.info` showing
   `count=0` always, and elevating `log.debug` to `log.warning`
   on the exception path to expose the trace. Fixed by
   importing `from alphabot.shared.config import settings as
   _settings` inside the method (matches the pattern used at
   line 1455 and 637).

**Live-verified post-fixes (10:41:56 UTC cycle 5)**:
```
[daytrade_ftse_v1] BSIF sizing chain blocked: in_flight_buy
[daytrade_ftse_v1] GSF  sizing chain blocked: in_flight_buy
[daytrade_ftse_v1] BOWL sizing chain blocked: in_flight_buy
```

Plus held positions (PETS, GNC, JD., BRFI, LIO) still
correctly fire ALREADY_HELD. Both gates work in tandem.

### Y154b — counter from closed lifecycles

- `_count_entries_today_from_db` switched from
  `orders WHERE status='FILLED'` to `trades WHERE opened_at >= today`.
- One row per closed lifecycle = one cap unit.
- `_build_portfolio_state` re-queries per cycle so the counter
  reflects current DB state (closed-today trades + within-cycle
  lifecycle closes).
- Removed both in-memory increments (line 2005 and line 2485).
- Cap log line now reads "lifecycles_today" instead of
  "trades_today" for clarity.

Y90 test class renamed `TestDaytradeCapCountsFilledOnly →
TestDaytradeCapCountsLifecyclesOnly`. New tests insert into
`trades` instead of `orders` and assert counter=N for N
distinct closed lifecycles.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y154a-IN-FLIGHT-BLOCKS-DUPLICATE-SUBMITS** — the in-flight
  BUY set MUST be queried per cycle from the orders table
  (status NOT IN terminal). Bypassing it allows the 30-sec
  duplicate-submission pattern. Skip code ``in_flight_buy`` is
  stable for analytics.
- **L-Y154b-COUNTER-IS-LIFECYCLES-NOT-SUBMITS** — the per-symbol
  daily cap bounds CLOSED round-trips, not raw BUY submissions.
  In-memory increments on submit are forbidden in this counter;
  daemon re-reads DB per cycle.

## §103 — Y156 + Y157 (2026-05-27 ~11:10 UTC)

Operator surfaced three things together:
1. "i cant see any of that on the dashboard, no crypto fills or
   trades in last 2 hours"
2. "what is the gate in flight buy? it means its already queued
   at IBKR and in process of filling?"
3. "for in flight buy blocks, lets change the chip to FILLING
   and a different more subdued GREEN to the bright GREEN on
   FILL"

### In-flight explainer (verbal, no code change)

`IN_FLIGHT_BUY` fires when a BUY order has been submitted to the
venue (IBKR or Binance), accepted, and is sitting in
`SUBMITTED`/`WORKING` status — queued at the venue, on the
order book, awaiting a match. Three sequential states of the
same BUY's lifecycle:

```
strategy emits BUY
    ↓ submit
status=SUBMITTED  → IN_FLIGHT_BUY skip on next cycle
    ↓ match
status=FILLED     → position appears in book
                  → ALREADY_HELD skip on next cycle
```

### Y156 — crypto trade-row sync via listStatus synthesis

**Symptom (live).** ALTUSDT had 94 BUY fills today, 9
OCO_CLOSED entries in `crypto_stops`, but **only 1 row in the
`trades` table**. Recent Trades widget silent for crypto for
hours. Holdings showed `qty=0` for all crypto names (broker's
in-memory book actually was zero between OCO close and next
BUY cycle — a 30-second blind window each loop).

**Root cause.** `trade_tracker.on_fill` for the SELL leg of an
OCO close was wired to the WS executionReport handler
`_route_oco_sell_fill_to_tracker`. That signal is unreliable on
Binance testnet:
- Timing: arrives sometimes hundreds of ms after listStatus
- Drops: not every OCO leg generates an executionReport that
  reaches us
- Ordering: when both legs of an OCO are involved, only the
  FILLED leg generates a useful executionReport — and if it's
  missed, the round-trip never closes in the tracker

The `listStatus ALL_DONE` event IS reliable — we observe every
OCO close transition `crypto_stops.status` from ACTIVE to
TRIGGERED. So the close-detection signal exists; the gap was
turning it into a tracker entry.

**Fix.** Extended `_handle_list_status` to complement the WS
executionReport path:

```python
self._mark_oco_closed(...)
await self._y156_close_tracker_from_list_status(
    symbol=symbol,
    list_client_order_id=list_client_order_id,
    order_list_id=order_list_id,
    exit_reason=exit_reason,
)
```

The new helper:
1. Re-queries Binance for `orderReports` (sub-ms cached call)
2. Finds the leg with `status=FILLED`
3. Pulls `executedQty` + `cummulativeQuoteQty`, computes avg
   fill price
4. Looks up the open position via PositionBook
5. Constructs a synthetic `Fill(side=SELL, qty=executedQty,
   price=avg)` with `is_synthetic=True`
6. Routes through `trade_tracker.on_fill` with the resolved
   `intended_exit_reason` (TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS /
   USER_CANCELLED / OCO_CLOSED)
7. Fires `trade_complete_callback` → trades row written
8. Calls `_zero_position_after_oco_close` so the book + DB
   reflect closed state

**Idempotent.** If the WS executionReport beat us, the tracker
entry is already closed and `_position_book.get` returns None
— the helper no-ops cleanly. The reconcile sweep's RECONCILED-
synthesis path remains the final safety net.

**Live-verified.** Post-restart at 11:10 UTC, crypto trade rows
now creating: ALTUSDT + REQUSDT both have new rows with
TAKE_PROFIT / STOP_LOSS / RECONCILED exit reasons. Dashboard's
Recent Trades widget now shows crypto activity.

### Y157 — FILLING chip

JS `actionChip()` signature extended: now takes `gateName`.
When `event_type=BLOCKED` AND `gate_name=in_flight_buy`:
renders **FILLING** chip with subdued green `#6dc97a` (border
`#54a85e`). Sits visually between the saturated FILL
celebration chip (`#1bc26e` with glow) and the orange BLOCK
chip — reads as "the order IS at the venue and matching, just
hasn't completed yet".

Cache-buster `y155b → y157`. Y174 no-cache header means next
page-load picks up the new bytes without manual purge.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y156-LISTSTATUS-IS-OCO-CLOSE-AUTHORITY** — the
  `listStatus ALL_DONE` event is the reliable close signal for
  Binance OCO brackets. The WS executionReport for the SELL
  leg is a HELPFUL secondary signal but not load-bearing —
  Y156 complements it with the listStatus-based synth path.
  Idempotency between the two paths must be preserved (each
  checks `position_book.get` returns non-None before writing).

### Y157b — center FILLING chip text

`.act-chip` defaults `min-width: 46px` + `padding: 2px 6px`,
sized for FILL/SOLD/NEAR (4-5 chars). `FILLING` is 7 chars and
hit the right border. `.act-filling` override: `padding: 2px
10px` + `min-width: 60px`.

### Y158 — age cap on `_fetch_in_flight_buys`

**Live audit (11:14 UTC)** found 18 stuck in-flight symbols:
- PEPEUSDT submitted 7+ days ago, still `SUBMITTED`
- DCH.GBP submitted 5+ days ago
- 16 LSE/HKEX symbols from earlier today (07:00-10:30 UTC)

The broker never wrote the EXPIRED transition when the venue
cleared these at session end. Y154a's gate then perpetually
counted them, blocking new BUY submissions for those symbols.

**Fix.** `_fetch_in_flight_buys` SQL now includes
`AND submitted_at >= ?` with a 5-minute cutoff:

```python
in_flight_max_age_seconds = 300
cutoff = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(seconds=300)).isoformat()
# WHERE submitted_at >= cutoff
```

**Rationale on the 5-min cap.** Healthy order fill times:
- Binance MKT crypto: instant
- IBKR LMT in liquid name: <1-2 sec
- IBKR LMT thin LSE (BOWL morning case): up to ~3 min

The BOWL pattern Y154a was designed to catch was a 30-sec
duplicate-submit race. 5 min is generous enough to cover
worst-case slow LSE matches but tight enough that
genuinely-expired venue orders fall out of the gate.

The stale DB rows themselves aren't cleaned by Y158 — that's a
separate sweep task (Y158a future). Y158 just stops them
poisoning the gate.

**Live-verified post-restart.** In-flight gate set went
**18 stuck symbols → 2 genuinely-recent** (BSIF, VCT).
208 `in_flight_buy` rejections in the next 90s are all for
those 2 — genuine duplicate-submit blocks within the 5-min
window, no longer phantom blocks for week-old orders.

### Explainer (verbal, no code change)

Operator's "only 1 trade for ALT and REQ since Y156" is correct
but reflects the trade_tracker's architecture, not a Y156 bug.
The tracker treats one (symbol, execution_mode, experiment_id)
key as a single running round-trip:
- BUY when flat → opens an OpenEntry
- BUY when held → APPENDS to the existing entry's qty
- SELL when held → reduces qty, returns CompletedTrade when fully closed

For ALTUSDT today: 17 BUYs all appended to one OpenEntry, then
the OCO close zeroed everything in one shot → 1 CompletedTrade
→ 1 trades row. From the operator's mental model each OCO
cycle is a discrete "trade"; from the tracker's POV they're
all one running position with multiple entries.

**Y156a (future)** would split each scalp loop into its own
lifecycle by treating each (BUY-fill, OCO-attach, OCO-close)
sequence as a discrete round-trip. Bigger change to the
tracker's contract; not blocking on §104.

### Architectural locks attached

- **L-Y158-IN-FLIGHT-GATE-HAS-AGE-CAP** — `_fetch_in_flight_buys`
  must include the `submitted_at >= now() - 5min` filter so
  stale SUBMITTED rows can't poison the gate. Test
  `test_y158_old_submitted_orders_excluded_from_in_flight`
  asserts via source-code inspection.
