## §133 — Y-MKT-CAPS audit + locked per-market caps for the market swap (2026-05-29 ~09:30 UTC)

### Context

Operator scoped a market swap (TSE → Korea, FTSE → Germany,
ASX kept) plus a pluggable-market refactor (Y-MKT1) and an
optional dynamic regime-aware soft-cap layer (Y-MKT-DYN). The
Y207a.1 lock `L-Y207A1-CAPS-SUM-OBEYS-GROSS-CEILING` requires
the peak-overlap arithmetic to be shown before any cap is
committed — same lesson that caught Y207a's 82% Asia-overlap
mistake 20 min after deploy.

Y-MKT-CAPS is the doc-only kickoff: the audit table itself.
Lock it before any code drop in the Y-MKT chain ships.

### Deliverable

`docs/Y-MKT_CAPS_AUDIT.md` — 4-phase peak-overlap audit:

| Phase | Tightest window | Sum | Headroom vs 60% |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Current Y207a.1 baseline | US/EU overlap | 52% | 8% |
| 2 — Y-MKT2 dual-running (Korea + TSE coexist) | US/EU overlap | 53% | 7% |
| **3 — Y-MKT3 dual-running (Korea + Germany + TSE + FTSE coexist)** | **US/EU overlap** | **57%** | **3%** |
| 4 — Y-MKT4 steady-state (TSE + FTSE retired; Germany lifts to 10%) | US/EU overlap | 51% | 9% |

Locked per-market hard caps (every value that may be committed at each phase boundary):

| Setting | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Phase 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US daytrade | 25% | 25% | 25% | 25% |
| FTSE daytrade | 12% | 12% | 12% | — (retired) |
| ASX daytrade | 12% | 12% | 12% | 12% |
| HKEX daytrade | 10% | 10% | 10% | 10% |
| TSE daytrade | 10% | 10% | 10% | — (retired) |
| Crypto daytrade | 12% | 12% | 12% | 12% |
| **Korea daytrade** | — | **6%** | 6% | 6% |
| **Germany daytrade** | — | — | **4%** | **10%** |
| `MAX_GROSS_DEPLOYED_PCT` | 60% | 60% | 60% | 60% |

### Key constraint that drives the table

Phase 3 (Germany shipped, FTSE not yet retired) is the
operational risk window — only 3% headroom against the 60%
ceiling. The 4% Germany launch cap is what keeps Phase 3
inside the lock. Germany lifts to 10% in Y-MKT4 (same commit
that retires FTSE) and the headroom restores to 9%.

### Interaction with Y-MKT-DYN

Y-MKT-DYN's dynamic soft-cap layer operates strictly **inside**
the §8 hard caps. Bull regimes can push soft cap up to 1.5×
hard but clamped at the hard ceiling. Phase 3 in particular
is engineered with both layers in mind: even if every active
market simultaneously hits bull regime, the §8 caps are the
binding constraint, and the static peak-sum already
validates against 60%.

### Behavioural rule documented

`L-Y207A1-CAPS-SUM-OBEYS-GROSS-CEILING` is hereby **extended
through all four Y-MKT phases.** Any deviation from §8 — cap
tweaks, dynamic-policy bull-overshoot, "just for tonight"
emergency adjustments — must include a re-derivation of the
relevant phase's peak-overlap table demonstrating the 60%
ceiling still holds.

### Open item filed (non-blocking)

`gate_max_gross_deployed` semantics worth a one-cycle spot-check
before Y-MKT3 ships: confirm it counts residual positions the
same as active, and crypto alongside equity. Not blocking
Y-MKT1 / Y-MKT-DYN; filed in §10 of the audit doc.

### What this lock enables

* Y-MKT1 can ship as pure refactor knowing the cap values it
  reads from each MarketProfile at each phase are pre-approved.
* Y-MKT-DYN can ship its policy layer knowing the hard ceilings
  are pre-locked and can be assumed-immutable from the
  policy's perspective.
* Y-MKT2/3/4 each carry a one-line cap edit that has its
  cross-overlap impact already proven.

## §134 — Y-MKT-DYN spec revised: shared-pool allocator (2026-05-29 ~10:00 UTC)

### Context

Initial Y-MKT-DYN sketch proposed "static hard cap per market + regime-multiplied soft cap inside hard." Operator pushed back with a cleaner framing: "the engine just moves them around all the time to stay under 60% deployed and maintain our maximum positions limits; that math has to be respected all the time."

That formulation makes the bot-wide 60% / 69-position cap the **binding invariants**, and per-market caps become risk-concentration safety ceilings, not the primary allocator. Y207a.1 hard caps stay as ceilings; the dynamic allocator sits below them.

### Deliverable

`docs/Y-MKT-DYN_SPEC.md` — implementation spec for a shared-pool allocator that:

* Treats `MAX_GROSS_DEPLOYED_PCT` (60%) and `MAX_TOTAL_DAYTRADE_POSITIONS_HARD` (69) as global invariants enforced by construction.
* On every BUY evaluation: computes `free_budget = 60% - Σ deployment_now` and splits it across active markets by `share[M] = (base_weight[M] × regime_mult[M]) / Σ_active`.
* `base_weight[M]` = the Y-MKT-CAPS hard cap percentage (operator-vetted).
* `regime_mult` = bull 1.5 / chop 1.0 / flat 0.5 / bear 0.2.
* Per-market effective cap = `min(hard_ceiling, deployment + share × free_budget)`. Never lifts above hard ceiling.
* Residual markets (closed but holding positions): their deployment/positions count toward used budget; they don't compete for share.
* Regime flips must persist ≥30 min before honoured (no whipsaw).
* On cap-shrink, existing positions ride; only new BUYs blocked. Matches Y181/Y206.2/Y207b.6 cooldown pattern.
* Each `MarketProfile` declares its cap policy: `static` (default; today's behaviour), `dynamic_pool` (this allocator), `manual_override`. Operator opts in per market as confidence builds.

### Why this is cleaner

* The 60% invariant is enforced **by construction** — it's not a separate check that could drift; the share allocation literally cannot propose a BUY exceeding free budget.
* Quiet windows (e.g., US-only 15:30–20:00 UTC) genuinely unlock the budget for US instead of stranding it under per-market static caps.
* Crowded windows tighten naturally — Phase 3 dual-running has 5 markets sharing the 3% headroom, allocated by regime fitness.
* Same drop-back behaviour as `L-Y207A1-CAPS-SUM-OBEYS-GROSS-CEILING`; nothing in the dynamic layer can breach the hard caps from Y-MKT-CAPS.
* Rollback is one commit: flip every market back to `static` policy and behaviour reverts to today's Y207a.1 exactly.

### Acceptance tests required

Property tests asserting the three invariants hold across any sequence of (BUY proposal, regime flip, position exit); regime-smoothing test; residual-accounting test; cap-shrink behaviour test; byte-identical regression for markets left on `static` policy; dashboard surfacing test.

### Position in chain

Ships after Y-MKT1 (the pluggable-market refactor — needs `MarketProfile.cap_policy_ref` hook). May ship in parallel with Y-MKT2 Parts A–C (broker-agnostic Korea work) since they don't touch sizing.

### What Y-MKT-DYN inherits and what it adds

| Inherits from Y-MKT-CAPS | Adds |
|---|---|
| Hard ceilings per market per phase | Shared-pool allocator + share calculation |
| 60% / 69 invariants | Regime weighting + 30-min smoothing |
| `L-Y207A1-CAPS-SUM-OBEYS-GROSS-CEILING` | `L-Y-MKT-DYN-INVARIANTS-ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` |

### Behavioural rule documented

When Y-MKT-DYN ships, the rule extends: not only must per-market caps sum-under-60% at peak overlap, but **at every moment** the live allocator output must satisfy the three invariants (I1, I2, I3 from §2 of the spec). The acceptance property tests are the forcing function.

## §136 — Y-MKT-DYN core shipped: CapitalAllocator + cap_policy (commit `60f11fa`, 2026-05-29 10:30 UTC)

### Deliverable

`alphabot/shared/markets/allocator.py` — `CapitalAllocator` class implementing the spec at `docs/Y-MKT-DYN_SPEC.md`. Three companion dataclasses: `PortfolioState` (live deployment + position counts per market), `AllocationDecision` (allocator output with effective cap + share + regime + ceiling-binds flag).

`MarketProfile.cap_policy` field added. Three values:
* `static` — default; returns `profile.cap_pct` directly. Zero behaviour change.
* `dynamic_pool` — share of live free budget weighted by `cap_pct × regime_multiplier`, clamped at `cap_pct`.
* `manual_override` — operator dashboard knob, bounded by `cap_pct` ceiling.

`Settings.REGIME_MULTIPLIERS` and `Settings.REGIME_STABILIZATION_MINUTES` added. Defaults: bull 1.5 / chop 1.0 / flat 0.5 / bear 0.2 with a 30-min stabilization window. Inert until a market flips to `dynamic_pool`.

### Three invariants enforced by construction

I1 (Σ deployment ≤ 60%) and I2 (Σ positions ≤ 46) are enforced **outside** the allocator by the existing `gate_max_gross_deployed` + `gate_max_total_positions` broker gates. The allocator constructs caps that, by share construction, cannot propose a BUY exceeding free budget. I3 (per-market hard ceilings) is enforced via `min(profile.cap_pct, …)` in every policy path.

### Zero behaviour change today

Every market on the registry defaults to `cap_policy="static"`. The allocator's `_static_decision` returns `profile.cap_pct` unchanged. Until operator opts a market into `dynamic_pool` or `manual_override`, the allocator is provably equivalent to today's static behaviour.

### 24 same-drop tests

`tests/test_drop_y_mkt_dyn_capital_allocator.py`:

* Static-policy zero-behaviour-change (parametrized across all 6 markets)
* Dynamic-pool share math under chop/bull/bear regimes
* Hard-ceiling clamp (I3) — even with 100% share in bull, effective cap ≤ profile.cap_pct
* Cap-shrink without force-trim — closed/inactive markets keep deployment as cap
* Regime smoothing — flip-then-revert inside the 30-min window is ignored
* Warmup behaviour — first-sighting returns "chop" (neutral default)
* Manual-override clamp — operator can't accidentally exceed the hard ceiling
* Residual accounting — closed-market positions count toward used budget, don't compete for share
* Free-budget / free-slot math exact, floored at zero
* Property-style invariant check across multiple (regime, deployment, positions) combos
* Unknown policy → explicit ValueError

All 24 pass. Regression: zero new failures across the broader suite.

### Out of scope (deferred to a follow-up drop)

The strategy sizing chain integration is not yet wired. The strategy still reads from `Settings.DAYTRADE_<MARKET>_CAP_PCT` directly. Wiring becomes a no-op so long as every market stays on `static` (the default), which makes it a safe follow-up: ship allocator → operator reviews math → wire into strategy → flip markets one at a time.

### Locks added

* `L-Y-MKT-DYN-INVARIANTS-ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` — every BUY proposal the allocator produces satisfies I1 / I2 / I3 by construction. The bot-wide gates are defence-in-depth, not the primary enforcement.
* `L-Y-MKT-DYN-STATIC-IS-DEFAULT-AND-REVERSIBLE` — every market defaults to `cap_policy="static"`. Rollback from any future opt-in is one commit flipping the field back. No state migration required.

## §138 — Y-MKT-DYN.2 live PortfolioState aggregation shipped (commit `f4feada`, 2026-05-29 10:30 UTC)

### Context

Y-MKT-DYN.1 shipped the strategy wiring with an empty PortfolioState scaffold (correct for static policy; insufficient when a market flips to dynamic_pool). Y-MKT-DYN.2 replaces the scaffold with a live aggregation helper. Zero behaviour change today — every market still on `cap_policy="static"` — but the moment any market flips, the shared-pool maths reads the accurate state.

### Deliverable

New static method on `DayTradeStrategyBase`:

```python
_build_allocator_portfolio_state(state, max_gross_pct, max_total_positions) -> PortfolioState
```

Iterates `state.all_positions`, groups by market via `MARKETS.values() → discipline → market_key`, and computes:

* `deployment_pct_by_market[m]` = `Σ |market_value| of m's positions / NLV`
* `positions_by_market[m]` = count of held positions in market m

Skips non-daytrade disciplines (swing / smallcap / scalp). Falls back to `|quantity| × avg_cost` when `market_value` is None (last price unknown). Defensive: NLV ≤ 0 returns empty (avoids divide-by-zero; allocator falls back to chop-default shares).

### The SizingConfig site is now:

```python
_alloc_state = self._build_allocator_portfolio_state(
    state,
    max_gross_pct=_settings.MAX_GROSS_DEPLOYED_PCT,
    max_total_positions=_settings.MAX_TOTAL_DAYTRADE_POSITIONS_HARD,
)
```

Static-policy decisions ignore PortfolioState fields entirely → byte-identical to pre-Y-MKT-DYN.2. Dynamic-pool decisions read the live values.

### 10 same-drop tests

* Correct deployment_pct + position count per market
* Multiple positions per market aggregate
* Non-daytrade disciplines skipped (us_swing / us_smallcap / us_scalp)
* NLV=0 defensive empty return
* `market_value=None` falls back to cost basis
* Short positions count via `abs(market_value)` — visibility into oversold-into-short class
* Static-policy robust to live state (zero behaviour change verified end-to-end)
* Dynamic-pool consumes live values (US flipped to dynamic_pool, decision reflects deployment + share + hard ceiling)
* Source pin on _base.py SizingConfig site

121/121 Y-MKT chain tests pass.

### Live state at deploy (~10:30 UTC)

* Strategy restarted, active. All 6 daytrade subclasses register.
* First post-restart cycle: FTSE 43 scans / 39 signals — clean.
* No errors from the helper's per-cycle aggregation.
* LUNCUSDT NOTIONAL filter errors continuing (pre-existing crypto dust position; unrelated to Y-MKT-DYN.2).

### Locks added

* `L-Y-MKT-DYN-2-LIVE-PORTFOLIO-STATE-AGGREGATED-FROM-POSITIONS` — the helper builds `deployment_pct_by_market` and `positions_by_market` from `state.all_positions` filtered to daytrade disciplines. CI test asserts the structure.
* `L-Y-MKT-DYN-2-SKIP-NON-DAYTRADE-DISCIPLINES` — swing / smallcap / scalp positions do not contribute to the daytrade allocator's view. Test enforces.

### What's now ready

Any market can be flipped from `cap_policy="static"` to `cap_policy="dynamic_pool"` via a one-line edit to its profile factory in `shared/markets/registry.py`. The allocator will immediately use the live deployment_pct + positions_by_market from `_build_allocator_portfolio_state`. No daemon code change required, no schema migration, no behaviour change for other markets (which stay static).

Rollback = one line back to `"static"`.

## §141 — Y-SCORE-US chain shipped: two-score AND fire model live for US (commits `b561e3b` → `18142d6`, 2026-05-29 afternoon)

Eight-commit chain that converts US daytrade from the legacy
binary-with-grading-bonus model to a two-score AND model, then
adds the dashboard surface + activity-stream filtering rules
the operator clarified during the US session.

### Why now

5-day analysis (export at commit `5af1506`, 2026-05-29 morning)
showed US trades clustering bimodally at `entry_score` 6 and 8-9
with a dead zone at 7 — the structural artefact of binary-then-
grading scoring where each gate contributes either 0 (fail) or
1+ (pass with curve bonus). The per-gate attribution was already
half there but mis-shaped: failed gates zeroed out instead of
contributing a graded value, and the composite "score >= 6"
fire condition was effectively a re-encoding of binary AND.

Operator spec (via Claude cousin) reshaped the framing mid-session
from "convert binary to scored" to "correctness + instrumentation
pass on an already-scored system" once the existing `score_passes`
path was surfaced. Per-gate independence (no blending into a
composite) was added by operator clarification — "two separate
scores keep the per-gate attribution clean".

### The deltas

Sequence shipped: B → C → F → A → F.1 → F.2/F.3 (D + E + G remain).

| Delta | Commit | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **B** | `b561e3b` | Two-score telemetry. `eligibility_passed`, `rvol_score`, `vwap_score` surface on `GatePipelineResult` + `DayTradeEvaluation`. Binary 10/0 placeholders. Logs `Y-SCORE-B: ...` per would-fire. No fire-decision change. |
| **C** | `2dc9f59` | Smooth 0-10 per-gate maps. RVOL anchors at 1.5/2.0/3.0/5.0 → 0/2/5/8/10. VWAP anchors (distance in ATR units as sigma-proxy) at 0/0.5/1.5/2.5/4.0 ATR → 0/3/7/10/5 (taper). Linear interpolation between anchors. Filled the dead `entry_score` 7-bucket. |
| **F** | `5bfec6f` | Dashboard two-score chip on NEAR events. Adapter appends two synthetic `dt-rvol-smooth` + `dt-vwap-smooth` `GateResult` rows so smooth scores persist to `signal_gates` via the existing wire — no migration. JS `gateChip()` dispatches: smooth scores present → `twoScoreChip("RVOL x.xx . VWAP y.yy")`; absent → legacy `gateLeds`. Per-pill colour relative to per-market mark (green ≥ mark / orange within 2.00 below / red beyond — band width 2.00 fixed so colour rule works after delta D moves the mark). Settings `US_DAYTRADE_RVOL_PASS_MARK` + `US_DAYTRADE_VWAP_PASS_MARK` default 5.0 each. |
| **A** | `e05575b` | US-only fire decision flip. `_us_fire = eligibility_passed AND rvol_score >= rvol_mark AND vwap_score >= vwap_mark`. Legacy `score_passes OR all_passed` path GONE for US; other markets keep legacy until their own Y-SCORE drops ship. Journal tag `(entry=two-score)` on US WOULD-BUY. |
| **.env override** | `13:27 UTC` | Operator override of placeholder default. `US_DAYTRADE_VWAP_PASS_MARK=3.5` appended to `.env` to admit candidates as close as ~0.625 ATR above VWAP (vs 1.0 ATR at default 5.0). Stated intent: "i want to see action and the stop losses to do their job." RVOL kept at 5.0. |
| **F.1** | `18ff215` | Dashboard NEAR-stream eligibility filter. Operator rule: "unless they pass the binary gates, they dont make it on to the activity stream." SQL `NOT EXISTS` clause excluding signals where any of `dt-catalyst` / `dt-atr-pct` / `dt-regime` failed. Universal across markets. ~21% reduction in NEAR rows over the last hour (68087 → 53729). |
| **F.2 + F.3** | `18142d6` | NEAR-stream "almost fired" rule. Operator clarification: at least one smooth score must be within ±2.00 of its mark (F.2) AND the signal must not have actually fired (F.3 — at least one smooth still below mark). Replaces the legacy Y135.1 `passed >= total - 2 AND passed < total` heuristic which broke at gate-count drift (5 → 7 with the synthetic rows). |

### Architectural decisions / locks

* **L-Y-SCORE-US-TWO-SCORE-AND-PER-GATE** — RVOL and VWAP each get their own 0-10 score and their own per-market pass mark. Fire = AND of both clearing their own marks. Per-gate attribution is the whole point: operator can query "which gate killed this trade" and "what would dropping VWAP's mark have captured" directly. No blending into a composite — that destroys attribution. Operator clarification mid-session overrode the original spec's combined-score framing.
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-ELIGIBILITY-PRE-FILTER** — `catalyst + atr_pct + regime` are a hard binary AND pre-filter. A candidate failing any of these is a hard reject regardless of how strong the smooth scores look. BRKR (this US open: rvol_smooth 5.84 + vwap_smooth 6.29 but atr_pct 0.55% + no-catalyst) is the canonical example.
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-SMOOTH-MAPS-INDEPENDENT** — each signal gate's 0-10 mapping is module-local in `daytrade_gate_pipeline.py` (`_smooth_rvol_score` / `_smooth_vwap_score`). Independently tuneable. Anchors are research-backed starting points, not edge — delta D's calibration is what makes them load-bearing.
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-LEGACY-TOTAL-SCORE-PRESERVED** — `DayTradeEvaluation.total_score` continues to sum only the 5 legacy `dt-*` gate scores (binary 0/_DT_GATE_PEAK). The two synthetic `dt-rvol-smooth` / `dt-vwap-smooth` rows are EXCLUDED from this sum so every existing consumer (analytics, near-miss tier classifier, capture writers) keeps the same number it always did.
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-A-IS-US-ONLY** — A's two-score AND fire decision applies only when `self.market_name == "us"`. FTSE / ASX / TSE / HKEX / crypto stay on the legacy `score_passes OR all_passed` path until their own Y-SCORE drops ship. Cross-market parity is the long-term goal but per-market calibration is required first (each market has its own gate-block patterns per the 5-day near-miss data).
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-DASHBOARD-FILTER-RULE** — NEAR activity-stream rows require ALL of (F.1) eligibility passed + (F.2) at least one smooth score within ±2.00 of its mark + (F.3) at least one smooth score below its mark (didn't actually fire). Marks pulled from Settings; other markets reuse US marks as universal reference until their own Y-SCORE drops ship. Universal across markets so the rule is consistent.
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-PAPER-IS-EXPERIMENT** — operator override of spec §1 "do not hand-pick a round number" guidance. In paper mode the experiment IS the calibration; ship A with 5.0/3.5 placeholders and let the data tell us. Memory `feedback_paper_mode_discovery` cited (paper is information gathering, not safety).
* **L-Y-SCORE-US-FX-DEFERRED-σ-IS-ATR** — VWAP smooth uses distance in ATR units as a sigma proxy rather than true rolling stdev of price-vs-VWAP. Avoids a new data-pipeline dependency. Refinement to true sigma deferred.

### Acceptance

Same-drop tests across the chain:
* B: 18 tests (eligibility / score fields / threading)
* C: 32 tests (anchor exactness / floor / cap / monotonicity / vwap peak+taper / missing-data / pipeline integration / legacy total_score unchanged)
* F: 8 tests (synthetic rows / Settings / per-market lookup)
* A: 10 tests (AND semantics / eligibility short-circuit / mark sensitivity / boundary)

Total: 68 same-drop tests pass. Y94 pipeline regression: 39/40 pass (pre-existing `test_gate_pipeline_disabled_by_default` failure unrelated; Y94 default-state assertion stale since 2026-05-23). Two Y94 assertions updated in delta F to accept the new gate names (`dt-rvol-smooth` / `dt-vwap-smooth`) per CLAUDE.md §3.

### Operationally — live state

* US daytrade fires through the two-score AND model as of 13:30 UTC US open (delta A's first cycle).
* Settings live: `US_DAYTRADE_RVOL_PASS_MARK=5.0` (Python default) + `US_DAYTRADE_VWAP_PASS_MARK=3.5` (.env override).
* First US fire under the new model: ESTC at 13:35:17 UTC — qty 24 @ $57.76, stop $56.89, TP $59.50, ibkr_id 47146. Stopped out at 13:36:08 UTC (-$4.80, 30s hold). Exactly the "stop loss does its job" data the operator asked to see.
* BRKR canonical "eligibility-fail veto": rvol_smooth 5.84 + vwap_smooth 6.29 (both clear marks) but atr_pct 0.55% + no-catalyst → eligibility=False → blocked. Legacy model would have fired BRKR at score=6.
* MSFT + ~30 other US symbols stuck out of session universe via qualify-storm at exact open instant 13:30:13 UTC (separate filed item — not Y-SCORE-related).
* Dashboard restart picked up F + F.1 + F.2 + F.3 in lockstep with the strategy restart for A. Cloudflare cache caveat applies — operator must purge `/static/js/daytrade_terminal.js` and `/static/daytrade_terminal.css` to see the new chip.

### Position in chain

### Per-market follow-ups (separate drops)

Y-SCORE-FTSE / ASX / TSE / HKEX / CRYPTO each need:
1. Per-market gate audit (eligibility / signal split differs per market per the 5-day near-miss data)

Recommended order (from spec): FTSE → ASX → TSE → HKEX → crypto (equity markets sharing gate helpers first; HKEX needs care as the worst-bleeding desk; crypto last as the gate set differs most).

## §142 — Y-LIVE-DATA + Y-RECONCILE spec + Y-LINE-UTIL (1/2/3) chain shipped: dashboard now tells the truth about IBKR market data (commits `05a4340` → `84e79ee`, 2026-05-29 afternoon)

Twelve-commit afternoon arc spanning three concerns the operator surfaced live during the US session: stale market data, DB↔IBKR drift, and paid IBKR-line under-utilisation. Each was a forensic dive into "the dashboard is lying to me" — different lies, all real.

### Why now

US session opened 13:30 UTC under the Y-SCORE-US two-score AND model (§141). The operator investigated stuck SMCX/PTIR/IPO/EVOK BUY limit orders and found three compounding issues:

1. The bot had been consuming **15-minute delayed IBKR market data for 33 days** despite an active live subscription. Strategy was sizing orders against 15-min-stale prices; by the time orders hit IBKR the real ask had drifted past the limit.
2. The broker daemon's `order_registry` lost track of pending entry LMTs on restart even though Y204's hydration arc handled positions + stops + daily counters — exposed when 9 SMCX/PTIR/IPO/EVOK orders couldn't be cancelled via the API after a restart.
3. Operator's IBKR Quote Booster tier supports **200 concurrent market data lines** but the bot was using **~27** (held positions only). 173 paid lines were idle.

The dashboard surfaced none of this — every position tile showed a "live" price as if the data was real-time, the IBKR-line utilisation was invisible, and stale prices had no visual signal. Operator's words 2026-05-29 afternoon: *"the dashboard absolutely HAS to tell me the truth."*

### The deliverables

| Commit | Drop | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `05a4340` | **Y-LIVE-DATA** | `alphabot/broker/market_data.py` was hardcoding `reqMarketDataType(3)` ("delayed-with-fallback") since the initial repo upload at `89c26f7` on **2026-04-26** — **33 days on delayed data**. Honours `settings.IBKR_MARKET_DATA_TYPE` now. Operator added `IBKR_MARKET_DATA_TYPE=1` to `.env`. Live ticks flowing within seconds of broker restart. |
| `96d2e3c` | **Y-RECONCILE spec** | `docs/Y_RECONCILE_SPEC.md` — five-drop chain (G1–G5) closing the DB↔IBKR drift gaps Y204 missed: broker entry-LMT rehydration, drift detector loop, orphan SELL bracket cascade-cancel, Error 201 backpressure, TSE Warning 399 closed-session handling. **Spec only — no code.** Tasks 57-61 filed for next session. |
| `978c356` `81b6a81` `e82ce87` `41cc99b` | **Y-LINE-UTIL.1** (+ 3 hotfixes) | 200-line master pool subscription engine. The broker now computes the top-200 ranked candidates across all 5 equity markets every 5 minutes and reconciles the IBKR subscription set against that + held positions. Pacing 1/sec per IBKR's `reqMktData` watchlist guidance. First refresh added 195 lines in 3m30s. Live-tested two hotfixes — initial `getattr(self, '_db_path')` lookup always returned None (use `settings.DB_PATH` directly); initial query used a correlated subquery that ran 79k× and hung the event loop (CTE rewrite + `asyncio.to_thread` fixed both). |
| `85778f1` `352c8af` | **Y-LINE-UTIL.2** (+ hotfix) | Dashboard truth surface — broker writes `var/master_pool_state.json` atomically after each refresh; `/api/health/services` reads it; new header chip `LN X/200` with by-market tooltip + last-refresh churn. Hotfix dropped an inline `from datetime import` that shadowed the module-level binding via Python's local-name rule (strategy chip earlier in the function raised `UnboundLocalError`). |
| `a8488b9` | **Y-LINE-UTIL.2.1** | **Inclusive cap**. Original algorithm pinned held positions ON TOP of the 200-line pool producing up to ~225 streams (218 in production at the time). Operator: *"inclusive cap then 3"*. Reordered to held → per_market → remainder all within `max_lines`. Live now: chip reads `LN 200/200` exactly. Also fixed held-position venue/currency defaulting to SMART/USD (mis-routed FTSE/ASX/HKEX/TSE held subscriptions); broker now extracts venue + currency from each Position's Instrument and passes it through. |
| `84e79ee` | **Y-LINE-UTIL.3** | Price staleness on every position chip. `_format_position_from_db` gains `price_age_s` (seconds since `live_price_cache.refreshed_at`); JS tints amber 30–89s, red ≥90s; hover shows exact age. Helper `_price_age_seconds()` is reusable. Closes the last "live price" lie — operator can no longer mistake a 60s-old tile for current. |

### Architectural decisions / locks

* **`L-Y-LIVE-DATA-HONOUR-SETTINGS`** — `MarketDataSubscriber` calls `reqMarketDataType(int(settings.IBKR_MARKET_DATA_TYPE))` on first subscribe; never hardcoded. Wishful comment ("IBKR upgrades silently") proven wrong — type 1 (LIVE) is what real-time entitlement requires. Logs the active mode at INFO level on the first call so the operator can grep the journal.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-INCLUSIVE-CAP`** — total IBKR subscriptions NEVER exceed `MAX_IBKR_LINES`. Held positions take priority within that budget (we own them, we need their ticks); per-market quota and remainder fill the rest.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-MASTER-POOL-PRIORITY`** — selection order: (1) held positions, (2) per-market top-N quota, (3) remainder by score across all markets. Symbols in step 1 keep `source="held_position"` even when they'd rank into the per-market band — for dashboard differentiation.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-PACING-1HZ`** — `ensure_subscribed_for_targets` paces subscribes at 1/sec per IBKR's `reqMktData` watchlist guidance. Even on failure the pacing tick consumes the budget (IBKR counts attempts).
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-OFF-LOOP-SQLITE`** — synchronous `sqlite3.execute` calls inside an asyncio coroutine block the event loop and hang every other task. The master pool refresh runs the SQLite work via `asyncio.to_thread`. Pattern applies to any future broker async task that touches the DB.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-CTE-OVER-CORRELATED-SUBQUERY`** — the original master pool query used a correlated subquery (`SELECT MAX(snapshot_at) FROM ranked_candidates rc2 WHERE rc2.market = ranked_candidates.market`) which ran once per row on a 79k-row table. CTE rewrite that pre-computes the latest snapshot per market in one pass: 30s timeout → 0.19s. Don't put correlated subqueries on `ranked_candidates`; use CTEs.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-TRUTH-IS-SNAPSHOT-FILE`** — the broker writes a singleton `master_pool_state.json` next to `DB_PATH` after every successful refresh. Atomic via `NamedTemporaryFile` + `os.replace`. Dashboard reads it in `/api/health/services`. Schema kept narrow so this ships without a DB migration; refactoring to a DB table is a Y-RECONCILE-class follow-up.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-PRICE-STALENESS-30-90`** — JS tints prices amber at `>= 30s` and red at `>= 90s`. Under the broker's 60s flush cadence, 30–89s is the **expected** steady-state band; ≥90s genuinely indicates a problem (broker down, cache stuck, flush failing). Thresholds pinned in `test_stale_band_thresholds_document_js_rule` so JS and test never drift.
* **`L-Y-LINE-UTIL-DATETIME-MODULE-LEVEL-ONLY`** — never re-import `datetime` (or any other module-level binding) inside a function in `routes_daytrade_terminal.py`. Python rule: any name assigned within a function is treated as local everywhere in that function, so earlier references to the same name raise `UnboundLocalError`. The strategy-chip block surfaced this exact bug at `352c8af` ship time.

### Live verification

* **Live data**: `live_price_cache` flag `is_delayed=0` on 129 of 130 rows in the 2-minute sample. Direct price-drift confirmation: ADSK moved $0.82 in 60 seconds, BRCK moved 0.15 in 60 seconds — real ticks flowing.
* **Master pool**: refresh log `master_pool: refreshed +176 / -0 (target=200 held=24 pool=176)` at 16:27:49 UTC; chip shows `LN 200/200` with `asx:44 held:24 hkex:55 lse:20 tse:37 us:20` distribution.
* **Price staleness**: `/api/engines/daytrade/positions` returns `price_age_s` per row — crypto positions at 18.8s (fresh, no tint), IBKR-side positions at 42.7s (amber tint, expected under 60s flush cadence).

### Operationally — live state at session close

* `IBKR_MARKET_DATA_TYPE=1` in `.env` (operator override 2026-05-29 ~14:08 UTC).
* `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300` in `.env` (operator override 2026-05-29 ~14:46 UTC — 15-min snapshots → 5-min).
* Master pool refreshing every 5 min on the broker's `_market_data_reconcile_loop`. `master_pool_state.json` updated each cycle.
* Diagnostic log line `market-data reconcile tick: iter=N flush_due=X pool_due=Y held=Z` is verbose. **TODO next session**: gate behind a debug flag or remove once steady-state confirmed.
* 9 stuck SMCX/PTIR/IPO/EVOK BUY orders manually DB-cleaned mid-session — Y-RECONCILE.2's drift loop will prevent this from accumulating again once shipped.

### Operator quotes captured

* *"why are we using delayed data i am subscribed"* — exposed the 33-day regression.
* *"the dashboard absolutely HAS to tell me the truth"* — drove Y-LINE-UTIL.2 + .3.
* *"i want 200 ALL THE TIME. top ranked from the 5 minute snapshots. a reasonable amount in and out each time. then when theres 3 markets, all their best qualified go into a master pool and we take the top 200 best, 20 top from each market and then top remainder regardless of market."* — locked as the master pool algorithm specification.
* *"inclusive cap then 3"* — Y-LINE-UTIL.2.1 + Y-LINE-UTIL.3 in two words.

## §144 — Y-RECONCILE.3 shipped: orphan SELL bracket cascade end-to-end regression + DB backfill script (commit pending, 2026-05-30)

### Scope

Y207b.2 (2026-05-29) already wired the live cascade — when a bracket parent's `OrderRejectedV3` / `OrderCancelledV3` reaches the dispatcher, the surviving `_stp` and `_tp` children get explicit `asyncio.create_task(registry.cancel(child_coid))` calls inside the same event-loop turn. Pre-Y207b.2 tests covered the *static* `compute_bracket_children_to_cancel` computation (Y207b.2's own file). Y-RECONCILE.3 closes the remaining two gaps from `docs/Y_RECONCILE_SPEC.md §4`:

1. **End-to-end regression test** (`tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_3_cascade.py`, 5 cases) — constructs a `OrderRegistry` with a recording-stub executor, simulates the dispatcher path verbatim (`on_cancel_event` / `on_reject_event` → `compute_bracket_children_to_cancel` → `asyncio.create_task(registry.cancel(...))`), and asserts both children's COIDs reached `executor.cancel`. Covers CANCEL path, REJECT path (TSE-storm class), already-terminal sibling skip, no-children-registered no-op, and the parent-terminal-before-enumerate ordering invariant.

2. **One-shot DB backfill** (`scripts/backfill_y_reconcile_3_orphan_brackets.py`) — walks the `orders` table for `_stp` / `_tp` children with `side='SELL'` and `status IN ('SUBMITTED','ACCEPTED')` whose parent COID has `status IN ('CANCELLED','REJECTED','FILLED')` and marks them `CANCELLED` with `rejected_reason='Y-RECONCILE.3 backfill — parent {status}'`. DRY-RUN by default; requires `--commit` (approval-gated per CLAUDE.md §6). IBKR-side cancel deliberately NOT attempted — orphans date from 2026-05-28/29 sessions, DAY orders are already venue-terminal, and GTC live-at-IBKR cleanup belongs to `scripts/y169_cleanup_orphans.py` run separately.

### Live orphan count as of dry-run (2026-05-30 morning)

| Parent status | Orphan SELL children |
|---|---|
| CANCELLED | 18,326 |
| REJECTED | 3,752 |
| FILLED (no open position) | 479 |
| **Total** | **22,557** |

83 SUBMITTED-parent children correctly excluded — those are still-in-flight brackets, not orphans.

(The morning report's "4,249" figure was *all* SUBMITTED SELLs without the parent-terminal join; the real orphan count is 5× larger.)

### Deferred from spec

Spec §4 def-of-done #3 (drift-reconciler cascade) — blocked on Y-RECONCILE.2 (DB↔IBKR drift detector loop) which doesn't exist yet. Will land in Y-RECONCILE.3.1 once Y-RECONCILE.2 ships.

### Architectural lock

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.3-CASCADE-PINNED** — the parent-terminal cascade (`compute_bracket_children_to_cancel` → `asyncio.create_task(registry.cancel(...))`) is now regression-pinned end-to-end in `test_drop_y_reconcile_3_cascade.py`. Any refactor that decouples `on_cancel_event` / `on_reject_event` from the cascade enumeration must keep the post-event-state-mutation → enumerate-children → cancel-each ordering or the smoke test will fail. The Y207b.2 source-pin test (greps main.py for the helper name) remains as the cheap regression — this file adds behavioural cover on top.

## §145 — Y-RECONCILE.3.2 shipped: nightly orphan-bracket sweep wired as J13 brain rule (commit `5a5a5dd`, 2026-05-30 07:18 UTC)

### Scope

Closes the operator's nightly-vs-hourly question that surfaced immediately after the Y-RECONCILE.3 backfill landed. Verdict: **nightly is correct, hourly is overkill** — post-Y207b.2 the live cascade fires synchronously inside the broker dispatcher, so steady-state should be zero new orphans per day. The nightly sweep doubles as a **canary**: any hit above the configured WARN threshold means the live cascade has regressed somewhere.

### Architecture

The sweep is a new J-rule (J13) inside the existing 10-minute brain `sweep` loop. It's gated by two short-circuits so it costs nothing 23h59m per day:

1. **Trigger window** — only fires when `now.hour == ORPHAN_BRACKET_SWEEP_UTC_HOUR` (default 0) AND `now.minute < 35`. The 35-minute window absorbs sweep-tick jitter (SWEEP_INTERVAL_S=600).
2. **Once-per-day idempotency** — checks `system_alarms` for `rule_key = 'ORPHAN_BRACKET_SWEEP:YYYY-MM-DD'`. Past the first run, subsequent ticks in the window return immediately.

When the gates open, the rule calls the shared `alphabot.db.orphan_brackets.find_orphans()` SQL, flips any orphans to CANCELLED via `apply_terminal_state()`, and writes the day's alarm.

### Alarm semantics

| Condition | Severity | passed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count == 0` | INFO | True | Idempotency row written; today is done |
| `0 < count <= threshold` | INFO | True | Cleanup ran; nothing concerning |
| `count > threshold` | WARN | False | **Canary** — live cascade has regressed |
| outside window | n/a | True | No-op, no SQL, no alarm |
| already-ran today | n/a | True | No-op, no SQL, no alarm |

Default threshold is 50 (`BRAIN_ORPHAN_BRACKET_SWEEP_WARN_THRESHOLD`). 50 is generous because Y207b.2 was overnight-stress-tested down to zero; anything above 50 in a single sweep is genuinely abnormal.

### Shared SQL truth — Rule 2 anti-drift defence

The orphan-finder SQL was deliberately moved out of `scripts/backfill_y_reconcile_3_orphan_brackets.py` into a new shared module `alphabot/db/orphan_brackets.py`. The script and the J13 rule both import from there. This closes the explicit Rule 2 hazard family — parallel SQL in two callers (script + brain rule) would silently diverge over time, exactly the bug class CLAUDE.md §2 calls out.

The two callers pass different `reason_prefix` values (`"Y-RECONCILE.3 backfill"` for the one-shot, `"Y-RECONCILE.3.2 nightly sweep"` for J13) so historical UPDATEs stay forensically distinguishable. The 22,557 rows from the 2026-05-30 06:28 UTC one-shot will always be tagged differently from anything the autonomous loop writes from here on.

### New settings

* `BRAIN_ORPHAN_BRACKET_SWEEP_HOUR` (default `0`) — UTC hour the rule fires in.
* `BRAIN_ORPHAN_BRACKET_SWEEP_WARN_THRESHOLD` (default `50`) — count above which the alarm escalates to WARN.

### Verified

* 8/8 new tests PASS (`tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_3_2_nightly_sweep.py`).
* Combined regression sweep (Y-RECONCILE.3 cascade + Y207b.2 mirror + Y95.1.3 sweep + Y169 orphan sweep + this drop): 50/50 PASS.
* Backfill script post-refactor dry-run against live DB: **0 orphans** — the morning's --commit + the live Y207b.2 cascade have steady-state'd.
* Brain restarted clean (2026-05-30 07:18:45 UTC). Synchronous `run_sweep_once()` reports `rules=6` (was 5 pre-Y-RECONCILE.3.2) confirming J13 is wired. Outside the trigger window during this test so the rule's contribution is the expected zero.

### Architectural locks

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.3.2-SHARED-SQL** — the orphan-finder + apply helpers live in ONE module (`alphabot/db/orphan_brackets.py`). Any future tweak that adds a SQL branch must go through there so both callers (script + J13) inherit it together. Parallel SQL is forbidden by Rule 2.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.3.2-SEVERITY-CANARY** — WARN above the configured threshold is intentionally the live-cascade-regression alarm. Raising the threshold without investigating the regression source defeats the canary's purpose; tune the threshold downward over time as Y207b.2's robustness is proven, never upward to silence a real signal.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.3.2-WINDOW-GATED** — the once-per-day window check + alarm-key idempotency are both necessary. The window check prevents J13 from running every 10 minutes; the alarm-key check prevents a second run if the broker restarts mid-window. Either guard alone leaks one of those failure modes.

### Files

* `alphabot/db/orphan_brackets.py` (new, shared module)
* `alphabot/brain/loops/sweep.py` (J13 added; settings imports extended)
* `alphabot/brain/settings.py` (two new settings)
* `scripts/backfill_y_reconcile_3_orphan_brackets.py` (refactor — imports from shared module)
* `tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_3_2_nightly_sweep.py` (new, 8 tests)
* `docs/DECISIONS_V3_2.md` (this entry)

## §146 — Y-RECONCILE.1 shipped: startup rehydration of pre-restart open orders (commit `9c3c50a`, 2026-05-30 07:40 UTC)

### Scope

Closes the half-gap Z2 (2026-05-11) left open. Z2 pulls a DB row into the in-memory `OrderRegistry` when a strategy *re-submits* the same COID after a broker restart — that path covered re-attached stops because the strategy resubmits them every cycle. But **entry LMTs** sit at IBKR untouched after their original submission: the strategy doesn't resubmit them, so the DB-replay-on-submit path never fires, and `POST /orders/cancel` returned 404 for any pre-restart entry-LMT COID.

Y-RECONCILE.1 adds a startup-time pass that fetches `reqAllOpenOrdersAsync()`, walks every IBKR open order's `orderRef` (= our COID), and seeds the registry from the matching DB row. After the pass, the API can cancel anything IBKR is showing as open.

### Architecture

New module `alphabot/broker/registry_rehydration.py`. One entry point: `rehydrate_registry_from_ibkr(registry, db_path, ibkr_coids) -> RehydrationReport`. For each COID:

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| already in registry | idempotent skip (hot-restart race where Z2 has repopulated it) |
| no DB row | WARN + leave unmanaged (manual TWS placement / row lost to pre-Z3 crash) |
| DB row terminal | WARN + leave alone (canonical drift case — Y-RECONCILE.2's territory) |
| DB row unparseable | WARN + leave unmanaged (one bad row must not abort the whole pass) |
| DB row SUBMITTED / PARTIAL | build OrderIntent, build OrderState with `is_replayed_idempotent=True`, insert into `_orders` + `_open_order_ids` |

Wiring in `broker/main.py` adds one block after the existing stops reconcile, before Y167's universe preload. Wrapped in try/except so rehydrate failure doesn't break the rest of startup.

### Live verification (2026-05-30 07:40 UTC restart)

```
Y-RECONCILE.1: rehydrate complete — ibkr_open=308 rehydrated=205
                                   already=0 no_db=0 terminal=103 unparseable=0
```

* **205 entries newly manageable** that the broker would have 404'd on cancel for, pre-Y-RECONCILE.1.
* **103 IBKR-still-alive-but-DB-CANCELLED** rows surfaced. These are the orphan `_stp`/`_tp` children whose parents the morning's backfill terminalised (per parent status) but IBKR didn't actually cancel — they're sitting working at the venue. **Y-RECONCILE.1 correctly flags them as drift and leaves them in DB hands; Y-RECONCILE.2 will drain them.**
* 0 unparseable, 0 missing-DB-row.

### Lock added

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.1-DB-ANCHORED** — the reconstruction reads from the DB, not from IBKR's `trade.order` fields. The strategy/analytics layer depends on canonical `Instrument` / `Discipline` / `strategy_name` that only the DB has. An IBKR-only order (manual TWS placement) is deliberately left unmanaged.

### Verified

* 7/7 new tests PASS — happy path, idempotency, no-DB-row, terminal-DB-row, unparseable, empty-input, hot-restart-race preservation.
* Regression sweep across Y-RECONCILE.1/.3/.3.2 + Y207b.2 + Z2 idempotency: 44/44 PASS.
* Lint clean.
* Broker restarted clean 2026-05-30 07:40:02 UTC. No errors from Y-RECONCILE.1 code in journal; the 7 errors emitted are pre-existing TSE Error 201 / Warning 399 storm (Y-RECONCILE.4 / .5 territory) and 3 stale `StopPlacementError` races (separate pre-existing bug).

### Files

* `alphabot/broker/main.py` (46 LOC added — post-HEALTHY rehydrate block)
* `tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_1_entry_lmt_rehydration.py` (new, 7 tests)
* `docs/DECISIONS_V3_2.md` (this entry)

## §147 — Y-RECONCILE.5 shipped: TSE Warning 399 closed-session handling (commit `83ed715`, 2026-05-30 07:57 UTC)

### Scope

The pre-Y-RECONCILE.5 TSE retry loop visible in the live broker journal during TSE off-hours was loud and bad: every strategy cycle re-emitted SELL EXITs for each TSE position that needed exit, IBKR responded Warning 399 + Error 201 + Cancelled, the registry marked `OrderCancelledV3`, counters fired, the strategy retried next cycle, same noise. Y-RECONCILE.5 carves Warning 399 out of the `Cancelled`-status handler so those cancellations are semantically distinct from real failures.

### Architecture (per spec §6)

* **`alphabot/broker/closed_session_tracker.py`** (NEW) — pure helpers, no global state. `WARNING_399_PHRASES` mirrors the Y207b.3 transient superset (single source of truth for "this cancel is venue-side housekeeping, not a real failure"). `parse_warning_399_resume_time(msg)` extracts the timestamp and applies a locale → UTC offset lookup; tolerates multi-word locales (Hong Kong, Europe/London, US/Eastern). `find_warning_399_resume_time(trade)` walks `trade.log`; returns parsed UTC resume_at, or now+1h fallback if phrase present without timestamp, or None if no Warning 399 anywhere. `trade_log_has_warning_399(trade)` is the cheap pre-check.

* **`alphabot/broker/events.py`** — new dataclass `OrderClosedSessionQueuedV3(at, client_order_id, symbol, side, resume_at, reason, execution_mode, experiment_id)`.

* **`alphabot/broker/orders.py`** — `OrderState` gains `closed_session_queued_until: datetime | None = None`. New registry method `on_closed_session_queued_event` marks the field without flipping status to terminal (status stays SUBMITTED, COID stays in `_open_order_ids`). `_working_mkt_sell_qty_by_symbol` drops orders whose `closed_session_queued_until` has passed so the strategy's next cycle can re-emit with a fresh COID.

* **`alphabot/broker/executor_live.py`** — in `_handle_status` Cancelled branch, when `trade_log_has_warning_399(trade)` is True: skip Y150 not-tradable misclassification (Error 201 here is a retry-storm artefact, NOT a KID issue — Y-RECONCILE.4 will fix Error 201's real semantics when it ships), skip `OrderCancelledV3` emit (so loss-streak / discipline-pause / panic-monitor counters DON'T fire), emit `OrderClosedSessionQueuedV3` with the parsed resume_at, log INFO once. The carve-out runs BEFORE the existing OrderCancelledV3 emit and BEFORE Y150 — order matters and is asserted by a source-pin test.

* **`alphabot/broker/main.py`** — dispatcher routes `OrderClosedSessionQueuedV3` to `registry.on_closed_session_queued_event`.

### Live verification (2026-05-30 07:57 UTC restart)

| Metric | Pre-deploy (07:39 UTC) | Post-deploy (last 5 min) |
|---|---|---|
| TSE EXIT retries per symbol | 15 / 10 min | 3 / 5 min (= 1 cycle then quiet) |
| `status='Cancelled'` for SELL TSE/HKEX | dozens | 0 |
| Y-RECONCILE.5 explicit fires | n/a | 0 (yet) |

The retry loop **is gone** — but Y-RECONCILE.5 isn't the primary path absorbing it. Y207b.3's existing Inactive-status suppression is catching the entire flow at the earlier `Inactive` status, so the `Cancelled` status (where Y-RECONCILE.5 hooks) is never reached for these. Y-RECONCILE.5 is acting as the structural backstop for the case where IBKR transitions the order all the way to Cancelled after a Warning 399 — which will happen eventually as orders age and the 15-cap saturates differently. The architecture is correct; live load isn't currently exercising the new path. That's fine.

### Verified

* 15/15 new tests PASS — parser (Japan, Hong Kong, unknown-locale, no-match), detector + finder + 1h fallback + phrase-set guard, registry handler (state mark, unknown-COID safety), working-qty filter (in-flight before resume, dropped after resume), source-pin guards for the executor + dispatcher.
* Combined regression sweep: 59/59 PASS across Y-RECONCILE.1/.3/.3.2/.5 + Y207b.2 + Z2 idempotency.
* All new files lint-clean. Pre-existing baseline lint in `executor_live.py` (N806 / RUF003 / RUF006 on Y207b.3 / Y7 / Y150 code) unaffected.

### Architectural locks

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.5-WARNING-399-MEANS-QUEUED** — Warning 399 in `trade.log` IS NOT a real failure. The executor must NEVER emit `OrderCancelledV3` / `OrderRejectedV3` / Y150 `_maybe_record_not_tradable` for these. Any future refactor that adds new error-string handling in the Cancelled branch must keep the Warning 399 carve-out as the FIRST branch.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.5-RESUME-TIME-IS-UTC** — the parser returns UTC. The locale lookup converts FROM exchange-local. Storing as exchange-local would silently misroute the working_qty filter by hours.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.5-SUBMITTED-WHILE-QUEUED** — orders in the queued state keep `status=SUBMITTED` so the strategy's normal in-flight check applies. `CLOSED_SESSION_QUEUED` was deliberately NOT added to `OrderStatus` enum — the flag on `OrderState` is sufficient and avoids a schema migration / cross-module status-enum proliferation.

### Locale-map follow-up

The post-deploy journal surfaced `Australia/NSW` as an ASX locale token. Y-RECONCILE.5's locale map has `Australia/Sydney` and `AEST` but not `Australia/NSW`. The eventually-correct fallback (treat unknown locales as UTC) means ASX-queued orders retry 10h early, hit Warning 399 again, block for another hour — functionally correct but inefficient. Add `Australia/NSW: 10` (and probably `Australia/Victoria`, `Australia/Queensland`) to `_LOCALE_OFFSET_HOURS` in a follow-up Y-RECONCILE.5.1 once we see what other locale tokens IBKR emits across the venues we support.

### Files

* `alphabot/broker/closed_session_tracker.py` (new, 166 LOC)
* `alphabot/broker/events.py` (+31 LOC — new event)
* `alphabot/broker/orders.py` (+54 LOC — OrderState field, registry handler, working_qty filter)
* `alphabot/broker/executor_live.py` (+105 LOC — Cancelled-branch carve-out, imports)
* `alphabot/broker/main.py` (+10 LOC — dispatcher branch)
* `tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_5_warning_399.py` (new, 15 tests)
* `docs/DECISIONS_V3_2.md` (this entry)

## §148 — Y-RECONCILE.2 shipped + Y-RECONCILE.2.1 backfill drained 4,941 historical drift rows (commits `bc0d245` + script run, 2026-05-30 08:09–08:13 UTC)

### Scope

Y-RECONCILE.2 (spec §3): the structural backstop. New broker daemon loop running every 60s post-HEALTHY compares DB `orders.status='SUBMITTED'` against IBKR's `reqAllOpenOrdersAsync()` snapshot; rows in DB but absent from IBKR (and older than 60s) get flipped to `CANCELLED` with `rejected_reason='drift_reconciled'`. Catches silent IBKR cancellations, Error 201 rejections the executor missed, broker-restart races, manual TWS cancels of bot orders.

Six safety guards (the operator-trust earners):

1. Connection HEALTHY check — degraded connection skips the cycle.
2. `reqAllOpenOrdersAsync` exception → skip cycle, log WARN.
3. 60s floor on `submitted_at` — fresh submits not yet in IBKR snapshot are untouched.
4. Y-RECONCILE.5 carve-out — orders with `closed_session_queued_until` set are skipped.
5. Circuit breaker — `BROKER_DRIFT_DETECT_MAX_PER_CYCLE=100` default; cycle skipped + CRIT logged if exceeded. Catches "IBKR returned glitch-empty snapshot" failure mode.
6. Kill switch — `BROKER_DRIFT_DETECT_ENABLED=false` in `.env`.

The loop deliberately bypasses `on_cancel_event` when mirroring the change into the in-memory registry — counters (loss-streak, discipline-pause, panic-monitor) MUST NOT increment, drift reconciliation is bookkeeping, not failure.

### Live deploy + Y-RECONCILE.2.1 backfill

First cycle post-deploy at 08:09 UTC fired the breaker:
```
Y-RECONCILE.2: circuit breaker — 5034 drift candidates exceeds max_per_cycle=100
```

Working exactly as spec'd. The 5,034 was real historical drift (5,147 SUBMITTED − 311 IBKR-open − Y-RECONCILE.5 carve-outs). Y-RECONCILE.2.1 (one-shot backfill `scripts/backfill_y_reconcile_2_drift.py`) drained the backlog under operator approval at 08:13 UTC:

| Stage | Count |
|---|---|
| BEFORE | 5,147 SUBMITTED |
| Updated | 4,941 (10 batches of ~500) |
| AFTER | 357 SUBMITTED |
| Tagged `drift_reconciled` | 4,941 |

The script reuses `alphabot.broker.drift_detector._read_submitted_rows` so the SQL is a single source of truth — Rule 2 anti-drift defence. Connects with `clientId=1` (read-only) so the live broker keeps running on `clientId=0`. Wider 1h floor than the live loop's 60s.

### Architectural locks

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.2-CIRCUIT-BREAKER-IS-MANDATORY** — the max-per-cycle check is the only thing between a glitch-empty IBKR snapshot and a blanket DB cancellation. Raising the threshold without first diagnosing why a cycle is producing > N candidates defeats the guard.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.2-BYPASSES-COUNTERS** — the detector flips `state.status` directly, NEVER through `on_cancel_event`. Drift is bookkeeping; counters that fire on real cancellations must stay quiet.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.2-Y5-CARVE-OUT-IS-BIDIRECTIONAL** — Y-RECONCILE.5 sets `closed_session_queued_until`; Y-RECONCILE.2 reads it to exclude. Either drop changing its understanding of that field must update the other.

### Verified

* 11/11 new drift-detector tests PASS.
* Combined regression 70/70.
* Lint clean. Pre-existing baseline noise in config.py unaffected.

### Files

* `alphabot/broker/drift_detector.py` (new)
* `alphabot/broker/main.py` (+40 LOC startup + shutdown wiring)
* `alphabot/shared/config.py` (+27 LOC four new settings)
* `tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_2_drift_detector.py` (new, 11 tests)
* `scripts/backfill_y_reconcile_2_drift.py` (Y-RECONCILE.2.1, new)

## §149 — Y-RECONCILE.5.2 shipped: extend Warning 399 carve-out to Inactive branch + stale_cutoff exemption (commits `ccaa2fa` + `5e69832`, 2026-05-30 08:47–08:50 UTC)

### Scope

The Y-RECONCILE.2 deploy at 08:09 surfaced 149-185 drift candidates per cycle in steady state. Forensic at 08:40 UTC traced the source: Warning 399 orders never reach the Cancelled status in production — IBKR keeps them at `status='ValidationError'` (the **Inactive** branch in `executor_live._handle_status`), which is where Y207b.3 silently suppresses `OrderRejectedV3` without setting `closed_session_queued_until`. After 5 min, `_working_mkt_sell_qty_by_symbol`'s stale_cutoff drops the order; the strategy sees no in-flight; it re-emits with a fresh COID; the cycle repeats every 5 min per held TSE position. ~2/min net new SUBMITTED rows; eventually IBKR drops some venue-side and the drift detector catches the remains.

**`/orders` endpoint confirmed at the time of diagnosis: 300 SUBMITTED orders in the registry, ZERO with `closed_session_queued_until` set** — proof that Y-RECONCILE.5's Cancelled-branch carve-out was never firing in live operation.

Two changes:

1. **`alphabot/broker/executor_live.py` Inactive branch** — before the existing Y207b.3 silent-suppress, check `trade_log_has_warning_399(trade)`. If true, parse the resume time (with the 1h fallback) and emit `OrderClosedSessionQueuedV3`. Falls through to the existing Y207b.3 path for non-Warning-399 transient phrases (`no_error_code`, "Market is closed", "outside regular trading hours") — those don't carry a resume time and treating them as queued would lie about state.

2. **`alphabot/broker/orders.py` `_working_mkt_sell_qty_by_symbol`** — closed-session-queued orders are exempt from the 5-min stale_cutoff until `resume_at` passes. Ordering: queue flag checked FIRST. If set and resume hasn't passed → count as in-flight regardless of stale_cutoff. If set and resume passed → drop. If no flag → fall through to the original stale_cutoff (no regression for non-queued orders).

3. **`alphabot/broker/api/_models.py` + `_helpers.py` follow-up** — expose `closed_session_queued_until` via the `/orders` endpoint so the operator can see which holds are queued vs actively working. Field was being set internally; just missing from the wire format.

### Live impact

| Metric | Pre-deploy (08:46 UTC) | Post-deploy (08:55 UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| Drift growth rate | 1.5/min net | ~0 (224 → 224 / cycle) |
| Y-RECONCILE.5.2 fires | 0/min | ~10/min |
| `/orders` with `closed_session_queued_until` set | 0 / 300 | 17 / 227 (growing) |
| Strategy retry loop on TSE off-hours | active (~2/min new EXIT submits per position) | gated (each symbol's first flag stops the loop) |

The 224 floor is pre-fix legacy state that the live loop's breaker still won't touch. Two paths to drain: (a) re-run the backfill script periodically, (b) wait for IBKR's venue-side queue to expire (June 1 for the Warning-399 horizon — `BROKER_DRIFT_DETECT_MAX_PER_CYCLE` will accept the smaller deltas naturally then).

### Architectural locks

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.5.2-INACTIVE-IS-WHERE-IT-LIVES** — the Cancelled-branch carve-out from Y-RECONCILE.5 ships but is the rare-path. Production reality is the Inactive branch. Any future refactor of `_handle_status` must preserve the Warning-399 carve-out at BOTH status branches.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.5.2-STALE-CUTOFF-EXEMPTION-IS-OPT-IN** — only orders with `closed_session_queued_until` set get the stale_cutoff exemption. Unflagged orders MUST still be dropped at 5 min — otherwise legitimately-stale orders (broker crash mid-cycle, ib_async lost callback) would never time out from the strategy's working_qty view.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.5.2-WIRE-FORMAT-INCLUDES-FLAG** — the `/orders` API must surface `closed_session_queued_until`. Without it the operator and dashboard can't tell queued holds from actively-working ones.

### Verified

* 7/7 new tests PASS.
* Combined regression 61/61 + the Y-RECONCILE.5 tests still 22/22 → no Y-RECONCILE.5 regression.
* Lint clean.
* Live observation 90s post-restart: 16 Y-RECONCILE.5.2 fires, 17 orders flagged in registry, drift count plateaued at 224.

### Files

* `alphabot/broker/executor_live.py` (+48 LOC — Inactive branch carve-out)
* `alphabot/broker/orders.py` (+38 LOC — stale_cutoff exemption)
* `alphabot/broker/api/_models.py` (+8 LOC — new optional field)
* `alphabot/broker/api/_helpers.py` (+8 LOC — state_to_response passes the field)
* `tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_5_2_inactive_branch.py` (new, 7 tests)

## §150 — Y-RECONCILE.4 shipped: per-(symbol, side) IBKR 15-cap pre-submit gate (commit `755009c`, 2026-05-30 09:06 UTC)

### Scope

Last item in the Y-RECONCILE chain. The structural backstop for any future emit pattern that re-creates the Error 201 storm condition Y-RECONCILE.5.2 quietens. Pre-submit gate that rejects when in_flight count for (symbol, side) is at the configured threshold (default 14, one below IBKR's 15-per-contract-per-side cap, leaving headroom for round-trip races).

### Architecture

* **`alphabot/shared/config.py`** — new setting `BROKER_IBKR_ORDER_CAP_PER_SYMBOL_SIDE: int = 14`. Threshold lives here so a future real-money deploy can adjust without code changes.

* **`alphabot/broker/order_types.py`** — two new `BrokerContext` fields:
  * `in_flight_buy_count_by_symbol: dict[str, int]`
  * `in_flight_sell_count_by_symbol: dict[str, int]`
  Distinct from `working_buy_qty_by_symbol` / `working_sell_qty_by_symbol` which sum *quantities* — IBKR's cap counts *orders*.

* **`alphabot/broker/orders.py`** — new helper `_in_flight_count_by_symbol_side()` returns the two count dicts. Wired into `ctx` alongside Y181's working_mkt_sell map in `submit()`. Includes closed-session-queued orders (Y-RECONCILE.5.2 flag) — IBKR keeps them in its queue and counts them against the cap. Gate name `gate_ibkr_order_cap` added to `_RISK_GATE_NAMES`.

* **`alphabot/broker/risk.py`** — new `gate_ibkr_order_cap` function. Placed in `GATES` right after `gate_duplicate_order_id`, before the expensive sizing gates, so a cap-out short-circuits the rest. Rejects with structured reason `"ibkr_order_cap_reached symbol=X side=Y in_flight=N cap=M"`.

### Live impact

The 09:06 UTC deploy followed Y-RECONCILE.5.2 by ~16 min, by which point the closed-session-queued retry loop was already gone. So the gate **deploys dormant**:

| Metric | Pre-Y-RECONCILE.4 (post-.5.2) | Post-Y-RECONCILE.4 |
|---|---|---|
| New TSE EXIT submits since restart | 0 (.5.2 was working) | 0 (still 0) |
| `gate_ibkr_order_cap` rejections | n/a | 0 |
| Error 201 in journal | 0 (.5.2 had quenched) | 0 |

This is the **best possible outcome**: Y-RECONCILE.5.2 prevents the symptom (over-emit during closed sessions); Y-RECONCILE.4 is the structural safety net for any future code path that could recreate the over-emit. Cap is provably correct via 12/12 isolated tests; live broker has nothing to gate against because the upstream fix is doing its job.

### Verified

* 12/12 new tests PASS:
  - below-threshold allow
  - at-threshold reject with structured forensic reason
  - BUY/SELL/symbol independence
  - settings tunability
  - terminal orders excluded
  - closed-session-queued included
  - source-pins on both `_RISK_GATE_NAMES` and `GATES` tuples
  - submit-path ctx wire-up source-pin
* Regression sweep: 126/127. The one failure (`test_default_limits_total_deployed_matches_plan`) is PRE-EXISTING baseline noise verified via `git stash` round-trip.
* Lint clean on all new files. 9 baseline lint errors in `config.py` / `orders.py` / `risk.py` are pre-existing.
* Broker restarted clean 2026-05-30 09:07:01 UTC.

### Architectural locks

* **L-Y-RECONCILE.4-CAP-COUNTS-ORDERS-NOT-SHARES** — the gate uses COUNTS via `in_flight_buy_count_by_symbol` / `in_flight_sell_count_by_symbol`. Don't conflate with the `working_buy_qty_by_symbol` / `working_sell_qty_by_symbol` maps which sum quantities; IBKR's 15-cap is per order, not per share.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.4-CLOSED-SESSION-COUNTS-TOWARD-CAP** — the Y-RECONCILE.5.2 queue flag does NOT exempt orders from this count. Queued orders consume IBKR cap slots; treating them as exempt would let the cap silently overflow.
* **L-Y-RECONCILE.4-PER-SIDE-INDEPENDENT** — BUY and SELL caps are separate. Never combine the maps.

### Files

* `alphabot/shared/config.py` (+13 LOC — new setting)
* `alphabot/broker/order_types.py` (+18 LOC — two new ctx fields)
* `alphabot/broker/orders.py` (+35 LOC — helper + ctx wire-up + _RISK_GATE_NAMES entry)
* `alphabot/broker/risk.py` (+65 LOC — gate function + GATES tuple entry)
* `tests/test_drop_y_reconcile_4_ibkr_order_cap.py` (new, 12 tests)
* `docs/DECISIONS_V3_2.md` (this entry)

| Y-RECONCILE.2 | ✅ shipped | DB↔IBKR drift detector loop |

## §151 — Y-RECONCILE.5.1 + Y-RECONCILE.3.1 shipped: chain wrap (commits `0e1a4bf` + `959f38b`, 2026-05-30 09:15–09:21 UTC)

### Y-RECONCILE.5.1 — locale map widening (commit `0e1a4bf`)

The 2026-05-30 08:50 UTC ASX FAR rejection journal carried `Australia/NSW` which the pre-.5.1 map didn't recognise. Pre-fix the parser fell through to UTC, putting `resume_at` 10h too early — eventually-correct (strategy retries early, IBKR rejects, backs off again) but inefficient.

`_LOCALE_OFFSET_HOURS` extended:

| Token | UTC offset | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Australia/NSW` | +10 | AEST (from live journal) |
| `Australia/Victoria` | +10 | AEST |
| `Australia/Queensland` | +10 | AEST |
| `Australia/Melbourne` | +10 | AEST |
| `Australia/Brisbane` | +10 | AEST |
| `British Summer Time` | +1 | BST (LSE DST) |
| `BST` | +1 | BST (LSE DST) |

All Australian states map to AEST per the spec's conservative-AEST policy; under DST (AEDT +11) the 1h-early fallback matches the existing "unknown locale → UTC" eventually-correct guarantee. Three new tests using the verbatim 2026-05-30 journal string for Australia/NSW + a BST test + a parameterised Victoria/Queensland test. 18/18 tests in the file PASS (15 → 18).

### Y-RECONCILE.3.1 — drift-cascade for OCA siblings (commit `959f38b`)

Closes the original Y-RECONCILE.3 spec §4 def-of-done #3. When Y-RECONCILE.2's periodic drift detector flips a bracket parent to CANCELLED (because IBKR no longer shows it in the open-orders snapshot), the surviving `_stp` / `_tp` children should also be cancelled — same Y207b.2 logic applied to the drift path. Pre-Y-RECONCILE.3.1 the children sat DB-SUBMITTED indefinitely (the live cascade only fires from event-driven cancels, not the periodic drift sweep).

Architecture:

* `_apply_drift_cancellations` now returns `tuple[int, int]` — `(parents_written, cascaded_children)`.
* New `DRIFT_RECONCILED_CHILD_REASON = "drift_reconciled_child"` for forensic distinguishability:
  * Parent rows: `rejected_reason='drift_reconciled'`
  * Child rows: `rejected_reason='drift_reconciled_child'`
* New `_compute_bracket_children_to_cascade(registry, parent_coid)` helper prefers Y207b.2's `compute_bracket_children_to_cancel` when the registry exposes it (live broker), with a suffix-walk fallback for bare-registry test fixtures.
* `detect_once` threads the cascaded count into the cycle report + the INFO log line.
* `DriftCycleReport` gains `cascaded_children: int = 0` (defaults zero for back-compat with existing test constructors).

6/6 new tests PASS. Y-RECONCILE.2 regression: 11/11. Full Y-RECONCILE chain regression: 79/79.

Operator pushed back when the first pass marked Y84 "working as designed." ## §155 — dashboard polish: Feed Engine open P&L + short-aware unrealized pct (commits `c7631b7` → `9c67c17`, 2026-05-30 11:35–11:55 UTC)

Three operator-driven dashboard tweaks. All on the daytrade terminal.

### Y208 — Feed Engine open-holdings P&L per market (commit `c7631b7`)

Operator framing: *"i want an OPEN P&L for the holdings on open markets ... if all flatten in 20 minutes, is it a net loss or net gain?"*

- New `.fc-holdings` row in each per-market widget: `N HOLDINGS  +$xxx` (signed, coloured)
- Hidden when the market has no open positions
- Backend `/api/stream/status` adds `open_pnl_usd` + `open_position_count` per market by joining `positions` to `live_price_cache` (same unrealised-P&L formula as the canonical engines.py:402 query)
- Discipline → market mapping covers all 8 daytrade disciplines including `germany_daytrade` + `korea_daytrade` queued for Monday/Tuesday permissions
- Same drop: `.fc-regime` font bumped 11px → 13px and chip 10px → 11px (operator: BULL/BEAR `mkt +0.45%` was reading too small)

### Y208.1 — append % after dash (commit `7238145`)

Operator follow-up: *"can you also add the % after an -"*. Format becomes `+$210 - +14.27%` / `−$129 - −3.50%`. Backend adds `open_pnl_pct` derived from per-discipline SUM(pnl_usd) over SUM(ABS(qty × avg_cost)) — same formula the cohort math already used; FX-stale rows drop out so a single missing price doesn't skew the denominator.

### Y209 — direction-aware unrealized_pnl_pct (commit `9c67c17`)

Operator surfaced: *"the unrealised values do not match at all the holdings in dashboard."* Investigation showed Y208's cohort math agreed exactly with `/api/positions` totals, but the per-row pct on the Holdings panel disagreed on shorts — formula `((last/avg) − 1) × 100` is direction-blind.

Worst-case witness: **PD (qty=−89, avg=$9.82, last=$7.44)** — `pnl_usd=+$211.67` but pct showed `−24.22%`, looking like a loss on the row while the dollar said gain.

Fix derives pct from the (correctly-signed) USD P&L over the absolute notional:

    pct = (pnl_usd / abs(quantity × avg_cost)) × 100

Two parallel sites updated in lockstep (Rule 2):
- `dashboard/db_queries/engines.py:409` SQL CASE
- `dashboard/api/_helpers.py:761` Python equivalent

All 6 shorts on the book now sign-agreeing. Longs unchanged (formula reduces to the old form when qty > 0). Pre-existing bug; observable since at least Y32 (2026-04 timeframe) when the dual-currency P&L computation landed.

## §156 — close the manual-MKT-exit oversell class (commits `28059d7` → `6688ba4`, 2026-05-30 11:25–12:22 UTC)

Operator-prompted forensic on the 6 shorts currently on the book (CZR/GBTG/HFD/FOXT/USA/PD), 4 of which were created **after** Y206 deployed on 2026-05-28. Common fingerprint: long BUY filled, bracket TP+STP attached, strategy fires DAYTRADE_TIME_STOP MKT, position oversells to exactly negative of its long quantity.

Root cause traced to a three-way failure mode:
1. The runner's atomic `modify_stop_to_market` returns False (broker COID-tracking gap, filed as Y-EXIT.2)
2. The legacy fallback path calls `cancel_stop(symbol)` which only cancels the STP child (keyed off the stops table)
3. The LMT TP child stays armed at IBKR — when price brushes it, the TP fires independently while the MKT exit is in flight → net SELL = 2N → position goes from +N to −N

Y181 (2026-05-28) closed the repeated-MKT-firing case (APE 296× re-fired SESSION_END_FLAT) but left this LMT TP race uncovered. Y207b.2 / Y-RECONCILE.3.1 cascade-cancel children when the bracket PARENT is CANCELLED — but here the parent stays FILLED, so the cascade doesn't trigger.

### Y210 + Y211 spec (commit `28059d7`)

`docs/Y210_Y211_SPEC.md` — paired drop architecture, staggered ship. Each drop closes one half of the gap (gate-side + runner-side); together they form defence-in-depth on the same shape as the Y76 + Y181 layering already present.

### Y210 — broker gate tightening (commit `cdbe509`)

New `BrokerContext.working_bracket_qty_by_symbol` field; new `OrderManager._working_bracket_qty_by_symbol()` builder filtering on COID suffix `_stp` / `_tp` with the same staleness + closed-session semantics as Y181's MKT-only map. `gate_sell_quantity` Y181 bypass extended:

```python
if (intent.order_type == OrderType.MKT
    and exit_reason in _MANDATORY_EXIT_REASONS
    and intent.quantity <= held - working_mkt
    and working_bracket == 0):     # ← NEW (Y210)
    return Allow()
```

When bracket children are armed, the bypass is denied; the existing `available <= 0` reject branch catches the intent. Fail-open: empty dict defaults to 0 via `dict.get(symbol, 0.0)` → reverts to Y181 baseline if the builder ever breaks. 7/7 new tests + 64 regression tests passing. Broker restarted 12:08:16 UTC, healthy.

### Y-EXIT.1 — Binance no-op for /stops/modify-to-market (commit `0c23544`)

Audit surfaced that the strategy's MultiBrokerProxy `modify_stop_to_market` broadcasts to BOTH brokers when the routing cache is cold (every strategy daemon restart). The Binance broker had no route at the URL — FastAPI's parametrised `DELETE /stops/{symbol}` matched it with `symbol="modify-to-market"` and returned **405**. The strategy's BrokerClient raised `BrokerRejectedError` on every cycle, the runner's `_fire_exit` logged a stacktrace, and fell back to legacy cancel+SELL on every mandatory exit.

Witnessed at 2026-05-30 11:23:11 UTC across 12 `DT_daytrade_tse_v1_*` + 1 `DT_daytrade_hkex_v1_1880` — every single exit hit the 405.

Y-EXIT.1 adds explicit Binance route `POST /stops/modify-to-market` that returns `{modified: false, client_order_id: <echoed>, last_error: "binance: ... (Y-EXIT.1)"}`. Strategy proxy treats False as "this broker doesn't own the COID" and continues to IBKR. Same precedent as Drop J.1's `/stops/modify` fix (1315 daily 405s). 5/5 tests. Crypto broker restarted 12:15 UTC. 25s soak: zero 405 stacktraces (was: ~272 per soak window).

### Y211 — runner pre-exit bracket cancellation (commit `6688ba4`)

Closes the runner-side leak. In `daytrade_stop_runner._fire_exit` legacy fallback path, before the existing `cancel_stop(symbol)`, also cancel the LMT TP child via `cancel_order(client_order_id=f"{parent_coid}_tp")`. Guarded on `parent_coid is not None AND closing_side == SELL` (matches the atomic-path branch guard — short covers + crypto skip cleanly). Wrapped in try/except; cancel_order's 404 handling is the "already gone via OCA" case. 5/5 tests covering A (atomic ok → no Y211 call), B (atomic fails + parent known → cancel called with `_tp` coid), C (no parent → no-op), D (transport raise → fail-soft), E (short cover → no Y211).

Strategy daemon restarted 12:22:37 UTC. Zero ERROR-level events.

### Combined architecture state

With all three layers live, a mandatory MKT exit for a long with armed bracket now:
1. Atomic `modify_stop_to_market` returns False cleanly (no 405 from Y-EXIT.1)
2. Y211 cancels `_tp` child via `cancel_order` (404 if already OCA-cancelled, no-op)
3. Existing `cancel_stop(symbol)` cancels `_stp` child
4. MKT SELL submitted → Y210 sees `working_bracket = 0`, allows it
5. Position flattens cleanly, no race, no oversell

If the race somehow still fires (broker registry lag, cancel transport blip), Y210's gate is the final backstop — MKT gets rejected, runner retries next cycle, no oversell.

### Y-EXIT.2 — explicitly parked

Operator-confirmed in chat: not needed right now. The architecture closes the safety class without it; Y-EXIT.2 would be a latency polish (sub-ms atomic vs ~100-300ms legacy three-call). Revisit only if Y210 gate-rejections pile up on the same symbol over many cycles. Triage entry remains in `docs/INVESTIGATION_TRIAGE_2026-05-30.md`.

### Locks

- `L-Y210-MANDATORY-MKT-EXIT-REJECTS-WITH-LIVE-BRACKET`
- `L-Y211-MANUAL-MKT-EXIT-CANCELS-FULL-BRACKET`
- `L-Y210-Y211-CLOSES-OVERSELL-VIA-LMT-TP-RACE`

## §158 — Y-DATA1 closure: crypto replay worker + J15 brain pulse (commits `518a5ed` → `bcf02f9`, 2026-05-30 13:00–13:25 UTC)

Closes the Y-DATA1 arc filed in §152 (S5) by shipping the real worker (Y-DATA1.1), an operational reliability follow-up (Y-DATA1.1c), and the nightly automation (Y-DATA1.2).

### Y-DATA1.1 — near-miss replay worker for crypto (commit `518a5ed`)

The morning diagnosis (`docs/Y_DATA_1_REPLAY_DIAGNOSIS_2026-05-30.md`) had identified the bars-source decision as the blocker. Choice made: on-demand fetch via the existing broker route, not a persistent bars store. Scope: **crypto only** because Binance's public klines is callable from any process; IBKR's `reqHistoricalDataAsync` is `ctx.connection`-bound (strategy-daemon-side) and needs a different wire (filed as Y-DATA1.1b).

Two-site fix to expose anchored windows:
- `alphabot/broker_binance/client.py` — `BinanceClient.get_klines` extended with `start_time_ms` / `end_time_ms` kwargs (thread through to Binance SDK's `startTime` / `endTime`)
- `alphabot/broker_binance/api.py` — `/historical/bars` route accepts optional `start_time` / `end_time` ISO-8601 query params. Backward-compatible — most-recent-N behaviour unchanged when neither is set.

Worker body in `alphabot/intelligence/near_miss_replay.py`:
- `_select_pending_batch` — tier-priority ordered (1 → 2 → 3 → NULL), oldest-first within tier, `discipline = 'crypto_daytrade'` filter, last-30-days bound (older rows should already be EXPIRED via the morning's one-shot)
- `_fetch_forward_bars` — HTTP to crypto broker `/historical/bars` with `start_at` + `start_at + 4h` window
- `_simulate_long_entry` — pure-function simulation: stop = −1.5%, TP = +3%, time-stop at horizon. Conservative ordering: when both stop and TP touch in the same bar, stop wins (matches IBKR/Binance OCA semantic)
- `_persist_result` — UPDATE near_misses with `simulated_*` columns + `replay_attempts` increment + `replay_completed_at`
- `replay_pending_batch` — entry point, async, returns batch for logging

13 tests pin: stop touch, TP touch, both-touch-stop-wins, horizon, MAE/MFE sign convention, empty/zero-entry defensive, tier-priority SELECT, crypto-only discipline filter, COMPLETED happy path, FAILED on fetch error / empty bars, non-crypto-discipline skip.

- 35-min trigger window inside the hour
- One-per-UTC-day idempotency via `system_alarms` rule_key

Drives the async worker from the sync J-rule via `asyncio.run()` — brain sweep is not in an event loop, so this is safe (vs reentrant `asyncio.run` which errors).

6/6 J15 tests pin: outside-window short-circuit (no worker call); inside-window fresh day → worker + INFO alarm + correct details_json shape; idempotent within day (second call no-op); worker raises → (False, 0), no alarm written, next day retries; window-minute > trigger window threshold → short-circuit; rule_key format embeds UTC date.

| `dt-rvol-smooth` | passed=0, score=0.0 (derives from above) |
| `dt-vwap-smooth` | passed=0, score=0.0 |

The pipeline was running **equity-style gates on crypto symbols**. Y201b's morning collapse (`f368836`, 11:07 UTC) had routed `_evaluate_symbol_crypto` through `_evaluate_via_pipeline`. The pipeline:
- VWAP needs a session-anchored window → crypto-24/7 has no `session_open_utc` → "could not be computed"
- Equity intraday rvol input → not populated for crypto → "RVOL 0.00x"

Smooth scores were therefore stuck at 0.0. Y-SCORE-CRYPTO's `rvol_score ≥ 2.0 AND vwap_score ≥ 2.0` couldn't ever clear. Not a marks-tuning problem — an upstream computation gap masked by the legacy `evaluation.all_passed` semantics until the new stricter rule exposed it.

### Y-SCORE-CRYPTO.1 — restore the native evaluator (commit `71ad34f`)

Per L-Y201A-AUDIT-BEFORE-DELETE doctrine, the right fix was to revert Y201b's crypto-specific collapse. Other equity collapses from Y201b stay — only crypto needed the native restore because crypto's gate semantics don't fit the equity pipeline's session-anchored model.

Restored body calls `evaluate_daytrade_crypto` (4 crypto-native gates from `signals/daytrade_crypto_gates.py`):
- `vol-regime` — ATR rolling-window band check (binary)
- `trend-15m` — 15-min close > open AND > prior (binary)
- `rvol-15m` — last 15m vol vs trailing 15m avg (smooth 0-10)
- `vwap-hold` — current_price vs vwap (smooth 0-10)

Then wires the smooth scores + eligibility into `DayTradeEvaluation` so the Y-SCORE-CRYPTO two-score AND-fire rule engages meaningfully:

    eligibility_passed = vol-regime.passed AND trend-15m.passed
    rvol_score          = rvol-15m.score
    vwap_score          = vwap-hold.score

Imports restored: `evaluate_daytrade_crypto` (Y201b had removed). 4/4 new tests in `test_drop_y_score_crypto_1_native_evaluator_restored.py` pin the wire.

### Y-SCORE-CRYPTO.2 — rvol mark 2.0 → 1.0 (commit `8b7623b`)

Post-restore, 14 fresh crypto signals showed `rvol-15m` peaking at **1.45** with avg 0.40. The `_curve` helper in `daytrade_crypto_gates.py` simply doesn't produce scores above ~1.5 in current crypto volume regimes. Mark at 2.0 was structurally impossible to clear.

Tuned 2.0 → 1.0. Captures the 4/14 signals with meaningful rvol bursts while still gating the 10/14 where rvol is 0.0 (mostly thin/no-flow).

### Y-SCORE-CRYPTO.3 — vwap mark 2.0 → 1.5 (commit `2e458f0`)

After .2 ship, 22 fresh signals: 6/22 cleared the new 1.0 rvol mark but **zero fired BUY** because vwap mark at 2.0 was the new binding constraint. Live vwap-hold distribution 1.26–2.50, avg 1.97.

Tuned 2.0 → 1.5. Operator-approved.

### Live verification at 13:52 UTC

**Crypto firing again.**

| Window (post 13:48 restart) | Value |
|---|---|
| Total signals | 39 |
| BUY | **5** (13% fire rate — within predicted 10-15% range) |
| HOLD | 34 |
| Crypto BUY orders submitted | 2 FILLED — LINKUSDT @ 10.9 units, APTUSDT @ 106.15 units, score 6.6/10 |

The two-score AND-fire model is now engaged with real, gating data.

### Final state of the marks dispatch

| Market | RVOL | VWAP |
|---|---|---|
| US | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| FTSE | 6.0 | 4.0 |
| ASX | 5.0 | 2.5 |
| TSE | 5.0 | 2.5 |
| HKEX | 5.5 | 3.0 |
| Germany | 5.0 | 3.0 (dormant) |
| Korea | 5.0 | 3.0 (dormant) |
| **Crypto** | **1.0** | **1.5** (live, Y-SCORE-CRYPTO.1+.2+.3) |

### Pattern surfaced — live-tune cycle as a normal workflow

Three operator decisions came inside ~20 minutes: revert architectural change → first marks tune → second marks tune. Each was directly informed by live distribution data captured between restarts. The L-Y-SCORE-CRYPTO-FOUR-GATE-MODEL lock survived intact — only the mark values changed, never the model shape.

This is the expected first-tune cycle workflow: ship the structural design, watch the live distribution for one session, tune the marks to match the distribution rather than guessing pre-ship. Worth re-running for US/FTSE/ASX/TSE/HKEX on Monday once their next live session produces fresh distribution data.
