## §211 — 2026-06-07 — Courtroom STOP/EXIT analysis: Phase 1 (pin one exit per verdict) + Phase 2 (the exit sweep)

**Reconstructed-from-code entry.** The session that shipped this was cleared before the §4.5 ritual ran; this is the record, written by reading the two commits + the live tree (tests re-run green at write time). Commits: **`a869eba`** (Phase 1) + **`b6628b2`** (Phase 2). Both committed AND pushed (tree clean, 0 ahead/behind origin/main). No schema change in either phase (Phase 2's crypto replay reuses `crypto_edge_observations`); brain restart only.

**The bug Phase 1 fixed (a correctness defect, not a feature).** `build_grid` filtered `src='sim'` but NOT `exit_config`, while `edge_observations` holds **four** sim exits per near-miss row (the Y221-P1 grid: `s1.5_t3.0` brackets at h30/h90/h240 + `s1.5_noTP_h240` let-it-run). So **every equity verdict was computed on a BLEND of all four exit rules** — a verdict on a meaningless average across hold-times and stop/TP brackets. On live data the exhaustion footprint pooled **896 obs across the 4 exits; pinned to the canonical 4h bracket it's 284** — the other 612 were rows from different exit rules contaminating the grid.

**Phase 1 fix (`a869eba`).** `SetupSpec` gains an `exit_config` field, default **`CANONICAL_EXIT = "s1.5_t3.0_h240"`** (1.5% stop / 3.0% TP / 4-hour — `near_miss_replay.py:213`). `build_grid` adds `AND exit_config = ?` when it's set (`courtroom.py:116-120`). **`exit_config=None` = don't filter** — used where the `src` already pins one exit: `close_flatten` reads `src='sim_close'` (the isolated close-phase rows) and sets `exit_config=None` (`footprints.py:222-223`). So each verdict is now **one clean exit rule**, not a blend. Test seeds aligned to the real canonical label (`test_y_edge3c_courtroom`, `test_y_edge4_footprints`, `test_y_promote_step2_apply`).

**Phase 2 — the exit sweep (`b6628b2`): "which hold-time / bracket does the edge hold best under?"** Phase 1 pins one exit per verdict; Phase 2 sweeps all four and ranks them, on both tracks:

- **Crypto** — the crypto store now replays **ALL 4 exit configs per session** (`crypto_edge.py`, `n_bars` widened to cover the 240-min horizons), so crypto is comparable across hold-times like equity. `exit_sweep_crypto(conn, w)` prosecutes the fire score under each exit → per-exit `{verdict, provisional, n_slides, hold_rate, fire_net_pct, fire_win_pct, fire_n}`, **sorted SURVIVED-first then by would-fire (≥6) cohort net** — top row = the exit the edge best holds under. Surfaced on the crypto courtroom card. **This is the live answer to "why does the desk lose on crypto": the edge is strongest at SHORT holds — 90-min bracket +1.27%/70% win, let-it-run worst +0.42%/39% — while the live ~0.55% stop is TIGHTER than these 1.5% brackets.** (Mirrors memory `courtroom-exit-sweep`.)
- **Equity** — `GET /courtroom/exitsweep?name=&w=` prosecutes ONE footprint under each exit (`replace(spec, exit_config=cfg.label)` → `build_grid` + `prosecute(persist=False)`), returns ranked per-exit `{verdict, provisional, n_slides, hold_rate, avg_net_pct, n}`. **`persist=False` — a sweep must not write 4× verdict rows.** 404 on unknown footprint. Lazy "compare exits" button per equity card (`app.js → y114-exitsweep`, `index.html`).

**Why this matters (the thesis):** a footprint can be NO-EDGE under the 4h bracket but real under let-it-run, or vice-versa — the verdict is meaningless without naming the exit it was reached under. Phase 1 makes every verdict honest (one exit); Phase 2 makes the exit choice itself a measured, ranked output instead of a hidden blend. It directly indicts the live crypto stop (0.55%) as too tight versus where the edge actually lives (the 1.5% short-hold brackets).

**Tests:** Phase 1 — seed-alignment across 3 suites, part of "966 edge/courtroom/distill/crypto/regime green" at commit time. Phase 2 — `exit_sweep_crypto` ranking + the equity endpoint (one row per exit, sorted, 404 on unknown). **Re-run at this ritual: the 4 touched suites (`test_crypto_edge`, `test_y_edge3c_courtroom`, `test_y_edge4_footprints`, `test_y_promote_step2_apply`) = 31/31 green.**

## §213 — 2026-06-07 — Regime capture-first: `regime_context` + short forward-return store (schema 93)

**Reconstructed-from-code (same session).** Commit **`8c57d50`** (**schema 93** — the DB's current version), scoped by **`71762ac`** (`docs/REGIME_AWARE_COURTROOM_CAPTURE_SCOPE.md`). **The thesis — capture leads the bear day.** So the courtroom can LATER answer *"does an edge persist across bull/flat/bear, for longs AND shorts"* — **before** shorting arms and **before** the first bear day. Capture-first per the Y216 sequence (sensor → bank → prove OOS → actuator). **Capture only; no analysis, no orders, all shadow/additive.**

**Grounded in the verified state** (`71762ac` scope): two regime systems exist (direction BULL/BEAR/FLAT + risk FULL/CAUTIOUS/DEFENSIVE); `edge_observations` carried only the risk posture; futures+crypto stores carried no regime; the short side logged candidates (`short_breadth_log`/`short_pool`) but **no forward returns**.

**Migration 093 builds the two missing capture stores:**
- **`regime_context`** — one consolidated regime row per market per capture: risk posture + universe-move + short-breadth bear gauge + VIX + a `direction_proxy`. The **joinable time series every observation is stamped against.** Rationale: the universe move is only retained 1 day in `ranked_candidates`, so persisting it here is the whole point. `backfill_regime_context` reconstructs recent sessions from the 400-day-retained breadth (breadth-based direction).
- **`short_edge_observations`** — the missing half: `short_pool` candidates replayed **FORWARD with an INVERTED bracket** (`simulate_short_exits`: stop ABOVE, TP BELOW), regime-stamped. So *"short edge on a bear day"* becomes answerable from banked data.

Wired into `nightly_edge.py` (regime capture first, then short distill). **Backfilled:** 7 markets' regime context (US/Korea/Germany **BEARISH** now) + 955 short obs / 5 days. **Honest early read: almost no bear-regime data yet (n=87) → no short edge to claim — exactly why we capture now.** Modules: `intelligence/regime_context.py`, `intelligence/short_edge.py`. 6 tests (short bracket math, direction proxy, both captures).

**Complements** `docs/REGIME_HARDENING_SCOPE.md` (the live-signal safety side — fail-CLOSED once shorts arm). The analysis layer + a validation gate (reliability / predictive validity / stability before regime is trusted to flip a two-sided book) are **explicitly DEFERRED** — capture now, prove later, actuate last.

## §214 — 2026-06-07 — Stop distance added to the courtroom exit sweep (`b12d01b`) — and the live crypto stop is the worst rung

**Operator: "what about % stops? 1% / 1.5% / 2% … we need to include that too."** The §211 exit sweep varied hold-time + TP but pinned the stop at 1.5%. §214 makes the **stop a swept axis**. Key property (corrects a worry from §211's framing): each exit config is a **full independent replay of every observation**, so a new stop level gets the **same n** as the canonical — adding stops does NOT thin the sample. The only cost is storage + a re-distill.

**The change (no migration — `exit_config` is an existing TEXT value):** `DEFAULT_EXIT_CONFIGS` gains three stop variants at the canonical 4h horizon + 3% TP, capped at 2% (operator: "never going further than 2%"): `s0.5_t3.0_h240` / `s1.0_t3.0_h240` / `s2.0_t3.0_h240` (1.5% already exists as `CANONICAL_EXIT`). **0.5% mirrors the live ~0.55% crypto stop** — the §211 sim-vs-live divergence made measurable. `EXIT_LABELS` + the sweep endpoints auto-iterate; the UI captions/headers now name the stop axis (asset `y116-stopsweep`), and the canonical-row tag still marks the 1.5% "4-hour bracket" as the verdict's exit. Tests: 3 count/set assertions updated same-drop (§3); 1207 green.

**Backfill:** crypto re-distilled (`distill_crypto_all`, banked bars — no broker) → 16 sessions, **all 7 configs balanced at 34,910 rows each** (the equal-n property, confirmed). Equity aggregates from `near_miss_exit_sim` (written by the replay), so equity's new stop rows **fill forward** as new near-misses replay under the 7 configs; a historical equity backfill = re-running the replay (the broker-touching path, `L-REPLAY-NEVER-HITS-BROKER-IN-HOURS`), deferred — not run.

**The finding (crypto, in-sample, ACCUMULATING — net of assumed cost):** at the 4h horizon, **tighter stops monotonically HURT** — 2.0% +0.838/60.4% win ≈ 1.5% +0.833/56.9% > 1.0% +0.788/48.6% > **0.5% +0.646/36.5%**. The live ~0.55% stop is the **worst rung of the ladder.** Short holds still beat all 4h-stop variants (90-min +1.224/69%, 30-min +1.149/68%). So the desk's live crypto loss is consistent with *both* a too-tight stop *and* too-long a hold — the rig now shows the operator exactly that, by exit. Verdicts stay ACCUMULATING until the windows bank; the net/win columns are the immediate read.

**Deferred (operator chose "% stops now"):** the ATR-realistic axis (`k×ATR` stops to match the desk's actual `0.75×ATR` sizing) needs ATR-at-entry banked per observation first (today only a boolean `elig_atr` gate-flag exists) — a capture-first follow-up if wanted.

## §216 — 2026-06-07 — Crypto real-time price feed via Binance WebSocket: Phase 1 (broker, DARK) (`aaeecdb`)

**Operator: "real-time prices for entry and exit."** Spec `docs/CRYPTO_WS_PRICE_SCOPE.md`. Phase 1 = the broker-side feed, built DARK + tested + deployed (flag off). Decisions baked from the spec §4 (operator: "go with your recommendations"): `@bookTicker` (mid price), ~10s ws-staleness fallback, REST stays as the floor.

**The component (`broker_binance/ws_price_stream.py`):** a background asyncio task holding ONE combined `@bookTicker` stream, feeding the EXISTING `CryptoPriceCache` in real time. NOT in the IBKR-shaped equity market-data daemon — the crypto broker already centralises the Binance connection + the cache everything reads, so the ws belongs there (architectural note in §3 of the scope). Resilient: parse + sanity-guard (reject a tick >20% off last), combined-stream SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE control frames (watch-set changes without reconnecting), reconnect with exponential backoff (Binance force-closes ~24h). `websockets` 16.0 (modern lib, not python-binance's legacy ws).

**Cache change (`price_cache.py`):** `update()` (ws write + sanity) + source/age on the snapshot; `refresh()` (the 30s REST poll) is now a **non-clobbering fallback** — it never overwrites a still-fresh ws tick and keeps fresh ws watch-set entries. So: socket alive → cache is real-time; socket dies → degrades to the 30s poll; both dead → `None` (honest). **No consumer change for STOPS** — the stop runner + `/positions` already read `price_cache`, so they go real-time for free once the flag flips. `/price` exposes `source` (ws|rest) + `age_seconds`.

**Flag:** `CRYPTO_WS_PRICE_ENABLED` (default false) + `CRYPTO_WS_PRICE_STALE_SECONDS` (10) + `CRYPTO_WS_PRICE_SANITY_DEVIATION` (0.20). Deployed dark; crypto broker restarted HEALTHY; **30 cache/ws tests + 255 broker-suite green.**

Then the rollout: shadow (log ws-vs-REST divergence) → flip `CRYPTO_WS_PRICE_ENABLED=true` → observe stop fills → optional 15s cadence. STOPS real-time is fully built and one flag-flip away; ENTRY needs Phase 2.

## §217 — 2026-06-07 — Crypto ws investigation: the entry feed was already a daemon ws (storming) — Step 1 fix (`b4cf235`)

**Operator: "real-time prices for entry and exit."** Investigating the entry path corrected a spec assumption + surfaced a live degradation:

**Architecture (corrected):** crypto **bars** (entry gates) come from the **market-data daemon**, not the crypto broker. The router is daemon-only (Y52); the daemon already runs a **fully-built Binance `@kline` WebSocket source** (`BinanceWSSource`, Y40, enabled by default). So the operator's original instinct ("put crypto in the market-data daemon and stream") was already realised — entry bars stream, exit price is the broker `price_cache` (Phase 1 §216, separate consumer). Two independent ws feeds, correctly.

**The live bug:** the daemon ws was in a **reconnect storm** — ~390 streams (65 crypto symbols × 6 `_POOL_TIMEFRAMES`: M1/M5/M15/H1/H4/D1) × ~2s pushes overflowed python-binance's **default 100-message internal queue** → `BinanceWebsocketQueueOverflow` → read-loop death → reconnect every ~1-20s. (Web-verified: Binance allows 1024 streams/connection + 5 control-msgs/s; the cap was purely the client library's.)

**Step 1 (`b4cf235`, shipped + deployed + verified):** `BinanceSocketManager(client, max_queue_size=10_000)`. Result: **0 overflow/read-loop errors over 5 min** (was constant); feed stable + real-time. 15 binance_ws tests green. **Entry real-time is effectively achieved** by this (the stream was always there; it was just crash-looping).

**Remaining (Step 2, NOT done — deliberately):** even post-Step-1, `binance_ws` does a **full socket reconnect on every subscription change** (`_subs_changed` → teardown+reconnect), ~11 reconnects / 5 min during universe churn, each a ~1s gap across all streams. The fix = a **raw `websockets` transport with incremental SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE** (the Phase-1 broker-ws pattern) — no queue cap, no full reconnects. Two sub-levers, both touch a LIVE shared bar source (crypto entry depends on it): (a) raw-ws transport (the real win, but a careful rewrite needing a soak to prove no silent bar-gaps); (b) trim `_POOL_TIMEFRAMES` to what's consumed — daytrade reads ONLY M5 (HTF derived from 5m), but the constant is **daemon-wide (shared with equity)**, so trimming needs cross-strategy verification. **Held for a focused, soak-verified pass — not rushed onto the now-stable live feed.** Updated `docs/CRYPTO_WS_PRICE_SCOPE.md` premise: entry = daemon ws (this), exit = broker ws (§216).

**Operator caught it via HOME:** HOMEUSDT ran +12% then gave back to +8.7% with no TP and a barely-protecting stop. Investigation exposed that **§219 (2% stop) and §220 (3% TP) did NOT land on the live crypto exit path**, and the operator's standing requirement is **"all crypto stops must always trail, at 2%."**

**What's actually true about the live crypto exit (now mapped correctly):**
- Crypto stops ARE trailing — **Binance server-side `trailingDelta`** (TRAIL mode), robust. Good.
- The trail **width** is the broker-side constant **`CRYPTO_TRAIL_DAYTRADE_BIPS`** (`broker_binance/stops.py`), via `compute_trailing_delta_bips_for_discipline` — it was **100 bips (1.0%)** (Y54), not the docstring's stale "150". **NOT** §219's strategy-side `stop_loss_pct`.
- The **initial** stop placement is **ATR-based** in the broker attach (HOME: entry−2×ATR = −4.47%), which **overrides** §219's passed 2% `stop_loss_pct`. So §219 never reached the live trail.
- The TP: crypto TRAIL mode has **no exchange TP**; §220's runner-side TP lives in `decide_action_hybrid`, which isn't the effective exit driver for crypto (the server-side trail is) — so the 3% TP wasn't firing.

**The fix (the right lever):** `CRYPTO_TRAIL_DAYTRADE_BIPS` **100 → 200** (2.0%). This is the live server-side trailing width for crypto_daytrade. Forward-looking: new crypto entries trail at 2%; existing positions keep their attached stop until they re-enter. 3 trail-test assertions updated; 321 broker/trail green; broker-crypto restarted, verified `200 bips = 2.0%`.

**Insight — the 2% trail may SUPERSEDE the 3% TP.** A 2% trailing stop lets a runner ride (HOME → +12%) and exits ~2% off the peak (~+10%), whereas a fixed 3% TP would have **capped HOME at +3%**, missing the run. So trail-only-at-2% is arguably better than `s2.0_t3.0` for crypto — the trail captures big moves the TP caps. The §220 TP not firing is therefore not necessarily a loss; trail-only is a coherent (better?) design. Open for the operator: keep trail-only-2%, or also force a 3% TP cap.

**Honest note:** §219/§220 were correct in intent but targeted the wrong layer (strategy-side hybrid) for crypto, whose live exit is the broker-side server trail. This is the crypto stop patchwork (multiple stop sources) the consolidation memory flags — the operator's "always trailing, 2%" is the clean north star; the consolidation should collapse to exactly that.

## §223 — 2026-06-08 — Crypto courtroom: ever-moving system + fast load (`f8b7fc5`)

**Operator observation:** the crypto courtroom tab shows CONVICTED (nothing survived — fine) but "appears stalled — surely it's a rolling thing? needs an UPDATE button or something to keep reviewing." Plus: the tab takes a long time to load.

- **C — trend + what's-next.** GET adds `last_prosecuted_at`, a verdict/beat-luck-p trend (the snapshot history — so CONVICTED reads as drift, not a dead-end), and `next_candidates` (banking gaps to the next window's first verdict, the best exit corner to watch/promote, re-try-in-a-bear-regime). ## §224 — 2026-06-08 — Crypto naked-stop audit: periodic Binance-truth auto-re-attach (`3c8f295`)

**Operator question → gap found:** "don't we have a naked-stop audit sweep already? or is that equity only?" → **equity/futures only.** `broker/stop_coverage_audit.py` asks IBKR directly every reconcile cycle and re-attaches naked stops. Crypto had only Y186 `_attach_missing_stops_on_startup` — which runs **once at boot** AND only checks the **DB** (`crypto_stops` ACTIVE rows). So a position entered after boot (AAVE at 08:34, after the 06:05 crypto-broker start) sat naked until the operator said "reattach" and I did it by hand.

**Built (operator: "make sure it's safe and does all the necessary verifications with Binance to be 100% sure it's naked"):** `broker_binance/stop_coverage_audit.py` — the Binance mirror of the IBKR audit (pure core `find_naked_crypto` + I/O orchestrator). **Two independent Binance verifications** before any re-attach:
1. **No live protective SELL stop** for the symbol in `get_open_orders()` (the venue truth, NOT the DB — a DB ACTIVE row whose Binance order was cancelled/filled is still naked). STOP_LOSS / STOP_LOSS_LIMIT only (covers OCO stop leg + the trailing stop); a TP LIMIT_MAKER or a BUY order is not protective.
2. **Position genuinely held** — total (free+locked) balance from `get_account()` >= position qty. Unbacked = drift → **SKIP + flag**, never place a SELL we can't cover.

Plus the IBKR audit's circuit-breakers: grace window (skip fresh — never race the strategy's own attach), per-cycle cap (5; more = systemic → flag, no storm), connection-healthy gate (`is_trading()`), long-only (negative qty skipped + flagged). Re-attaches the **2% trail** (§222).

**Wiring:** periodic loop in the crypto broker (`_naked_stop_audit_loop`, every 60s, settings-gated `CRYPTO_NAKED_STOP_AUDIT_*`), started after reconcile, cancelled on shutdown. Re-attach callback `_reattach_naked_stop` → `attach_stop(..., trailing_delta_bips=200)`.

**Net:** crypto now self-heals naked stops like equity/futures — detect (alarm + §223 sweep check) → **auto-re-attach** (this) → 90-min force-exit backstop (Y185) as the last line. Manual re-attach no longer needed in steady state. Verified live: loop started, all 8 held crypto positions covered at 200bips, zero audit errors. Also fixed 2 stale trail-bips tests (§221 set daytrade 100→200). 10 new pure-core tests pass.

## §225 — 2026-06-08 — Stream-gate retired FTSE + ASX so US gets the full IBKR budget (`e27c685`)

**Operator:** "dashboard shows LSE streaming 175 — hope it's actually turned off, US will get the whole 180." It was NOT.

**Root cause — trading-off ≠ streaming-off.** The 2026-06-06 markets-retirement set `DAYTRADE_FTSE_ENABLED` / `DAYTRADE_ASX_ENABLED=false`, which turns off the STRATEGY (`main_daytrade.py` won't register the discipline). But the market-data daemon's streaming has a SEPARATE gate — `pool_config._DORMANCY_FLAG_BY_MARKET` — and it only covered HKEX/TSE/Korea/Germany. **US/FTSE/ASX were hardcoded "always on"** (they predate the Y141 dormancy concept). So `is_market_streaming_enabled("ftse")` returned `True` unconditionally → the daemon kept subscribing LSE (~175 IBKR lines) the moment its session opened, eating the 200-slot budget that should go to US during the 13:30–15:30 UTC overlap — and firing a spurious `ftse CYCLE_CADENCE_STALL` (streaming a market no strategy evaluates).

**Fix (code-only):** add `"ftse": "DAYTRADE_FTSE_ENABLED"` + `"asx": "DAYTRADE_ASX_ENABLED"` to `_DORMANCY_FLAG_BY_MARKET`. The `.env` flags were already false and `is_market_streaming_enabled` reads them fresh, so no `.env` change needed. Now both retired markets are excluded from the stream pool.

**Verified live** (US + LSE both in session at 13:39 UTC): the daemon logged `line budget: cap=200 ... discretionary=174 across 1 open market(s)` — US only; LSE excluded despite being open. US gets the full discretionary budget. 13 dormancy tests updated/pass.

**Lesson:** retiring a market needs the flag AND (for the pre-Y141 markets) the streaming dormancy gate — they're separate. Re-enabling FTSE/ASX is now the same two-flag flip as the others.

## §227 — 2026-06-08 — Real-time IBKR book sync: 3 fixes in `ibkr_realtime_sync.py` (`d9daa51`)

**Root cause:** Stops rehydrated after a broker restart had no event handlers. When NVRI's stop triggered, IBKR pushed the fill but nobody was listening — position sat below the stop for ~2h before the 30s reconcile loop caught it.

**Three complementary fixes** in `alphabot/broker/ibkr_realtime_sync.py`:

- **Fix 1 — positionEvent push subscription:** `reqAccountUpdates()` + `ib.positionEvent += handler`. TWS pushes every account position change (stop triggers, manual TWS trades, reconnects) in real-time. Position closure detected ~1s vs 30s poll.
- **Fix 2 — attach handlers to rehydrated trades:** After `reqAllOpenOrdersAsync()` rehydrates pre-existing stop/entry orders, attach `fillEvent + statusEvent` handlers to any trade not already in `executor._trades`. Stop-trigger fills after a broker restart are now visible immediately.
- **Fix 3 — execDetailsEvent global execution stream (safety net):** `ib.execDetailsEvent` fires for every execution on the account regardless of session/clientId. Catches manual TWS trades, previous-session stops, anything that slips through Fixes 1+2. Z1 dedup prevents double-counting.

## §228 — 2026-06-09 — Y226: gate `/positions` with 503 during post-reconnect resync (`113c91b`)

**Root cause of 2026-06-08 ALLY/AAP/WSC short creation:** `SESSION_END_FLAT` fired against a stale `position_book` immediately after the broker reconnected from a gateway disconnect. Missed fill events during the disconnect meant `position_book` showed longs that IBKR had already closed, so the SELL went past zero into short territory. `gate_sell_quantity` (Y76/Y87/Y168/Y181/Y210) is logically correct but its inputs come from `position_book`, which is stale during the ~2-3s `force_resync_from_ibkr` window after reconnect.

**Fix:** `/positions` returns 503 while `_pending_freshness_sweep` is True (post-reconnect resync in flight). The stop-runner reads `/positions` every cycle; a 503 means it sees no positions, fires no exits, and retries next cycle — after the resync has completed and `position_book` reflects IBKR truth.

Wire: `resync_pending_fn=lambda: self._pending_freshness_sweep` passed from `AlphaBotBroker.__init__` → `build_api` → `BrokerRouteContext` → `routes_positions`. None in tests/legacy callers → no behaviour change. 4 tests. Layer 2 (`held ≤ 0` guard) was already present in `gate_sell_quantity` — not built again.

**§227 + §228 together:** fills land in ~1s (§227), reconnect windows are gated (§228). 30s reconcile remains backstop.

## §233 — 2026-06-09 — Remove RVOL gate from futures

**Rationale:** Index futures (ES/NQ/ESTX50/DAX etc.) have institutional baseline volume — a 1.2× RVOL requirement was blocking 70% of session time. Data from `fut_signal_funnel`: average RVOL during session-active cycles is 1.2–1.4×, so 1.2 is roughly the 50th percentile. VWAP + ATR are sufficient for entry confirmation on deep liquid instruments; RVOL adds no additional confirmation value the way it does for equity (where unusual volume identifies informed buying).

## §234 — 2026-06-09 — Mobile futures holdings + trades + operational incident

**Mobile fix:** `renderMobileFutures` renders two new cards — "FUT Holdings" (open contracts with P&L) and "FUT Trades" (closed trades with P&L). Both visible below the distance-to-trigger card in the mobile stack. Eurex = gold, US = blue. Wired into the existing `pollFuturesActivity` loop.

**Operational incident — Eurex stops lost on broker reconnect (2026-06-09 ~18:31 UTC):**

Operator opened IBKR TWS which kicked the gateway (one session per account — known `gateway-tws-session-conflict` class). Broker went RECONNECTING → gateway restarted → broker restarted. During the reconnect, ESTX50/SX7E/DAX had entered with bracket children (STP+TP) which were CANCELLED on reconnect. The equity stop-coverage audit cannot route Eurex futures stops ("position not found in book" — `stop_manager` doesn't know how to route a futures STP). Time-stop (20 min) also didn't fire because the FuturesRunner lost in-memory state on restart.

**Manual resolution:** Manually submitted MKT SELL exits for all 3 naked Eurex positions via `/orders/submit` with `instrument_canonical_id` and `intended_exit_reason=DAYTRADE_FLAT_CLOCK`. **US futures (MES/MNQ/M2K) were unaffected** — their stops were re-attached by the stop-coverage audit on restart.

**Root gap identified:** Eurex futures stops not re-attachable by the equity stop-coverage audit. When a Eurex bracket's STP child is cancelled on reconnect, no automatic fallback exists. The FuturesRunner's time-stop is the only safety net but it needs in-memory state. Fix: Eurex-aware stop re-attachment in the stop-coverage audit (deferred — not built this session).

**Additional stop re-attaches (maintenance sweeps):** RYAN, EC, ESRT, ALK — all naked after broker restart, all re-attached via `/stops/attach` with 1.5% fallback, logged to `agent_audit`.

## §236 — 2026-06-10 — Zero-tolerance futures stop architecture (P1 + P2 + Y-FUT-STOP-REATTACH + _build_intent)

**Context:** 2026-06-09 ESTX50 held NAKED 12h 39min — its bracket TRAIL was orphan-swept 8s after fill, and the re-attach path (`replace_stop`) only ratcheted, never re-attached. A deep-research pass (Renaissance/Citadel/FINRA/FIA/Knight-Capital) confirmed: no firm publishes the specific policy; regulators are principles-based ("reasonably designed" + near-real-time monitoring); Knight Capital established that letting runaway unprotected exposure persist with NO automated intervention is the violation. The choice of recovery mechanism is the firm's to define and automate. Verdict: **1 retry, then flatten, in seconds** is a defensible documented policy.

**Y-FUT-STOP-REATTACH (`f52f58b`+`2e17703`):** `POST /stops/attach-futures-trail` — attaches a standalone SELL TRAIL to an existing futures position (the equity `attach_stop` is symbol-keyed, can't route futures by con_id). `executor_live._build_order` gained a TRAIL branch (was falling into STP_LMT → AssertionError). `FuturesBrokerAdapter.list_open_positions` detects a naked held position and calls it. Also fixed: US-futures adapter logging spurious "unknown conId" for Eurex positions (hardcoded `eurex_desk.DISCIPLINE` filter → added `discipline` param); orphan-sweep cancelling futures stops in the fill-to-DB race (skip `eurex-`/`usfut-` coids); entry-driver in-flight cooldown (5-min) to stop the BUY storm.

**P1 — exit-on-2nd-reattach-failure (`e8fa816`):** a naked futures position re-attaches; if the re-attach FAILS on a tradeable market twice (~30s), the position is FLATTENED. Market-closed rejections don't escalate (frozen, can't exit). Exit guarded against double-submit on fill-to-DB lag.

**P2 — TRAIL-safe modify (`e8fa816`):** `modify_stop_price` on a TRAIL set `auxPrice` while `trailingPercent` was populated → IBKR Error 320 → CANCELLED the order → naked (the bug that bit the operator's manual stop-lift). Now sets `trailStopPrice` (the trigger) and never touches auxPrice; STP/STP_LMT unchanged.

**_build_intent venue derivation (`08bd05b`):** the shared FuturesBrokerAdapter hardcoded `Venue.EUREX`/`Currency.EUR`/`EUREX_DAYTRADE`, so a us_futures exit built a EUREX/EUR intent for a CME/USD contract → broker rejected the desk's own exits. Now derives venue/currency/discipline from the contract + adapter discipline.

## §237 — 2026-06-10 — CME phantom-position incident: import fix (Part A) + controlled cleanup (Part B)

**Incident:** a us_futures entry storm on 2026-06-09 (18:25–18:53, same class as ESTX50, pre-cooldown) accumulated 47 MES / 22 MNQ / 29 M2K (~$3.4M notional, ~€301k margin) at IBKR. The DB recorded only a fraction (the `HYGIENE_TRADE_PERSIST_DROP` fill-write failure). The position book NEVER imported them → permanent R2 recon break + margin drain that blocked legit stop placement (the ESTX50 Error 201).

**Root cause:** `InstrumentFactory._from_ibkr_future` was EUREX-only (written 2026-06-04, never updated when CME/CBOT venues were added 2026-06-06). IBKR reports CME micros with an EMPTY `exchange` field; the resolver defaulted venue→EUREX while keeping currency=USD → EUREX+USD incoherent → `position_from_ibkr_snapshot` raised → position SKIPPED every reconcile cycle.

**Part A (`fbb33ca`):** map the exchange code → venue (EUREX/DTB→EUREX, CME/GLOBEX→CME, CBOT/ECBOT→CBOT); when exchange empty, infer from currency (EUR→EUREX, USD→CME). Safe because a futures venue is identity-only (IBKR routing uses the conId-pinned FuturesContract) and CME/CBOT are USD-equivalent for the coherence check.

**Part B (`41f27b0`, executed):** staged operator-attended cleanup script `scripts/cleanup_us_futures_phantom.py` (check→disable→import→flatten→reenable). Ran it: all three imported as `future:CME:...` then flattened at IBKR (one symbol per broker-restart to clear the transient drift — see §238). us_futures desk re-enabled. ~€301k margin freed, R2 breaks resolved.

## §238 — 2026-06-10 — Reconcile-pause hardening (P3 self-heal + P3b non-drifted-exit exemption)

**P3 — book self-heals on flat positionEvent (`f3f796e`):** the Part B flatten exposed a cascade — each multi-partial-fill SELL closed the position at IBKR, but the fill-vs-realtime-sync race left a stale book residual (book=9, IBKR=0) → drift → reconcile PAUSED → blocked the next symbol's exit (needed a restart per symbol). Root cause: `PositionBook.force_close_if_held()` did not exist — `ibkr_realtime_sync` called it via getattr and silently no-op'd, so a flat positionEvent couldn't clear the residual. Added the method (conId-pinned for futures, bare symbol for equity) + wired it so a `qty==0` positionEvent closes the book row immediately. The Z5 `_reduce_long` raise (long-doesn't-flip-short) and the reconcile_paused order gate were deliberately NOT touched.

**P3b — non-drifted protective exits flow while paused (`2cff688`):** the reconcile_paused gate is global — ANY drift rejected EVERY SELL, stranding clean exits on unrelated symbols (the 2026-06-09 ESTX50 case: a futures qty-mismatch blocked every US-equity session-end exit for 3 hours). Insight: only the DRIFTED symbols have an untrustworthy book; every other symbol matches IBKR AND its book is fresh-on-fill, so a SELL reducing its held long is as safe as a normal exit (gate_sell_quantity re-clamps against the same fresh book). Added `BrokerState.reconcile_drift_symbols` (missing_at_ibkr ∪ qty_mismatch ∪ sign_flips), set on pause / cleared on resume; `orders.py` allows a SELL with `held>0 & qty<=held & symbol NOT in drift set` to fall through to the gates. Drifted symbols + all BUYs + oversized exits stay rejected. Did NOT need an IBKR-truth-at-gate read — the "not in drift set" scoping + fresh-on-fill book is sufficient and avoids the 2026-06-03 runaway-short risk.

**Deferred:** the fill-vs-sync `_reduce_long` over-apply still raises (Z5 invariant kept); P3's self-heal makes it non-fatal in practice. A futures-aware stop-coverage audit (the §234 root gap) is now largely subsumed by Y-FUT-STOP-REATTACH + P1.

## §239 — 2026-06-10 — Futures sizing upgrade: fixed cash-risk model

**Problem:** the desk sized futures positions by notional/margin caps without accounting for the actual cash exposure created by the 1.5% trailing stop and contract multipliers. Margin is small; real stop-loss risk can be large.

**New model (professional fixed-risk sizing):** size_futures already computed `risk_per_contract = stop_ticks × tick_value × fx` — equivalent to `entry × stop% × multiplier` but using the actual placed stop distance (ATR-based when ATR > 0, 1.5% fallback otherwise). The risk budget was already `RISK_PER_TRADE_EUR = €500`. The formula, floor(), and below-one rejection were already correct.

**Three fixes deployed (commit `12fadd0`):**
1. **Multiplier fill-path bug** — `emit_position_snapshot` lacked a multiplier param; every fill wrote `multiplier=1.0` to DB, overwriting the correct value. ESTX50 showed 1.0 (should be 10.0). Fixed: threaded `position.multiplier` through `_persist_position_after_fill` → `emit_position_snapshot` → `upsert_position`.
2. **US futures FX** — US contract risk is in USD; the €500 cap is in EUR. `run_once` now passes live EURUSD from `/fx/rates` as `fx_contract_to_base = 1/rate`. Fallback to 1/1.08.
3. **Dashboard risk transparency** — tap-to-expand now shows: entry, stop distance (pts), stop %, risk/contract, max loss. Mobile card shows max loss. Sizing `[sizing]` log added to `plan_entry`.

**Decision §239-D1 (2026-06-10):** ESTX50 accepted as **entry DARK** under the €500 cap. At entry ~5977, mult=10, 1.5% stop → €897/contract, floor(500/897)=0. The existing 2-lot position continues to be managed by the runner (stops, exits) until it closes naturally. No new ESTX50 entries will open at this cap. To re-enable: raise `RISK_PER_TRADE_EUR` (e.g. to €1000 → 1 contract) OR wait for a lower-ATR cycle where the placed stop is tighter than 1.5% (ATR < 89.7 pts → risk < €500). Similarly FDAX (DAX full contract, mult=25, ~€9000/contract) is always-dark; only FDXM (mult=5, ~€1800 → 0 at €500) and SX7E (mult=50, ~€200 → 2 contracts) trade in meaningful size.

**Products that trade under €500 cap:**
- SX7E: ~2 contracts (€400 risk) ✓
- MES: ~2 contracts (€240 risk at ~5500, after FX) ✓
- M2K: ~2 contracts (~€197 after FX) ✓
- MYM: ~2 contracts (~€175 after FX) ✓
- FDXM: 0 — dark
- ESTX50: 0 — dark (§239-D1)
- MNQ: 0 — dark at 28000 (~€780/contract)

## §240 — 2026-06-10 — Zombie-order cancel: the double-sell / phantom-short root cause

**Incident (afternoon):** at US RTH open (13:30 UTC) EC/ESRT/ALK appeared as SHORTS at IBKR (EC=−40, ESRT=−117, ALK=−14), local book agreeing, reconcile NOT paused. Operator flattened (BUY-to-close, confirmed IBKR-truth first; my first MKT batch mis-parsed `accepted` and one ESRT MKT silently filled, then the LMT batch stacked → had to re-flatten — operator-side lesson: confirm each fill before the next).

**Root cause (the recurring class):** session-end EXIT SELL orders marked CANCELLED in our DB but left LIVE at IBKR overnight. Y-RECONCILE.1 already DETECTED them at startup ("IBKR has open order X but DB status is CANCELLED") and **logged-and-walked-away**. At RTH open the zombie SELLs fired; the fills arrived with coids our DB called CANCELLED → `on_fill_event` dropped them as unknown-coid orphans → reconcile imported the resulting IBKR state as shorts. Same family as 2026-06-03 (uncontrolled net shorts on a long-only desk).

**Fix (`7ae4280`):** `rehydrate_registry_from_ibkr` now takes `ibkr_trades` + `ib`; when a DB-terminal order is still live at IBKR it calls `ib.cancelOrder(trade.order)` immediately and logs CRITICAL (`zombie_cancelled` count on the report + startup line). Without an ib handle the old warn-and-leave is preserved. Wired at both call sites in main.py. **Verified on first restart: cancelled 4 zombies** (incl. a yesterday MPT stop). 2 tests (cancel-with-ib, fallback-without-ib). The whole "stale EXIT fires at open → dropped fill → imported short" chain is closed at source.

## §241 — 2026-06-10 — Futures sizing v2: price risk against the DEPLOYED stop + hard position cap

**Bug:** `plan_entry` sized risk against the ATR initial stop, but the submitters deploy a native 1.5% IBKR trail and IGNORE the ATR stop. When ATR was tight (MES 0.16%) the sizer priced 7–9 contracts for a €500 budget while the real 1.5% trail made the actual risk ~$5k (the 7-lot MES the operator caught). The §239 morning work (multiplier fill-path, US FX, dashboard breakdown) was correct but sized off the wrong stop.

**Fix (`f7d9352`), the operator's formula:** `risk_per_contract = entry × stop% × multiplier × FX`; `contracts = floor(cap / risk_per_contract)`.
1. `deployed_initial_stop_price()` — the stop the submitter actually places (native_trail_pct when set, else ATR), trail distance snapped UP to a tick so priced risk ≥ deployed risk. `plan_entry` sizes + sets `plan.stop_price` from this.
2. **Hard position-risk cap** — a final independent clamp recomputing real max-loss from the deployed stop; clamps/rejects so a position can never exceed its € cap even if `size_futures` regressed.

**Behavioural consequence:** at €500, products whose 1-lot 1.5% risk exceeds the cap go DARK (FDXM €1822, FDAX €9112, MNQ €755). SX7E→2, ESTX50→1 (€1000 cap), MES→1, M2K→2, MYM→1. Raise via `_RISK_PER_TRADE_EUR_BY_KEY`. Live held positions untouched (new entries only). 7 tests incl. the operator's SX7E worked example.

## §242 — 2026-06-10 — Futures entry gate: 3-bar momentum burst (replaces VWAP position)

**Operator decision:** on deep liquid index futures, VWAP-position entry gets in too late — by the time price is back above VWAP the move is half over. Replace it with a velocity flip off a confirmed pullback.

**The gate (`98f4b9f`):** after the kept session/regime/ATR/RVOL spine, `decide_futures_entry` fires LONG on the last 5 closes showing ↓↓↑↑ — `c[-4]<c[-5]` (falling), `c[-3]<c[-4]` (new low), `c[-2]>c[-3]` (up1), `c[-1]>c[-2]` (up2). Strict inequalities → a flat bar can't fire. Optional `momentum_atr_min_move` floor (0.0=off). VWAP is DEMOTED, not deleted — still computed + captured as `vwap_dist_pct` for the courtroom; just no longer a gate. No volume condition (explicit operator decision — permanent deep liquidity). `recent_closes` added to features; dashboard distance-to-trigger board state map updated. **Spec note:** the brief's `momentum_bars_required=4` can't evaluate condition 1 (5 closes needed); set to 5, guard uses `max(param,5)`; operator CONFIRMED 5. Long-only today (bearish→SHORT deferred to short-arm). Tests: clean flip fires, <5 bars / one-up-close / flat-bar → no signal, ATR still gates, VWAP still computed.

**Test debt cleared (`514d874`):** 16 stale futures tests (runner §231 native-trail, dashboard refactor fixtures, §233 config drift, §231 submitter stop) restored — full futures suite 274 green. All confirmed stale, no live bugs.

## §243 — 2026-06-10 — Futures dashboard truth pass (held-time, @STOP, avg unit, momentum display)

Four fixes so the FUT section stops lying. (1) **Distance-to-Trigger shows momentum, not VWAP** (`27f708b`, the §242 follow-up): arrows ↓↓↑↑ + leg count + LONG-READY chip via `_momentum_view`; VWAP demoted to context. (2) **MOM column alignment** (`918e48f`). (3) **True IBKR held-time** (`3dc12b6`): two holdings showed "held 21h" — a closed position's DB row is zeroed-but-kept and on reopen the upsert preserves the OLD `opened_at` (Z3). `_resync_db_positions_from_book` now drags the DB `opened_at` FORWARD to the in-memory book's (IBKR truth) when it lags, firing only on a genuine reopen (a continuously-held position has book==DB). ESTX50 21h→4.0h, SX7E→4.7h. (4) **@STOP column + avg unit detection** (`3dc12b6`): replaced the ambiguous RISK column with **@STOP** = the realised outcome IF the stop triggers, measured from entry exactly like P&L so the two are comparable and never summed (green=locked-in gain, red=capped loss); "downside to stop" (the old RISK = bridge between them) moved to detail. This exposed the `avg_cost` unit inconsistency — stored per-unit USD for some contracts (ESTX50, MES) and total-cost = price×mult for others (SX7E) — which, when entry fills are absent, drove the MES −$1,036,275 / ESTX50 €108k phantom P&L. Both EUR + US enrich paths now detect the unit from the avg-to-live ratio (per-unit → ratio≈fx; total-cost → ratio≈fx×mult). Root (broker stores avg_cost inconsistently) is a data issue; the detector makes display robust. 17 dashboard + 52 reconcile tests green.

## §244 — 2026-06-10 — PAPER-ONLY big-clip caps: ES / NQ / MNQ size exactly 1

**Operator decision (paper only):** ES/NQ flash LONG-READY but never fill — full-size clips (mult 50/20) floor to 0 contracts at the €500 desk risk (`floor(cap/risk_per_contract)=0`). While paper-trading the operator wants to exercise exactly ONE of each (and MNQ, the mult-2 micro, which also floored at €500). Added `_PAPER_ONLY_RISK_PER_TRADE_USD_BY_KEY` in `us_futures_desk.py` (`0a9ea79` ES/NQ, `ebeb416` MNQ): `es=5500, nq=8700, mnq=870` (EUR base, mirroring `RISK_PER_TRADE`). Sized to fit exactly 1 at the LIVE price (ES ~7310→€4,747/ctr, NQ ~28644→€7,440/ctr, MNQ→€744/ctr) with ~16% headroom; **can never reach 2** intraday (needs a 25–42% price drop), and harmlessly returns to 0 if the price rises past ES ~8470 / NQ ~33495.

**⚠️ REVERT BEFORE REAL-MONEY GO-LIVE.** 1 ES risks ~10×, 1 NQ ~17× the normal €500 per-trade budget. The desk is `execution_mode="paper"` and there is NO runtime live/paper flag gating this — the guard is the loud comment + memory `paper-only-es-nq-cap`. (The operator's original $4,125/$6,000 numbers were a stale price estimate of mine; corrected against live prices via AskUserQuestion before setting.)

**Truthful activity board (`0a9ea79`):** new `sizeable_contracts` on every activity row, computed from the SAME desk caps + deployed-stop risk the sizer uses (`_sizing_caps()` sourced from `contract_configs()` so it never drifts). Green "N ctr" badge on LONG-READY, red "0 ctr" when too big for the cap. **Cache-buster** bumped `?v=tradetap → ?v=20260610b` on the JS+CSS includes — the prior static buster let an already-open tab keep running stale in-memory JS (the "blank holdings window" the operator hit).

## §245 — 2026-06-10 — Double-stop reattach churn on fresh bracket entries

**Symptom:** enabling MNQ (§244) caused a ~2-minute storm of stop submit/reject/cancel the moment it first filled — constant IBKR mobile pings, "over-covered / double-stop" audit lines, and `gate_sell_quantity` rejections ("no uncommitted long to sell — held 1.0, 1.0 in-flight SELLs, 2.0 working bracket"). Verified against IBKR truth: positions matched (18=18), gates held, **no short ever created** — noise, not risk.

**Two compounding bugs** in `FuturesBrokerAdapter.list_open_positions`' naked-stop detection (`4c7ff7d`): (1) **con_id=None stops were DROPPED** — `_active_stops_by_con_id` keyed coverage by con_id only, skipping any stop the venue surfaces with `con_id=None`, which is exactly how a just-placed reattach TRAIL lands → the adapter's own reattach was invisible to the next tick → it re-reattached forever → the audit kept cancelling the duplicate. (2) **No grace for the bracket stop to register** — a freshly bracket-entered position carries its protective stop as a STP_LMT *bracket child* that surfaces ACTIVE a few seconds late; reattaching in that window places the second stop and starts the loop.

**Fix (both fail-safe — they only ADD coverage recognition, never remove it; the broker `gate_sell_quantity` remains the backstop against a real short):** `_active_stops_indexes()` now indexes ACTIVE stops by con_id AND by symbol (coverage matches either, so a con_id=None reattach TRAIL counts); a 30s **entry grace** (`_reattach_grace_s`) suppresses reattach on a position whose `opened_at` is known and younger than the grace (unknown opened_at → no grace, so a genuinely orphaned position is still protected without delay; the zero-tolerance reattach/flatten for real mid-life orphans is unchanged). 4 new tests (within-grace suppression, post-grace reattach, unknown-opened-at immediate, null-con_id symbol coverage); 19 adapter + 47 related green.

**Related (no code, recorded for the file):** the same session's "phone dinging constantly, nothing on the dashboard" alarm was NOT an incident. FRMI in particular — the operator got "sell confirmations" — was verified FLAT at IBKR (its own `positionEvent` streamed `qty=0.0000` continuously, zero fills, not in the broker book); the "sells" were the bracket's two protective SELL legs being placed + cancelled across 4 unfilled entry attempts. The standing lesson: the phone dings on every ORDER event (submits/cancels/reattaches), the dashboard shows only completed TRADES — mobile always looks far busier than the book actually is.

## §246 — 2026-06-11 — V-LEDGER Phase 3 cutover: the projector becomes the authoritative writer of IBKR positions

**Decision (operator: "build and flip phase 3"):** flip the execution-sourced ledger from SHADOW to AUTHORITATIVE for the IBKR `positions` table. This caps the V-LEDGER arc built across the prior session (Phase 0 capture `fc2b6fc` → Phase 1 projector `7b2f717` → Phase 1b shadow loop `544140b` → Phase 2 clean opening-balance cutover `38b1676`). Full design + ops doc: `docs/EXECUTION_LEDGER_PHASE3.md`. Commits `c7e2987` (writer + wiring, dark) + `0461bc5` (IBKR-only scoping); flag flipped in `.env`.

**What it does.** `positions` is now a deterministic fold of the immutable `executions` log (`ledger_writer.project_and_write_positions`): upsert open positions (signed — a short is written honestly), zero closed lots. It runs on the fill path (`persistent_sink.emit_execution`, atomic with the IBKR-venue capture, in the same txn), every reconcile cycle, and the brain `ledger_shadow` safety-net (~307s). This kills the drift/drop/staleness/blindness/avg-cost-phantom class **structurally** for equities + futures — none can exist when `positions = fold(immutable log)`.

**Reconcile → compare-and-alert (no mutation).** Under `LEDGER_AUTHORITATIVE=true` the three destructive DB-mutation helpers (`_y35_persist_position_to_db`, `_resync_db_positions_from_book`, `_zero_ghost_db_positions`) no-op. Instead `emit_venue_corrections` compares the projection to the IBKR snapshot; on divergence it appends ONE auditable `kind='venue_correction'` execution = the delta (so the next projection matches the venue) + alarm — a deterministic self-heal in the log, NOT a `force_resync` wipe. The in-memory `PositionBook` is still synced to IBKR (the sizing reference) and the **reconcile-PAUSE halt signal is unchanged** — only reconcile-as-*mutation* of the DB retired, not reconcile-as-*halt*.

**Two deliberate scope calls.** (1) **IBKR only.** Live book at cutover = FRMI −75 (IBKR) + 4 crypto (Binance). The IBKR reconcile is blind to Binance, so without scoping `emit_venue_corrections` would see the 4 crypto positions as "missing at IBKR" and emit zeroing corrections — wiping live crypto. `_is_ibkr()` (skips `crypto:` canonicals) guards both writer functions; the fill hook fires only on `venue==IBKR`. Crypto = Phase 5. (2) **`trades` NOT rewritten.** Phase 2 proved backfilling the 15,346 historical `fills` is non-viable (it folds to 473 phantom-open / 143 impossible shorts — the fills carry the same drops the ledger fixes), so the log is forward-only and cannot reproduce the 1,529 historical trades + their `exit_reason`/`regime`/`pnl_usd` metadata the courtroom reads. Positions (the drift surface) are owned by the projector; trade-drops are already prevented by the on_fill race fix (`orders.py:on_fill_event`).

**Rollback (instant):** `LEDGER_AUTHORITATIVE=false` + restart broker+brain → old path byte-for-byte (the flag only affects broker + brain; full suite proves zero behaviour change with it off).

**Verified live.** Dry-run vs the live log: reproduced FRMI −75 exactly (0 add / 0 zero / 0 mismatch), crypto untouched. Post-flip: shadow `5=5, 0 divergences, clean`; broker logs `ledger_writer: authoritative write — open=1` + `book matches IBKR — trading RESUMED` each cycle, 0 venue_corrections, no errors. 9 new `test_ledger_writer` cases; full broker/db suite 1,909 passed (2 pre-existing env-config failures, unrelated). FRMI −75 cover (BUY 75) queued for the 13:30 UTC open — projection nets to flat when it fills, or reconcile self-heals via venue_correction if the rehydrated cover fill isn't captured. **Remaining (operator-gated, post-soak):** Phase 4 (delete the dead patchwork incl. `drift_detector`) + Phase 5 (crypto onto the same ledger).

## §247 — 2026-06-11 — Phase-3 soak gate wired into the sweeps + crypto closing-fill capture (the soak's first catch)

**Soak canary (`scripts/ledger_soak_check.py`, commits up to `c369991`).** Phase 4 (deleting the old reconcile patchwork) is gated on the §246 cutover staying clean across trading sessions. Built a read-only canary the FULL + LIGHT maintenance sweeps now run every cycle (recreated both cron prompts; standing item also in `docs/WEEKEND_MAINTENANCE_AUDIT.md` since the crons are session-only). Verdict is on the **IBKR slice only** (what the cutover governs): WARN = a live IBKR projection-vs-table divergence (real regression, surface+buzz); WATCH = `venue_correction`s present (a fill bypassed capture, self-heals, trace it); PASS = IBKR projection==live + 0 IBKR venue_corrections. The `venue_correction` count is **IBKR-venue-scoped** — crypto corrections must not trip the IBKR verdict.

**Crypto closing-fill capture (`65ae6a4`) — the soak's first real catch.** The canary immediately surfaced a genuine gap: crypto **entry** BUYs were captured (executor order-create response) but async OCO/stop **SELL exits** fill at Binance and surface ONLY on the user-data WS stream — bypassing the executor — so the executions log never saw the close and the projection lingered as a phantom-open (HOME/PAXG closed live but still projected open). Fix: `CryptoReconcile._capture_execution_from_ws` captures EVERY WS `executionReport` TRADE fill, keyed by the Binance `tradeId` (`BINANCE-{symbol}-{tradeId}` — the SAME exec_id the entry capture uses → idempotent on both paths), with `instrument_canonical` rebuilt via `InstrumentFactory` so a SELL nets the BUY to flat. Fail-soft; crypto stays SHADOW (Phase 5) but capture is now complete. The 2 pre-fix stragglers (HOME/PAXG) were netted with one-time `venue_correction` closes (venue-flat backfill). 4 new tests; crypto broker suite 259 passed. Soak now PASS, all-ledger shadow clean. **Lesson reinforced:** the canary earned its keep on day one — a "soak gate" that finds real gaps is worth more than one that always says PASS.

## §250 — 2026-06-11 — Pre-flight safe-flatten gate: IBKR-truth confirmation kills the recurring EOD-flatten short

**Trigger (operator).** "The end-of-day flatten created a short last night and often does this — it needs a pre-flight check; can I just do a broad flatten or is there risk?" Diagnosed live: ESTX50 (long) has an active stop, FRMI is a −75 short with its cover queued. A broad flatten would (a) double-sell ESTX50 (flatten MKT + its resting stop both fill → short) and (b) deepen FRMI's short (a blind SELL on a short). So a broad flatten is UNSAFE; the operator is right. Commit `c18810e`.

**The real mechanism.** The desk's exit path is already heavily defended (Y77 sign-aware, Y181/Y182 dedup, Y211 cancel-both-children, Y-OVS two-phase cancel→breather→re-check→MKT, atomic STP_LMT→MKT modify). The residual gap: the Y-OVS breather is ONE tick, and **Phase B then trusts the strategy `/positions` snapshot — which can still lag a racing protective-stop fill.** Phase B fires the stale long qty → oversells → SHORT (the FRMI/Y-OVS-incident fingerprint: BUY → SELL TRAIL FILLED → EXIT MKT FILLED → short).

**The fix — confirm IBKR TRUTH the instant before the Phase-B submit.** New pure `alphabot/strategy/safe_flatten.py:safe_flatten_verdict` bounds the order to what IBKR actually holds, in IBKR's direction: IBKR flat → SKIP (the stop already closed it); sign(book)≠sign(IBKR) → SKIP (don't sell into a short — the FRMI shape); IBKR reduced → fire ONLY `|ibkr_qty|` (never the stale book qty); IBKR unavailable → fail OPEN to the book qty (transient ≠ unsafe; the Y-OVS guards remain the backstop). Wired in `_fire_exit` Phase B via `broker_client.get_position` (now §246 ledger-authoritative). **It can never emit more than IBKR holds → cannot create a short.** Only the legacy/orphaned-bracket path is gated; the atomic modify is race-free and untouched. Gated by `SAFE_FLATTEN_PREFLIGHT_ENABLED` (default ON; instant kill-switch → flip off + restart strategy). 10 new safety tests (incl. a grid invariant that fired-qty ≤ |ibkr_qty|) + 115 stop-runner regression green. Strategy restarted + healthy. This is the durable answer to "it often does this" — and note it builds directly on §246: the flatten is safe now because `get_position` is finally IBKR-truth.

## §251 — 2026-06-11 — Futures P&L reconciled across the dashboard (holdings↔trades currency, master totals, by-market) + Direction window deleted

**Trigger (operator).** "Holdings showed healthy profit, the closed trade showed a healthy loss — they need to match. Also desk-stats master P&Ls aren't taking in futures, nor the header bar. And I don't like the Direction window — delete it." Three currency/aggregation bugs + a UI removal, all on the futures P&L surface. Commits `b9ae25c` + `89d850c` + `6915d2d`.

**(1) holdings↔trades currency mismatch (`b9ae25c`).** Diagnosed live: a closed ESTX50 trade recorded `entry=6989` on a contract trading at `6040` native EUR — exactly ×1.155 (EUR/USD). The `trades` table stores entry/exit in USD (fill VWAP × FX, the Y32 USD-canonical contract) while holdings (Part B §248) compute native EUR — so a trade never matched the holding it came from (~15% off, could flip sign). `_convert_eurex_trades_to_eur` divides entry/exit/pnl by the live EUR/USD so a closed EUREX trade reads native EUR like holdings; `pnl_pct` (invariant) untouched; no-FX → flagged not guessed. (Durable fix = store native at trade_tracker — follow-on.) Also restored Desk Stats: the V5 DIRECTION panel had been inserted at the TOP of the desk-stats column (data was always live — purely positional); moved it below, then deleted entirely.

**(2) master P&L excluded futures (`89d850c`).** The desk-stats TODAY query + the header perf-strip (`_day_pnl`, `_day_pnl_buckets`) filtered to `_DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES` (equity+crypto, no eurex/us_futures), while `master_metrics` (the rolling windows) has NO discipline filter and already counted futures — so TODAY/header silently dropped them. New `_PNL_DISCIPLINES` superset (= `_DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES` + eurex_daytrade + us_futures_daytrade) used at the P&L-total sites ONLY (not the broad list that drives activity/scanner). Futures `pnl_usd` is USD + multiplier-aware (EUREX ×10/×50, US ×5), so it sums straight into the USD master. Hardcoded 8-placeholder IN-clauses → dynamic.

**(3) Direction window deleted (`89d850c`).** Removed the desktop panel + its poll; the V5 direction signal still captures in the backend (shadow), just not shown.

**(4) by-market breakout (`6915d2d`).** The BY MARKET (TODAY) breakdown still keyed off `_DAYTRADE_DISCIPLINES`; switched its query+loop to `_PNL_DISCIPLINES` + added discipline→market maps (eurex→EUREX, us_futures→US FUT). Ties out exactly: CRYPTO +17.48 + EUREX −67.30 = −49.82, matching the master + header. 

**Net:** holdings (EUR) ↔ trades (EUR) ↔ master totals ↔ header ↔ by-market all consistent and all include futures. 55 desk-stats + 23 futures-terminal tests green. The throughline — every futures P&L bug this run was the same disease as §248: a number computed in the wrong currency basis, or an aggregate filtered to exclude futures. **Durable follow-on:** store trade entry/exit in native currency at the trade_tracker so the dashboard needs no live-FX conversion.

Follow-ons to §251, both operator-directed. Commits `9e420ad` (native ccy) + `04a06f8` (live price); by-market trimmed to live desks in `21b87f3`.

(Residual: the md-daemon's freshest is the last COMPLETED 1m bar — no in-progress tick — so ~1 min lag remains; true sub-minute would need the daemon to expose the in-progress bar.)

## §253 — 2026-06-11 — Trailing stops fixed at the ROOT: place native trail once, verify, FLATTEN if gone (no re-attach churn)

Commit `7161418`. Operator, after months of naked-futures pain: *"review the whole thing from the ground up and tell me how we place trailing stops on IBKR. it can't be that hard but we can't achieve it."* A ground-up review (3 parallel code audits) inverted the assumption.

**The surprise: placement was never broken.** A native IBKR `TRAIL` bracket child is server-side + GTC and **survives broker restarts** — proven live this session (the 5 held futures TRAILs came back, alive and ratcheting, after two restarts; NQ's trigger had ratcheted 28306→28473). What failed was **durability**, in the reconcile *re-attach* path: when a position read naked, the audit re-attached a **blind off-tick fallback STP** (`entry × 0.95`, never tick-snapped — `Instrument.to_ibkr_contract()` raises for a FUTURE, so the tick-rounding pass is a structural no-op, and futures disciplines aren't in `FALLBACK_STOP_PCT`/`ATR` either). IBKR rejected the off-grid price → marked the order **`Inactive`** → `find_naked_positions` (correctly) doesn't count Inactive as covered → re-detect naked → re-attach forever (the live NQ/MNQ "placed but NOT STICKING after 3 cycles, backing off 600s" churn). Compounding it: our own machinery (orphan-sweep, modify, the re-attach itself) poking otherwise-healthy children.

**The operator's reframe — the fix:** *"if we successfully place a native trailing stop, why are we messing with it at all? verify that it is there and leave it the hell alone!"* New policy `BROKER_STOP_COVERAGE_FLATTEN_ON_NAKED` (default OFF; **ARMED in .env**): the stop-coverage audit READS IBKR truth and **never re-attaches or modifies**. A held LONG confirmed naked for `BROKER_STOP_COVERAGE_FLATTEN_CONFIRM_CYCLES` (2) **consecutive** cycles — debouncing a single flaky `reqAllOpenOrders` read — and **past** a post-restart `BROKER_STOP_COVERAGE_FLATTEN_BOOT_SETTLE_S` (120s) window — so a slow boot order-sync can't false-flag a healthy book — is **MARKET-EXITED**. The exit goes through `_flatten_executor` (broker): fresh independent IBKR position read → `safe_flatten_verdict` (the §250 primitive — bounds the order to ≤ what IBKR holds, in IBKR's direction; **cannot oversell into a short**) → MKT tagged `STOP_COVERAGE_NAKED_FLATTEN`, a mandatory-exit reason whose Y210 `working_bracket==0` guard is satisfied by definition (a naked position has zero live children). A naked **SHORT** is never auto-flattened here — it stays the B5 pause-for-operator (a drift incident, not a torn-off stop). Scope = **all IBKR disciplines** (operator pick); crypto is a separate broker (§224 owns it), untouched.

**Why this is the durable fix, not another patch:** it doesn't depend on enumerating every way a child can die. Healthy → audit sees the live TRAIL → does nothing. Gone → flatten. The re-attach churn (the off-tick Inactive loop) is bypassed entirely when armed. Files: `config.py` (3 flags) · `reconcile.py` (`_handle_naked_flatten` streak + boot-settle, `flatten_fn` injection, early-return that preserves the over-coverage cancel) · `main.py` (`_flatten_executor`) · `risk.py` (mandatory-exit reason) · `stop_coverage_audit.py` (action-neutral logging). **12 unit tests** (2-cycle debounce, boot-settle defer, healthy-left-alone, streak-clears-on-reappear, naked-SHORT-pauses, conId-keyed futures, safe-no-op, flag-off dormant, bad-snapshot-untouched); `scripts/stop_flatten_verify.py` harness; 62 existing stop/flatten/reconcile tests still green (3 pre-existing repo failures unrelated, verified on a clean tree).

## §255 — 2026-06-11 — Profit-ratchet ("dynamic expanding take profit"), all disciplines

Commit `2de174e`. Operator, watching futures jump into significant profit they couldn't bank: *"we need a way for them to know to exit and bank it… can we have a dynamic expanding take profit?"* The native 1.5% trail can't bank a modest run — on NQ it sits ~$8.7k below the peak, so a €4k gain rides all the way back to ~breakeven (the Y160 breakeven floor saves it from a loss but banks nothing).

**Evidence first** (the desk's discipline). `scripts/futures_giveback_analysis.py` simulates a peak-tracking synthetic stop over the REAL 5m price paths (open positions + closed trades, per discipline). The verdict was stark: the **1.5% trail NETS NEGATIVE on futures** (−$2,590, −32% of the theoretical peak — on the big movers it gives back so much it exits below entry). A **give-back-as-%-of-peak** rule dominated every fixed-trail at every setting: **20% give-back banked ~$4.8k (+$7.4k vs the trail, 61% of peak)**. Re-ran for equity (marginal — tiny peaks, +$39, pctpeak-20 still best) and crypto (+$1,232 vs a bleeding −$617 actual; pctpeak-20 ≈ trail-0.3% ≈ best). 20% was optimal across ALL THREE; **shipped at 25%** to hedge live whipsaw (the 5m backtest can't see the intra-bar noise the live ~15s poll does, which premature-exits more than the bars show).

**Mechanism — one helper, both spines, no new order path.** Pure `profit_ratchet_exit(entry, current, running_extreme, giveback_frac, activation_frac, is_short)` in `shared/futures_stop_logic.py`: arm once peak gain ≥ entry×ACTIVATION (0.15%); exit when price retraces ≥ GIVEBACK (25%) of the peak gain, i.e. current ≤ entry + peak_gain×(1−giveback). The protected floor RATCHETS UP with the peak (winners run) while the give-back tightens in absolute terms with profit — the "dynamic expanding take profit". Wired into the futures decision (`decide_futures_stop_action`, inside the native-trail branch, BEFORE the time-stop; params via `FuturesStopParams.profit_ratchet_*` from `eurex_desk`/`us_futures_desk` `stop_params_for`) and the equity/crypto decision (`decide_action_hybrid`, after take-profit, before the time-stop; params from settings via `_decide_hybrid`). Each returns an `exit` decision with reason `DAYTRADE_PROFIT_RATCHET` and fires through the discipline's EXISTING exit path (`submit_market_exit` futures / `_fire_exit` equity+crypto) — **identical safety surface to the live time-stop exits** (futures trails aren't in the equity `working_bracket`, so the gate passes; the runner's exit handles the bracket). The native trail stays the catastrophe floor underneath. Flag `PROFIT_RATCHET_ENABLED` (default off; armed in .env), `PROFIT_RATCHET_GIVEBACK` (0.25), `PROFIT_RATCHET_ACTIVATION` (0.0015). 14 tests; verified live (DAYTRADE_PROFIT_RATCHET on BA seconds after arming).

**Bonus (safety):** arming = more exits, which surfaced that the §250 safe-flatten pre-flight calls `broker_client.get_position` — never routed by `MultiBrokerProxy`, so it raised AttributeError and **fail-opened on EVERY exit** (the anti-short IBKR-truth gate was silently OFF; LONG_ONLY + the Y-OVS two-phase still protected, so no shorts). Added `MultiBrokerProxy.get_position` routing → the pre-flight is functional again. The throughline: arming new behaviour is the best way to find a dead guard.

## §257 — 2026-06-11/12 — Dropped-trade fix (force-close race) + $18,144 P&L recovery

- **Recovery:** the fills were never lost (executions log) — reconstructed all 6 futures + SX7E via the projector (cross-checked hand-math; caught a $1,155→$231 M2K slip), wrote them as `DAYTRADE_SESSION_END_FLAT` (NOT RECONCILED — those are excluded from desk stats). ## §271 — 2026-06-17 — Two display/semantics CONTRACTS pinned (LOCKED PROF; signed net_atr) + A/B eval durably scheduled

Operational session (bug-fixes + ops; detail in HANDOVER_64). Two recurring-regression risks are pinned here as contracts so a future instance can't re-break them, plus the gate A/B eval is now on a session-independent schedule. Commits `1e5b3e34`→`b5152ed1`.

- **LOCKED PROF is a GUARANTEED-FLOOR contract, distinct from @STOP (`bd5203f1`).** The futures terminal's per-holding "LOCKED PROF" was rendering the raw signed at-stop outcome (`(stop−entry)×mult×qty`) — so a normal protective stop *below* entry showed a **negative "lock"** (MBT: −$232) and the gold LOCK line drew at the stop price (below entry → pinned to the chart floor). Contract going forward: **LOCKED PROF = the at-stop outcome floored to a real guaranteed profit — positive ONLY when the stop sits above entry, else `None`** (new backend helper `_locked_profit()`, field `locked_profit_usd/eur` on every holding builder; test `TestLockedProfitFloor`). `None` ⇒ the frontend hides BOTH the readout (shows "—") AND the gold lock-line — never a negative lock, never a floor-pinned line. **The separate `@STOP` cell keeps the honest SIGNED outcome** (it may be a loss — "if stopped here you'd realize −$232"); do NOT floor `@STOP`. This is the SECOND lock-line render fix (§270 was the first, on the *other* terminal `daytrade_terminal.js`); the contract now lives in code + a test so it stops recurring. Also fixed in the same drop: IN/LOCK/OUT chart ref-labels were illegibly blurred by `preserveAspectRatio="none"` stretching in-SVG `<text>` → moved to a crisp HTML overlay (`.rax`).
- **`persist_net_atr_min` is a SIGNED, directional threshold — not a magnitude (`b5152ed1`).** Confirmed + documented after an operator question: the gate is `net_atr >= +min` for LONG and `net_atr <= −min` for SHORT (futures_entry.py:345/352). A falling tape (`net_atr<0`) can **never** satisfy the LONG side — the desk does not chase a −2.0-ATR down-move into a long. The field comment previously read `|net move|` (absolute-value phrasing, misleading); corrected to state the signed/directional behavior. Behavior was always correct; only the comment was wrong.
- **Gate 80→70 A/B eval — durably scheduled for the 23rd (`1fa981d1` + OS `at` job).** The CronCreate `durable:true` flag did NOT persist (reported "Session-only … dies when Claude exits"; no `.claude/scheduled_tasks.json` written), so the eval is scheduled via a system-level **`at` job (job 2, 2026-06-23 08:17)** — independent of any Claude session — running `scripts/gate_ab_cron.sh` (runs `gate_ab_eval.py` + `gate_threshold_study.py`, telegrams the verdict). **Lesson: for a multi-day reminder that MUST fire, use `at`/cron (atd is active), not CronCreate `durable` — it is session-only here.** Must run before bar_history's 7-day prune.
- **Eurex regime badge fixed (`1e5b3e34`).** The dashboard regime badge keyed off the retired full-size `ESTX50` (no md feed → empty `{}`); pointed it at the live micro `ESTX50_MC`. Same dead-symbol class as the §270 board-tile drop.

## §272 — 2026-06-17 — SIM & courtroom GATE-TOURNAMENT overhaul (Drops 1–4) + holdings-card layout fix

Operator ask: "we changed our gates a lot, the SIM and courtroom need a complete overhaul." A 4-agent read-only review (`docs/SIM_COURTROOM_GATE_OVERHAUL_REVIEW.md`, PLAN rev 2) found the SIM, courtroom, AND dashboard all still measure the **retired ↓↓↑↑ burst** (and older reversion footprints), not the live **momentum-persistence** gate. Root cause was architectural: the analytics **reimplemented** the signal in replay, so they rot on every gate change. The operator pushed for a future-proof design ("I don't want to always start from zero if we tune gates") → a **gate tournament over stored bars**. Commits `8242a4d0`→`94386309` (all pushed).

**Architecture / the lock that prevents the next rot.** Capture is already gate-agnostic: futures 1m bars are kept INDEFINITELY (`retention.py` Stone 0), context in `fut_signal_funnel`, outcomes in `trades`. A gate is a **parameterised function over those bars**, so:
- **L-GATE-ONE-IMPL (Lock 1): one gate implementation, shared by live AND replay.** The replay calls the LIVE `compute_features` + `decide_futures_entry(params)` — never a reimplementation. A gate change in `futures_entry.py` now flows into the SIM/courtroom automatically, zero edits. THE fix for the recurring drift.
- **Bars are the system of record** — derived gate numbers (`green_density`/`net_atr`/`atr_expanding`) are recomputed at replay time, never stored as the foundation. The rev-1 plan to add capture columns to the live daytrade daemon was DROPPED (not needed; also avoided any approval-gated desk touch — the whole overhaul is analytics + UI).

**Shipped (analytics + UI only; no trading-path change):**
- **Drop 1 `intelligence/fut_gate_replay.py`** — the shared core. `decide_for_window` (live features→live decision) + `replay_gate_over_funnel` (replay any params over the funnel, 1m, strict look-ahead, forward returns + the replay-vs-funnel **fidelity** reconciliation stat). Live probe: **99.3% agreement** replaying the live gate over 5,000 real cycles (proves Lock 1).
- **Drop 2 `intelligence/fut_gate_tournament.py`** — the parametric tournament: a registry of entrants (live gate + density/net_atr sweeps) replayed in ONE pass, ranked by gross forward edge. Live: density=60 *looks* better than the live 70 (gross), 80 worse — actionable only after Drop 3.
- **Drop 3 `intelligence/fut_gate_courtroom.py`** — Tier-A verdicts on entrants, reusing the EXISTING engine (walk_forward + beat_luck + BH-FDR + Deflated-Sharpe + cost), own deflation family, persisted to `courtroom_verdicts`. Live dry-run: 294 trials all ACCUMULATING (1m history ~3–4 days old — the honest guardrail: tune on a verdict, not gross noise).
- **Drop 4 (surface + console + cleanup + terminal):** new PIN-gated `GET /edge/gate-tournament` + brain-console **INTEL → 🏆 GATES** tab (leaderboard, live gate flagged + fidelity); `prosecute_gate_all` wired into `nightly_edge.py` (verdicts accrue nightly); removed **~342 lines of DEAD equity/crypto courtroom UI** from `app.js` (renderCourt/renderCourtCrypto + 404 callers + Asset toggle — full call-graph verified before deletion); **live terminal rewired to the live gate** — ARMED off `state_reason` (momentum_persistence_*), readiness/trigger off `green_density`, density colour 80→70, ATR colour off `atr_expanding` (was the removed `atr_pass` band), desktop + mobile. (Cache-bust: bumped the `?v=` asset version `y228-mob2`→`drop4-gates` so browsers fetch the new `app.js` — without it the GATES tab silently no-op'd on the cached old file.)
- **Drop 4e (resurface the EXISTING SIM + COURTROOM tabs).** Drop 4 *added* the new GATES surface but left the old SIM/COURTROOM showing the burst as "LIVE". 4e fixes that: COURTROOM `_family_verdicts` gains a **`gate`** family (`gate_*`), the families panel **leads with the live gate**, the burst is relabelled "(RETIRED) benchmark", and the trending "LIVE" badge → "EX-LIVE" (`b4992922`); the SIM tab is relabelled "burst benchmark (RETIRED)" with a banner pointing to 🏆 GATES (`34872ae0`). **Two operational lessons (now in HANDOVER_65 RESUME):** (1) a Python route change needs an `alphabot-brain` **restart** or it 404s on the old process; (2) bump the `?v=` asset version on EVERY `app.js`/`app.css` change or browsers serve the cached old file.

**Tests:** 24 new (8+6+8+2) all green; ruff+mypy clean on new code; `node --check` clean on the frontend. **Deferred:** cold-start (verdicts stay ACCUMULATING until ~3×W sessions of 1m bank); INSTR full-size `'ESTX50'` label removal (cosmetic — confirm the micro's served symbol first); benchmark entrants (old burst/footprint) + an exit-policy axis as future tournament extensions (review §7).

**Also this session (operational):** futures-terminal holdings card trimmed ~30% in height (`e7231cda`) — chart region −30% + P&L/LOCKED-PROF KPIs un-stacked side-by-side (desktop + mobile), fonts unchanged; the chart's fixed viewBox keeps all labels/ref-lines intact.

New lock: **L-GATE-ONE-IMPL**. Doc of record: `docs/SIM_COURTROOM_GATE_OVERHAUL_REVIEW.md`.

## §274 — 2026-06-18 — futures trade-recording integrity (dropped-short recovery + gap-tolerant fix) + ratchet restart-seed + desk-stats full-size exclusion

Operator-driven live (paper) session. Theme: **data integrity** — shorts were "disappearing" from the books, the profit-ratchet was under-protecting after restarts, and the desk-stats P&L "never looked right." Four threads, all shipped + deployed + merged + pushed to main (`b3a708e9`→`006c7ec9`, fast-forward).

- **Short-cover trade-recording gap — diagnosed, recovered, fixed at root (`0c5d49eb`).** Operator: shorts hit profit then "disappeared — nothing in trades." Forensics: every futures round-trip is an `usfut-`/`eurex-` entry order paired with a `coid_` exit; 5 SHORT covers (11:08–11:43 UTC) had **no `trades` row** and a phantom `open_entries` row keyed on the COVER coid. Root cause = the **OrderFilledV3 emission gap** (orders fill at IBKR but never transition off SUBMITTED → the `trade_tracker` never sees the close) **racing the `positionEvent(qty=0)` force_close** (`force_close_if_held` wipes the book row first). So the short's in-memory `OpenEntry` was gone by the time the cover BUY reached `on_fill`, and the FLAT+BUY path **unconditionally opened a phantom LONG** (the FLAT+SELL path already reconstructs a lost long before opening a short — the BUY path had **no symmetric reconstruct**; that asymmetry was the bug). The positionEvent-flat safety net (`force_complete_entry`) couldn't help either — it `return None` when there are no captured exit fills. **Fix:** new `trade_tracker._on_flat_buy` mirrors the SELL path — reconstruct a lost SHORT from the immutable `executions` log and CLOSE it with the cover BUY; only open a fresh LONG when there's nothing to cover. Extracted the shared close+dedup tail into `_close_open_entry_with` (longs byte-identical); `trade_tracker_reconstruct._reconstruct_ibkr_from_executions` made **direction-aware** (a `qty<0` lot rebuilds as a SHORT: entry=SELL, `is_short=True` — was long-only). Reuses the `_recon_closed_sigs` dedup so a repeat cover can't double-book (the ESTX50-9x guard). **This makes trade RECORDING tolerant of the OrderFilledV3 gap** rather than depending on that flaky event. 7 tests (`tests/test_short_cover_reconstruct.py`), zero regressions. **NOTE:** the emission gap *itself* (413+ orders stuck SUBMITTED-with-fill) is still unfixed at the order-state-machine level — deeper broker work; recording is now gap-tolerant, which is what matters for the books.

- **Recovered 14 dropped round-trips from the immutable executions log.** (a) The 5 the operator spotted — reconstructed idempotently (guarded on the cover coid) + the 3 phantom `open_entries` cleared: `scripts/sql/shorts_recovery_20260618.sql`, exit_reason `RECONSTRUCTED_SHORT_COVER`, **net +$55.25**. (b) A **systematic sweep** via `ledger_projector.project(executions)` (the authoritative fold) diffed against `trades` (robust **price + close-to-second** dedup, which correctly excluded 2 false-missing longs) found **9 MORE** dropped USD round-trips: `scripts/sql/shorts_backfill_sweep_20260618.sql`, exit_reason `RECONSTRUCTED_BACKFILL`, **net −$77**. Combined **14 rows, net −$21.75**; re-verified **0 genuine round-trips still missing**. The 3 corrupt **ESTX50** rows (qty 9/10 full-size contamination, impossible 6283→7099 prices) were DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — they belong to the separate `estx50_pnl_reconcile`, not this gap. (Recovered rows are `RECONSTRUCTED_*`, NOT `RECONCILED_*`, so they DO count in the P&L feed — correct, they're real round-trips.)

- **Ratchet restart peak-loss fix (`b3a708e9`).** Operator: positions hit profit then go negative — "why isn't it firing?" A 25-min instrumented clean-watch (`ratchet-trace` TEMP log in `futures_runner.py`, commit `f6b54087`) proved the ratchet **fires correctly when armed** (caught an M6E short arm at +$13.8 → bank on the 25% give-back). The "sometimes not" is mostly the **arm floor** (sub-$10-peak positions never arm → ride the 20-min FLAT_CLOCK), already addressed by `PROFIT_RATCHET_ACTIVATION_FLOOR_USD=10`.
