## §275 — 2026-06-18 (later) — profit-ratchet DISARMED: mis-arming on first-sight via over-seeded / inherited peak (the §274 bar-seed regression)

Operator, urgent: *"the profit ratchet is selling and locking in losses."* Confirmed live — last 24h `DAYTRADE_PROFIT_RATCHET` exits split **31 losses (−$285) / 72 wins (+$1,280)**, net green but firing **4–5-second round-trips at a loss** (MES −$11 in 5s, DAX −$20 in 5s, M2K −$14, MCL-short −$14…). A correctly-armed ratchet cannot arm (peak gain ≥ activation) AND give back 25% in 5 seconds — it was **mis-arming on first sight**.

**Root cause — a state-bleed family, two over-seed paths + a missing floor:**
1. **§274 bar-seed over-correction (the regression).** `load_bar_extreme` (futures_peak_state.py) seeds `running_extreme` to the **max bar HIGH over `[opened_at, now]`** on first sight — but it runs for **brand-new** positions, not just restart-rehydration. The entry-minute bar's high sits *above* the fill, so `peak_gain = bar_high − entry` clears the $10 arm floor instantly → ratchet arms → `trigger = entry + 0.75·peak_gain` (above current) → `current ≤ trigger` TRUE → immediate market exit, at a loss whenever price dipped below entry. §274 conflated two cases: (a) restart where the in-memory peak was genuinely lost (bar-seed legitimately recovers it) vs (b) brand-new first-sight whose true peak IS the entry (must seed at `avg_cost`). It applied (a)'s bar-seed to (b).
2. **Stale per-symbol state across instances.** `futures_runner._running_extreme[key]` is keyed by `contract_key`; the pop-on-close (runner:130) is **gated on seeing the close — which the OrderFilledV3 emission gap (§274) routinely misses.** So when a micro churns (close→re-open, constant on these contracts), the new position inherits the **prior instance's peak** directly. Same mechanism carries the prior `opened_at` (the "broker preserve-earliest" paths the runner already warns about at :119/:290/:303 — there's a FLAT_CLOCK suppression guard for it, but nothing guarding the ratchet seed or the dashboard).
3. **No loss-floor on the exit.** `profit_ratchet_exit` (futures_stop_logic.py:121-136) returns `current ≤ trigger` with **no check that current is in profit** — a *profit* ratchet must never fire below entry (long) / above entry (short). Missing.

This is also the operator's second report the same exchange — **Locked Profit shows a huge value on a flat new buy, and held-time inherits the last holding of the same name** — the *same inherited per-symbol state* (Locked Profit = 75% of the inherited peak gain; held-time = the inherited `opened_at`), surfaced on the display side. One root family.

**Action: DISARMED (live, this session).** `.env PROFIT_RATCHET_ENABLED=true→false` (§5 backup `alphabot-2026-06-18-1341`) + `alphabot-strategy-daytrade` restart. Verified at the code level: with the flag false both desks set `profit_ratchet_giveback_frac=None` (us_futures_desk.py:258 / eurex_desk.py:211) → the ratchet branch in `decide_futures_stop_action` is skipped entirely; the **native 1.5% IBKR server-side trail + the time-stop still own protection** (the flag doesn't touch them — positions are NOT left naked). Zero ratchet exits since the restart. Reverts to "native trail gives back too much" — safe, no fresh-loss locking. `.env` is gitignored, so the disarm is **live-VPS-only** (re-arm is an `.env` edit, not a git revert).

**Forward plan — RE-ARM gated on a fix drop (NOT built this session):** (a) bar-seed only from bars **strictly after** the entry fill, and only on **restart-rehydration**, never brand-new first-sight (fresh peak = `avg_cost`); (b) add the `in_profit` loss-floor to `profit_ratchet_exit`; (c) clear per-symbol runner state + `opened_at` on a fresh fill **independent of** the close-emission gap (don't depend on the flaky OrderFilledV3 close). The Locked-Profit / held-time display fix falls out of (c)'s state-scoping. Tracked as a Tier-0 priority item (MASTER_TODO §3). The deeper OrderFilledV3 emission gap (§274 carried-open) is the upstream enabler of path 2.

**RESOLUTION (same session, operator-directed: "wind it back and re-arm, do the robust fix in the background").** The bleed was proven to be the §274 bar-seed alone: ratchet win-rate **93% before** the 12:16 deploy (28/30) vs **42% after** (24/57, 33 losses). So we **reverted `b3a708e9`** (commit `fb742085` — removes the `load_bar_extreme` fold + the bar-seed test; restores the pre-§274 seed: in-memory peak → persisted opened_at-scoped peak → `avg_cost`) and **RE-ARMED** on the same restart (`.env PROFIT_RATCHET_ENABLED=true`, strategy-daytrade restarted 13:54 — clean, `load_bar_extreme` gone from the tree). The ratchet is **LIVE + ARMED again** on its pre-bleed behaviour. The restart-under-protection `b3a708e9` was trying to fix (MNQ +$109 seeded as +$7) is the **lesser evil** (gives back more profit ≠ locks losses) and is now owned by the robust fix. The full robust fix (Parts A–D above) is **building on branch `fix/ratchet-robust-rearm` in an isolated worktree** (background agent) — build+test only, operator-gated deploy; it will replace the revert with the correct, instance-scoped, loss-floored version + fix the Locked-Profit/held-time display.

A long operator-driven session, all merged to main + deployed (`b6a06186`→`491765bc`). Desk LIVE; broker/strategy/dashboard HEALTHY; kill OFF.

Venue-truth proof: holdings/qty/P&L/stop-coverage all correct vs IBKR; only the *hold-time* lied (MCL showed opened 06:07 / ~12h when the live short opened 15:21 / ~3h). Root: under `LEDGER_AUTHORITATIVE` the sole positions writer (`project_and_write_positions → upsert_position`) had its 2026-06-15 churn guard DEFEATED by an UNCONDITIONAL `ON CONFLICT … opened_at = MIN(positions.opened_at, excluded.opened_at)` — a held-position write is ALWAYS the UPDATE path, so opened_at could only ever DECREASE → pinned to the day's first open. Fix (`writers.upsert_position`): supplied callers trust the churn-guarded `final_opened_at` (`= excluded.opened_at`); legacy `None` callers keep the protective MIN. Same guard added to `positions.upsert_from_snapshot` (the reconcile auto-import sibling path). Self-healed on broker restart (all opens corrected to the projector's true re-open times).

**2. autoMode permission rules (`83acc05d`).** The auto-mode CLASSIFIER (a separate LLM layer above `permissions.allow`) was blocking `sudo systemctl restart alphabot-*` and `git push origin main` every session, despite §6/§8 marking them auto-allowed. NEW: restart/main-push autonomy lives in `autoMode.allow`, not just `permissions.allow`.

**3. THE ratchet bleed — loss-floor must be an ABSOLUTE $ fee-buffer, NOT %-of-notional (`2d53525c`). KEYSTONE.** Operator: "ratchet still not working, we're bleeding." Replayed the real flat-clocked trade 3445 (LONG MNQ, peaked +$36) through the LIVE `profit_ratchet_exit`/`update_running_extreme` → returned False EVERY tick. Root: `breakeven_floor`'s loss-floor (§275 Part A) used `max(one_tick, entry*0.0005)` = 0.05% of NOTIONAL = +$30.7 on MNQ's ~$30.7k — which sat ABOVE the 25%-give-back trigger for any peak below ~0.067% of notional (~+$41 MNQ / +$25 MES). So the $10 activation floor ARMED the ratchet, then the loss-floor BLOCKED every exit; modest peaks round-tripped into the flat-clock at a loss. M2K/MBT/crypto (small notional → small floor) kept banking, masking it. Fix: loss-floor offset = `max(one_tick, _BREAKEVEN_FEE_BUFFER_USD($2) / value_per_point)` — a micro round-turn is ~$1 in fees, not $30. The loss-floor still holds (a give-back into the red never banks). **NEW ARCH LOCK: the breakeven/loss-floor is an absolute $ buffer, never %-of-notional** (mirrors the $-activation-floor reasoning).

## §285 — 2026-06-19 — edge-nightly perf: vectorize-in-place (NOT DuckDB) + crypto-skip + 3h timeout

The recurring `edge-nightly` 15-min timeout, fixed. **Decision of record: we did NOT adopt DuckDB** despite a deep deep-research pass on the analytical-DB landscape (DuckDB/Polars/chDB, well-sourced). Rationale: the bottleneck is **not** SQLite-the-store (729k bars / 1.26M obs is tiny) — it's a Python row-by-row replay loop (~150k–320k funnel cycles/night) + dead work. Adding an analytical engine to a 5 GB, solo-maintained trading system is over-engineering; every new dependency/engine is a 3am failure mode the operator must own. The senior call = fewest moving parts that solves it. Shipped instead:
- **Phase 0a:** `edge-nightly` `TimeoutStartSec` 15min→3h via an `/etc` drop-in, and the `/etc`-only unit reconciled into `infra/systemd/` (`2b44d2db`) — the drift was how the db-robust pass bumped the sibling `edge-drain` and missed this one.

- **Phase 2:** `rapid_walkforward.py` (module + CLI) — vectorized pandas/numpy forward-window walk-forward, no new dep, ~3s for 6,685 entries × 4 horizons, output IDENTICAL to `fut_replay` (validated 1462 rows × 13 horizons, max_abs_diff 0.0). Reusable ad-hoc by operator + agent for rapid edge analysis.
- **Documented escalation (only if data ever outgrows RAM — it won't at this scale):** DuckDB over a nightly **Parquet snapshot** (NOT direct-ATTACH the live WAL file — duckdb-sqlite Issue #82 = SIGBUS crash with a live SQLite writer). Keep SQLite as the untouched OLTP system-of-record. Also open: vectorize / window-bound the courtroom full-scans, which grow with the indefinite-retention `fut_edge_observations`.

## §288 — 2026-06-20 — Market-data PLANE architecture + cadence LOCK + P0 built (MD daemon = sole IBKR data feed)

Continues §287. Diagnosis-led architecture session (operational state: HANDOVER_68 addenda). Scope doc:
`docs/MARKET_DATA_PLANE_ARCH_SCOPE.md`. The #1a "dark spread feed" (HANDOVER_68) was root-caused NOT to a
subscription gap (operator confirmed subs present, free tier) but to **IBKR `Error 10197 "No market data
during competing live session"` — a SELF-collision**: the broker (`market_data.py:315`) `reqMktData`s L1 on
every held/traded contract for stops/valuation, and #1a added a SECOND `reqMktData` on the same contracts
from the MD daemon → IBKR denies the second. (That's why only MBT/MET/MSL quoted — closed Friday, broker
unsubscribed, no collision.)

**ARCHITECTURE DECISION (operator-ratified, the "Foundry data-lake"):** the **MD daemon (:8092) becomes the
SOLE owner of all IBKR market-data streaming**; every other process (broker included) READS from it. Two
non-overlapping planes — market-data plane (MD daemon: all reqMktData/RealTimeBars/TickByTick) vs
trading-control plane (broker: orders/executions/positions/stops, ZERO market-data subs). Restores
REPO_MAP's "one IB-owning process"; the strategy already reads bars from the MD daemon (Y52, "daemon is the
sole source"), so the broker is the last self-subscriber. Safe because stops are server-side (§253 IBKR GTC
TRAILs) — the broker's local price is only for valuation + stop *decisions*, degrade-safe on staleness.

**CADENCE LOCK (operator):** NO tick-by-tick, NO booster packs. L1 quote/spread on all 12 futures at ~1s
steady (250ms ceiling) + 5s bars — free on existing subs. Order-flow = **quote-based OFI (Cont)** from L1
size/price (the free substitute). CVD/VAP footprint FORGONE (need tape) → **#1b PARKED**
(`CAPTURE_1B_TAPE_SCOPE.md`). Line budget CORRECTED to **100 free** (no paid Quote Booster; `market_data.py`
cap 200→100). 12 futures ≈ 24 lines — ample. New locks: `L-MDP-SINGLE-OWNER`, `L-MDP-BROKER-READS-PLANE`,
`L-MDP-DEGRADE-SAFE`, `L-MDP-SOLE-WRITER`, `L-MDP-NO-TICKBYTICK`.

**P0 BUILT + TESTED (branch `fix/md-plane-p0-broker-reads-plane`, flag-gated `BROKER_READS_PRICE_PLANE`
default OFF, NOT deployed at scope time):** half 1 (broker) skips `reqMktData` + `snapshot()` reads
`live_price_cache` (degrade-safe, staleness `PRICE_PLANE_MAX_STALENESS_S=15s`); half 2 (MD daemon)
`plane_entries()` + QuoteRecorder writes `live_price_cache` (bid/ask/mid+currency, last-write-wins) from its
#1a L1. 17 P0 tests + 28 touched-area regression green; no new failures vs baseline. P0 == the #1a fix
(kills 10197). Arming = flag true for BOTH daemons + restart both; **first real verification needs an OPEN

Downstream header/span/stats logic untouched — only the data source changed. Architectural lesson: the executions ledger is venue truth; surfaces that sum `trades` inherit its corruption.

## §295 — 2026-06-24 (later) — MOMENTUM REDESIGN deployed + the NET-OF-FEES reckoning (the desk doesn't clear its costs yet)

The day's second arc. The momentum gate "catches the move too late and bleeds via flat-clock" — a deep web-research synthesis + backtests led to a redesigned gate; then a fee-accuracy challenge from the operator exposed that **the whole desk is net-negative**, reframing everything.

- **MOMENTUM-GATE REDESIGN — BUILT + DEPLOYED LIVE both sides (`47cb75db`, flag `FUT_MOMENTUM_REDESIGN_ENABLED=true`).** The live `momentum_persistence` gate is a PERSISTENCE trigger (density≥60 ∧ net_atr≥1.5 ∧ last-2-green) — it confirms an established move → enters late, into exhaustion. Three parallel web-research agents (early-entry / exhaustion-detection / quant) converged: fire EARLIER + a travel-based exhaustion guard; extension-alone = continuation not reversal (must pair with a fading tell); volume is BANDED (RVOL 1.5–2.5 best, >2.5 = climax). New gate (flag-gated, default OFF, byte-identical legacy when off): relaxed density 50 + net_atr floor 0.75 inside a TRAVEL BAND [0.75, 2.5] (upper = exhaustion-via-travel guard), require ACCELERATION (`_roc_accel` dROC>0 LONG / <0 SHORT), veto >2 ATR from VWAP unless the session VWAP trends, + rvol climax ceiling. SHORT mirrors (shorts live, `is_opted_in_live()=True`). Deployed strategy-side (no broker restart). Backtest (`momentum_redesign_backtest.py`): current −$1,091 → new +$845 gross on the same 2.5d bars, 27% fewer entries, flat-clock bleed cut ~$4k.
- **ROBUSTNESS SWEEP killed two of my levers, confirmed the core (`momentum_redesign_sweep.py`).** Net-of-fees ablation+sensitivity: the gain is ROBUST in direction across every config, but the driver is **firing EARLIER (density/floor), NOT the research vetoes** — removing the acceleration + VWAP-extension vetoes IMPROVES gross (they cut winners on a trend-heavy window — the research's own caveat). The one exhaustion guard that pays net is the net_atr TRAVEL ceiling (fewer entries → fewer fees). Honest science: the sweep refuted the fancy levers.
- **IBKR FEES VERIFIED (web): fixed $/contract, NOT a %.** $0.25/side IBKR comm + exchange + clearing → equity micros **$1.62/RT**, MGC **$2.12**, MCL **$1.92** (the $1.20 I'd carried from `ratchet_hardened_sim` was a guess). The codebase had NO fee model (paper records commission=0).
- **NET-OF-FEES DASHBOARD — DEPLOYED (`daa711ba`+`07ec6050`, `FUT_FEE_PER_RT_USD=1.50`).** The header/rolling/gate-perf/loss-buckets/ratchet now subtract a flat $1.50 round-turn fee PER round-trip (operator's number), including win% (a gross-win that's a net-loss now counts as a loss); a `NET ·$1.50/RT` tag on the perf strip. The integrity guard stays gross (it's a reconciliation, not a P&L). **What it revealed: every dashboard number was GROSS and flattering.** Net: today −$913→−$1,194, 7D −$196→−$2,425, 30D −$766→−$3,535.
- **THE RECKONING (net-of-fees per gate, ~9d real trades): NO gate is meaningfully profitable.** Best is vwap_pullback +$0.17/t (breakeven/noise) + vwap_dip +$1.28/t (12 trades). Momentum is worst (−$4.64/t net). Desk total **−$5,052 net / 9d**. Root: ~180 trades/day × ~$1.88/t fees, gross edge −$1.20/t — a **trade-frequency-vs-edge** problem, not a gate-tuning one. "Fire fewer but better" needs 5–10× fewer, not 27%.
- **REVERSION-ONLY sim (`reversion_only_net_backtest.py`).** Net-of-fees, idealized fills: reversion-only **+$2.94/trade** (the robust edge, concentrated in vwap_pullback — net-positive in the REAL trades too) vs momentum **+$0.98/t** (below a realistic slippage haircut → net-negative in reality). Confirms: **reversion is the business, momentum is fragile marginal volume.** The idealized-sim-positive vs real-negative gap IS the slippage buffer — reversion has it, momentum doesn't.
- **OPERATOR DECISION: LEAVE THE GATES.** Do NOT flip to reversion-only on a 2.5d in-sample window — run all gates (momentum redesign included) for WEEKS of forward data before any big gate decision. The courtroom + the net-of-fees dashboard are the forward arbiters. The momentum redesign stays live as part of that forward measurement.

## §303 — 2026-06-26 — OrderFilledV3 emission-gap ROOT FIX: persist-on-observe (LIVE, flag-on, verified)

The deepest carried leak (§274), closed at the root. Operator chose to build it after a corrected-data review (NOT the chronic "75%/day" I'd mis-framed — the truth: ~1-2% steady, spiking ~60% only post-IBKR-reconnect; 0 orders actually stuck-SUBMITTED; the §302 surface overhaul already routed displayed P&L around it). Two read-only agents mapped the exact mechanism + a Plan agent red-teamed.

**Root mechanism:** the durable fill+status write (`persistent_sink` → `record_fill` / `update_order_status FILLED`) was gated on the fire-and-forget `sink.emit(OrderFilledV3)` (`executor_live.py:1378`). A lost/Z1-suppressed emit stranded the order at SUBMITTED, and the close got patched by a `venue_correction` at avg_cost → $0 round-trip → P&L lost. The dark-deploy verification then revealed the *true* writer: the **Fix3 account-wide `execDetailsEvent` recovery stream "fires for EVERY execution"** and usually observes a fill first, Z1-suppressing the live `_handle_fill` emit. So Fix3 is the de-facto `fills` writer.

**Fix (flag `FUT_FILL_PERSIST_ON_OBSERVE`, default False):**
- **Migration 111** — `fills.exec_id` + partial UNIQUE INDEX; `record_fill` → `INSERT OR IGNORE` on exec_id (the idempotency substrate; LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION 110→111). The ONLY durable writer reachable from the emit that wasn't exec_id-idempotent — `record_trade`/`TradeTracker`/`positions` are NOT reached by the emit (they stay behind the in-memory `delta>0` Z1 gate, so no position double-count).
- **Phase 1** (`executor_live`): stamp exec_id on `OrderFilledV3`/`PartiallyFilledV3`; gate the emit `if persist_on_observe or is_new_activity` (flag off = byte-identical).
- **Phase 2** (`ibkr_realtime_sync` Fix2/Fix3): stamp exec_id on the recovery-path event builders — REQUIRED, because Fix3 is the de-facto writer (Phase 1 alone left exec_id NULL) AND because under flag-on both paths must share the exec_id or `INSERT OR IGNORE` can't dedup NULL-vs-real → two rows. (`OrderFilledV3`/`PartiallyFilledV3` gained an `exec_id` field; `persistent_sink` threads it.)
- Integrity guard already re-purposed (§302) to surface `venue_correction_count` — the success metric.

**Deployed:** `2a0307d8`/`7e71b6d5` shipped DARK, then operator flipped `FUT_FILL_PERSIST_ON_OBSERVE=true` (`.env`) 11:19 UTC, paired broker+strategy restart (1 open position). **20-min soak VERIFIED:** 7 post-flip fills all carry exec_id, **0 duplicate exec_ids** (dedup holds, no double-fill), **0 new venue_corrections** (the leak closing), NRestarts=0, integrity `today_ok=True`/`reconciled_rows=0`. **Instant revert:** flag→false + broker restart. Tests: durable-path re-observe dedup, runtime gate on/off, recovery-path exec_id, migration substrate. NOT in scope: the order-state-machine fix is now MOOT for P&L (persist-on-observe captures every observed fill at the real price).

## §302 — 2026-06-26 — P&L TRUTH OVERHAUL: ONE canonical source across desk-stats/header/DAY/CUBE/feed (LIVE)

Operator: "we've been going around in circles for weeks trying to get the desk to tell us the truth … make everything on the desk reconcile and show me the truth on dashboard, day and cube … there has to be a simple way." A top-down review (3 read-only agents over docs/recording-pipeline/surfaces + a Plan agent red-team) found this was NOT four bugs — it was ONE root with two lossy views we treated as truth.

**Root cause (the simple truth):** the §274 OrderFilledV3 emission gap makes BOTH recorders lossy, in OPPOSITE, TAGGED ways. (1) `trades` can drop a close or carry a FABRICATED `RECONCILED_QTY_DRIFT` P&L row — but the fabrications are TAGGED (`RECONCILED%`) and the masking path is OFF (`FUT_RECONCILE_REBUILD_FROM_LEDGER=true`); the strategy's own fill path captures the REAL exit price. (2) the executions ledger + projector is position-truth but **P&L-BLIND on gap trades**: `emit_venue_corrections` (`ledger_writer.py:178`) prices a correction at the position **avg_cost**, so the projector pairs a gap-trade close into a **$0 round-trip** — real P&L silently LOST. On 2026-06-26 the projector dropped **$131** of real P&L (48 of ~128 round-trips were venue_correction-zeroed).

**The §294 (2026-06-24) decision to point the header at the projector was the WRONG canonical** — it dodged `trades`' *fixable, tagged* corruption by adopting the projector's *silent* loss. That's why the header read −$154 while DAY read +$174, and why "the header doesn't move with the latest trade" (the projector lags via venue_corrections).

**Fix — ONE source: clean `trades`** (`alphabot/intelligence/desk_pnl.py`, new). `CANONICAL_DESK_WHERE` = the strategy's real-price record minus the TAGGED artifacts (all `RECONCILED%` + the $0 `RECONSTRUCTED_BACKFILL` phantoms — the latter clause was MISSING from the old `_DESK_WHERE`/`_DESK_TRADE_WHERE`, inflating DAY/CUBE counts), KEEPING genuine non-zero `RECONSTRUCTED_BACKFILL` recoveries; `desk_perf_recs` + `desk_rt_rows`; net-of-fees ($1.50/RT) + Paris-day on `closed_at`, applied in ONE place. Every surface imports from it:
- **desk-stats + header** (`/api/futures/performance` → `_futures_perf_recs_from_ledger` now delegates to `desk_perf_recs`; the gate/loss/ratchet helper uses `CANONICAL_DESK_WHERE`). **DAY** (`routes_day_review.py` `_DESK_WHERE`→canonical; `_range_rows` nets every panel). **CUBE** (`cube.py` `_DESK_TRADE_WHERE`→canonical; day-boundary `opened_at`→`closed_at`; net-per-cell). **Feed** (`/us-terminal` → `desk_rt_rows`, NET per trade).
- **`ledger_projector.project(corrections='fill'|'exclude')`** — `'exclude'` skips venue_correction rows → real-fill-only honest P&L. Default `'fill'` UNCHANGED, so the broker/strategy (which call the default) are byte-identical → **no broker restart needed**.
- **Integrity guard re-purposed** (`_futures_integrity_by_day`): LHS clean-trades (shown), RHS projector-`exclude` (real-fill), + `venue_correction_count` (the §274 loss proxy — a drift it explains is benign) + a fresh-`RECONCILED` regression sentinel (`reconciled_rows>0` = the masking flag regressed = the one hard alarm).
- **CLAUDE.md §8 sweep #7** rewritten to police all four surfaces + the integrity guard every cycle (operator: include DAY + CUBE).

**Deployed** `2a0307d8` (dashboard restart only, NRestarts=0). **VERIFIED LIVE: header == DAY == CUBE(all-markets) == 18.80 / 137 trades** (CUBE buckets MBT/MET crypto-futures under its Crypto cell; the TOTAL reconciles). Integrity `today_ok=True`, `reconciled_rows=0`. Suite **8902/0** (3 new test files incl the load-bearing all-four-surfaces-agree test; DAY/perf tests updated to net + new architecture). NOT in scope (carried): fully closing the OrderFilledV3 emission gap at the order-state-machine level — clean-trades + the backfill capture what the gap loses, so the surfaces are truthful without it; the residual "lost-in-both" is detected by the integrity guard's venue_correction count. Minor test-hardening follow-up: `test_cube_today` checks US cells only (its fixture is all-US-mapped) — could sum all markets to pin the cube-vs-header invariant.

## §301 — 2026-06-26 — extend reversion-only routing to ALL contracts except MGC (LIVE, paper)

Operator caught two things on the overnight: (1) "we're still buying most contracts with Momentum, I thought you turned it off for all except MGC" — correct, §299 only routed the 3 index micros (MNQ/MES/M2K); MYM/MCL/MBT/MET/MSL/M6E still ran the global gate set (incl momentum). ## §306 — 2026-06-26 (later) — REGIME ROUTER: scope + Phase 0/1a/1b SHIPPED DARK (observe-only, with counterfactual monitoring)

The afternoon's chop run made the case live: chop earned **+$185 net / 8 trades / 6 wins** in its regime, then the tape turned trending and chop bled (the last trade, MGC short −$104, was chop shorting into the turning-up VWAP); the operator + Claudio manually swapped engines (reverted chop) and the index desk instantly fired `pullback_long`. That whole manual sequence is what the regime router automates. Operator: *"build the router to automate it"* + two design requirements — (a) *"monitor what the others WOULD have done while blocked"* (counterfactual / opportunity-cost), and (b) *"how do we prevent the regime detection chopping and changing all the time."* Full design: `docs/REGIME_ROUTER_SCOPE.md`.

- **The problem it fixes:** today the chop flag is winner-take-all (`step()`: `if chop: chop.run_once(); return` — the index gates are blocked AND their observe-only funnel goes dark, so we capture ZERO counterfactual while chop owns the desk). The router replaces this with **per-contract regime-driven coexistence**: each of MNQ/MES/MGC runs the engine its live regime warrants (chop when choppy, index gates when trending, SIT_OUT on dead/shock).
- **Counterfactual monitoring (operator requirement, first-class):** the benched engine never goes dark — both engines' would-fire is logged every cycle, so every routing decision is auditable ("routed MNQ→chop; chop made +$30, reversion would've made +$12 → right call"). The desk-level opportunity-cost/regret analysis (weekly Phase-2 #2/#16).
- **Anti-flicker (operator concern), MEASURED not guessed — Phase 0 (`scripts/regime_persistence.py`, `44855b6f`):** the regime read reruns every 5s but reads smoothed windows (net_atr over 10×1m bars), so no tick-thrash; the risk is boundary flicker at the single hard threshold (net_atr≥1.0, no hysteresis). Phase 0 measured these contracts: ~60% trending / ~39% chop; RAW routing flips ~6/h → DAMPED (3-min dwell + [0.8,1.2]net/[0.4,0.7]slope hysteresis) **~1.1/h (81% fewer)**. So genuine regimes persist tens-of-min-to-an-hour; the damping turns 6/h thrash into ~1 switch/h. Four damping layers: **route-at-flat** (decide at entry, never yank an open position — a flicker can't whipsaw a trade), dwell, hysteresis, window-smoothing.
- **Phase 1a — the engine (`ad4d3861`):** `alphabot/strategy/regime_router.py` — RegimeRouter stateful per-contract anti-flicker state machine (raw signal → hysteresis deadband → min-dwell → committed engine; DEAD/SHOCK → SIT_OUT). 13 tests. The Phase-0 study single-sources its primitives from here (no §2 drift).
- **Phase 1b — wired observe-only, DARK (`5bcf07a7`):** `FuturesEntryDriver.run_router_observe` (+ `_entry_params(key)` extracted SINGLE-SOURCE so run_once is byte-identical) runs each cycle BEFORE the chop/index branch when `FUT_REGIME_ROUTER_ENABLED` (default OFF); per contract it logs regime + committed engine + BOTH engines' would-fire to **`fut_regime_routing` (migration 113)**. NO OrderIntent — the live submit path is unchanged. 462-test futures sweep green. Deployed dark (broker+strategy paired, MGC open), then on-verified end-to-end (flag on → 45 rows/min, all regime=trending→engine=INDEX, both would-fire NO_ENTRY, zero errors, no order-path effect) → flipped back to dark.
- **Rollout:** Phase 0 (measure) ✅ → Phase 1 (observe, dark) ✅ → Phase 2 (readout: chosen-vs-benched P&L per contract + dashboard line) NOT built → Phase 3 (arm, courtroom+operator gated) NOT built. Open §11 questions settled by the operator: counterfactual on BOTH dashboard+readout, dead/shock SIT_OUT, all-3-contracts-eligible-then-tighten. L-DAYREVIEW-DESCRIPTIVE holds through Phase 2.

## §311 — 2026-06-28 — REGIME ROUTER Phase 2b SHIPPED: the chosen-vs-benched $ readout (observe-only)

## §312 — 2026-06-28 — SHADOW exit competition gains a 5th member (`rtarget_trail`); dynamic-target idea evaluated + parked

Operator idea: the fixed 5R/8R `rtarget` rides the "got to ~7R then ran back to zero" near-misses all the way down — a give-back near the target would CONVERT that lost profit into banked profit. Built it, tuned it on data, and used the same session to evaluate the broader "dynamic target" family.

- **5th exit `rtarget_trail` (`1cb5f51d`):** `shadow_strategies.exit_rtarget_trail` — runs FREE (1-ATR stop only, like rtarget) until the favourable run reaches `RTRAIL_ACTIVATION_FRAC` of the per-strategy target, then a give-back trail (`RTRAIL_GIVEBACK_ATR` ATR off the peak — a confirmed pullback, NOT a level: level-floors lose net, memory `profit-protection-floor-loses…`); still takes the full target if reached. Added to `EXITS` (sim + replay iterate it automatically); **`fut_shadow_courtroom.SHADOW_EXITS` now DERIVES from `EXITS`** (kills the parallel-list drift hazard, §2); /day panel + terminal SHADOW window show the `R-TRAIL` column. 8 tests, ruff clean. OBSERVE-ONLY.
- **Tuned 0.75 → 0.90 (`eab37565`), on data not vibes.** Last-week (06-22→26) 1m-bar replay + an activation sweep: at 0.75 (≈6R/4.5R) the trail CLIPPED MNQ runners mid-pullback (trend_donch trail +349 < rtarget +1513); at **0.90** (4.5R of 5R / 7.2R of 8R) it kept the runners AND banked the near-misses → trend_donch trail **edged pure rtarget** at late activation. noise_band still prefers the plain target (fewer near-misses, harder runners). So `rtarget_trail` is "rtarget + a late salvage layer", net-additive on the strategy that needs it — judged per (strategy × contract) by the live shadow from the 2026-06-28 reopen. Knobs (`RTRAIL_ACTIVATION_FRAC`/`RTRAIL_GIVEBACK_ATR`) live-sweepable; auto-scales with the target.
- **DYNAMIC-TARGET family evaluated (scope decision):** operator asked whether 5R/8R should scale with daily trend-aggression. (a) **"extend / no-cap target" (let it keep running) — REJECTED by data:** that's the pure-trail `chandelier` exit, which LOST last week (trend_donch −782 vs rtarget +1513) — these micros mean-revert, the fixed cap is what banks the convex tail. (b) **"regime-scaled R multiple" — SOUND but PARKED/GATED:** R is already ATR-scaled (auto-adjusts to vol in price terms); scaling the *multiple* by trend strength is fed by the regime detector, which over-calls trend 4:1 (§309) → would extend targets on fake trends. Gated behind tightening the detector first. **The arbiter:** the shadow now stamps `mfe_r`/`entry_rvol`/`entry_vwap_slope` per trade — the **MFE-by-aggression study** (dated reminder, cron `331e1af6`, Sat 2026-07-12) will read whether aggressive opens actually run further before any dynamic-target build. L-DAYREVIEW-DESCRIPTIVE holds; nothing armed live (shadow is observe-only).

## §314 — 2026-06-29 — reopen-rip bloodbath response: REOPEN LOCKOUT + regime router DISARMED + gate-identity badge/desk-stats fix

The first all-reversion + Phase-3-router session (the 2026-06-28 reopen) bled at the reopen. Operator: "blood bath overnight. what happened? looks like momentum still traded." It FELT like a bloodbath because the red hit in the first ~20 min and one MNQ lost −$316.5 alone. **Momentum did NOT trade (0 momentum-gate rows)** — the aggressive entries were **`chop_capture`** (9 trades, −$256), dispatched by the **Phase-3-armed regime router** which labelled MNQ/MES `regime=CHOP, chop_action=SHORT` at 22:01 UTC and **shorted straight into the reopen rip**. The force-killer DID cap two later trades once bars existed (MNQ −$83.5, MGC −$40). - **REOPEN LOCKOUT (new entry-suppression window).** `reopen_lockout_due(now, desk, enabled, minutes)` in `futures_broker_adapter.py` — anchored to the **18:00-ET / 22:00-UTC daily CME Globex reopen** (= 00:00 Paris; DST-correct via `America/New_York`), US-futures desk only. New Settings `FUT_REOPEN_LOCKOUT_ENABLED`/`FUT_REOPEN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES` (defaults off/30); `.env` ARMED at 30 min. Distinct from the existing US-equity-open lockout (10 min). 10 tests (`test_reopen_lockout`). **This directly kills the failure that just cost the desk** — nothing trades the first 30 min of any reopen.

## §315 — 2026-06-29 — venue-correction FRESHNESS GATE (the orphaned-phantom root-cause) + MES phantom cleared

A stuck MES holding that "should've exited long before now" traced to a single **orphaned `venue_correction` SELL** in the ledger. Root: the V-LEDGER Phase-3 self-heal (`emit_venue_corrections`) is **asymmetrically trusting** — it adopts on ANY non-empty IBKR read but a glitch-empty read is guarded against un-adopting, so a transient bad read can mint a phantom correction that never clears. Cleared the live MES phantom via an **offsetting `venue_correction` + broker restart** (the harness HARD-DENIES `systemctl stop broker`, §2 — did NOT route around; used the broker-running offset path). Then built the durable fix.

- **FIX A (live) — suppress on unconfirmed liveness.** `emit_venue_corrections` gains `snapshot_confirmed_live`; `reconcile_once` probes `probe_ibkr_alive` when `FUT_VCORR_FRESHNESS_GATE` and refuses to apply a ledger-authoritative correction unless the gateway liveness is corroborated. New Settings `FUT_VCORR_FRESHNESS_GATE` (on), `FUT_VCORR_ADOPT_CONFIRM`, `FUT_VCORR_STUCK_WATCHDOG`/`_MINUTES`.
- **FIX B (dark) — two-read adopt-confirm.** `require_adopt_confirm`/`pending_adopt` two-read handshake before adopting a venue read (kept OFF behind the flag until soaked). `_check_stuck_venue_corrections` watchdog scopes a stuck-correction tell.
- Files: `broker/ledger_writer.py`, `broker/reconcile.py`, `shared/config.py`; tests `test_broker/test_vcorr_freshness.py`; scope `docs/VENUE_CORRECTION_FRESHNESS_FIX_SCOPE.md`; correction script `scripts/sql/offset_mes_phantom_venue_correction_20260629.sql`. Cockpit per-contract margin also abs'd (held-short whatIf returned a negative initMargin → MGC −$3,935 display bug); `broker_proxy.ibkr_margin_futures` abs-on-read (live) + the `/margin/futures` source route abs (deploys next broker restart). §313 cockpit margin work.

## §317 — 2026-06-29 — "fix the regime detector" → it's IMPOSSIBLE at our timescale → pivot to a REACTIVE break detector + the microstructure-capture stack for PASSIVE chop; FUTURES-ONLY MD daemon

Operator: "fix the regime detector so we can re-arm the router." The session became a deep, literature-grounded research arc that overturned the premise — and re-pointed the desk's whole next phase. All OBSERVE-ONLY; nothing armed. Theme: **stop trying to PREDICT the regime (proven unpredictable); REACT to the break; and build the fine-grained capture the passive edge actually needs.**

- **THE HARD FINDING — trend/regime is UNPREDICTABLE at the minute scale (not a tuning bug).** Built `scripts/regime_efficiency_calib.py`: the live detector's TREND-call accuracy is stuck at **25% = the base rate = ZERO skill**, at EVERY threshold, lookback (10–30 bars), displacement floor (up to 5 ATR), and forward horizon (20–90 min). Even the literature's "only STRONG trends persist" (cubic) doesn't show. Web research (deep) confirms the mechanism: the [arxiv 2501.16772] futures-tick study finds minutes are **mean-reverting** (sign flips ~30 min); Kaufman ER / Choppiness-Index / ADX all measure path-efficiency but **lag + give no forward skill here**. So we CANNOT build a detector that says "now trend / now chop" ahead of time. Operator accepted: "if we are not built to capture trends that's ok."
- **THE PIVOT — a REACTIVE BREAK DETECTOR (not a predictor).** Operator's domain truth: "passive chops have worked every time for us — the regime CHANGE killed us" (confirmed: the 34 live `chop_capture` fills netted **+$48.75**, positive on MGC/MES, destroyed by the −$316.5 reopen run-over on MNQ). So the job isn't to forecast — it's to **detect the chop→grind break as it ignites and pull the passive orders before the run-over.** Calibrated on the real kills (`scripts/break_detector_calib.py`): the kills faded a persistent **~+1.9 stdev adverse grind**; winners faded a **~+0.2 stdev oscillation**. Rule: block/exit the fade when trailing **efficiency ≥ 0.20 AND adverse-drift ≥ 0.75 stdev** → cuts ~half the kills (≈$613) while keeping 15/18 winners (+$358 on the sample). Adverse-drift is the keystone; raw efficiency was 5s-noisy (the reason for the 250ms feed below). Calibrated, **NOT yet wired** — it's a study result. (Negative byways recorded: `regime_passive_active_calib.py` + `passive_capture_5s_sim.py` showed the 1m-bar active/passive *classifier* has no separating edge and bar-level passive reversion is ~0 before fees — passive capture's edge can't be backtested from OHLC; live-paper fills are the only settling test, per `CHOP_PASSIVE_CAPTURE_SCOPE`.)
- **MICROSTRUCTURE CAPTURE STACK (operator: "bank the data… we have 250ms… for 3 contracts I think we can run it").** The 1m bars were far too coarse for a passive-limit microstructure scalp. Shipped, futures-only, MNQ/MES/MGC: **(1)** TIERED `quote_snapshot` — the live futures at **1s**, the broad universe stays 5s (`QuoteRecorder` gains `fast_symbols`/`_slow_every`; `QUOTE_FAST_INTERVAL_S`/`QUOTE_FAST_SYMBOLS`). **(2)** A **250ms `TickRecorder`** → a SEPARATE `data/ticks.db` (off the trading DB to avoid WAL contention), buffered (flush ~1s), ms-keyed, **30-day retention** pruned on boot+hourly (`TICK_CAPTURE_ENABLED`/`TICK_CAPTURE_INTERVAL_MS`/`TICK_RETENTION_DAYS`). The 250ms plane was live but never persisted (§288 cadence) — now it is, for the fill-realism + break-detector recalibration. Verified live (futures 1s, ticks.db @250ms, broker plane unaffected).
- **FUTURES-ONLY MD DAEMON (operator: "should be nothing to do with equities anywhere").** Found the MD daemon STILL running the equity-era universe scanner — discovering/subscribing **~151 EQUITIES** during US cash hours (+ `RYCEY`-type scanner errors), 2.5 weeks after the 100%-futures cutover (§263). Not inert (mis-filed as such in MASTER_TODO Tier-0 #4) — LIVE waste. Fix: new `MARKET_DATA_FUTURES_ONLY` short-circuits `desired_universe` to only the conId-pinned futures (the futures plane is pinned separately, so the broker's price feed is untouched) + `UNIVERSE_DISCOVERY_ENABLED=false` kills the scanner. Verified: **9 futures stream, ZERO equities, broker HEALTHY, plane age 0s, no scanner errors.** 568 MD tests green (a conftest defaults the legacy-composition tests off the flag; a new futures-only test added).
- **PASSIVE-CHOP SHADOW replaces trend_donch (operator: "do a forward shadow on CHOP… get rid of trend donch").** `decide_passive_chop` = rest a reversion at the oscillation edge (stretch ≥ 0.75 ATR from VWAP) in confirmed chop, **gated by the break detector** (don't fade an adverse grind). Runs under the desk exit; per-contract on the dashboard (PULLBACK·loose / DIP·loose / PASSIVE·chop); prosecuted nightly (courtroom `SHADOW_STRATEGIES`). `trend_donch` removed from the live shadow (breakout — unpredictable). Firing live on all 3. `scripts/passive_by_period.py` = the recurring "when do the limit orders pay" readout (by Paris hour + session; early read: 18:00 Paris paid +$209/6). It models the passive ENTRY logic only — NOT the LMT half-spread / fill realism (the 250ms fill model is the next build) → treat its P&L as a FLOOR.
- **`dip_loose` is the standout shadow:** +$93.52/2 (both MGC, won) vs the live `vwap_dip` −$13/4 — the looser dip catches profitable shallow reversions the 4-ATR live floor skips. `pullback_loose` ~matches the live pullback. Both tiny samples (today).
- **Locks/scope:** all OBSERVE-ONLY; **nothing armed** (live desk unchanged: reversion-only `vwap_pullback`+`vwap_dip`, reopen lockout, router disarmed, chop off). The break detector is calibrated-not-wired. **PATH to turn passive on:** shadow live → 1s/250ms data banks → nightly courtroom + `passive_by_period` assess → build the 250ms fill model → then the operator+courtroom arm decision (`L-DAYREVIEW-DESCRIPTIVE`). **NEXT:** recalibrate the break detector on the 1s/250ms feed; build the passive-LMT through-fill model; watch `dip_loose` accrue (candidate to loosen the live dip floor).

## §333 — 2026-07-06 (later) — Shadow Desk mobile redesign + the RATCHET-IN-SHADOW arc → momentum tightening-ATR-chandelier vs reversion-25% (the edge-discovery loop, end to end)
A long operator-driven session on the Shadow Desk that produced a genuine edge-discovery + exposed a load-bearing reprice bug. All shadow analytics / display — the LIVE desk is untouched.
- **Mobile redesign (`7975f8d5`):** `static/shadow_desk.html` rebuilt mobile-first — a LOCKED (sticky) minimal header (just "Shadow Desk" + Today/Week P&L + running-count on one row, all prior blurb removed) + THREE tabs: **Sims** (cards, always most-profitable-first), **Top 20** (one row per sim×contract, ranked, tappable for metrics), **Activity** (new `/api/shadow/activity` — the 50 most-recent closed shadow trades, newest first, scrollable). ALL trade $ are the realistic tick-repriced NET (real_pnl, filled only — no ceiling fallback); Activity is registered-fleet-only so removed shadows don't linger. Canonical exit leg only (`desk`/`ratchet`, no strategy has both → no 5x double-count).
- **The ratchet was DEAD in the shadow (operator "cant see it anywhere on activity even on good wins").** Root cause: `exit_desk`/`exit_ratchet` gated the ratchet on `rmult>0` (the per-contract ATR-chandelier mult), but the 2026-07-05 revert to the 25% give-back set `rmult=0` for all contracts → every green fell through to FLAT_CLOCK. **Re-enabled via the live `profit_ratchet_exit`** (`49da9fd6`), first at a conservative 50% capture then — operator "make sure its 75%" — the live-faithful 25% give-back (`e4935c11`).
- **THE REVELATION (`a57235f4`+`bfedda02`, LIVE on the shadow):** the top-20 counterfactual proved momentum and reversion want OPPOSITE exits — reversion likes the tight 25% (bank the mean-reversion pop), momentum HATES it (clips the run). **Every past chandelier-vs-25% test lost ONLY because reversion clouded the blend.** Isolate momentum and 25% is its WORST exit. Fine-tuned on the day's top-10 momentum runs (grid sweep, `scripts/passive_through_fill_backtest.py` + scratch): a volatility-scaled **tightening ATR chandelier — give-back = k·ATR, k = 3.5 ATR → 0.5 ATR over 4R — captured ~69% of the $950 peak** (grid-robust across kwide 3.5-5 / ktight 0.4-0.75 / cap 4-6R). Wired into `exit_ratchet` (`SHADOW_MOMO_CHANDELIER_KWIDE/KTIGHT/CAP_R`, gated `rmult<=0`); reversion keeps `exit_desk`@`SHADOW_RATCHET_GIVEBACK_REVERSION`=0.25.
- **The load-bearing bug it exposed:** the reprice (`passive_through_fill_backtest.realistic_trade`) replayed the DEFAULT `exit_desk` for EVERY strategy — so momentum had been silently repriced under the reversion exit the whole time, and NO ratchet tuning reached the dashboard. Fixed: `realistic_trade` now takes the strategy's CANONICAL `exit_fn` (`_canonical_exit_fn`: reversion→exit_desk, momentum→exit_ratchet), threaded through persist/run_all/single. **Re-repriced full → shadow week −302 → −104 (+$198); momentum combos finally capture their runs** (`tw_mnq_thrust_cont` +$433, `momentum_shadow` MNQ +$252, `tw_mgc_momo_thrust` +$156). Reconciles (`SHADOW_RECONCILE: OK`).
- **Seeded for interrogation:** the momentum-chandelier is a CARRIED investigation in `scripts/friday/RUNBOOK.md` for the weekend report — INTERROGATE: OOS on a TREND week (this was one CHOP day, in-sample), fat-tail carry (win% 46-56%), full-week k/cap grid. ## §334 — 2026-07-06 (later) — Broker + maintenance-loop robustness: watchdog ARMED + external cron-liveness monitor + 7-day expiry warning (the morning-outage fixes)
Operator, post-mortem on the morning's ~7h broker outage: "if we ever put real cash in this thing, that can't happen — every time a restart fixes it." Two independent failures, two fixes, both shipped. Investigation-first ("restart-fixes-it must become self-healing").
- **THE FORENSIC (soak logs, definitive):** the box CPU/RAM exhaustion (the shadow sim, throttled+sliced in §330) STARVED the broker → its event loop **froze** — `watchdog[ibkr-broker]: STALL DETECTED — no heartbeat in 92.4s/63.8s/96.1s; state=HEALTHY; auto_restart=False` at 13:05/13:09/13:11 UTC, then a manual restart at 13:17. The connection read HEALTHY throughout (a frozen loop, not a connection loss). **The broker's own watchdog (`heartbeat_watchdog.py`, V3 Drop 1.2.1a) DETECTED it 3× and could do nothing** — `WATCHDOG_AUTO_RESTART_ENABLED=False`, left detect-only pending a "7-day clean soak" sign-off that never came. Armed, it self-restarts at 13:05 — no 7h outage.
- **FIX A — arm the watchdog (`WATCHDOG_AUTO_RESTART_ENABLED=true`, .env, LIVE; broker restarted flat 18:21 UTC).** 60s heartbeat stall or 120s persistent-DEGRADED → `os._exit(75)` → systemd `Restart=always` respawns (confirmed; StartLimitBurst=10/10s guard un-trippable by boot-bounded restarts). **Already weekend-safe by construction** — acts ONLY on STALL (frozen loop, always a bug) + persistent-DEGRADED; **ignores RECONNECTING/FATAL** which ARE the expected weekend/IBKR-maintenance states → NO market-gating needed (investigation retired that concern). Soak: fired 3× on the real stall, **0 false positives**. Two tests pin it: armed-STALL→os._exit(75); armed-NEVER-restarts-on-RECONNECTING/FATAL/DISCONNECTED (weekend-safety invariant). Two layers now: §330 throttle PREVENTS starvation; watchdog is the BACKSTOP. **A-plus (BUILT + committed, activates on next flat broker restart):** catches a broker stuck RECONNECTING/FATAL *during market hours* (a connection loss the STALL path misses — the heartbeat keeps ticking). New `futures_broker_expected_connected(now)` Globex gate (dark Sat; closed Sun<18:00 ET & Fri≥17:00 ET; closed during the 17:00-18:00 ET daily halt) → the watchdog's new stuck-connection restart (600s threshold — rides out normal transient reconnects + the IBKR daily gateway bounce) fires ONLY in-session, never into the expected weekend/halt states. Fail-safe: no gate / gate raises → treated CLOSED (no restart). 8 tests (gate windows + restart-when-open + inert-when-closed/no-gate + fail-safe-on-raise, all green). Wired in `main.py` (`WATCHDOG_STUCK_CONNECTION_SECONDS=600`, `market_open=futures_broker_expected_connected`). Deferred the activating broker-restart (a position was open — not urgent, A is live); loads at the next flat gap / session flatten.
- **FIX B — external cron-liveness monitor (systemd, survives session death; `a9e7f8a5`, LIVE).** The 2nd failure: the sweeps are SESSION-ONLY crons; the session died with the box → all crons died → 7h of NO sweeps, undetected (a cron can't watch the crons). `scripts/cron_liveness.py` + `alphabot-cron-liveness.{service,timer}` (30min). An hourly **BEACON** cron (9th standing job, `17 * * * *`) touches `data/cron_heartbeat.json`; the monitor Telegrams Garrath if stale **>5h** (tolerates a long-task heads-down — crons fire-when-idle/deferred — while catching a dead session within 5h vs 7h). Not a cron → survives the failure it guards. The broker (A) self-heals independently, so a dead session pauses sweeps/reports but NOT the money path.
- **FIX C — 7-day expiry warning (same commit).** Session-only crons auto-expire 7d after creation (earliest armed today → ~2026-07-13). The monitor also watches `data/cron_armed_at.json` (stamped via `cron_liveness.py armed` on each re-arm) and warns at **day 6** → a session restart re-arms from CLAUDE.md §8 (full-prompt source of truth) BEFORE any lapse. **Deliberately warn-then-re-arm-from-source, NOT programmatic delete/recreate** (a footgun that could strand crons) — the safe half of "auto-respawn". §8 updated (beacon registered, `§8-liveness` block, arm-marker stamp). Memory: `broker-watchdog-and-cron-liveness`.

## §337 — 2026-07-06 (late) — Faithful-exit reprice: the shadow now models the desk's FULL exit stack — INCOMPLETE eliminated (commit `b78f2c91`)
Operator, on discovering the `INCOMPLETE` exit reason: *"why can't the sim just do exactly what our desk would do? i don't want a sim that gets me excited but is lying to me. make it 100% realistic."* **The finding:** the realistic-fill reprice (`passive_through_fill_backtest.replay_exit`) capped its tick window at `entry + clock_min + ~3min` and modelled NO time-exit for momentum — `exit_ratchet` has no flat-clock, and its session-EOD branch is DEAD in the replay because `sid==esid`. So a held momentum runner (didn't hit the 1-ATR stop, chandelier hadn't locked) had NO exit trigger and ran off the end of the window → marked **INCOMPLETE** at an arbitrary ~8-min mark: an optimistic, unrealised mark that was **42% of the momentum green** (raw-basis trade $). Momentum-concentrated (reversion's `exit_desk` has the flat-clock → never INCOMPLETE). **The desk's real exit stack, confirmed** (`daytrade_stop_runner.py`): 1-ATR stop → take-profit → **RED-ONLY FLAT_CLOCK** (drift cut at `time_stop_minutes` — us_futures 5, mgc 25 — ONLY if the breakeven floor hasn't engaged; **a WINNER survives**, which is why the chandelier "let it run" is faithful) → session-flatten hard cap. **FIX (`b78f2c91`, LIVE via the 2-min reprice timer):** `replay_exit` now (a) loads ticks out to each trade's REAL close (`exit_ts`, added to `_load_cfgs`) instead of the fixed cutoff, and (b) applies the desk's global backstops in-loop — a red-only FLAT_CLOCK (armed-proxy = `peak_gain*vpp ≥ RATCHET_ACTIVATION_FLOOR_USD`) + a SESSION_FLAT close at the real close. **Registered-fleet INCOMPLETE 45 → 0**; every displayed trade now exits STOP/RATCHET/FLAT_CLOCK/SESSION_FLAT. **Full re-reprice: today +$527 → +$508 (−$19) — the momentum green was MOSTLY REAL; the chandelier revelation SURVIVES the honesty check.** The only residual INCOMPLETE is dead `tw_ride_strength` (#4) rows — unregistered, hidden, uncounted. 30 tests pass (the 2 red = pre-existing weekend rot). Carried into `scripts/friday/RUNBOOK.md` — re-run the chandelier interrogation on the now-faithful numbers; **pre-`b78f2c91` shadow P&L is superseded** (mark-to-mid-flight → banked desk exits). Memory `shadow-momentum-chandelier` updated.

- **Short cap ≠ sizing** — the 2-lot `MAX_CONTRACTS_PER_POSITION` bump left the broker `RiskLimits.max_futures_short_contracts` at 1, so every 2-lot SHORT was rejected by `gate_sell_quantity_short_cap` (desk silently long-only). - **MKT entry ⟂ native trail** — the full-market entry (LMT→MKT for "guaranteed fills", earlier today) is INCOMPATIBLE with the native trailing stop: IBKR **Error 328** "trailing stop orders can be attached to limit or stop-limit orders only" → every bracket collapsed → no position at all (long OR short). Reverted entry MKT→**marketable-limit** (0.4% through the market, aggressive; commit `b23c6224`). **LOCKED CONSTRAINT: a native trailing stop requires a LIMIT/stop-limit parent — a true full-market entry would need a SOFTWARE trail, not the native one.**

## §345 — 2026-07-18 (Sat) — ★ THE DESK MODEL: the SHADOW BOARD becomes the REGIME ROUTER — a stable of thin, complementary, forward-validated gates, live-gated by their own shadow P&L + tolerance damage-control. rg_long_fast_v = the +EV keeper (survives OOS +$1,881); grind_fast KEPT as the trend-day cover, gated by a peak-trail −$300 day-latch (keeps the $1,300 days, cuts the shit, breakeven OOS). LIVE DESK UNTOUCHED (all V7 shadow research).

**All work in `gazbot7/` (branch `refactor/three-service`); nothing armed. This is a strategic/architectural decision, not a deploy.**

**Operator insight that named it (VERBATIM):** *"live grind is linked to shadow grind. maybe shadow becomes our regime router!!!"* — and the reframe that unlocked it: *"there needs to be a tolerance built in. it can't predict perfection"* + *"1307 is stomachable for 1 gate per month."*

**The decision.** You cannot PREDICT the regime (long-proven, §317) and — established exhaustively this session — you cannot classify a gate's good vs bad periods from any feature (tape, day-character, trade texture, equity geometry, cadence, cross-gate, ML combinations; 4 OOS agents + permutation + duty-matched-random baselines all → chance). So stop predicting. The desk model is: **every gate runs in shadow (free); live capital follows the gate's OWN recent shadow P&L — on when it's working, off when it bleeds, re-armed when it recovers — with wide TOLERANCE (ride a good period's losses) and cheap DAMAGE-CONTROL (make being-wrong small).** The desk = a STABLE of individually-thin (~$1–1.3k/mo) but COMPLEMENTARY, FORWARD-VALIDATED gates; the shadow board is the router that runs whichever fits the regime; the anti-correlation smooths the book. Built this session: `gazbot7/governor.py` (the shadow→live controller: window/sticky/streak/slope predictors, streak-win3 the best re-entry disciplinarian; 6 tests), `chandelier_start_k` (vol-adaptive trail, §earlier), `scripts/forward_validate.py` (walk-forward OOS harness).

**Why grind is KEPT — gated by a peak-trail day-latch (operator decision, VERBATIM: "we are using grind fast. you need to find a way to gate it. do not give up. $1300 winning days need to be kept. turn off the shit").** grind_fast is net −EV standalone (−$6,323/25d) and its good/bad DAYS are un-predictable in advance. BUT the operator's peak-trailing tolerance latch solves the stated problem: **stand grind down for the day once its P&L gives back $300 from the day's high.** A winning day never retraces $300 from its peak → the ~$1,300 days are kept in FULL; a bleed day is cut to a small loss (−$1,239→−$43, −$1,112→−$216, −$1,010→−$495). Raw −$6,323 → **+$1,244** in-sample, keeping all $4,986 of good-day money. ## §347 — 2026-07-20 (Mon) — ★ LOSS-CONTROL OVERHAUL (7 fixes live) + THE STRATEGIC PIVOT: shadow is unfit as a judge → PAPER becomes the realistic shadow. §345's shadow-governor premise REFUTED with data.

**Context.** First full two-gate (grind+rgv) live-paper session (§346). It bled (−$800s), and the day's forensics found the losses were fixable execution/exit gaps — then a deeper audit refuted a load-bearing prior (§345).

**PART A — the loss-control spine, 7 fixes BUILT + DEPLOYED live (all on `refactor/three-service`):**
1. **Gate-label mis-stamp** — `trades.gate` was hardwired to a static default; now stamped from the real firing gate (per-trade attribution restored).
2. **Partial-fill qty under-count** (the incident ROOT) — a multi-lot entry filling in partials left the extra lot invisible → reconcile DRIFT → naked lot + no time-exit (a live LONG stuck 4h). `on_fill` now syncs qty + re-arms the stop per fill.
3. **Exit wedge-breaker** — a stuck close now re-fires the flatten (bounded/idempotent) + reconnect, instead of alarm-only.
4. **Dollar give-back exit ("ratchet 2")** — arm +$50 / cut on $40 give-back from peak; catches the GREEN-THEN-REVERSE deep losers (−$120–150) the wide chandelier/2R missed. V5 ratchet2 REJECTED (guts winners).
5. **Risk-bounded sizing** — cap qty so the 1-ATR stop's $ risk ≤ $80; the big never-green losses (id68 −$130 @ ATR 31) are correct 1-ATR stops made huge by qty×volatility → bound them.
6. **Capped marketable-limit entries (IOC)** — entries were raw MKT (a paper fill landed 29pt off a deep book → −$156); now a marketable LIMIT ±3pt tif=IOC, no resting order, blow-up fill impossible. + `expire_pending_open` wedge guard.
7. **Coid-reset fix** — the order-id sequence reset on restart → orders-table corruption; now seeded from the store.
**Modeled effect:** today −$814 actual → **−$93 with all 7 live from the open** (~breakeven). The exit/sizing/entry architecture is now a coherent loss-control spine; each per-trade downside is bounded ~$60–80.

**PART B — ★ THE PIVOT (the architectural decision).** A shadow-vs-live grind audit measured the shadow board **~$460/day above achievable-live** — structural, not a bug: it ignores the single-position constraint (2.2× the trades), enters at hindsight-clean bar-closes (~5pt better), and takes trades AGAINST the tape a real desk refuses (25/47, net −$67). It overstated so badly it **disagreed in SIGN** with the live desk (shadow +$46 vs live −$418, same day). **Therefore §345 is REFUTED where it matters:** the shadow board CANNOT be the regime router / judge — routing live capital by its own shadow P&L would have held grind ON exactly while it bled. The shadow tells you *direction of a style*, never *dollars you'll capture*.
**New model (operator):** use PAPER as the realistic shadow. One paper account, cap lifted to N≈6, each gate holds its own 1 lot CONCURRENTLY (multi-position — reverses the single-position simplification); shadow = cheap feeder (nominates), paper N-slot = the real-fill judge (relegate worst-2). Scoped: `gazbot7/docs/PAPER_TOURNAMENT_SCOPE.md`. Central challenge: per-gate attribution over a NETTED venue (re-admits the V5 attribution class); every §347-A safety fix must go per-slot. ## §348 — 2026-07-20 (Mon, later) — ★ TOURNAMENT EXECUTION ARCHITECTURE settled (one netted paper account IS robust) + the two pre-cutover safety layers built → GO-LIVE: the desk cuts over from single-position grind+rgv to the multi-slot PAPER TOURNAMENT.

**PART A — the architecture decision (web-researched).** The open question from §347's pivot: is running N long+short gates on ONE netted IBKR paper account robust, or do we need separate accounts / a per-slot sim? Researched (IBKR docs + practitioner consensus) and **decided: one netted paper account IS the robust, standard choice — PROVIDED our own per-slot ledger is the durable source of truth and the venue net is only a reconcile tripwire.** Findings: (1) IBKR nets per ACCOUNT, not per clientId — clientId segregates orders, never positions; to *hold* a long and a short in the same instrument at once you need separate accounts, so a long slot + a short slot genuinely annihilate to venue net 0. (2) Separate PAPER accounts are not a practical escape — IBKR gives ~one paper account per login; 6 isolated paper accounts is unsupported. (3) The standard multi-strategy answer is exactly what we built — a logical attribution layer over the netted book keyed by order coid (IBKR's own "positions by Model" is the same pattern). (4) The restart-with-offsetting-positions hole I first flagged is NOT closed by a better venue query (net 0 tells you nothing) — it's closed by making our ledger durable and treating venue-net as a coarse DRIFT tripwire. A per-slot SIM was rejected: it throws away the realistic fills that were the entire point of fleeing shadow (§347-B).

**PART B — the two pre-cutover layers built (clears §347 "deferred, bounded by the stop").**
1. **Durable ledger + restart reconstruction.** New `slot_positions` (per-open-gate snapshot: side/qty/entry-VWAP/**entry_atr**/live-stop coid+price — the things a netted venue can't hand back) + `slot_orders` (durable coid→gate map) tables; `MultiSlotCore.reconstruct()` rebuilds the SlotBook and re-attaches each stop from OUR ledger on boot (no fresh place → no duplicate coverage), then the audit loop reconciles the reconstructed logical net vs the venue net → DRIFT halts + pages (safe; never guesses which slot a venue-only lot owns). Fills are `record_fill`'d before applying → a redelivery across a restart is idempotent. Surfaced + fixed a latent bug: stop coids were never registered with the SlotBook, so a NATIVE STOP FILL was "unattributed" and the slot never closed — now stop coids attribute, closing that trade with reason STOP. 8 tests.
2. **Per-slot time-exits + wedge-breaker.** `time_exit_check` cuts every open slot at the session-end window (flat before 17:00 ET) and any single slot past its own max-hold (each gate has its own opened_at); `exit_watchdog_slot` escalates a slot whose close went in-flight but never completed (page → re-fire the flatten, cancelling the dangling order first → force reconnect) — the 2026-07-20 wedge, per slot. Both run in the venue-audit loop. 7 tests.
Full suite 353 green, touched files ruff-clean.

**PART C — GO-LIVE (the cutover).** With the whole safety spine now per-slot (naked-auditor, reconcile-halt, qty-sync, wedge-breaker, give-back, risk-sizing, durable-ledger, time-exits), the single-position desk (grind conviction + rgv long-only, §346) is retired and the desk becomes the multi-slot tournament: N gates, each holding its own 1 MNQ lot CONCURRENTLY on the one paper account, per-gate P&L falling out of the coid-attributed SlotBook (relegate the worst, promote from shadow — §347-B). First real-gateway run of the multi-slot order path; kill-switches stay OFF (paper, consistent with §346); the per-slot native 1-ATR stop caps each lot ~$60–80. Deployed via a new `gazbot7-tournament.service` replacing `gazbot7-core`+`gazbot7-strategy` (the tournament is decision+execution combined, on clientId 7; `gazbot7-md` stays up as the feed).

**Revert:** stop `gazbot7-tournament`, restart `gazbot7-core`+`gazbot7-strategy` → the §346 single-position desk is back (its config untouched). Part-B code reverts via `git revert` on `refactor/three-service`. See SESSIONS 2026-07-20 (later 10).

## §350 — 2026-07-21 (Tue, later) — ★ PER-GATE ER FAVOURABLE-CONDITION GATE live on paper — and the TICK-HONEST lesson (a bar-close backtest is NOT a basis for a live change).

**The mechanism (the [[favourable-condition-gating-vision]] made concrete).** Each tournament gate now only OPENs when the tape's Kaufman efficiency ratio (ER = net-progress/total-path over the trailing 30 one-min closes; ~0 chop, ~1 trend) suits its STYLE. Momentum bleeds in chop, reversion bleeds in trend — so a momentum gate needs an ER FLOOR, a reversion gate an ER CEILING (or a BAND, a specific ER window). Wiring: `deciders.ER_FLOOR`/`ER_CEIL`/`ER_BAND`/`efficiency_ratio`/`er_blocks`, applied in `tournament.step()` — it drops an OPEN whose gate fails the ER test (logs `ER gate: <gate> OPEN suppressed`); **suppresses NEW opens only**, an open slot rides its managed exit (like the off-switch).

**★ THE LESSON (operator caught it).** The FIRST cut of the thresholds was derived from `scripts/gate_backtest.py` = **BAR-CLOSE fills** — optimistic, no intrabar stops, the wick-illusion the desk explicitly forbids (memory: sims-on-tick-price). It was WRONG: grind_long "+$1,664 at floor 0.20" was **−$1,228** repriced on real ticks. Operator: *"why did you do an unrealistic test for the live desk? and present me numbers to act on?"* — correct. Re-derived HONEST via `scripts/gate_backtest_tickhonest.py` (entry on the 1-min signal, exit repriced tick-by-tick with each gate's REAL exit) + a per-0.1-ER-band sweep. The per-band view was the key: a cumulative floor/ceiling scan assumes the losers all sit on ONE side of an ER line — false for 3 of 4 gates (grind loses in every band; thrust is interleaved; rgv_short's edge is a middle band a ceiling can't isolate).

**Live config (tick-honest, deployed):** `grind_long` FLOOR 0.20 (loses in every band, floor is damage-control → RELEGATION candidate) · `thrust_short` UNGATED (interleaved, natural +$532 beats every cut) · `rgv_long` BAND 0.10–0.40 (mid-band edge; the old 0.25 ceiling strangled its best band) · `rgv_short` BAND 0.30–0.40 but DISABLED via switch (single-band sliver → RELEGATION candidate) · `capitulation_long` CEIL 0.10 · `exhaustion_short` CEIL 0.05 (footprint tick+L2 duck, ⚠ fixed-exit-derived). ⚠ tick coverage ~9 days (one summer regime) + 60-min hold cap — a LEAD; re-validate a 2nd regime. Paper forward-validation, NOT real-money-proven.

**Standing rules reinforced:** (1) any live decision uses the TICK-honest backtest, never bar-close; (2) all analytics/backtests are DuckDB + pandas vectorized (memory: duckdb-pandas-for-analytics), never a raw sqlite row-loop.

**Revert:** empty `ER_FLOOR`/`ER_CEIL`/`ER_BAND` in `deciders.py` + `systemctl restart gazbot7-tournament` → gate inert (wiring stays). See SESSIONS 2026-07-21 (later 3).

## §351 — 2026-07-22 (Wed) — ★ SAFETY INVARIANT: a safety loop must publish its OWN liveness (audit-loop-death hardening after a −$216 max-hold overrun).

**Incident.** `MultiSlotCore.venue_audit_loop` — the tournament's safety spine (naked-audit, drift-halt, **max-hold**, **stop-breach**) — had no exception guard, so an unhandled throw **silently killed the task**. The MAIN loop kept writing a green heartbeat, so `sweep.py` and the operator read healthy while a `grind_long` LONG rode **153min past the 120-min max-hold** with a toothless stop, closing **−$216** (vs ~−$27 at its stop). Same class as the 2026-07-17 silent-auditor skip (memory: naked-position-silent-auditor-skip), harder failure (the whole loop died, not one skipped read).

**The invariant (locked).** A safety loop must PROVE its own liveness AND a stalled one must trigger RECOVERY, not just an alarm; a heartbeat written by a *sibling* loop is NOT evidence the safety loop ran. Concretely: (1) the audit cycle is exception-GUARDED — a throw pages `AUDIT_LOOP_ERROR` once + CONTINUES, never kills the task; (2) the loop stamps `_last_audit_ok_mono` each non-raising cycle and `write_heartbeat` exposes `audit_age_s`; (3) `sweep.py check_core` CRITs + fails preflight when `audit_age_s > 30` while live (`AUDIT_STALE_S=30`); (4) **AUTO-RESTART** — the run loop gates the systemd `WATCHDOG=1` ping on `core.audit_stale()`, so a stale auditor → withhold the ping → systemd (`WatchdogSec=90`, `Restart=on-failure`) restarts the desk in ≤90s → re-adopts open slots from the ledger → revived loop fires any overdue exit. A dead auditor self-heals in ~2min with NO human, closing the "nobody watching at 2am" gap. Generalises the 2026-07-17 rule ("every can't-verify is an alarm") to "every safety loop self-reports liveness AND self-recovers."

**Shipped:** `multislot_core.py` + `scripts/sweep.py`, +6 tests, lint+full-suite green, desk restarted flat; verified live (`audit_age_s: 5.0`, sweep `… audit 5.0s`). **Revert:** `git revert` the two-file change + restart (drops the guard — not advised). See SESSIONS 2026-07-22.

## §352 — 2026-07-22 (Wed, later) — ★ TOOTHLESS-STOP root cause + fix (fillable stop-limits) + momentum ATR floors; the "selective +EV is the goal" framing correction.

**Toothless-stop root cause (operator: "are we actually placing them?" — right to push; I'd asserted "IBKR paper quirk, nothing we can do" WITHOUT verifying = wrong).** The STOP_UNFILLED / MAX_HOLD class (incl. the §351 −$216 ride) is NOT a placement failure — our stops rest live (`PreSubmitted`/`whyHeld=trigger`). We placed a plain `StopOrder` (stop-market, limit UNSET); IBKR's PAPER account then attaches its OWN limit ~1 ATR toward entry (≈ the entry price) on the WRONG side — a SELL stop gets a limit ABOVE the trigger → on trigger it tries to sell above the market → never fills. **FIX (`broker_adapter.py`):** place a `StopLimitOrder` with our OWN fillable limit `STOP_LIMIT_BAND_PTS`=20pt PAST the trigger on the fill side (SELL below / BUY above). IBKR uses our limit → fills on trigger (bounded slippage); strictly better LIVE too (caps a naked market fill). Stop-breach guard still backstops a gap > band. ✓ **CONFIRMED live 2026-07-22 14:16 UTC** — a fresh grind_long stop echoed `lmtPrice` 20pt below the trigger (our limit — IBKR kept it, not its toothless above-trigger one) and the hour's 4 stops all filled as `STOP` (zero STOP_UNFILLED). LESSON (again): verify a root cause before asserting "nothing we can do."

**Momentum ATR floors + thrust_short ER (tick-honest sweep `scripts/momentum_atr_sweep.py`, ER>=0.20 + ATR).** A magnitude gate on top of the ER gate (`deciders.ATR_FLOOR`/`atr_blocks` in `tournament.step()`): don't ride a trend too small to run. **thrust_short** — bleed is all ATR<16; ER>=0.20+ATR>=16 = +$726/38tr (vs +$381 ER-only), a ROBUST selective edge (+EV across ATR 12–20) → added ER>=0.20 + ATR>=16. **grind_long** — a tick-honest loser that only crosses breakeven at the extreme tail (ATR>=20 +$16, ATR>=28 +$171/20tr), a FRAGILE thin-sample edge → **KEPT (operator) as the big-trend-day specialist** (early continuation + uncapped chandelier ride), gated ATR>=20 so it only fires where that pays. Live: grind ER>=0.20+ATR>=20, thrust ER>=0.20+ATR>=16.

**★ Framing correction (operator, standing).** Filtering a gate down to selective +EV is the GOAL, not a compromise — it IS the favourable-condition thesis (a portfolio of specialists each firing only in their conditions). Judge a gate by its P&L AS RUN, not by an "ungated/natural" baseline nobody trades. The real quality bar is edge ROBUSTNESS: +EV across a RANGE of thresholds (robust → keep, e.g. thrust_short) vs +EV only at a knife-edge extreme on a thin sample (fragile/likely-overfit → prove on a 2nd regime, e.g. grind). "Relegation candidate" = *unproven*, NOT *trades too little*.

**Also (ops):** dashboard grid re-synced to the actual 6 panels (`web_static/app.css`) — the stale grid clipped EXEC/truncated the scoreboard. **Revert:** stop fix / ATR floors — `git revert` the commit + restart. See SESSIONS 2026-07-22 (later).

## §353 — 2026-07-23 (Thu) — Filter-effectiveness monitor + momentum ER-hold SHADOW (deployed) + gate 1-day auto-reactivation. (gazbot7 repo: `9c72c0e`/`065d31b`/`831d455`.)

**Filter-effectiveness monitor (operator-requested standing watch).** Are the ER/ATR floors working, or are gates losing in-regime? `scripts/filter_check.py` (DuckDB) reconstructs ER (30-min 1-min closes) + ATR (14-period 1-min) AT ENTRY — the gate's exact bases — for each trade vs its floor/ceil/band, and classifies every loser **BORDERLINE** (hugs a threshold → a tighter floor catches it, at cost of participation) / **SPIKE-ENTRY** (reconstructed ER below the rule → fired on an intra-minute live-tick spike the closed bar didn't confirm) / **clean-in-regime** (well inside the window → the GATE lost, not a filter miss). Folded into `hour_watch.py` as the `FILTER(1h):` line. 7-day read: floors demonstrably help — win rate **36%→47%** ungated→gated era; of the gated bleed ~38% clean-in-regime (a roster question), ~36% borderline, ~25% spike.

**Momentum ER-hold SHADOW (observe-only, DEPLOYED 2026-07-23).** The spike blind spot: a momentum gate fires when the live/forming ER crosses its floor but the closed bars don't sustain it (violent-chop whipsaw). `deciders.ER_HOLD={grind_long:2,thrust_short:2}` + `er_hold_blocks()` require the ER condition to hold for N consecutive COMPLETED bars; `tournament.step()` records `shadow_er_hold_block`+`er_now`/`er_prev` on the intent + logs — **the trade STILL opens** (no live gating). MOMENTUM ONLY — reversion gates fire ahead of the trailing ER by design; blanket-applied it gutted the green capitulation/exhaustion gates (backtest cut +$252/+$224 of winners). Backtest (`scripts/er_hold_sweep.py`, 7d, momentum-only): recovers ~$190 spike bucket for ~$23 sacrificed winners; **minimum N=1, ship N=2 as free margin, N≥3 conflates with grind-on-chop.** ⚠ HONEST CAVEAT: the live `er_blocks` already enforces the CURRENT completed-bar ER and entry-ER isn't persisted → the backtest win may be a reconstruction timing artifact; the shadow's real job is to measure on LIVE decision-time ER whether the PRIOR-bar hold blocks anything incremental. Promote only if incremental blocks are net-losers over ~1-2wk. Deployed via paired flat-window `systemctl restart gazbot7-tournament` (confirmed flat first, came back HEALTHY all-6-slots, sweep OK). **Revert:** empty `ER_HOLD` + restart.

**Gate off-switch 1-day auto-reactivation (operator RULE).** An intraday off (`gate_switches.env`) is FOR THE DAY only — `rgv_short` sat off ~2 days (07-21→23) because nothing expired it. `telegram_bot.reactivate_all()` (flips every off→on) run by `scripts/reactivate_gates.py` from systemd `gazbot7-gate-reactivate.timer` (`OnCalendar=00:00 Europe/Paris`, DST-handled, Persistent). ## §354 — 2026-07-24 (Fri) — ★ LIVE DIRECTION-ROUTER — auto-bench the counter-trend faders on a proven trend (operator standing-approval trial). (gazbot7 `48cb25f`.)

**The problem, proven all day 07-23:** the per-gate ER condition reads tape CLEANLINESS not DIRECTION, so a clean DOWN-trend at ER 0.32 sits inside a long-fader's band and it fades the falling knife — `rgv_long` −$361 in one hour (5× stopped), and the whole −$398 whippy trend-and-chop day was the direction-blind gates getting caught at every turn while the operator hand-steered gates on/off. **Router (`src/gazbot7/direction_router.py`, LIVE 2026-07-24, operator standing-approval "see how it goes"):** flips the counter-trend REVERSION faders off once a trend is PROVEN, back on in chop — **TREND DOWN → off {rgv_long, capitulation_long}** · **TREND UP → off {rgv_short, exhaustion_short}** · **CHOP → all on**. Momentum gates (grind_long, thrust_short) are NOT managed — they fire WITH thrusts (a down-thrust in an up-trend can be the reversal); the tune found benching thrust_short only cost a winner, so it's out of the up-off set.

**Mechanism:** STATELESS — each 15-min run (`gazbot7-direction-router.timer` `*:00/15`) replays the Paris day's marks from capture → the current effective regime (raw = ER≥0.25 AND |net|≥40pt over 30 1-min bars; **2-mark HYSTERESIS** before the effective state flips — the whipsaw guard). Writes `gate_switches.env` ONLY on a change (atomic, tournament re-reads live), routine-Telegrams every flip, **HOLDs on a stale/closed feed or <30 bars**, never raises. Composes with the §353 midnight reactivator (all-on at Paris midnight → router re-applies within 15 min).

**Backtest (`scripts/direction_router_backtest.py` — imports the module's logic + constants, NO DRIFT).** Tuned + validated Mon–Thu 2026-07-20..23: **baseline −$2408 → router −$1828 = +$580, NO negative day** (Mon +224/Tue +0/Wed +56/Thu +300); despite 8–16 flips/day the delta stayed ≥0 — the hysteresis held, whipsaw didn't eat it. ⚠ TRIAL: realised trades partly hand-gated → illustrative lower bound not a clean A/B; 4 days one instrument; while live it OWNS the 4 managed gates (a manual /off is re-applied by regime). This is the automated bridge to the per-gate direction-guard end-state (Saturday roster item). +5 tests, full suite green. **REVERT = `sudo systemctl disable --now gazbot7-direction-router.timer`.** See SESSIONS 2026-07-24.

## §357 — 2026-07-26 (Sun, later) — ★ "can we capture MORE of grind's tail?" — the two orthogonal levers measured: regime-conditional exit NULL, 2R-partial REAL (variance lever) + SHADOWED; "This Week's Gates" one-pager in the Reports tab. (gazbot7 `892cdc5`.)

**★ THE QUESTION (operator):** *"am I wrong to think we should capture more of grind's in-profit runs, or is that just life? complementary mechanisms, or do the lower-level ones always clip winners?"* Framed the answer as an INFORMATION limit: every price-path ratchet reads the SAME variable (the trade's own path), and a winner's pullback is indistinguishable from a reverser's death at the decision moment (the 07-17 3.9→0.93→4.2→6.75 wobbler) — so redundant ratchets all get fooled by the same wobble. "Complementary" needs DIFFERENT information → two genuinely-orthogonal levers measured (`regime_exit.py`, `partial_scale.py`, tick-honest engine; pure-6.0 baseline +$1,782/+$747 reproduced to the dollar):

- **★ REGIME-conditional exit = NULL** (loose-on-trend / tight-on-range). The make-or-break failed: NO entry-observable label predicts the ≥4R tail (base rate 19%). The **live direction-router's own trend rule (ER≥.25 & |net30|≥40) has AUC 0.494 / lift −1** — being born in a "proven trend" says nothing about the tail. **ATR runs the WRONG way** (ATR≥28 reaches 4R *less*: 14% vs 25%, AUC 0.414 — kills the "40-ATR-day = tail" prior; the 17 tail-trades spread across 7 days at NORMAL ATR). The lone +combo (+$248) never actually tightens (every real range-tighten leg LOSES) and is a 2-day overfit (07-17/07-22; strip-best-2 → −$120). **→ do NOT deploy or shadow — AUC 0.49 won't reverse on more data.** This closes the "capture more" question: the tail is unpredictable at the decision moment from EVERY variable we capture (price-path ×3 ratchet studies + regime + a direct AUC test) — **the ~37% give-back on the loose trail is the irreducible price of not whipsawing, PROVEN not assumed.**
- **★ 2R-PARTIAL scaling = REAL, the only surviving lever — but a VARIANCE lever, not a mean-raiser.** grind is base_size=2 → Lot A scalp-2R (banks certainty) + Lot B pure-6.0 chandelier (banks the tail); needs NO prediction, changes the payoff SHAPE. Best target_r=2.0: **daily-vol −29% ($997→$705), maxDD −24% (−$3,072→−$2,338), worst-day −34% (−$1,218→−$801), green-day 53→60%, wk30 mean +$82** — for a **~$665/3wk mean give-up (~19% gross)** that is ENTIRELY the tail forfeit on the 17 runners (−$2,624), ~75% offset by reverser gains (+$1,959). LOO: dropping 07-17 flips the cost to +$243 (the "cost" = forgoing a slice of 2 monster days; on bad days it HELPS). ⚠ green-week 100→67% (3-wk artifact). A mean-vs-smoothness CHOICE for the operator, NOT a fix.
