## §358 — 2026-07-27 (Mon) — ★ STOP-fill fix (ContFuture→concrete Future, VERIFIED) + REGIME-3-EXIT SELECTOR (exits chosen by regime) + ROUTER momentum-chop VETO. (gazbot7 `4351279`, `da98af0`, `ae55ab6`, `56ef119`; router loosen `1ffb086`.)

A live-desk day — three architectural changes, each validated in production (paper) through a violent 4-regime-flip session.

**★ STOP-FILL — rest protective stops on the concrete front-month Future, not the continuous ContFuture.** Root-caused the recurring `STOP_UNFILLED` class (~18% of stop-exits; 4/4 overnight ≈ −$200): IBKR intermittently never fires a resting stop's TRIGGER on a **continuous** contract — the order sits `PreSubmitted/whyHeld='trigger'` with price 10s+ past the level, so the breach-guard market-flattens (bounded ≈1 ATR). The §352 fillable-limit was intact; the trigger *upstream* of it never fired. NOT gate-specific, NOT the money leak (the guard bounded every loss). Fix = qualify the concrete Future off the ContFuture's conId and rest stops on it (same conId → positions/naked-audit reconcile; entries/exits stay ContFuture). **VERIFIED live** — a native stop triggered + Filled at its trigger; 11 clean `STOP` / 0 new `STOP_UNFILLED` since deploy. The ContFuture-trigger bug is CLOSED. `IBBrokerAdapter.stop_contract`.

**★ REGIME-3-EXIT SELECTOR — a new exit-selection architecture.** Instead of one fixed exit per gate, every gate now picks its exit WIDTH by the router regime AT ENTRY (frozen for the trade's life): aligned-trend → **WIDE** lock-chandelier (ride), chop → **TIGHT** k1.5 (bank before give-back), counter → **k2.0**. Native 1-ATR STP still owns the loss; the give-back overlay is OFF under it (the chandelier is the sole managed profit exit). Chosen over per-gate exits because the tick-honest width sweep (`scripts/exit_selector_sweep.py`, 260 realised entries) found the REGIME map unambiguous (aligned→lock +$2382, chop→k1.5, counter→k2.0) and the **regime-only** selector beats the best single fixed exit **+$756 OOS / 6-of-7 leave-one-day-out days**, while per-gate×regime OVERFITS (−$512 OOS). `SlotSpec.adaptive_exit`, `_regime_mode()` mirrors the router thresholds (no drift). ⚠ the aligned-WIDE magnitude leans on the one trend day (07-27) — forward-validate. Confirmed live: green `CHANDELIER` exits printed (both the counter-mode bank and the aligned ride).

**★ ROUTER MOMENTUM-CHOP VETO — the symmetric completion of the direction-router.** The router already reads CHOP live; now it benches the MOMENTUM gates (`grind_long`, `abs_veto_long`, `abs_veto_short`) in CHOP, mirroring faders-off-in-trends. Momentum gates fire on short bursts that revert in choppy tape: realised 07-20..27 the momentum book is **−$757 in CHOP-regime@entry vs +$18 in TREND** (robust — chop bled them 5 of 7 days; grind_long alone −$598 chop vs −$16 trend). Directly closes the −$195 grind/abs_veto chop bleed today (analysis: all 8 of their losers fired in CHOP, 0 in a benchable trend — a chop problem, not directional). `CHOP_OFF` in `direction_router.py`. (Router trigger also loosened 0.25/40 → 0.20/30 via `router_study.py`, `1ffb086`.)

⚠ All validated on ~1 week / a single violent whipsaw day (4 regime flips) — the day's P&L was ugly (≈−$155) but every mechanism behaved as designed and was verified live. ## §359 — DUAL-SLOT SCALE-OUT: the unified profit exit (2026-07-29, LIVE)

**Decision:** replace every gate's profit exit with a **dual-slot scale-out** — each gate splits into two independent 1-lot sub-slots that both fire on ONE signal: **Lot A** a fixed-R scalp (guaranteed floor, bank early) + **Lot B** a chandelier (ride the fat tail). Native 1-ATR stop owns the loss; Lot B → breakeven after A banks. BIG-RUN gates (grind_long, abs_veto_short, abs_veto_long, exhaustion_short) → A@2.5R + B wide lock-chandelier (3.5/6/0.5). FADERS (rgv_short, capitulation_long) → A@1.5R + B tight k1.5. `slot_strategy.scaleout_slots()` builds 12 sub-slots via `replace()` off `tournament_slots()` (one source of truth); `tournament._base()` strips `_A/_B` so base-name benching / the 55s abs-veto / the exhaustion 5s-confirm apply to both lots. Env-switchable slate `scaleout`. gazbot7 `5b0913b` (+7 tests) + scoreboard fix `d65596d`.

**Why (the research):** the give-back on the wide lock-chandelier felt catastrophic (a +$292 exhaustion monster gave back to +$22) because lock_r=6 was unreachable — MFE is FAT-TAILED (median winner ~6R, tail to 60R). Sweeps proved **tightening the single trail LOSES money** (the tail dominates every config) — the web-consensus + data answer is scale-out (bank a partial, ride the rest), which our base_size=2 was built for. Chose dual-slot (two full slots) over a partial-exit mechanism to avoid surgery on the safety spine (per-lot stop re-arm / naked-audit / ledger) — it reuses the proven whole-slot path and shows Lot A/B as separate dashboard cards.

**★ Load-bearing lesson: BACKTEST EXITS ARE UNRELIABLE ON THIS DESK.** Three faithful-looking tick-reprice backtests all failed validation (5–10× off actual realized, both directions) — the live desk exits worse (cadence/fills/other paths). We deployed on the operator's call (it's paper) and measured LIVE: **first win abs_veto_short A+B = +$768 (A +232 floor / B +536 tail) — the mechanism proven on real fills.** Rule going forward: validate exit changes LIVE or via the honest shadow repricer, NEVER a fresh backtest.

**Status:** proven-live but small-N (this +$768 + a −$166 whipsaw debut). Revert = slate `tournament`. Forward-validate over more days. See SESSIONS 2026-07-29, memory `dual-slot-scaleout-live`. (Also this session: the orphan-stop → phantom-long → drift-halt incident exposed a real gap — **no orphan-order cleanup on boot** — build it; memory `orphan-stop-phantom-incident`.)

## §364 — 2026-09-03 (Thu) — ★★★ THE TUNNEL ARC: the structure is real on BOTH contracts, the break is worth nothing on EITHER, and the live alert's founding number was withdrawn.

**The operator's read, in his words:** *"it will run and then hover around vwap for a while. then run again"* (09-02), then after a night on the gold chart, *"mgc shows a nice grind up since open … tunnel. run. tunnel. run. i think we are on to something. we will trade between the tunnels. just a few runs per day."* This entry covers the whole arc, including the part that went wrong, because the wrong part is the load-bearing lesson.

**THE STRUCTURE IS REAL, HELD OUT, AND GOLD MATCHES THE INDEX.** A 2-state Gaussian HMM on log true range, fitted on the first two thirds of each symbol's sessions and measured on the last third: MGC spends **63.1%** of minutes inside a compression against MNQ's **66.0%**, leaves one **5.9** times a session against **5.6**, median tunnel **57m / 12.6pt ($126)** against **63m / 76.5pt ($153)**. ★ On the raw fit the two contracts are the **same instrument in dollars** — a quiet minute is **$10.34** of range on gold and **$10.28** on the index, an active one **$30.15** and **$29.24**, with both persistence probabilities agreeing to 0.001. Fitted independently; nobody aimed at that.

**DECISION — GOLD GETS ITS OWN FIT AND ITS OWN FEATURE. Two traps, either of which ships a plausible wrong answer.**
- **2.5% of MGC minutes have a true range of EXACTLY ZERO** (MNQ: 0.20%) — no print, or one print at the previous close. On a log scale zero is minus infinity: floored, that spike takes a whole state and the fit returns *quiet = 0.03pt covering 2.5% of minutes*, which is **a dead-tape detector wearing the shape of a compression detector**, and it would have run green and silent forever. Those minutes are now MISSING observations — the state propagates through them by transition alone, which is what "no information" means.
- **Gold's absolute range drifts with its own vol regime.** Quiet measures 0.64 → 1.72 → 1.30pt across three independent thirds while gold went 3350 → 5000 → 4400. A fixed-threshold model therefore **ROTS** — 2025 thresholds would call an ordinary 2026 minute active. Scoring each minute against a **causal trailing median** of its own tape returns quiet 0.73/0.77/0.75 and active 1.57/1.62/1.54 on the same three thirds: the same model three times. *A parameter that has to be re-fitted to stay true is a parameter that will one day not be re-fitted.*

**DECISION — NO MGC ALERT IS ARMED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** Matched-hour control, racing from the END of the break bar (racing from its own timestamp replays the decision minute), one break per tunnel (counting every minute outside multiplies one event by its duration): the 60-minute excursion after a break is **1.04×** control on MGC and **1.02×** on MNQ. Direction by first passage at ±1/±1.5/±2 ATR: MGC **0.498 / 0.535 / 0.523** against a control of ~0.498 — a coin flip; MNQ **0.444 / 0.489 / 0.475** — mildly adverse. Gold is the *less bad* of the two in all three measurements, which is not an edge. An alarm firing six times a session with nothing behind it spends the one channel that also carries naked-position alarms.

**DECISION — THE `1.75×` CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN FROM A LIVE SERVICE.** `tunnel_watch` was armed 09-02 19:45Z printing, in every message, *"MEASURED: expect ~1.75x normal 60m excursion — SIZE only."* That was the entire justification for the alert existing. Re-derived with the service's **OWN** parameters and its own break definition over the same 240 sessions: **1.02× in ATR, 1.08× in points** (n=752). Six control definitions across MNQ and MGC — any minute / quiet-only / active-only, in ATR and in points — span **0.82–1.32×**, and the most flattering mixed-yardstick variant (break scaled by a PRE-break ATR, control by its own) reaches only 1.13×. Nothing reaches 1.75×. The **direction** half replicated (0.459/0.513/0.499 vs 0.494/0.498/0.497) and was kept.
- **Fixed first, written up second.** Message rewritten to *"⚠ NO EDGE MEASURED — a STATE CHANGE, not a forecast"*, `build_message()` extracted so a test can EXECUTE the text, three tests added that forbid the number returning, service restarted **05:27Z**.
- **The service stays running** because the operator asked to see the transition, not because an edge exists. Whether it stays at all is his call and is recorded as open, not settled.
- ★ **The lesson is not "a number was wrong". It is that the FOUNDING number of a live instrument went nine hours without anyone re-deriving it, and it only fell because a second contract forced the same pipeline to be written twice.** An instrument's founding number is the one least likely to be re-checked, because checking it threatens the instrument. Banked as [[a-live-instruments-founding-number-must-be-re-derived]].

**ALSO TESTED — the operator's OTHER reading.** "Between the tunnels" can mean fading the box rather than trading the break. Scored causally (the tunnel is only ever what has happened SO FAR — using the finished box reads the answer off the back of the page, since its edges are by definition where price turned): MGC **gross +$0.21/trade**, i.e. exactly zero, **net −$4.29** after the $4.50 round trip, −$11,781 across 2,749 held-out trades. MNQ loses before costs.

**WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the only thing:** the tunnel as a **FILTER ON WHEN TO LOOK**, with direction supplied by something else — his own eye (65% over 20 positions against the tape's 50%), the session block, the VWAP stretch. Every cell above is a coin flip because the break carries no direction *by itself*; nothing here says a compression is a bad place to be watching for one. Not done, and not small.

**Delivered:** `scripts/tunnel_fit_mgc.py` (11 executing tests), harnesses and fitted parameters in `reports/tunnel_mgc/`, report at `/v7/static/tunnel_2026-09-03.html` (Reports index now matches `tunnel_<date>`), MGC on the dashboard chart tab with the same window toggles and every MNQ-desk overlay suppressed on gold, STATE §1c. 1036 tests green. `3c18327`, `6af09e0`.

## §363 — 2026-08-19 (Wed) — ★★ THE OPERATOR'S HANDS ARE THE EXIT. Build presence, not a replacement: 1 Hz peak watch + a 0.02s claim path.

**The day:** +$726 in 23 minutes, and **all three exits were `MANUAL_CLAIM`** — rider +$544, abs_veto_short_B +$94, abs_veto_short_A +$88. This is not an anecdote, it is now the pattern: roughly half the rider's live trades are manual claims and they are the largest winners, while eleven months of testing say every FIXED automated exit loses. On 08-18 three independent studies tried to reproduce the claims with a level — $100 to $600, ATR-scaled, two-lot — and every one of them loses money.

**The decision: stop trying to replace the judgement, and start supplying what he actually lacks.** He is not claiming at a dollar figure. He took 137pt on a 39.05-ATR day (**3.5x ATR**) in eleven minutes; he is reading an impulse exhausting. What he lacks is not judgement but **presence** — he can only watch when he happens to be at the screen, and by his own account only *"the first 90 minutes after open, then it usually calms down"* (which is already exactly what `ENTRY_CUTOFF_MIN` encodes: 13:30Z → 15:00Z).

**The operator asked the sharp version of the question:** *"why cant claude watch it like i watch it and make judgement calls and claim. why do we need algorithms."* Answered honestly and it drove the design:
- The compute objection is dead — 90 minutes at one look a minute is 90 calls; the router already spends 288/day.
- **The real blocker is AUTHORITY, not intelligence.** Claude's entire power here is writing one permissions file. That boundary is why the 08-13 OAuth expiry cost nothing: 125 dead ticks over 10.5 hours and the desk was fine, because a router that stops deciding leaves the switches alone. An actor that stops deciding leaves a position nobody closes.
- **Algorithms exist to be WRONG IN PUBLIC.** A specified rule can be tested over 231 sessions; discretion cannot, which is why neither of us can yet separate his skill from the purple patch he named himself (Q4 direction accuracy 66.7% vs ~50% for the prior nine months, and a rule with no logic at all improves monotonically Q1→Q4).
- **So: Python owns the floor, the machine owns the attention, the operator owns the trigger.**

**BUILT — `gazbot7-rider-peak-watch.service`.** 1 Hz open P&L off `MD_STREAM` `tape` (verified live at 1.03 msg/s). URGENT at **+$200** ("start watching"), a ping per **$50** new high-water mark, a **give-back** alert $75 off the peak, and a **stall** alert at 3 minutes with no new high. The rider's own tick is `*:*:05` — **once a MINUTE** — which was the finest resolution anything on this desk had on an open position.
- READ-ONLY by construction: no `ib_async`, no `placeOrder`, no `INTENTS`, asserted by test against the source. *A notifier that dies is a missed message; an actor that dies is a naked position.*
- Rungs fire only on a NEW high, so a position chopping across $300 cannot machine-gun the one Telegram channel that also carries naked-position alarms.
- **Silence is alarmed** — holding with no tape for 90s pages critically. A watcher that quietly stops watching is indistinguishable from a calm market, and that is this desk's signature failure.
- The STALL alert exists because time-since-new-high is only useful as a TRIGGER: a stalled move fires no rung and no give-back, so as message decoration it would appear exactly when it was irrelevant.
- P&L pinned by test to the real booked trade to the penny: `(29470.75−29607.50) × −1 × 2 × $2 − $1.50×2 = $544.00`. **$2/pt is PER LOT** — mixing per-lot and per-position is what turned a "$200 claim" into $100 banked in the 08-18 study.

**BUILT — `gazbot7-day-rider-claim.path`, and this one is worth money.** The Claim button writes a flag file that the rider only read **on its next tick — up to 60 SECONDS later**. On this very trade the rider's tracked peak was 29458.75 and the claim filled at 29470.75: **12 points, $48**, on a move he watched roll over in real time. A `.path` unit now starts the rider on the inotify write. **Measured end-to-end: 0.02s.**
- ⚠ **`PathModified`, NEVER `PathExists` — this is a live hazard, not a style choice.** `claim_requested()` documents an orphan: a tick can exit by hard-flat or venue stop before the claim branch is reached, *"leaving the file behind with nothing to consume it"* for up to `CLAIM_MAX_AGE_S` = **15 minutes**. Level-triggering would restart the rider in a tight loop for that whole quarter of an hour against the shared IB gateway. Confirmed live during the test: the rider was closed, so the flag was still on disk after the trigger.
- ⚠ **THE INDIRECTION IS NOT THE BUG AND WAS NOT TOUCHED.** The web process still never places an order — 2026-08-06 is what a button reaching the broker directly does (flattened without checking whose position it was, tournament book +2 against a venue of 0, desk halted 11 minutes with the safety block skipped). This unit changed only WHEN the flag is read. The 60s tick remains the FLOOR: if the path unit is dead the claim is picked up on the next tick exactly as before.

**BUILT — `WATCH_RT` in the entry notification.** Confirmation now reads `rt 0.48 → WATCH — favourable band`, so he knows at 13:30 whether today is one of the ~26% the tape has historically paid. Reporting only, wired to no switch, made a pure function so the boundary is testable. **First out-of-sample instance the same day: the +$544 trade confirmed at rt 0.48 — the filter would have kept it. n=1.** Also killed a lie that had been in that message since it was written: it said *"flat 21:00"*, which is the CME halt; it now renders from `FLAT_UTC_MIN` and a test forbids the literal.

**ANSWERED AND CLOSED — can the watcher read the L2 book?** *"heaps of buyers still there so should keep climbing?"* **No, and it must not be rebuilt.** Tested to destruction on 22.6M ticks: far-side depth imbalance vs forward move corr = −0.005 / −0.006 / **+0.006** at 15/5/3min (the sign flips — that is noise); %continued ~50% in every depletion band; OFI over 3.28M snapshots has contemporaneous R² **0.35–0.43** but predictive R²≈0 with a **47–49% hit rate, below a coin flip**, and 0 of 64 cells clear cost. **The far side thins CONCURRENTLY because price eats it, never before.** That is precisely why the DOM feels predictive — the correlation is real, it is just simultaneous. The honest substitute shipped instead is **extension in ATR**, which is descriptive and carries **no threshold on purpose**; a constant there would be an instrument reporting healthy about something it never checked. Genuinely untested and PARKED (not refuted): depletion RATE and cancellation/pull flow, both needing sub-250ms event-time we do not capture.

45 tests across the three files, full suite green. `3c32185`, `281541e`.

## §362 — 2026-08-16 (Sun) — ⛔ NOTHING ACTS UNDER DRIFT. Settled; do not reopen.

**Operator, asked directly whether any safety check should ACT while the desk is in `drift`:
*"no. dont act under drift. leave it."***

Context. On `drift` the tournament's audit loop skips its entire safety block — max-hold, the naked
auditor, re-protect, stop-breach and the exit watchdog. That hole was found on 2026-08-06 and stayed
open because closing it looks trivial and is not. Today it was made **VISIBLE** (counted, published
as `safety_skipped_cycles`, alarmed at cycles 1/12/60 naming each inactive protection, `sweep` CRITs
while holding) and the question of whether to make it **ACT** was put to the operator. The answer is
no.

**Why this is the right call and not merely a deferral.** Drift means our book and the venue disagree
on a **shared, netted** account. Every one of those checks places or cancels an order. Acting on a
position whose ownership is unknown is precisely the 08-06 cascade: a flatten sized on the ACCOUNT
net rather than our share, and a protective stop left resting with no position behind it, which fired
hours later and opened a naked short. The governing rule — *nobody may act unless venue == the sum of
EVERY desk's claim* — is not weakened here.

**The accepted cost, stated plainly:** while drift persists with an open position, that position is
unmanaged. It has no max-hold cut, no stop-breach check and no re-protect. What it does have, as of
today, is a desk that says so loudly instead of showing green.

⚠ **A future session will read "the safety block is skipped on drift" and want to close it.** Don't.
This is decided. `tests/test_drift_safety_visibility.py::test_the_order_path_is_NOT_armed_under_drift`
fails if an order-placing call appears in that branch, and that failure is a REGRESSION, not progress
— do not edit the test to accommodate it. Reopening needs a fresh operator decision *and* an answer
to the ownership question, not a refactor.

## §361 — 2026-08-16 (Sun) — ★★ The project files were stranded in the retired repo for 17 days

**The decision: STATE / SESSIONS / DECISIONS move to `gazbot7/docs/`, and CLAUDE.md becomes purely
instructional again.**

`STATE.md`, `SESSIONS.md` and `DECISIONS_V3_2.md` lived in `/home/alphabot/alphabot2/docs/` — the V5
tree that CLAUDE.md itself declares RETIRED. All three last written **2026-07-30**, the day the
router was made permanent. Seventeen days of V7 history never reached them: the day rider, the
shared-account incident, the IBKR-is-truth ruling, the systemd migration, the gold desk, the shadow
trim.

**The consequence, and it is the reason this matters:** because the real state files were
unreachable, **CLAUDE.md became the de-facto STATE.md** — 492 lines, read verbatim every session,
with a 60-line changelog entry as its largest section. Instructional content and desk state had been
merged for weeks, so the file I read to learn HOW TO BEHAVE was mostly telling me WHAT THE DESK IS,
and both were degrading.

**What each file is for, and the test for where something goes:**
- `/root/CLAUDE.md` — how I behave. Session-start procedure, standing method traps, operator rules,
  the timer/watcher inventory. **Test: would a session that does not know this make a BAD DECISION?**
- `docs/STATE.md` — what the desk IS, right now. Overwritten, never appended. Re-scanned, never
  recalled.
- `docs/SESSIONS.md` — what CHANGED (A → B), why, how to revert. Append-only.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` — the architectural WHY. Numbered, permanent.

**Also decided:** the Friday report's phase list must FIT ITS WINDOW. It declared 1,755m of section
timeouts against a 228m budget and nothing compared the two, so which sections got built was decided
by clock order rather than value. Greenfield clusters now ROTATE 2 per ISO week, each phase is capped
at a fair share rather than handed all remaining time, and the arithmetic is logged at preflight.
Dropped clusters are logged — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it did not.

⚠ STATE.md's previous edition described one desk, 8 services and a 1.9GB `capture.db`. Reality is
three desks, 36 units and 5.3GB. **A state file nobody can reach is worse than no state file**: it
still reads as authoritative.

## §360 — 2026-07-30 (Thu) — ★★ Router trial DAY 2: first 2 green days ever + momentum ER-floor tuning (grind 0.35 validated / abs_veto no-floor) + `/v7/router` panel. (gazbot7 `9767c67`, `e58e1e0`.)

The router-tune trial (§359-era, Claude managing gate benching) was extended by the operator to a 5-min cadence and delivered the desk's **first two green days in a row ever** (07-29 +$638.5, 07-30 +$586). More importantly it fed evidence-backed gate improvements.

**Momentum-long ER floors (`deciders.ER_FLOOR`, `9767c67`), grounded in a 10-day entry-ER reprice (07-20..30):**
- `grind_long` FLOOR **0.35 — VALIDATED**. Flips grind −$670 → **+$58** over 10 days. The killer was the *mid* ER band 0.20–0.35 (−$431 @18%W on 07-30 alone) — rotation legs that read trendy on the 30-min clock but reverse. Reverses the 07-25 rehab (§355) that DROPPED grind's floor ("runners & false-starts share ER 0.14") — that was a trend-week finding; this is a rotation-day one. grind has no absorption-veto, so the ER *is* its trend-confirmation.
- `abs_veto_long` — operator picked 0.25, but the same backtest **DISPROVED it (−$121)**. abs_veto is **bimodal**: winners at LOW ER (0.04–0.18, veto-caught early thrusts — e.g. today's +$251 fired at ER 0.06) AND at high ER (≥0.35); losers ONLY in the mid-band 0.25–0.35. A floor removes its low-ER gems. Its 55s absorption-veto already does the fake-filtering, so **abs_veto wants NO ER floor** (already +$232/10d on its own), or a mid-band 0.25–0.35 EXCLUSION (≈+$460, a code build). **Revert to no-floor recommended/pending operator.**
- LESSON: a plain ER floor fits a NO-veto gate (grind); a veto/absorption gate (abs_veto) wants no floor. Backtest = inline reprice-by-removal (LEAD, needs multi-regime validation) off `gazbot7.db` trades × `capture.db` bars.

**abs_veto (veto) vs grind (no-veto):** abs_veto is the reliable momentum gate — its veto lets it catch thrusts early, then the scale-out banks it (A target + B chandelier). grind CHURNS even floor-gated (buys into resistance/stalls). 07-30 live: abs_veto +$630 (A +202 / B +428) vs grind −$53. Directive-in-practice: run momentum through abs_veto, keep grind mostly benched; grind needs a veto/absorption-check or resistance-awareness, not just an ER floor — a Friday rehab item.

**Built LIVE:** `/v7/router` dashboard panel (`web.py router_json` + `web_static/router.html`, `e58e1e0` + brightness/Paris-time) — multi-clock regime read (30-min gate-ER vs day-ER: the "why is ER 0.30 still chop?" answer = alternating legs cancel), per-gate on/off + auto-derived reason, shadow-family cross-check (momentum-long/short/reversion), timestamped activity stream (Paris time), 2-slot holdings; reads live from `router_trial_log.txt` + switches + DBs, nothing hardcoded. + `scripts/recent_trades.py` (the live bleeding check — exit_reason wall-of-STOP per gate; aggregate P&L hides a stale-tail-masking-a-bleeding-scalp). Dashboard-only (`gazbot7-web`) restart.

**Dual-slot scale-out (§359) proven repeatedly:** 5 dual-profit exits on 07-30 (Lot A TARGET + Lot B CHANDELIER both green): +$163/+$111/+$146/+$72/+$251 — the long-side mirror of yesterday's abs_veto_short +$768.

Revert trial: `cp gate_switches.env.pre-trial gate_switches.env` + re-enable `gazbot7-direction-router.timer`. Revert ER floors: edit `deciders.ER_FLOOR` + restart flat. ⚠ N-small/one-regime throughout; the WRAP cron (21:55 UTC 07-30) scores the trial + re-hands the auto-router.

## §365 — 2026-09-04 (Fri) — ★★★ THE STALE-BOOK FAMILY: four bugs, one root — a book that lags the venue was read as truth. (gazbot7 `15ee4b2`, `643d9e2`, `52dd5ea`, `230d837`.)

Started from *"trying to buy and its not working"* and ended four commits later. Every one of these is the same mistake wearing different clothes: **a record written on one cycle was compared against a venue sampled on another, and the difference was believed.**

**1. THE FALSE KILL, and why the guard could not catch it.** At 16:42:10Z the operator's manual claim closed a SHORT 4 at the venue. The rider rewrites its state once a MINUTE, so for a few seconds the books still said `rider -4` against a venue of 0. `desk_reconcile` confirmed and stopped both desks. Its protection was *"two independent VENUE reads, six seconds apart, with the same imbalance"* — but **a claim is a FILE, not a venue read.** Both reads drew the same unchanged stale claim, agreed perfectly, and confirmed. *The guard re-sampled the wrong side of its own equation and was therefore blind to the exact race it was written to catch.* The DECISION: a breach is confirmed only once **every desk has REWRITTEN its claim** since the imbalance was first seen and still disagrees with IBKR. This is deliberately NOT a weakening — `may_place_order()` already refuses every new order whenever the invariant fails, kill file or not, so nothing can be OPENED during the extra ~60-90s; only the PERSISTENT bench is deferred, and that is precisely the action that must not fire on a race. **The cost of getting this wrong was asymmetric and had already been paid:** `day_rider=off` sits upstream of `buy_requested()`, so the false kill silently ate every BUY press for four hours, and this service never re-arms itself.

**2. THE LOST LOT.** The profit ladder and a per-lot claim can both fire in ONE tick. `step()` builds `out = dict(st)`; the ladder wrote its reduced count to `out` and the claim branch re-read `st` — **two lots left the venue and the book deducted one.** `targets_done` had it worse: re-reading `st` DISCARDED the rung the ladder had just spent, so it could fill twice. This is what FEEDS bug 1 — it leaves the book claiming a lot the venue does not hold. (First seen 2026-08-31, SESSIONS §379; the root cause was recorded then and the code was not changed.)

**3. THE FABRICATED FILL — and the decision NOT to extend the fix to exits.** The IBKR paper engine fills every lot beyond the first at **exactly 0.1% of price**, adverse, rounded to the tick — a price that never prints. 21/21 multi-lot rider orders measure 0.09897-0.09998%, invariant across sessions, sides and volatility regimes; real slippage varies with liquidity and this does not vary at all. **$2,916.50 over 32 orders / 101 lots, against an all-time booked P&L of -$1,771.44** — the artefact is larger than the entire recorded loss. Entries are now marketable LIMITS, because a limit cannot fill worse than its price. **EXITS WERE DELIBERATELY LEFT ON MARKET ORDERS:** *"NEVER HOLD OVERNIGHT. EVER."* is absolute and an exit that does not fill is unbounded, whereas the fabricated fill costs a bounded number of points. A limit belongs only where the failure mode is "no position", which is free. ⚠ The cure introduced its own hazard and it had to be closed in the same change: **a limit can partial-fill where a market order could not**, and both entry paths booked the REQUESTED quantity — which is bug 1's condition exactly. `place_entry()` returns the FILLED quantity, both call sites book it, the ladder is trimmed to it, the stop is sized from it, and the remainder is cancelled.

**4. THE POSITION PRICED AGAINST ITSELF.** `drift_read` is anchored to the 13:30 cash open and returns price 0.0 outside it. The manage path read `px = rr.price or entry`, so outside US hours it priced the open position off **its own entry**: `ahead_pt` read 0 on a trade $220 down, `peak` never moved, **the trail could never arm and no ladder rung could ever fire.** Nothing errored — heartbeat advancing, `venue_ok` true, reconciler clean, note reading *"riding"*. **The entire exit machinery was switched off while every instrument reported healthy.** Fixed with a symbol- and timeframe-pinned tape reader; `entry` survives as the last-resort fallback on purpose, because with no tape at all an inert comparison beats a stale price that could fire a rung.

**★ AND THE SAME BLINDNESS ALMOST BROKE THE FIX FOR BUG 3.** A market order needs no price; a LIMIT must be priced. Pricing entries off `drift_read` alone would have **refused every manual press outside US hours** — the fix would have broken the button it was written to protect. Caught before shipping only because the state file showed `entry_atr: 0.0`.

**ON ATR (operator: *"do the atr one for new entries only"*).** A blind entry froze `arm_atr` at 0 and trailed on the FIXED 150pt rule instead of 4 x ATR — ~29pt vs 150pt at the measured 7pt tape ATR. `last_tape_atr()` **calls `drift.compute()` rather than re-deriving the formula**, because `trail_level`'s own docstring warns that scaling the trail off a differently-defined number is this desk's live/lab divergence — so there is exactly ONE definition of "the rider's ATR", asserted equal to drift's own at five independent times to 1e-9. **New entries only, enforced by test:** the manage path carries `arm_atr` forward untouched, so an open position keeps the rule it was opened under.

**METHOD NOTE, because three of these were invisible to behavioural tests.** Bugs 2, 4 and the buy-while-holding silence are all *"both versions behave identically unless a second thing happened in the same tick / outside a particular window"*. They are asserted **against the SOURCE**, the way `test_tunnel_watch.py` asserts the read-only boundary — and each guard was verified to FAIL on the old code before landing. Two further bugs were caught by writing those tests: an unbounded ATR window that made an equivalence check pass for the wrong reason (returning the same ATR for three different times of day), and a negative-age guard that the bound then made unreachable, deleted rather than left as false comfort.

**⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENCE.** Backing out $2,916.50 would put the book at roughly +$1,145, and that is **not** a claim that the desk is profitable — inside the paper book the money is really gone. It says the number **is not a measurement of the strategy**. Single-lot fills are clean; every multi-lot comparison is contaminated. Whether a LIVE account behaves this way is UNKNOWN and must not be assumed away. `execution-cost-autopsy-stage1`'s *"the desk bleeds DIRECTION not cost"* was concluded without knowing this and needs re-deriving on the clean subset.
